dative.english: In the new department she is being deployed as head.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Feminine dative article der with the weak adjective ending -en. Als Leiterin takes no ending, because als passes through the nominative case of the subject sie.

genitive.german: Er setzt die Erfahrung seines ganzen Teams gezielt ein.
genitive.english: He deploys his whole team's experience in a targeted way.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Erfahrung: seines with the neuter genitive -es, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's own -s. Die Erfahrung is the accusative object of einsetzen.

einsetzen.proTip: Einsetzen is separable, so the prefix splits off in main clauses (Ich setze ... ein) and the participle takes ge- in the middle: eingesetzt. Three senses to keep apart: deploy or use something (accusative object), begin or set in (no object), and the reflexive sich einsetzen für + accusative, meaning to campaign for something.

halten.note: Strong verb meaning 'to hold', 'to stop', and 'to consider'. Verbs do not decline for case, but halten is worth learning precisely for its case government, because its two most common fixed patterns use different cases: jemanden für etwas halten takes the accusative, while von etwas halten takes the dative.

nominative.german: Der Bus hält direkt vor unserem Haus.
nominative.english: The bus stops right in front of our house.
nominative.hint: Subject of hält, so nominative; masculine nominative article der. Note the vowel change in the present tense: halten becomes hält in the third person singular. Vor unserem Haus is dative, marking position.

accusative.german: Ich halte ihn für einen wirklich guten Lehrer.
accusative.english: I consider him a really good teacher.
accusative.hint: Accusative required by für in the fixed pattern halten für, which means 'to consider'. Einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en. Ihn is also accusative, as the object of halte.

dative.german: Was hältst du eigentlich von meinem neuen Plan?
dative.english: What do you actually think of my new plan?
dative.hint: Dative required by von in the fixed pattern halten von, which means 'to think of'. Meinem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en. Contrast this with the accusative in halten für.

genitive.german: Sie hält die Hand des kleinen Kindes ganz fest.
genitive.english: She holds the small child's hand very tight.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Hand: the article becomes des, the adjective takes the weak ending -en, and the noun adds the genitive -es. Die Hand is the accusative object of halten.

halten.proTip: Forms: halten – hielt – hat gehalten, with a vowel change in the present (du hältst, er hält). The two patterns that learners mix up are halten für + accusative (to consider) and halten von + dative (to think of). Also useful: sich halten an + accusative, meaning to stick to a rule.

beschleunigen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to accelerate, to speed up'. Verbs do not decline for case. Beschleunigen works both transitively, where it takes a plain accusative object, and intransitively, where the thing speeding up is simply the subject. Its be- prefix is inseparable and unstressed, which has consequences for the participle.

nominative.german: Der schnelle Zug beschleunigt sehr gleichmäßig.
nominative.english: The fast train accelerates very evenly.
nominative.hint: Subject of beschleunigt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. This is the intransitive use, with no object at all.

accusative.german: Die neue Software beschleunigt den ganzen Prozess erheblich.
accusative.english: The new software speeds up the whole process considerably.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beschleunigen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective ganzen takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: Mit einem besseren Motor beschleunigt das Auto deutlich schneller.
dative.english: With a better engine the car accelerates considerably faster.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the comparative adjective besseren takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Das beschleunigt die Entwicklung des ganzen Marktes.
genitive.english: That accelerates the development of the whole market.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Entwicklung: the article becomes des, the adjective takes the weak ending -en, and the noun adds the genitive -es. Die Entwicklung is the accusative object.

beschleunigen.proTip: Regular and weak: beschleunigte, hat beschleunigt. Because be- is an inseparable, unstressed prefix, the participle has no ge- — beschleunigt, never 'gebeschleunigt'. The same rule covers be-, ge-, er-, ver-, zer-, ent-, emp-, miss-. Opposites: verlangsamen and abbremsen.

führen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to lead, to guide' and, in formal usage, 'to drive a vehicle'. Verbs do not decline for case. Führen takes a plain accusative object when it means to lead someone or run something, and it also forms the very common pattern führen zu + dative, meaning 'to lead to' a result.

nominative.german: Der schmale Weg führt direkt zum kleinen See.
nominative.english: The narrow path leads directly to the small lake.
nominative.hint: Subject of führt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Zum kleinen See is dative, because zu always governs the dative.

accusative.german: Sie führt die kleine Gruppe durch das ganze Museum.
accusative.english: She leads the small group through the whole museum.
accusative.hint: Direct object of führen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; kleine takes the weak ending -e. Durch das ganze Museum is accusative too, governed by durch.

dative.german: Das Fahrzeug darf nur von einem erwachsenen Fahrer geführt werden.
dative.english: The vehicle may only be driven by an adult driver.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which marks the agent in a passive sentence and always governs the dative. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en.

genitive.german: Er führt die Geschäfte seines Vaters seit zwei Jahren.
genitive.english: He has been running his father's business for two years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Geschäfte. Seines shows the masculine genitive -es and the noun adds its own -s: Vaters. Die Geschäfte is the accusative object of führen.

führen.proTip: Weak throughout: führte, hat geführt. Three senses: lead or guide (eine Gruppe führen), run or manage (ein Geschäft führen), and the formal 'drive' (ein Fahrzeug führen — everyday German says fahren). Learn führen zu + dative for consequences: Das führt zu großen Problemen.

schauen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to look'. Verbs do not decline for case, but schauen is worth learning for its prepositions, which take different cases: schauen auf takes the accusative, while nach jemandem schauen and the separable zuschauen take the dative. In everyday German it also takes a plain accusative object for watching things.

nominative.german: Das kleine Kind schaut neugierig aus dem Fenster.
nominative.english: The small child is looking curiously out of the window.
nominative.hint: Subject of schaut, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Aus dem Fenster is dative, because aus always governs the dative.

accusative.german: Er schaut den ganzen Abend einen alten Film.
accusative.english: He watches an old film all evening.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schauen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Den ganzen Abend is also accusative, but as an accusative of duration rather than an object.

dative.german: Sie schaut jeden Tag nach dem kranken Nachbarn.
dative.english: Every day she looks in on the sick neighbour.
dative.hint: Dative required by nach, which always governs the dative. The adjective takes the weak -en, and Nachbar is a weak (n-) noun, so it adds -n outside the nominative singular.

genitive.german: Von hier aus schaut man auf die Uhr des alten Turms.
genitive.english: From here you look at the clock of the old tower.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Uhr: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Auf die Uhr is accusative, because schauen auf always takes the accusative.

schauen.proTip: Weak: schaute, hat geschaut. It is the everyday word in southern Germany and Austria, where the north says gucken and more formal German says sehen. Three patterns with three different cases: schauen auf + accusative, nach jemandem schauen + dative, and jemandem zuschauen + dative.

entstehen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to arise, to come into being'. Verbs do not decline for case, and entstehen is strictly intransitive: it can never take an accusative object, because the thing that comes into being is the subject. Its source is expressed with aus + dative or durch + accusative, and it forms the perfect with sein.

nominative.german: Aus diesem kleinen Streit entstand ein großes Problem.
nominative.english: A big problem arose out of this small argument.
nominative.hint: Subject of entstand, so nominative — with entstehen the thing that comes into existence is always the subject, never an object. Neuter ein has no ending, so the adjective takes the strong ending -es.

accusative.german: Durch einen einzigen kleinen Fehler ist der ganze Schaden entstanden.
accusative.english: The whole damage arose from a single small mistake.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative. This accusative comes from the preposition, not from entstehen — the verb itself takes no object. Der ganze Schaden is the nominative subject.

dative.german: Aus dieser alten Idee ist ein völlig neues Projekt entstanden.
dative.english: A completely new project arose out of this old idea.
dative.hint: Dative required by aus, which always governs the dative. Dieser is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: So entstand die erste Fassung des berühmten Romans.
genitive.english: That is how the first version of the famous novel came into being.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Fassung: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die erste Fassung is the nominative subject.

entstehen.proTip: Forms: entstehen – entstand – ist entstanden, with sein in the perfect because it describes a change of state. It has no passive and no accusative object, so 'etwas entstehen' is impossible — use erzeugen or schaffen for that. The inseparable ent- prefix means there is no ge- in the participle.

wirken.note: Weak verb with two senses: 'to have an effect, to work' and 'to seem, to come across'. Verbs do not decline for case. In the 'seem' sense it takes a predicative adjective, which carries no ending at all; in the 'have an effect' sense it forms the pattern wirken auf + accusative.

nominative.german: Das neue Medikament wirkt schon nach wenigen Minuten.
nominative.english: The new medicine takes effect after just a few minutes.
nominative.hint: Subject of wirkt, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Nach wenigen Minuten is dative, governed by nach.

accusative.german: Seine ruhigen Worte wirkten auf die jungen Zuhörer sehr stark.
accusative.english: His calm words had a very strong effect on the young listeners.
accusative.hint: Accusative required by auf in the pattern wirken auf — this auf is always accusative, even though nothing moves. The plural article die is followed by the weak adjective ending -en. Stark is predicative and takes no ending.

dative.german: Mit seiner ruhigen Stimme wirkte er ausgesprochen sicher.
dative.english: With his calm voice he came across as decidedly confident.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Seiner is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak -en. Sicher is a predicative adjective after wirken and therefore has no ending.

genitive.german: Die Worte des alten Lehrers wirkten noch lange nach.
genitive.english: The old teacher's words had a lasting effect for a long time afterwards.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Worte: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Nachwirken is separable, which is why nach stands at the end.

wirken.proTip: Weak: wirkte, hat gewirkt. The two senses take different shapes — Die Tablette wirkt (has an effect) versus Er wirkt müde (seems tired), where the adjective is predicative and endingless. Learn wirken auf + accusative. Related words: die Wirkung, wirksam. Don't confuse it with wirklich, which is a separate word meaning 'really'.

lösen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to solve', 'to loosen or release', and, reflexively, 'to dissolve'. Verbs do not decline for case. In all its transitive senses lösen takes a plain accusative object; the reflexive sich lösen takes an accusative reflexive pronoun and describes something coming apart on its own.

nominative.german: Der feste Knoten löste sich schließlich von selbst.
nominative.english: The tight knot finally came loose by itself.
nominative.hint: Subject of löste, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Sich is the accusative reflexive pronoun, and the whole thing describes an unassisted process.

accusative.german: Sie hat die schwierige Aufgabe erstaunlich schnell gelöst.
accusative.english: She solved the difficult task astonishingly quickly.
accusative.hint: Direct object of lösen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; schwierige takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In dem warmen Wasser löst sich das Salz sofort.
dative.english: In the warm water the salt dissolves immediately.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location rather than a movement. Neuter dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. The full form in dem is kept for emphasis; it would usually contract to im.

genitive.german: Er löste das Problem des ganzen Teams in einer Stunde.
genitive.english: He solved the whole team's problem in an hour.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Problem: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Das Problem is the accusative object of löste.

lösen.proTip: Weak: löste, hat gelöst. Three senses with one accusative object each: solve (ein Problem lösen), loosen or release (eine Schraube lösen, Verspannungen lösen), and dissolve, normally reflexive (Der Zucker löst sich). The noun die Lösung covers both 'solution to a problem' and 'solution' in the chemical sense.

bestehen.note: Strong verb with four distinct patterns, each with its own case — this is the main thing to learn about it. Bestehen aus + dative means 'to consist of'; bestehen auf + dative means 'to insist on'; with a plain accusative object it means 'to pass' an exam; and the impersonal es besteht + nominative means 'there is'.

nominative.german: Bei diesem Wetter besteht ein großes Risiko.
nominative.english: In this weather there is a considerable risk.
nominative.hint: Nominative, because in the impersonal es besteht pattern the thing that exists is the grammatical subject. Neuter ein has no ending, so the adjective takes the strong ending -es.

accusative.german: Sie hat die schwere Prüfung ohne größere Probleme bestanden.
accusative.english: She passed the difficult exam without major problems.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bestehen in its 'to pass' sense, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; schwere takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Das Team besteht aus fünf sehr erfahrenen Mitarbeitern.
dative.english: The team consists of five very experienced employees.
dative.hint: Dative required by aus in the pattern bestehen aus. There is no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative plural ending -en, and the noun adds the dative plural -n: Mitarbeitern.

genitive.german: Es besteht die Gefahr eines wirklich schweren Unfalls.
genitive.english: There is the risk of a really serious accident.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gefahr: eines with the masculine genitive -es, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's own -s. Die Gefahr is the nominative subject, with es as a placeholder in first position.

bestehen.proTip: Forms: bestehen – bestand – hat bestanden, with no ge- because be- is inseparable. Four patterns, three cases: aus + dative (consist of), auf + dative (insist on), in + dative (consist in), and a bare accusative for exams. The impersonal es besteht die Gefahr / die Möglichkeit is extremely common in written German.

fühlen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to feel'. Verbs do not decline for case. Transitively fühlen takes a plain accusative object (einen Schmerz fühlen). Far more common is the reflexive sich fühlen, which takes an accusative reflexive pronoun and then a predicative adjective — and predicative adjectives never take endings.

nominative.german: Der kranke Mann fühlt sich heute schon viel besser.
nominative.english: The sick man feels much better already today.
nominative.hint: Subject of fühlt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Besser is a predicative comparative after sich fühlen and therefore takes no ending at all.

accusative.german: Ich fühlte plötzlich einen scharfen Schmerz im Rücken.
accusative.english: I suddenly felt a sharp pain in my back.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive fühlen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Im Rücken is dative, marking location.

dative.german: In diesem alten Haus fühle ich mich sehr wohl.
dative.english: I feel very comfortable in this old house.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Diesem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en. Note that mich here is accusative — the reflexive pronoun of sich fühlen.

genitive.german: Er fühlte die angenehme Wärme des offenen Feuers.
genitive.english: He felt the pleasant warmth of the open fire.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wärme: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die angenehme Wärme is the accusative object of fühlte.

fühlen.proTip: Weak: fühlte, hat gefühlt. The reflexive pronoun in sich fühlen is accusative, so Ich fühle mich gut, never 'mir'. The adjective after it stays endingless because it is predicative: Sie fühlt sich krank. Related: das Gefühl, and the near-synonym sich anfühlen for how something feels to the touch.

ausdehnen.note: Separable verb meaning 'to expand, to extend'. Verbs do not decline for case. Transitively ausdehnen takes an accusative object; reflexively sich ausdehnen describes something expanding by itself and takes an accusative reflexive pronoun. Being separable, its prefix splits off in main clauses.

nominative.german: Das warme Metall dehnt sich ganz langsam aus.
nominative.english: The warm metal expands very slowly.
nominative.hint: Subject of dehnt ... aus, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Sich is the accusative reflexive pronoun, and the separable prefix aus stands at the end.

accusative.german: Die Firma will ihr Geschäft nach Osten weiter ausdehnen.
accusative.english: The company wants to expand its business further eastwards.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausdehnen, so accusative. Neuter ihr has no ending and is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case.

dative.german: Nach dem Umbau dehnt sich der Garten bis zu dem kleinen Bach aus.
dative.english: After the conversion the garden extends as far as the small brook.
dative.hint: Dative required by zu, which always governs the dative. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Bis simply reinforces the limit and adds no case of its own here.

genitive.german: Sie dehnten die Grenzen des alten Reiches immer weiter aus.
genitive.english: They kept expanding the borders of the old empire further and further.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Grenzen: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Grenzen is the accusative object of dehnten ... aus.

ausdehnen.proTip: Separable, so the prefix leaves in main clauses (Ich dehne ... aus) and the participle takes ge- in the middle: ausgedehnt. The stress falls on aus, which is the giveaway for separability. The participle ausgedehnt works as an adjective meaning 'extensive'. Near-synonyms: erweitern and sich erstrecken.

beherrschen.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to master, to have command of' and 'to control, to dominate'. Verbs do not decline for case, but the government matters here: beherrschen always takes a direct accusative object, where English often uses a preposition ('to have command of', 'to be good at').

nominative.german: Der junge Pianist beherrscht sein Instrument einfach perfekt.
nominative.english: The young pianist has simply perfect command of his instrument.
nominative.hint: Subject of beherrscht, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Pianist is a weak (n-) noun, and the nominative singular is its one form without -en.

accusative.german: Sie beherrscht drei fremde Sprachen völlig fließend.
accusative.english: She has completely fluent command of three foreign languages.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beherrschen, so accusative plural. After a bare numeral with no article, the adjective takes the strong plural ending -e. Note that German uses a plain accusative here where English needs 'command of'.

dative.german: Viele fürchten, eines Tages von einem Computer beherrscht zu werden.
dative.english: Many fear being controlled by a computer one day.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which marks the agent in a passive construction and always governs the dative. Eines Tages is a genitive time expression meaning 'one day'.

genitive.german: Er beherrscht die Regeln des komplizierten Spiels ganz genau.
genitive.english: He knows the rules of the complicated game very precisely.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Regeln: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Regeln is the accusative object of beherrscht.

beherrschen.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge- in the participle: beherrschte, hat beherrscht. Always a direct accusative object — eine Sprache beherrschen, never 'in einer Sprache'. Reflexively sich beherrschen means to control oneself. Compare plain herrschen, which is intransitive: Hier herrscht endlich Ruhe.

jagen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to hunt' and 'to chase'. Verbs do not decline for case. Plain jagen takes an accusative object (ein Tier jagen), but the separable compounds nachjagen and hinterherjagen take the dative instead — a contrast worth noticing, since the meaning barely changes.

nominative.german: Der alte Jäger jagt schon seit vierzig Jahren.
nominative.english: The old hunter has been hunting for forty years already.
nominative.hint: Subject of jagt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Seit vierzig Jahren is dative, because seit always governs the dative.

accusative.german: Die schwarze Katze jagt eine kleine Maus.
accusative.english: The black cat is chasing a small mouse.
accusative.hint: Direct object of jagen, so accusative. Feminine eine is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; kleine takes the mixed-declension ending -e after an ein-word.

dative.german: Der junge Hund jagt dem roten Ball hinterher.
dative.english: The young dog chases after the red ball.
dative.hint: Dative required by hinterherjagen, which governs the dative rather than the accusative. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Plain jagen would have taken an accusative here instead.

genitive.german: Sie jagen die Tiere des großen Waldes schon lange nicht mehr.
genitive.english: They have long since stopped hunting the animals of the great forest.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Tiere: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Tiere is the accusative object of jagen.

jagen.proTip: Weak: jagte, hat gejagt. Plain jagen takes the accusative, but nachjagen and hinterherjagen take the dative: Er jagt dem Erfolg nach. Related words: der Jäger, die Jagd. There is also a figurative sense meaning 'to race': Die Zeit jagt, and jemanden aus dem Haus jagen means to throw someone out.

verändern.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to change' — to make something different from what it was. Verbs do not decline for case. Transitively verändern takes an accusative object; reflexively sich verändern means 'to change' in the intransitive sense, with an accusative reflexive pronoun.

nominative.german: Das Wetter hat sich in den letzten Tagen völlig verändert.
nominative.english: The weather has changed completely in recent days.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat sich ... verändert, so nominative; neuter nominative article das. Sich is the accusative reflexive pronoun, and in den letzten Tagen is dative plural after in.

accusative.german: Der neue Chef hat die ganze Firma spürbar verändert.
accusative.english: The new boss has noticeably changed the whole company.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verändern, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; ganze takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Über die Jahre hat sich viel an dem alten Haus verändert.
dative.english: Over the years a lot has changed about the old house.
dative.hint: Dative after an in the pattern sich verändern an, which describes where a change shows. Neuter dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Über die Jahre is accusative, governed by über.

genitive.german: Die neue Technik verändert das Leben der ganzen Gesellschaft.
genitive.english: The new technology is changing the life of the entire society.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Leben. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive ending. Das Leben is the accusative object.

verändern.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: veränderte, hat verändert. Transitive with an accusative object, reflexive for change that happens by itself. Compare the neighbours: ändern is usually a deliberate, specific alteration (den Termin ändern), wechseln means to swap one thing for another (die Wohnung wechseln).

leuchten.note: Weak verb meaning 'to shine, to glow'. Verbs do not decline for case, and leuchten is intransitive — it never takes an accusative object, so you cannot 'leuchten something'. What it can take is a dative person you light the way for, and a direction with in + accusative.

nominative.german: Der helle Mond leuchtet über dem stillen Dorf.
nominative.english: The bright moon shines above the quiet village.
nominative.hint: Subject of leuchtet, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Über dem stillen Dorf is dative, because it marks a position rather than a movement.

accusative.german: Er leuchtete mit der Lampe in den dunklen Keller.
accusative.english: He shone the lamp into the dark cellar.
accusative.hint: Accusative after in, because the phrase expresses movement into somewhere. Masculine den with the weak adjective ending -en. This accusative comes from the preposition — leuchten itself takes no object.

dative.german: Sie leuchtete mir mit dem Handy den ganzen Weg.
dative.english: She lit the whole way for me with her phone.
dative.hint: Dative pronoun marking the person for whom the light is provided — jemandem leuchten. Den ganzen Weg is accusative, but as the stretch covered rather than an object of leuchten.

genitive.german: Die Lichter der ganzen Stadt leuchteten in der Nacht.
genitive.english: The lights of the whole city shone in the night.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Lichter. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive ending. Die Lichter is the nominative plural subject.

leuchten.proTip: Weak: leuchtete, hat geleuchtet. It is intransitive, so the thing that shines is always the subject. For 'to illuminate something' with an accusative object you need beleuchten instead: Die Lampe beleuchtet den Tisch. Related: das Licht, die Leuchte, and the adjective leuchtend.

beginnen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to begin'. Verbs do not decline for case. Beginnen can take a plain accusative object (den Kurs beginnen), but its most characteristic pattern is beginnen mit + dative, where German uses the dative exactly where English uses 'with'.

nominative.german: Der neue Kurs beginnt schon am nächsten Montag.
nominative.english: The new course begins as early as next Monday.
nominative.hint: Subject of beginnt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Am nächsten Montag is dative, since am is an + dem.

accusative.german: Nach der Pause beginnen wir den zweiten Teil.
accusative.english: After the break we'll begin the second part.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beginnen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the ordinal adjective zweiten takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: Sie beginnt immer mit dem schwersten Thema.
dative.english: She always begins with the hardest topic.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit in the fixed pattern beginnen mit. Neuter dative dem, with the superlative adjective schwersten taking the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Im April beginnt endlich die Arbeit des neuen Teams.
genitive.english: In April the work of the new team finally begins.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Arbeit: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Arbeit is the nominative subject.

beginnen.proTip: Forms: beginnen – begann – hat begonnen; the participle has no ge- because be- is inseparable. The pattern to memorise is beginnen mit + dative: Wir beginnen mit der ersten Übung. Anfangen is the everyday separable equivalent with the same pattern (Wir fangen mit der Übung an), while starten normally belongs to machines and races.

töten.note: Weak verb meaning 'to kill'. Verbs do not decline for case; they conjugate and assign case. Töten is strictly transitive: the thing killed is always a plain accusative object, which is the one case fact to remember about it. Its intransitive counterpart is sterben, where the person who dies is the subject instead.

nominative.german: Der starke Frost tötete alle jungen Pflanzen.
nominative.english: The heavy frost killed all the young plants.
nominative.hint: Subject of tötete, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Töten has no case form itself but requires a nominative subject.

accusative.german: Das neue Gift tötet die kleinen Insekten sofort.
accusative.english: The new poison kills the small insects immediately.
accusative.hint: Direct object of töten, so accusative plural. The plural article die is the same in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; the adjective takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Mit einem einzigen Schlag tötete er das große Tier.
dative.english: With a single blow he killed the large animal.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit, which always governs the dative. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

genitive.german: Die späte Kälte tötete die Blumen des kleinen Gartens.
genitive.english: The late cold killed the flowers of the small garden.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Blumen: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Blumen is the accusative object of tötete.

töten.proTip: Weak throughout: tötete, hat getötet, and always with an accusative object. Its intransitive partner is sterben, which takes sein and no object: Er ist gestorben versus Man hat ihn getötet. Umbringen is the everyday word and ermorden the legal one; töten is the neutral term.

scheinen.note: Strong verb with two senses: 'to shine' and 'to seem'. Verbs do not decline for case, and scheinen is intransitive in both senses — it never takes an accusative object. In the 'seem' sense it normally takes zu + infinitive and can add a dative person: Mir scheint das richtig.

nominative.german: Die warme Sonne scheint schon den ganzen Morgen.
nominative.english: The warm sun has been shining all morning already.
nominative.hint: Subject of scheint, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Den ganzen Morgen is accusative, but as an accusative of duration, not an object of scheinen.

accusative.german: Der Mond schien die ganze Nacht durch das offene Fenster.
accusative.english: The moon shone through the open window all night.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative. Neuter das with the weak adjective ending -e. This accusative comes from the preposition — scheinen itself takes no object.

dative.german: Mir scheint dieser ganze Plan viel zu riskant.
dative.english: This whole plan seems far too risky to me.
dative.hint: Dative pronoun marking the person to whom something seems — scheinen takes a dative person in this sense. Dieser ganze Plan is the nominative subject, and riskant is predicative, so it has no ending.

genitive.german: Das helle Licht des vollen Mondes schien durch die Bäume.
genitive.english: The bright light of the full moon shone through the trees.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Licht: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Das helle Licht is the nominative subject.

scheinen.proTip: Forms: scheinen – schien – hat geschienen. The 'seem' sense normally takes zu + infinitive: Er scheint müde zu sein. Two derived words to keep apart: anscheinend means 'apparently' (probably true), while scheinbar means 'seemingly' (but not actually so).

bedecken.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to cover'. Verbs do not decline for case. Bedecken takes an accusative object for the thing being covered, and mit + dative for the thing it is covered with — so a single sentence often shows both cases at once, which is worth watching for.

nominative.german: Dichter Schnee bedeckt seit Tagen das ganze Feld.
nominative.english: Thick snow has covered the whole field for days.
nominative.hint: Subject of bedeckt, so nominative. There is no article, so the adjective must carry the case itself with the strong masculine nominative ending -er.

accusative.german: Im Winter sollte man den Kopf mit einer warmen Mütze bedecken.
accusative.english: In winter you should cover your head with a warm hat.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bedecken, so accusative; masculine der becomes den. Note the contrast in the same sentence: mit einer warmen Mütze is dative, governed by mit.

dative.german: Sie bedeckte das schlafende Kind mit einer dicken Decke.
dative.english: She covered the sleeping child with a thick blanket.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it. Das schlafende Kind is the accusative object.

genitive.german: Dicker Staub bedeckte die Möbel des alten Hauses.
genitive.english: Thick dust covered the furniture of the old house.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Möbel: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Möbel is the accusative object.

bedecken.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: bedeckte, hat bedeckt. The frame is etwas mit etwas bedecken — accusative for what gets covered, dative for what covers it. The participle bedeckt also describes the sky: Der Himmel ist bedeckt. Compare decken (den Tisch decken) and zudecken.

steigen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to rise, to climb'. Verbs do not decline for case. Steigen is intransitive and forms its perfect with sein, because it describes a change of place or level — so prices, temperatures and people all steigen, and none of them takes an accusative object.

nominative.german: Die Preise steigen in diesem Jahr besonders stark.
nominative.english: Prices are rising particularly sharply this year.
nominative.hint: Subject of steigen, so nominative plural; the nominative plural article is die. With steigen the thing that rises is always the subject. In diesem Jahr is dative, marking a time.

accusative.german: Er stieg die steile Treppe ganz langsam hinauf.
accusative.english: He climbed the steep staircase very slowly.
accusative.hint: Accusative marking the stretch covered with hinaufsteigen. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the structure identifies the case; steile takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Dichter Rauch stieg aus dem alten Schornstein.
dative.english: Thick smoke rose from the old chimney.
dative.hint: Dative required by aus, which always governs the dative. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en on alten.

genitive.german: Der Wert des kleinen Hauses ist stark gestiegen.
genitive.english: The value of the small house has risen sharply.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Note the perfect with ist, as steigen always takes sein.

steigen.proTip: Forms: steigen – stieg – ist gestiegen, always with sein. For climbing a mountain German prefers auf einen Berg steigen or the transitive besteigen. The separable family is enormous and worth learning as a set: einsteigen, aussteigen, umsteigen, aufsteigen, absteigen.

bewundern.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to admire'. Verbs do not decline for case. Bewundern always takes a direct accusative object, where English often adds a preposition — jemanden bewundern, not 'an jemandem'. That direct government is the key fact about it.

nominative.german: Alle Gäste bewunderten das neue Haus am See.
nominative.english: All the guests admired the new house by the lake.
nominative.hint: Subject of bewunderten, so nominative plural. Alle is a der-word and takes the strong plural ending -e in the nominative; Gäste is the umlauted plural of Gast.

accusative.german: Ich bewundere ihren großen Mut ganz besonders.
accusative.english: I particularly admire her great courage.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bewundern, so accusative: ihren shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective großen takes the weak -en after it.

dative.german: Mit offenem Mund bewunderte das Kind die bunten Bilder.
dative.english: Open-mouthed, the child admired the colourful pictures.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. There is no article, so the adjective must carry the case itself with the strong masculine dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Sie bewundert die Arbeit des jungen Künstlers sehr.
genitive.english: She greatly admires the young artist's work.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Arbeit: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Arbeit is the accusative object.

bewundern.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: bewunderte, hat bewundert. Always a direct accusative object. Related: die Bewunderung, bewundernswert. Don't confuse it with sich wundern über + accusative, which means 'to be surprised at' — same root, very different meaning.

sterben.note: Strong verb meaning 'to die'. Verbs do not decline for case. Sterben is intransitive and takes sein in the perfect: the person who dies is the subject, never an object. The cause is expressed with an + dative — an einer Krankheit sterben — which is the pattern worth memorising.

nominative.german: Der alte Mann starb im vergangenen Winter.
nominative.english: The old man died last winter.
nominative.hint: Subject of starb, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. With sterben the person who dies is always the subject.

accusative.german: Sie starb, ohne ihren einzigen Sohn noch einmal gesehen zu haben.
accusative.english: She died without having seen her only son again.
accusative.hint: Accusative — but as the object of sehen, not of sterben, which never takes an accusative object at all. Ihren shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en.

dative.german: Sein Großvater starb an einer schweren Krankheit.
dative.english: His grandfather died of a serious illness.
dative.hint: Dative required by an in the fixed pattern sterben an. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Der letzte König des kleinen Landes starb kinderlos.
genitive.english: The last king of the small country died childless.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after König: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Kinderlos is predicative and takes no ending.

sterben.proTip: Forms: sterben – starb – ist gestorben, with a vowel change in the present (du stirbst, er stirbt). The cause takes an + dative: an Krebs sterben, an einer Verletzung sterben. For killing use töten. Note gestorben sein describes the state, while the perfect ist gestorben reports the event.

brechen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to break'. Verbs do not decline for case. Brechen works both ways: transitively with an accusative object and haben in the perfect, and intransitively with sein when something breaks by itself. It also changes its vowel in the present: du brichst, er bricht.

nominative.german: Der dünne Ast brach unter dem schweren Schnee.
nominative.english: The thin branch broke under the heavy snow.
nominative.hint: Subject of brach, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. This is the intransitive use, with no object at all.

accusative.german: Sie hat sich beim Sturz den rechten Arm gebrochen.
accusative.english: She broke her right arm in the fall.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive brechen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective rechten takes the weak ending -en. Sich is a dative reflexive pronoun marking whose arm it is.

dative.german: Das dünne Eis brach unter dem schweren Wagen.
dative.english: The thin ice broke under the heavy cart.
dative.hint: Dative after the two-way preposition unter, because the phrase states a position rather than a movement. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Er hat das feierliche Versprechen seines Vaters gebrochen.
genitive.english: He broke his father's solemn promise.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Versprechen. Seines shows the masculine genitive -es and the noun adds its own -s. Das feierliche Versprechen is the accusative object.

brechen.proTip: Forms: brechen – brach – gebrochen, with the present-tense vowel change du brichst, er bricht. Auxiliary depends on the use: haben when transitive (Ich habe den Arm gebrochen), sein when intransitive (Der Ast ist gebrochen). Very productive in compounds: zerbrechen, abbrechen, unterbrechen, ausbrechen, einbrechen.

brennen.note: Mixed verb meaning 'to burn, to be on fire'. Verbs do not decline for case. Brennen is normally intransitive — the thing on fire is the subject, and there is no accusative object. It is called mixed because it changes its vowel like a strong verb but takes the weak endings: brannte, gebrannt.

nominative.german: Das alte Haus brannte die ganze Nacht.
nominative.english: The old house burned all night.
nominative.hint: Subject of brannte, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. With intransitive brennen the burning thing is always the subject.

accusative.german: Die Sonne brannte den ganzen Tag auf das trockene Feld.
accusative.english: The sun beat down on the dry field all day.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration rather than an object — brennen takes no object here. Masculine den with the weak adjective ending -en. Auf das trockene Feld is accusative too, governed by auf in its directional sense.

dative.german: In dem kleinen Ofen brennt ein warmes Feuer.
dative.english: A warm fire is burning in the small stove.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Ein warmes Feuer is the nominative subject, with the strong ending -es because ein has none.

genitive.german: Das Dach des alten Hauses brannte zuerst.
genitive.english: The roof of the old house burned first.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Dach: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Das Dach is the nominative subject.

brennen.proTip: Mixed conjugation: brennen – brannte – hat gebrannt, sharing the pattern with kennen, nennen, rennen and senden. Intransitive, so it takes haben and no object. Useful relatives: verbrennen, abbrennen, anbrennen (to catch or burn in cooking), and the alarm call Es brennt!

betrachten.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to look at closely' and 'to regard, to consider'. Verbs do not decline for case. Betrachten takes a plain accusative object, and in the frame etwas als etwas betrachten the phrase after als copies that accusative rather than taking a case of its own.

nominative.german: Der Besucher betrachtete das große Gemälde sehr lange.
nominative.english: The visitor looked at the large painting for a very long time.
nominative.hint: Subject of betrachtete, so nominative; masculine nominative article der. Das große Gemälde is the accusative object.

accusative.german: Sie betrachtet das Projekt als ihren größten Erfolg.
accusative.english: She regards the project as her greatest success.
accusative.hint: Accusative, because als copies the case of das Projekt, the accusative object of betrachtet. Als never assigns a case of its own — ihren shows the masculine accusative -en and the superlative takes the weak -en.

dative.german: Mit großem Interesse betrachtete er die alten Fotos.
dative.english: With great interest he looked at the old photos.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. There is no article, so the adjective carries the case itself with the strong neuter dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Er betrachtet die Entwicklung des jungen Marktes ganz genau.
genitive.english: He observes the development of the young market very closely.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Entwicklung: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Entwicklung is the accusative object.

betrachten.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: betrachtete, hat betrachtet. It implies deliberate, sustained looking — stronger than sehen, closer to 'to contemplate'. The frame etwas als etwas betrachten copies the accusative, which is why als ihren, not 'als ihr'. Reflexively sich betrachten means to look at oneself.

verbrennen.note: Mixed, inseparable verb meaning 'to burn up, to burn completely'. Verbs do not decline for case. It follows brennen in its forms (verbrannte, verbrannt) and splits by auxiliary: haben when transitive with an accusative object, sein when intransitive. Reflexively it takes a dative reflexive pronoun.

nominative.german: Die alten Briefe sind im Feuer völlig verbrannt.
nominative.english: The old letters burned up completely in the fire.
nominative.hint: Subject of sind ... verbrannt, so nominative plural; the plural article die with the weak adjective ending -en. This is the intransitive use, which takes sein.

accusative.german: Er hat alle alten Papiere im Garten verbrannt.
accusative.english: He burned all the old papers in the garden.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive verbrennen, so accusative plural. Alle is a der-word carrying the plural ending -e, so the adjective drops to the weak ending -en. Transitive use takes haben.

dative.german: Ich habe mir die Hand an dem heißen Topf verbrannt.
dative.english: I burned my hand on the hot pot.
dative.hint: Dative after an, because the phrase states contact and position rather than movement. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Mir is a separate dative reflexive pronoun.

genitive.german: Das Feuer verbrannte die Möbel des ganzen Hauses.
genitive.english: The fire burned up the furniture of the whole house.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Möbel: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Möbel is the accusative object.

verbrennen.proTip: Mixed and inseparable: verbrannte, hat or ist verbrannt, with no ge- because ver- is inseparable. Haben when you burn something (Ich habe das Holz verbrannt), sein when something burns up (Das Holz ist verbrannt). Reflexively the pronoun is dative: Ich habe mir die Finger verbrannt.

entdecken.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to discover'. Verbs do not decline for case. Entdecken always takes a plain accusative object. In the passive, the discoverer appears as von + dative for a person and durch + accusative for a means — a distinction worth watching, since both translate as English 'by'.

nominative.german: Ein junger Forscher entdeckte die alte Stadt im Dschungel.
nominative.english: A young researcher discovered the ancient city in the jungle.
nominative.hint: Subject of entdeckte, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the adjective must carry the case with the strong ending -er. This is mixed declension.

accusative.german: Wir haben einen kleinen Fehler im Text entdeckt.
accusative.english: We discovered a small mistake in the text.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entdecken, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en. Im Text is dative, marking location.

dative.german: Ich wurde zum Glück von einem tollen Verlag entdeckt.
dative.english: Fortunately I was discovered by a great publisher.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which marks the agent in a passive sentence and always governs the dative. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en.

genitive.german: Sie entdeckten die Reste des alten Tempels.
genitive.english: They discovered the remains of the ancient temple.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Reste: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Reste is the accusative object.

entdecken.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: entdeckte, hat entdeckt. Always a direct accusative object. Related: die Entdeckung, der Entdecker. Compare finden, which is about locating something you were already looking for — entdecken implies the thing was previously unknown.

schaffen.note: Careful: these are two different verbs sharing one infinitive. Weak schaffen (schaffte, hat geschafft) means 'to manage, to get done'. Strong schaffen (schuf, hat geschaffen) means 'to create'. Neither declines — verbs conjugate — and both take an accusative object, so only the past forms tell them apart. Both are shown below.

nominative.german: Der fleißige Student schafft die Prüfung ganz sicher.
nominative.english: The hard-working student will certainly pass the exam.
nominative.hint: Subject of schafft, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. This is the weak verb meaning 'to manage'. Student is a weak (n-) noun, and the nominative singular is its one form without -en.

accusative.german: Wir haben die schwere Arbeit noch rechtzeitig geschafft.
accusative.english: We got the hard work done in time after all.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schaffen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; schwere takes the weak ending -e. Geschafft is the weak participle.

dative.german: Mit großer Mühe schaffte er die schweren Kisten in den Keller.
dative.english: With great effort he got the heavy boxes down into the cellar.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine dative ending -er. In den Keller is accusative, marking direction.

genitive.german: Der Künstler schuf die Figuren des berühmten Brunnens.
genitive.english: The artist created the figures of the famous fountain.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Figuren: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Note schuf — the strong past, which marks this as the 'create' verb.

schaffen.proTip: Two verbs, one infinitive. Weak: schaffen – schaffte – hat geschafft, 'to manage' (Ich habe es geschafft!). Strong: schaffen – schuf – hat geschaffen, 'to create' (Er schuf ein Meisterwerk). Both take an accusative object, so the past tense and participle are your only clues. Note also Arbeitsplätze schaffen (to create jobs) with the strong forms.

erobern.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to conquer, to capture'. Verbs do not decline for case. Erobern always takes a plain accusative object — the place or thing taken. Beyond the military sense it is very common figuratively, with the same accusative government: den Markt erobern, jemandes Herz erobern.

nominative.german: Das fremde Heer eroberte die alte Stadt in einer Nacht.
nominative.english: The foreign army conquered the old city in a single night.
nominative.hint: Subject of eroberte, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Die alte Stadt is the accusative object.

accusative.german: Ich denke, dieses neue Produkt wird den Markt erobern.
accusative.english: I think this new product will conquer the market.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erobern, so accusative; masculine der becomes den. This is the figurative use, which takes exactly the same accusative as the literal one.

dative.german: Mit einer erstaunlich kleinen Armee eroberte er das ganze Land.
dative.english: With an astonishingly small army he conquered the whole country.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en; the adverb erstaunlich modifies the adjective and has no ending itself.

genitive.german: Sie eroberten schließlich die Hauptstadt des großen Reiches.
genitive.english: In the end they conquered the capital of the great empire.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Hauptstadt: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Die Hauptstadt is the accusative object.

erobern.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: eroberte, hat erobert. Always a direct accusative object. The figurative uses are everyday German: den Markt erobern, die Herzen erobern, die Charts erobern. Related: die Eroberung, der Eroberer.

entwickeln.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to develop'. Verbs do not decline for case. Transitively entwickeln takes a plain accusative object; reflexively sich entwickeln means 'to develop, to evolve' by itself, with an accusative reflexive pronoun and the starting point marked by aus + dative.

nominative.german: Die junge Firma entwickelt seit Jahren neue Programme.
nominative.english: The young company has been developing new programs for years.
nominative.hint: Subject of entwickelt, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Neue Programme is the accusative object, with the strong plural ending -e because no article is present.

accusative.german: Sie haben ein völlig neues Verfahren entwickelt.
accusative.english: They developed a completely new procedure.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwickeln, so accusative. Neuter ein has no ending, so the adjective carries the case with the strong ending -es; the adverb völlig modifies it and takes no ending.

dative.german: Aus dem kleinen Laden entwickelte sich ein großes Geschäft.
dative.english: Out of the small shop a large business developed.
dative.hint: Dative required by aus, which always governs the dative and here marks the starting point. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Sich is the accusative reflexive pronoun.

genitive.german: Die Firma entwickelt die Technik des neuen Modells weiter.
genitive.english: The company is developing the technology of the new model further.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Technik: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Technik is the accusative object of entwickelt ... weiter.

entwickeln.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: entwickelte, hat entwickelt. Transitive with an accusative object, reflexive for development that happens by itself, with the source in aus + dative. Related: die Entwicklung, der Entwickler, das Entwicklungsland.

tauchen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to dive' and, transitively, 'to dip'. Verbs do not decline for case. Its auxiliary depends on the meaning: sein for the movement into water (Er ist ins Wasser getaucht), haben for the activity (Wir haben zwei Stunden getaucht). The transitive use takes an accusative object.

nominative.german: Der junge Taucher taucht jeden Sommer im warmen Meer.
nominative.english: The young diver dives in the warm sea every summer.
nominative.hint: Subject of taucht, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Im warmen Meer is dative, marking a location, and jeden Sommer is an accusative time expression.

accusative.german: Sie tauchte die Hand vorsichtig in das kalte Wasser.
accusative.english: She carefully dipped her hand into the cold water.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive tauchen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case. In das kalte Wasser is accusative too, but governed by in in its directional sense.

dative.german: In dem klaren See kann man wirklich gut tauchen.
dative.english: You can dive really well in the clear lake.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location rather than a movement. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Sie tauchten stundenlang in der Nähe des alten Schiffes.
genitive.english: They dived for hours near the old ship.
genitive.hint: Genitive required by the fixed expression in der Nähe + genitive: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. In der Nähe is itself dative after in.

tauchen.proTip: Weak: tauchte, with sein for the movement and haben for the activity. Transitively it means 'to dip' and takes an accusative object. The separable compounds are very common: auftauchen (to surface, and figuratively to turn up) and untertauchen (to go under, and figuratively to go into hiding).

funktionieren.note: Weak verb meaning 'to work, to function'. Verbs do not decline for case, and funktionieren is intransitive — a machine funktioniert, but you cannot funktionieren something, so it never takes an accusative object. Note also that verbs ending in -ieren take no ge- in the participle.

nominative.german: Der neue Drucker funktioniert endlich wieder richtig.
nominative.english: The new printer is finally working properly again.
nominative.hint: Subject of funktioniert, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. With this verb the working thing is always the subject — there is no object.

accusative.german: Ohne einen neuen Akku funktioniert das alte Handy nicht.
accusative.english: Without a new battery the old phone doesn't work.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by ohne, which always takes the accusative. Einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en. This accusative comes from the preposition, not from the verb.

dative.german: Mit dem alten Kabel funktioniert der Drucker leider nicht.
dative.english: With the old cable the printer unfortunately doesn't work.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit, which always governs the dative. Neuter dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en on alten.

genitive.german: Die Technik des neuen Systems funktioniert einwandfrei.
genitive.english: The technology of the new system works flawlessly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Technik: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Technik is the nominative subject.

funktionieren.proTip: The participle is hat funktioniert, with no ge- — that rule covers every -ieren verb: studiert, passiert, reserviert, telefoniert. It is strictly intransitive. In everyday speech Germans more often say Das geht nicht or Das klappt nicht than Das funktioniert nicht.

erfinden.note: Strong, inseparable verb meaning 'to invent' and also 'to make up' a story. Verbs do not decline for case. In both senses erfinden takes a plain accusative object. Its participle erfunden doubles as an attributive adjective, and there it does take adjective endings: eine erfundene Geschichte.

nominative.german: Ein deutscher Ingenieur erfand den ersten brauchbaren Motor.
nominative.english: A German engineer invented the first usable engine.
nominative.hint: Subject of erfand, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the adjective must carry the case with the strong ending -er. This is mixed declension.

accusative.german: Er hat die ganze Geschichte einfach erfunden.
accusative.english: He simply made the whole story up.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erfinden, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; ganze takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Von einem völlig unbekannten Handwerker wurde der Apparat erfunden.
dative.english: The apparatus was invented by a completely unknown craftsman.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which marks the agent in a passive sentence and always governs the dative. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en.

genitive.german: Er erfand die Figuren des berühmten Romans in einem Sommer.
genitive.english: He invented the characters of the famous novel in one summer.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Figuren: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Figuren is the accusative object.

erfinden.proTip: Forms: erfinden – erfand – hat erfunden, with no ge- because er- is inseparable. Both senses take an accusative object. Related: die Erfindung, der Erfinder, and the adjectival participle erfunden. Compare entdecken, which is finding something that already existed.

beschränken.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to limit, to restrict'. Verbs do not decline for case. Its key pattern is beschränken auf + accusative — this auf is always accusative even though nothing moves — and the thing being limited is a plain accusative object as well.

nominative.german: Das neue Gesetz beschränkt die Rechte der großen Firmen.
nominative.english: The new law limits the rights of the large companies.
nominative.hint: Subject of beschränkt, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Die Rechte is the accusative object.

accusative.german: Wir beschränken die Diskussion auf einen einzigen Punkt.
accusative.english: We're limiting the discussion to a single point.
accusative.hint: Accusative required by auf in the fixed pattern beschränken auf. Einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en. Die Diskussion is the accusative object of the verb itself.

dative.german: Mit dieser klaren Regel beschränkt man den Aufwand erheblich.
dative.english: With this clear rule one limits the effort considerably.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Dieser is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Das beschränkt die Freiheit des einzelnen Bürgers.
genitive.english: That limits the freedom of the individual citizen.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Freiheit: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Freiheit is the accusative object.

beschränken.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: beschränkte, hat beschränkt. The pattern to memorise is beschränken auf + accusative, including the reflexive sich beschränken auf ('to confine oneself to'). The adjective beschränkt means 'limited', and of a person, rather rudely, 'narrow-minded'.

herausfinden.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to find out'. Verbs do not decline for case. Herausfinden takes a plain accusative object or a dass-clause. Being separable, the prefix heraus splits off in main clauses and the participle takes ge- in the middle: herausgefunden.

nominative.german: Der junge Reporter fand die ganze Wahrheit schnell heraus.
nominative.english: The young reporter quickly found out the whole truth.
nominative.hint: Subject of fand ... heraus, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. The separable prefix heraus stands at the end of the clause.

accusative.german: Ich möchte endlich den wahren Grund herausfinden.
accusative.english: I'd finally like to find out the real reason.
accusative.hint: Direct object of herausfinden, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective wahren takes the weak ending -en. With a modal the verb stays whole at the end.

dative.german: Von meinem alten Kollegen habe ich es zufällig herausgefunden.
dative.english: I found it out by chance from my old colleague.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which always governs the dative. Meinem shows the masculine dative -em, the adjective takes the weak -en, and Kollege is a weak (n-) noun, adding -n outside the nominative singular.

genitive.german: Sie fand den Namen des neuen Besitzers schnell heraus.
genitive.english: She quickly found out the name of the new owner.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Namen: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Den Namen is the accusative object; Name is a weak noun and adds -n.

herausfinden.proTip: Separable and strong: fand heraus, hat herausgefunden, with ge- inside the word. It takes an accusative object or a dass-clause: Ich habe herausgefunden, dass er recht hatte. In speech heraus is usually shortened to raus: rausfinden. Compare erfahren (to learn of) and feststellen (to establish).

verbringen.note: Mixed, inseparable verb meaning 'to spend' — but only time, never money. Verbs do not decline for case. Verbringen always takes an accusative object naming the stretch of time, and the manner or place is added with a preposition carrying its own case.

nominative.german: Die ganze Familie verbringt den Sommer immer am Meer.
nominative.english: The whole family always spends the summer at the sea.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbringt, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Den Sommer is the accusative object, and am Meer is dative.

accusative.german: Ich verbringe jeden freien Tag auf dem Wasser.
accusative.english: I spend every free day on the water.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbringen, so accusative. Jeden is a der-word carrying the masculine accusative -en, so the adjective drops to the weak ending -en. Auf dem Wasser is dative, marking a location.

dative.german: Wir haben den ganzen Urlaub bei meinen Großeltern verbracht.
dative.english: We spent the whole holiday at my grandparents' place.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by bei, which always governs the dative. Meinen shows the dative plural -en and the noun adds the dative plural -n: Großeltern.

genitive.german: Er verbrachte die letzten Jahre seines Lebens in Italien.
genitive.english: He spent the last years of his life in Italy.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Jahre. Seines shows the neuter genitive -es and the noun adds its own -s: Lebens. Die letzten Jahre is the accusative object.

verbringen.proTip: Mixed and inseparable: verbringen – verbrachte – hat verbracht, no ge-. It takes an accusative time expression: Zeit verbringen, den Abend verbringen, das Wochenende verbringen. Never use ausgeben for time — that verb is only for money. Compare bleiben, which is intransitive and takes sein.

verlieren.note: Strong, inseparable verb meaning 'to lose'. Verbs do not decline for case; they conjugate and assign case. Verlieren always takes a plain accusative object. Note that it is not used for getting lost oneself — German uses sich verlaufen on foot and sich verfahren by car for that.

nominative.german: Der kleine Junge verlor seinen neuen Schlüssel.
nominative.english: The little boy lost his new key.
nominative.hint: Subject of verlor, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Junge is a weak (n-) noun, and the nominative singular is its one form without -n.

accusative.german: Sie hat gestern ihren wichtigsten Kunden verloren.
accusative.english: Yesterday she lost her most important client.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verlieren, so accusative. Ihren shows the masculine accusative -en, the superlative takes the weak -en, and Kunde is a weak (n-) noun, so it adds -n outside the nominative singular.

dative.german: Bei dem Streit hat er die Geduld mit seinem Bruder verloren.
dative.english: In the argument he lost patience with his brother.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit, which always governs the dative. Seinem shows the masculine dative -em. Die Geduld is the accusative object of verloren.

genitive.german: Durch diesen Fehler verlor er das Vertrauen des ganzen Teams.
genitive.english: Through this mistake he lost the whole team's trust.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Vertrauen: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Durch diesen Fehler is accusative, governed by durch.

verlieren.proTip: Forms: verlieren – verlor – hat verloren, with no ge- because ver- is inseparable. Always an accusative object. For getting lost yourself use sich verlaufen (on foot) or sich verfahren (driving) — never verlieren. Opposites: finden and gewinnen.

zerstören.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to destroy'. Verbs do not decline for case. Zerstören takes a plain accusative object. Its passive is worth noting because German splits what English calls 'by': durch + accusative for an impersonal cause, von + dative for a person.

nominative.german: Das schwere Erdbeben zerstörte die ganze Stadt.
nominative.english: The severe earthquake destroyed the whole city.
nominative.hint: Subject of zerstörte, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Die ganze Stadt is the accusative object.

accusative.german: Durch das große Feuer wurde die alte Halle zerstört.
accusative.english: The old hall was destroyed by the big fire.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative and marks an impersonal cause in the passive. Die alte Halle is the nominative subject of the passive sentence.

dative.german: Mit einer einzigen Bemerkung zerstörte er die gute Stimmung.
dative.english: With a single remark he destroyed the good mood.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Der lange Krieg zerstörte die Denkmäler der alten Stadt.
genitive.english: The long war destroyed the monuments of the old city.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Denkmäler. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive ending.

zerstören.proTip: Weak and inseparable, so no ge-: zerstörte, hat zerstört, always with an accusative object. In the passive, use durch + accusative for a cause and von + dative for a person. The zer- prefix means 'to pieces' throughout: zerbrechen, zerreißen, zerschneiden.

heißen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to be called'. Verbs do not decline for case, and heißen is special in the case it assigns: like sein and werden it is a linking verb, so the name after it stays in the NOMINATIVE, not the accusative. Er heißt Peter — Peter is nominative.

nominative.german: Der neue Kollege heißt übrigens Thomas.
nominative.english: The new colleague is called Thomas, by the way.
nominative.hint: Subject of heißt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Thomas is nominative too, because heißen links two nominatives rather than taking an object.

accusative.german: Das heißt aber nicht, dass wir einen neuen Plan brauchen.
accusative.english: But that doesn't mean we need a new plan.
accusative.hint: Direct object of brauchen, so accusative — not of heißen, which never takes an accusative object. Einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en.

dative.german: Man hieß den Gast mit warmen Worten willkommen.
dative.english: The guest was welcomed with warm words.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by mit. With no article the adjective takes the strong dative plural ending -en, and the noun adds the dative plural -n. Willkommen heißen is the one use of heißen with an accusative object: den Gast.

genitive.german: Der Titel des neuen Buches heißt einfach nur 'Zeit'.
genitive.english: The title of the new book is simply 'Time'.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Titel: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Der Titel is the nominative subject.

heißen.proTip: Forms: heißen – hieß – hat geheißen. The crucial point is the predicate nominative: Ich heiße Anna, Er heißt Peter — never an accusative. Other uses: es heißt ('it is said', 'the saying goes') and das heißt, abbreviated d. h., meaning 'that is'. The only transitive use is jemanden willkommen heißen.

umrunden.note: Weak verb meaning 'to circle, to travel all the way around'. Verbs do not decline for case. Here um- is an inseparable prefix with the stress on the stem, which means it never splits off and the participle takes no ge-: umrundet. It always governs a plain accusative object.

nominative.german: Ein kleiner Satellit umrundet die Erde in neunzig Minuten.
nominative.english: A small satellite circles the earth in ninety minutes.
nominative.hint: Subject of umrundet, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the adjective takes the strong ending -er. Satellit is a weak (n-) noun, and the nominative singular is its form without -en.

accusative.german: Das alte Schiff umrundete das gefährliche Kap.
accusative.english: The old ship rounded the dangerous cape.
accusative.hint: Direct object of umrunden, so accusative. Neuter das is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; the adjective takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In einem einzigen Tag umrundet die Station die Erde mehrmals.
dative.english: In a single day the station circles the earth several times.
dative.hint: Dative after in, which takes the dative for periods of time. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

genitive.german: Der Satellit umrundet den Kern des großen Planeten.
genitive.english: The satellite circles the core of the large planet.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kern: des and the weak adjective ending -en. Planet is a weak (n-) noun, so its genitive singular is Planeten, not 'Planetes'.

umrunden.proTip: Inseparable because the stress falls on the stem: umrundete, hat umrundet, no ge-. Contrast the separable um- verbs, which do split and do take ge- inside: Ich steige um, ich bin umgestiegen. Near-synonym: umkreisen, which behaves exactly the same way.

fallen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to fall'. Verbs do not decline for case. Fallen is intransitive and takes sein in the perfect, so it never has an accusative object — for dropping something you say etwas fallen lassen. It very often adds a dative pronoun naming the person affected.

nominative.german: Der erste Schnee fällt hier schon im November.
nominative.english: The first snow falls here as early as November.
nominative.hint: Subject of fällt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Note the vowel change in the present tense: du fällst, er fällt.

accusative.german: Der Apfel fiel durch das dichte Laub auf den Boden.
accusative.english: The apple fell through the thick foliage onto the ground.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative. This accusative comes from the preposition — fallen itself takes no object. Auf den Boden is accusative too, marking direction.

dative.german: Das volle Glas fiel ihm plötzlich aus der Hand.
dative.english: The full glass suddenly fell out of his hand.
dative.hint: Dative pronoun naming the person affected — a very common German pattern where English uses a possessive ('out of his hand'). Aus der Hand is dative too, governed by aus.

genitive.german: Die Preise des neuen Modells sind stark gefallen.
genitive.english: The prices of the new model have fallen sharply.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Preise: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Note the perfect with sind, since fallen always takes sein.

fallen.proTip: Forms: fallen – fiel – ist gefallen, with sein and the present-tense vowel change du fällst, er fällt. Learn the dative-of-the-person pattern: Mir ist das Glas gefallen. The separable family nearly all take a dative object too: gefallen (to please), auffallen (to strike someone), einfallen (to occur to someone).

reichen.note: Weak verb with three senses and three different structures: 'to be enough' (intransitive, often with a dative person), 'to hand something to someone' (dative person plus accusative thing), and 'to extend, to reach' (usually with bis zu + dative). Verbs do not decline for case, but this range of government is worth learning as a set.

nominative.german: Eine einzige Stunde reicht für die ganze Arbeit.
nominative.english: A single hour is enough for the whole job.
nominative.hint: Subject of reicht, so nominative. Feminine eine is identical in nominative and accusative; the adjective takes the mixed-declension ending -e. Für die ganze Arbeit is accusative, governed by für.

accusative.german: Sie reichte ihm einen heißen Kaffee über den Tisch.
accusative.english: She handed him a hot coffee across the table.
accusative.hint: Direct object of reichen in its 'hand over' sense, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Ihm is the dative indirect object.

dative.german: Das Geld reicht mir noch bis zum Monatsende.
dative.english: The money is still enough for me until the end of the month.
dative.hint: Dative pronoun naming the person for whom something suffices — reichen takes a dative person in this sense, never an accusative. Das Geld is the nominative subject.

genitive.german: Der Garten reicht bis an die Mauer des alten Klosters.
genitive.english: The garden extends as far as the wall of the old monastery.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Mauer: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Mauer is accusative after an, which here marks a limit reached.

reichen.proTip: Weak: reichte, hat gereicht. Three structures: Das reicht mir (dative person), Reich mir bitte das Salz (dative plus accusative), and Der Weg reicht bis zum See (bis zu + dative). Related: ausreichen (to suffice) and erreichen (to reach a goal), which is transitive with an accusative.

nutzen.note: Weak verb with two governments that are easy to confuse. Meaning 'to use something', it takes an accusative object: eine Chance nutzen. Meaning 'to be of use to someone', it takes a DATIVE object: Das nutzt mir nichts. Verbs do not decline, but this split is the central fact about nutzen.
