nominative.german: Die neue Methode nutzt allen Beteiligten sehr.
nominative.english: The new method is of great use to everyone involved.
nominative.hint: Subject of nutzt, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Allen Beteiligten is the dative object required by this sense of nutzen.

accusative.german: Wir nutzen den freien Tag für einen kleinen Ausflug.
accusative.english: We're using the free day for a small trip.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nutzen in its 'make use of' sense, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective freien takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Diese Regel nutzt vor allem den kleinen Firmen.
dative.english: This rule benefits the small companies above all.
dative.hint: Dative plural, required by nutzen in its 'be of use to' sense. The dative plural article is den, the adjective takes the weak ending -en, and Firmen is the plural form.

genitive.german: Sie nutzt die große Erfahrung ihres alten Lehrers.
genitive.english: She makes use of her old teacher's great experience.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Erfahrung: ihres, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die große Erfahrung is the accusative object.

nutzen.proTip: One verb, two cases: accusative for 'to use' (die Zeit nutzen), dative for 'to benefit' (Das nutzt niemandem). The variant nützen means the same and is preferred in the south. Related: benutzen and verwenden, both accusative only, plus der Nutzen and nützlich.

schlagen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to hit, to beat, to strike'. Verbs do not decline for case. Schlagen takes a plain accusative object and changes its vowel in the present tense: du schlägst, er schlägt. It also commonly adds a dative pronoun for the person affected, as in Das Herz schlug ihm bis zum Hals.

nominative.german: Der starke Wind schlug die ganze Nacht gegen das Fenster.
nominative.english: The strong wind beat against the window all night.
nominative.hint: Subject of schlug, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Gegen das Fenster is accusative, because gegen always governs the accusative.

accusative.german: Er hat den Nagel mit einem Hammer in die Wand geschlagen.
accusative.english: He hammered the nail into the wall.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schlagen, so accusative; masculine der becomes den. Mit einem Hammer is dative, and in die Wand is accusative because it expresses direction.

dative.german: Vor Aufregung schlug ihm das Herz bis zum Hals.
dative.english: His heart was pounding in his throat with excitement.
dative.hint: Dative pronoun naming the person affected, where English uses a possessive ('his heart'). Das Herz is the nominative subject of schlug.

genitive.german: Die alte Uhr des hohen Turms schlägt jede volle Stunde.
genitive.english: The old clock of the high tower strikes every full hour.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Uhr: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Jede volle Stunde is an accusative time expression.

schlagen.proTip: Forms: schlagen – schlug – hat geschlagen, with the present-tense vowel change du schlägst, er schlägt. Accusative object. Very productive: vorschlagen (to suggest — dative person plus accusative thing), einschlagen, zuschlagen, and eine Mannschaft schlagen for beating a team.

schrumpfen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to shrink'. Verbs do not decline for case. Schrumpfen is intransitive and takes sein in the perfect, so it never has an accusative object — the thing getting smaller is always the subject. To make something shrink you need verkleinern or schrumpfen lassen.

nominative.german: Der alte Pullover ist beim Waschen stark geschrumpft.
nominative.english: The old jumper shrank a lot in the wash.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist ... geschrumpft, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Note the auxiliary sein, which schrumpfen always takes.

accusative.german: Über die letzten Jahre ist der Markt deutlich geschrumpft.
accusative.english: Over the last few years the market has shrunk considerably.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by über in its 'over a span of time' sense. The plural article die is followed by the weak adjective ending -en. This accusative comes from the preposition, not from the verb.

dative.german: In den letzten Jahren ist die Zahl der Nutzer eher geschrumpft als gestiegen.
dative.english: In recent years the number of users has shrunk rather than grown.
dative.hint: Dative plural after in, which takes the dative for periods of time. Den is the dative plural article, the adjective takes the weak ending -en, and the noun adds the dative plural -n.

genitive.german: Die Zahl der jungen Mitglieder schrumpft weiter.
genitive.english: The number of young members keeps shrinking.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural expressing 'of' after Zahl. The genitive plural article is der and the adjective takes the weak ending -en; Mitglieder is the plural form.

schrumpfen.proTip: Weak and intransitive: schrumpfte, ist geschrumpft, always with sein. There is no accusative object — use verkleinern or reduzieren for making something smaller. Its opposites are wachsen (ist gewachsen) and steigen. Related noun: die Schrumpfung.

stürzen.note: Weak verb that splits by auxiliary. Intransitively it means 'to fall, to plunge' and takes sein. Transitively it means 'to topple, to overthrow' and takes haben plus an accusative object. Verbs do not decline for case; this auxiliary split is the thing to watch.

nominative.german: Der alte Mann ist auf der nassen Treppe gestürzt.
nominative.english: The old man fell on the wet stairs.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist ... gestürzt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. This is the intransitive use, which takes sein and has no object.

accusative.german: Die Demonstranten stürzten schließlich die alte Regierung.
accusative.english: The demonstrators finally toppled the old government.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive stürzen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; the adjective takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Auf dem nassen Boden stürzte sie ziemlich schwer.
dative.english: She fell rather badly on the wet floor.
dative.hint: Dative after the two-way preposition auf, because the phrase states a location rather than a movement. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Preise des neuen Modells stürzten innerhalb einer Woche.
genitive.english: The prices of the new model plunged within a week.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Preise: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Innerhalb einer Woche is also genitive, because innerhalb governs the genitive.

stürzen.proTip: Weak: stürzte, with sein for falling (Er ist gestürzt) and haben for toppling (Sie haben die Regierung gestürzt). The reflexive sich stürzen auf + accusative means 'to pounce on'. Related: der Sturz, and abstürzen for planes crashing and computers freezing.

umkreisen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to orbit, to circle around'. Verbs do not decline for case. As with umrunden, the um- here is an inseparable prefix carrying no stress, so it never splits and the participle has no ge-: umkreist. It always takes a plain accusative object.

nominative.german: Ein kleiner Mond umkreist den fernen Planeten.
nominative.english: A small moon orbits the distant planet.
nominative.hint: Subject of umkreist, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the adjective carries the case with the strong ending -er. Planeten is accusative, and the -n comes from its weak noun class.

accusative.german: Die Erde umkreist die Sonne in einem Jahr.
accusative.english: The earth orbits the sun in one year.
accusative.hint: Direct object of umkreisen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case. In einem Jahr is dative, marking a period of time.

dative.german: Mit großer Geschwindigkeit umkreist die Station die Erde.
dative.english: The station orbits the earth at great speed.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective must carry the case itself with the strong feminine dative ending -er.

genitive.german: Der Satellit umkreist den Kern des fernen Systems.
genitive.english: The satellite orbits the core of the distant system.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kern: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Den Kern is the accusative object.

umkreisen.proTip: Inseparable, so umkreiste, hat umkreist with no ge-. The stress test is reliable: stress on the stem means inseparable (umKREIsen), stress on the prefix means separable (UMsteigen). Figuratively it also means to circle around a topic. Related noun: die Umlaufbahn.

aufbauen.note: Separable weak verb meaning 'to build up, to set up'. Verbs do not decline for case. Aufbauen takes a plain accusative object. Being separable, the prefix auf splits off in main clauses and the participle puts ge- in the middle: aufgebaut.

nominative.german: Der junge Unternehmer baut gerade eine neue Firma auf.
nominative.english: The young entrepreneur is currently building up a new company.
nominative.hint: Subject of baut ... auf, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. The separable prefix auf stands at the end of the clause.

accusative.german: Sie haben das ganze Zelt in einer knappen Stunde aufgebaut.
accusative.english: They put the whole tent up in barely an hour.
accusative.hint: Direct object of aufbauen, so accusative. Neuter das is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; ganze takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: Nach dem Krieg wurde die Stadt mit großer Mühe wieder aufgebaut.
dative.english: After the war the city was rebuilt with great effort.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine dative ending -er. Nach dem Krieg is dative too, governed by nach.

genitive.german: Er baut die ganze Organisation des neuen Vereins auf.
genitive.english: He is building up the entire organisation of the new club.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Organisation: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die ganze Organisation is the accusative object.

aufbauen.proTip: Separable and weak: Ich baue ... auf, hat aufgebaut with ge- inside. Accusative object. Three senses: assemble something physical (ein Zelt aufbauen), develop something over time (eine Firma aufbauen), and reflexively sich aufbauen vor + dative, to plant oneself in front of someone. Related: der Aufbau.

zurücklegen.note: Separable weak verb meaning 'to cover a distance' and also 'to put aside, to set by'. Verbs do not decline for case. In both senses zurücklegen takes a plain accusative object. Being separable, zurück splits off in main clauses and the participle takes ge- in the middle: zurückgelegt.

nominative.german: Der schnelle Läufer legt jeden Tag zehn Kilometer zurück.
nominative.english: The fast runner covers ten kilometres every day.
nominative.hint: Subject of legt ... zurück, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Zehn Kilometer is the accusative object and jeden Tag an accusative time expression.

accusative.german: Wir haben an diesem Tag eine sehr lange Strecke zurückgelegt.
accusative.english: That day we covered a very long distance.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zurücklegen, so accusative. Feminine eine is identical in nominative and accusative; the adjective takes the mixed-declension ending -e after an ein-word.

dative.german: Mit dem alten Fahrrad legte er den Weg täglich zurück.
dative.english: He covered the route daily on the old bicycle.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Neuter dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en. Den Weg is the accusative object of legte ... zurück.

genitive.german: Der Zug legt die Strecke des ganzen Tals in zwanzig Minuten zurück.
genitive.english: The train covers the stretch of the whole valley in twenty minutes.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Strecke: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Strecke is the accusative object.

zurücklegen.proTip: Separable and weak: hat zurückgelegt, with ge- inside. Two senses, both accusative: cover a distance (eine Strecke zurücklegen) and put aside or reserve (Geld zurücklegen, Ich lasse mir das Buch zurücklegen). Note that zurück is invariable as always.

fangen.note: Strong verb meaning 'to catch'. Verbs do not decline for case. Fangen takes a plain accusative object and changes its vowel in the present tense: du fängst, er fängt. Its reflexive sich fangen means to regain one's balance or composure.

nominative.german: Die schnelle Katze fängt fast jede Maus im Garten.
nominative.english: The fast cat catches almost every mouse in the garden.
nominative.hint: Subject of fängt, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Note the vowel change in the third person singular: fangen becomes fängt.

accusative.german: Er fing den harten Ball mit einer einzigen Hand.
accusative.english: He caught the hard ball with a single hand.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fangen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective harten takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: Mit einem großen Netz fingen sie die letzten Fische.
dative.english: With a large net they caught the last fish.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Sie fangen die Fische des kleinen Sees schon lange nicht mehr.
genitive.english: They have long since stopped catching the fish of the small lake.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Fische: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Fische is the accusative object.

fangen.proTip: Forms: fangen – fing – hat gefangen, with the vowel change du fängst, er fängt. Accusative object. Related: anfangen (to begin — separable, with mit + dative), gefangen (captive), der Fang, and the children's game Fangen spielen.

dehnen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to stretch'. Verbs do not decline for case. Transitively dehnen takes a plain accusative object; reflexively sich dehnen describes something stretching by itself, with an accusative reflexive pronoun — and it works for time as well as material: Die Stunde dehnte sich.

nominative.german: Das warme Gummi dehnt sich ganz leicht.
nominative.english: The warm rubber stretches very easily.
nominative.hint: Subject of dehnt, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. Sich is the accusative reflexive pronoun of the intransitive use.

accusative.german: Vor dem Sport dehnt sie immer die müden Muskeln.
accusative.english: Before sport she always stretches her tired muscles.
accusative.hint: Direct object of dehnen, so accusative plural. The plural article die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; the adjective takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Mit einer langsamen Übung dehnt man den ganzen Rücken.
dative.english: With a slow exercise you stretch the whole back.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it. Den ganzen Rücken is the accusative object.

genitive.german: Der Physiotherapeut dehnt die Muskeln des rechten Beins.
genitive.english: The physiotherapist stretches the muscles of the right leg.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Muskeln: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Muskeln is the accusative object.

dehnen.proTip: Weak: dehnte, hat gedehnt. Transitive with an accusative object, reflexive for stretching by itself — including metaphorically of time. Compare ausdehnen (to expand in area or scope) and strecken (to stretch out a limb). Related: die Dehnung, dehnbar.

ausgehen.note: Separable strong verb with three senses: 'to go out' socially, 'to run out' of something, and — most important for written German — ausgehen von + dative, meaning 'to assume, to proceed from'. Verbs do not decline for case; it is that dative pattern that matters most here. It takes sein.

nominative.german: Am Wochenende geht die ganze Familie gern aus.
nominative.english: At the weekend the whole family likes to go out.
nominative.hint: Subject of geht ... aus, so nominative; feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. The separable prefix aus stands at the end of the clause.

accusative.german: Wir gehen jeden zweiten Freitag zusammen aus.
accusative.english: Every other Friday we go out together.
accusative.hint: Accusative time expression stating how often — German puts such phrases in the accusative. Jeden is a der-word with the masculine accusative -en, so the ordinal takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Ich gehe vorerst von einem guten Ergebnis aus.
dative.english: For now I'm assuming a good result.
dative.hint: Dative required by von in the fixed pattern ausgehen von, meaning 'to assume'. Einem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

genitive.german: Das Geld des ganzen Projekts ging viel zu schnell aus.
genitive.english: The money for the whole project ran out far too quickly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Geld: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Das Geld is the nominative subject.

ausgehen.proTip: Separable and strong: ging aus, ist ausgegangen, always with sein. The pattern to memorise is ausgehen von + dative, and its everyday shorthand Ich gehe davon aus, dass ... — indispensable in formal German. Also Das Benzin geht aus (runs out) and Es ist gut ausgegangen (it turned out well).

suchen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to look for, to search'. Verbs do not decline for case. Suchen has two equally correct structures with almost the same meaning: a plain accusative object (Ich suche den Schlüssel) or suchen nach + dative (Ich suche nach dem Schlüssel), which suggests a longer or vaguer search.

nominative.german: Der alte Mann sucht seit einer Stunde seine Brille.
nominative.english: The old man has been looking for his glasses for an hour.
nominative.hint: Subject of sucht, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Seit einer Stunde is dative, because seit always governs the dative.

accusative.german: Wir suchen dringend einen neuen Mitarbeiter.
accusative.english: We're urgently looking for a new employee.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchen, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en. Note that German needs no preposition here, unlike English 'look for'.

dative.german: Sie sucht schon lange nach einer besseren Wohnung.
dative.english: She has been looking for a better flat for a long time.
dative.hint: Dative required by nach in the pattern suchen nach. Einer is the feminine dative form and the comparative adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Er sucht im Internet die Adresse des neuen Büros.
genitive.english: He is looking online for the address of the new office.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Adresse: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Adresse is the accusative object.

suchen.proTip: Weak: suchte, hat gesucht. Both structures are standard — a bare accusative, or nach + dative for a more open-ended search. Watch the relatives, which have quite different meanings: besuchen (to visit), versuchen (to try), untersuchen (to examine), all inseparable and all with an accusative object.

sinken.note: Strong verb meaning 'to sink' and, of numbers, 'to fall'. Verbs do not decline for case. Sinken is intransitive and takes sein, so it never has an accusative object — a ship sinkt, but you cannot sinken a ship. For that German uses the weak transitive senken or versenken.

nominative.german: Das alte Schiff sank in nur wenigen Minuten.
nominative.english: The old ship sank in just a few minutes.
nominative.hint: Subject of sank, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. With sinken the thing going down is always the subject.

accusative.german: Durch den langen kalten Winter sind die Temperaturen weiter gesunken.
accusative.english: Because of the long cold winter the temperatures have fallen further.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative. Masculine den with the weak adjective ending -en on both adjectives. This accusative comes from the preposition, not from sinken.

dative.german: Die Sonne sank langsam hinter dem hohen Berg.
dative.english: The sun slowly sank behind the high mountain.
dative.hint: Dative after the two-way preposition hinter, because the phrase states a position rather than a movement into a place. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Wert des alten Hauses ist deutlich gesunken.
genitive.english: The value of the old house has fallen considerably.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -es. Note the perfect with ist, since sinken always takes sein.

sinken.proTip: Forms: sinken – sank – ist gesunken, always with sein and never with an object. Its transitive partner is the weak verb senken: die Preise senken (to lower prices) versus die Preise sinken (prices fall). The opposite is steigen, which behaves identically.

treiben.note: Strong verb meaning 'to drift' when intransitive and 'to drive, to push' when transitive. Verbs do not decline for case. The auxiliary follows that split: sein when something drifts, haben when someone drives something. It also forms the everyday fixed phrase Sport treiben.

nominative.german: Das kleine Boot trieb stundenlang auf dem offenen Meer.
nominative.english: The small boat drifted for hours on the open sea.
nominative.hint: Subject of trieb, so nominative; neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e. This is the intransitive use, with no object at all.

accusative.german: Der Bauer trieb die Kühe früh auf die Weide.
accusative.english: The farmer drove the cows out to the pasture early.
accusative.hint: Direct object of the transitive treiben, so accusative plural. The plural article die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case. Auf die Weide is accusative too, marking direction.

dative.german: Das nasse Holz trieb ruhig auf dem stillen Wasser.
dative.english: The wet wood drifted calmly on the still water.
dative.hint: Dative after the two-way preposition auf, because the phrase states a location rather than a movement. Neuter dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Wind trieb das Boot in die Mitte des großen Sees.
genitive.english: The wind drove the boat into the middle of the large lake.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Mitte: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Mitte is accusative after in, which marks direction here.

treiben.proTip: Forms: treiben – trieb – getrieben, with sein when drifting and haben when driving something. The fixed phrase Sport treiben is the one every learner needs. Related: antreiben (to propel), vertreiben (to drive away), betreiben (to operate a business), and der Trieb.

überleben.note: Weak, inseparable verb meaning 'to survive'. Verbs do not decline for case. Überleben takes a plain accusative object for what was survived — den Unfall überleben — or stands alone with no object at all. The prefix über- is unstressed here, which makes it inseparable and leaves no ge- in the participle.

nominative.german: Nur zwei Passagiere überlebten den schweren Unfall.
nominative.english: Only two passengers survived the serious accident.
nominative.hint: Subject of überlebten, so nominative plural. After a bare numeral there is no article and no adjective, so nothing carries a visible ending here; the verb agreement shows the case.

accusative.german: Der alte Baum hat sogar den harten Winter überlebt.
accusative.english: The old tree even survived the hard winter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of überleben, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective harten takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: Mit großem Glück überlebte er den schweren Absturz.
dative.english: With great luck he survived the serious crash.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong neuter dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Er überlebte die vollständige Zerstörung der ganzen Stadt.
genitive.english: He survived the complete destruction of the entire city.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zerstörung. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive ending. Die Zerstörung is the accusative object.

überleben.proTip: Inseparable, so überlebte, hat überlebt with no ge-. The stress test works here too: überLEben is inseparable, but ÜBERlaufen with stress on the prefix is separable and gives übergelaufen. It takes an accusative object or none at all. Related: der Überlebende, das Überleben.

sparen.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to save' (money, time, or resources). Verbs do not decline for case — they conjugate for person and tense. Sparen is transitive and requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was spart man?). The examples below show case in sentences containing sparen.

nominative.german: Der Student spart jeden Monat etwas Geld für den Urlaub.
nominative.english: The student saves some money every month for the vacation.
nominative.hint: Subject of spart, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; Student is a weak (n-) noun, but takes no ending in the nominative singular.

accusative.german: Durch die neue Software sparen wir viel Zeit.
accusative.english: Through the new software we save a lot of time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sparen, so accusative. Uncountable singular noun Zeit with the invariable quantifier viel; feminine Zeit takes no case ending.

dative.german: Mit dem neuen Auto sparen wir erstaunlich viel Benzin.
dative.english: With the new car we save an astonishing amount of petrol.
dative.hint: Dative required by the preposition mit, which always governs the dative. Neuter dative article dem, followed by the weak adjective ending -en on neuen.

genitive.german: Die Vorteile des Sparens liegen für viele Menschen auf der Hand.
genitive.english: The advantages of saving are obvious to many people.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vorteile. Sparen is a capitalized gerund (nominalized neuter infinitive), taking the neuter genitive article des and ending -s.

sparen.proTip: Key prepositions: sparen an + dative means 'to economize / skimp on' (an der falschen Stelle sparen); sparen auf/für + accusative means 'to save up for' (auf ein Auto sparen). Distinguish sparen (to save money/effort) from retten (to rescue/save a life).

erforschen.note: Transitive verb with the inseparable prefix er- meaning 'to research, explore, systematically investigate'. Verbs do not decline for case. Erforschen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was erforscht man?).

nominative.german: Die Wissenschaftlerin erforscht unbekannte Tiefseegebiete.
nominative.english: The female scientist is researching unknown deep-sea areas.
nominative.hint: Subject of erforscht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; female suffix -in takes no ending in the singular.

accusative.german: Das Team erforscht die Ursachen des Klimawandels.
accusative.english: The team is researching the causes of climate change.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erforscht, so accusative plural. Plural definite article die; noun Ursachen ends in -n.

dative.german: Die Biologen helfen der Universität, seltene Tierarten zu erforschen.
dative.english: The biologists help the university research rare animal species.
dative.hint: Dative indirect object required by helfen (to help someone). Feminine dative article der; noun Universität is unchanged in the singular.

genitive.german: Die Ergebnisse des Projekts helfen uns, das Phänomen besser zu erforschen.
genitive.english: The results of the project help us to better explore the phenomenon.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ergebnisse. Neuter genitive article des with the noun ending -s on Projekts.

erforschen.proTip: The inseparable prefix er- never takes ge- in the past participle: erforschen – erforschte – hat erforscht. Compare erforschen (to research thoroughly, transitive with direct object) with forschen (to conduct research in general, intransitive, e.g. forschen nach + dative).

schützen.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to protect, guard'. Verbs do not decline for case. Schützen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (wen oder was schützt man?). Prepositions vor + dative or gegen + accusative indicate the hazard.

nominative.german: Der Zaun schützt den Garten vor wilden Tieren.
nominative.english: The fence protects the garden from wild animals.
nominative.hint: Subject of schützt, so nominative. Masculine nominative definite article der; noun Zaun takes no ending.

accusative.german: Diese Sonnencreme schützt die empfindliche Haut zuverlässig.
accusative.english: This sunscreen protects the sensitive skin reliably.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schützt, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; empfindliche takes the weak ending -e after the definite article.

dative.german: Die warme Mütze schützt vor dem eisigen Wind.
dative.english: The warm hat protects against the icy wind.
dative.hint: Dative required by the preposition vor, which with schützen governs the dative. Masculine dative article dem with weak adjective ending -en on eisigen.

genitive.german: Wir schützen die seltenen Tiere des Waldes vor Wilderern.
genitive.english: We protect the rare animals of the forest from poachers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession/origin after Tiere. Masculine genitive article des with the noun ending -es on Waldes.

schützen.proTip: Fixed prepositions: jemanden vor + dative schützen emphasizes protection from a present danger or harm (vor der Kälte, vor Gefahren); schützen gegen + accusative often indicates protection or resistance against illness or attack (gegen das Virus).

wachsen.note: Strong intransitive verb meaning 'to grow, increase'. Verbs do not decline. Wachsen takes a nominative subject and has no accusative direct object (it forms its perfect tense with sein: ist gewachsen).

nominative.german: Der Baum wächst jedes Jahr einen halben Meter.
nominative.english: The tree grows half a metre every year.
nominative.hint: Subject of wächst, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with noun Baum.

accusative.german: Die Pflanze wächst den ganzen Sommer über sehr schnell.
accusative.english: The plant grows very quickly throughout the entire summer.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long' (wachsen is intransitive and takes no direct object). Masculine den with weak adjective ending -en on ganzen.

dative.german: Mit jedem sonnigen Tag wächst meine Zuversicht.
dative.english: With every sunny day my confidence grows.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition mit. Masculine dative jedem with weak adjective ending -en on sonnigen.

genitive.german: Das Vertrauen der Bürger wächst von Tag zu Tag.
genitive.english: The trust of the citizens is growing from day to day.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural expressing possession after Vertrauen. Genitive plural article der; noun Bürger adds no ending in the plural.

wachsen.proTip: Wachsen is strong and changes its stem vowel with an umlaut in 2nd/3rd person singular present: ich wachse, du wächst, er wächst. Principal parts: wachsen – wuchs – ist gewachsen. Idiom: einer Aufgabe gewachsen sein (+ dative) means 'to be up to / capable of a task'.

interpretieren.note: Regular verb of foreign origin ending in -ieren meaning 'to interpret, explain'. Verbs do not decline. Interpretieren takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was interpretiert man?).

nominative.german: Der Professor interpretiert das alte Gedicht sehr modern.
nominative.english: The professor interprets the old poem in a very modern way.
nominative.hint: Subject of interpretiert, so nominative; masculine nominative article der.

accusative.german: Wir interpretieren seine plötzliche Stille als stille Zustimmung.
accusative.english: We interpret his sudden silence as silent consent.
accusative.hint: Direct object of interpretieren, so accusative. Feminine possessive seine; plötzliche takes mixed ending -e; noun Stille takes no ending.

dative.german: Aus diesen Zahlen interpretiert der Experte einen positiven Trend.
dative.english: From these figures the expert interprets a positive trend.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus, which always requires the dative. Dative plural diesen; plural noun Zahlen ends in -n.

genitive.german: Der Kritiker interpretiert die Absicht des Autors völlig falsch.
genitive.english: The critic interprets the author's intention completely incorrectly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Absicht. Masculine genitive article des with foreign noun ending -s on Autors.

interpretieren.proTip: Verbs ending in -ieren do not add ge- in the past participle: interpretieren – interpretierte – hat interpretiert (never geinterpretiert). Collocation: etwas interpretieren als + accusative/nominative (to interpret sth as).

verbessern.note: Regular transitive verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to improve, correct'. Verbs do not decline. It takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object. Reflexively (sich verbessern), it means 'to make progress' or 'to correct one's own mistake'.

nominative.german: Das neue Training verbessert die Kondition der Läufer.
nominative.english: The new training improves the runners' stamina.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbessert, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das with weak adjective ending -e on neue.

accusative.german: Ich möchte mein Deutsch in diesem Kurs gezielt verbessern.
accusative.english: I would like to improve my German in a targeted way in this course.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbessern, so accusative. Neuter possessive determiner mein with no ending; Deutsch has no case ending.

dative.german: Mit dieser Methode verbessert er seine Aussprache täglich.
dative.english: With this method he improves his pronunciation daily.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition mit. Feminine dative demonstrative dieser; noun Methode is unchanged in the singular.

genitive.german: Die Maßnahmen des Chefs verbessern das Betriebsklima deutlich.
genitive.english: The boss's measures significantly improve the working atmosphere.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Maßnahmen. Masculine genitive article des with the noun ending -s on Chefs.

verbessern.proTip: Inseparable prefix ver- never takes ge- in the past participle: verbessern – verbesserte – hat verbessert. Reflexive usage: 'Ich muss mich verbessern' can mean either 'I must improve my skills' or 'Let me correct what I just said'.

annehmen.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to accept' (an offer, parcel, phone call) or 'to assume / suppose'. Verbs do not decline. Annehmen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object.

nominative.german: Der Nachbar nimmt das Paket gerne für mich an.
nominative.english: The neighbour gladly accepts the parcel for me.
nominative.hint: Subject of nimmt ... an, so nominative. Masculine article der; Nachbar is a weak (n-) noun, but remains Nachbar in the nominative singular.

accusative.german: Ich nehme diesen wichtigen Anruf sofort an.
accusative.english: I am answering this important phone call immediately.
accusative.hint: Direct object of annehmen, so accusative. Masculine accusative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on wichtigen; noun Anruf has no ending.

dative.german: Sie hilft mir gerne dabei, die Einladung anzunehmen.
dative.english: She gladly helps me to accept the invitation.
dative.hint: Dative personal pronoun governed by helfen (to help someone); annehmen appears in the infinitive clause.

genitive.german: Aus Mangel an Beweisen müssen wir die Richtigkeit des Berichts annehmen.
genitive.english: For lack of evidence we must assume the correctness of the report.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Richtigkeit. Masculine genitive article des with noun ending -s on Berichts.

annehmen.proTip: Annehmen is separable and vowel-changing in the present tense: ich nehme an, du nimmst an, er nimmt an. Principal parts: annehmen – nahm an – hat angenommen. The elevated reflexive phrase sich einer Sache (genitive) annehmen means 'to take care of / attend to something': Er nahm sich des Problems an.

riesig.note: Adjective meaning 'huge, gigantic, immense'. As an attributive adjective before a noun, it takes standard adjective declension endings (strong, weak, or mixed). Predicatively or adverbially, it stays uninflected (Das Haus ist riesig).

nominative.german: Ein riesiger Hund bellte uns am Eingangstor an.
nominative.english: A huge dog barked at us at the entrance gate.
nominative.hint: Subject of bellte ... an, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending, so riesig takes the strong masculine nominative ending -er: riesiger.

accusative.german: Wir haben einen riesigen Bären im Wald gesehen.
accusative.english: We saw a huge bear in the forest.
accusative.hint: Direct object of gesehen, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; riesigen takes the weak ending -en; Bär is an n-noun and adds -en.

dative.german: Auf einem riesigen Feld wuchs goldener Weizen.
dative.english: Golden wheat grew on a huge field.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the two-way preposition auf (location). Neuter dative einem; riesigen takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Trotz der riesigen Entfernung besuchen wir uns regelmäßig.
genitive.english: Despite the huge distance we visit each other regularly.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Feminine genitive article der; riesigen takes the weak ending -en; feminine noun Entfernung has no genitive ending.

riesig.proTip: In casual German, riesig is often used adverbially as an intensifier meaning 'hugely / thrilled': Ich habe mich riesig gefreut (I was thrilled / immensely pleased). Comparative forms: riesiger, am riesigsten.

echt.note: Adjective meaning 'real, genuine, authentic'. When placed before a noun it takes standard adjective declension endings. Predicatively or adverbially, it stays uninflected and is frequently used to mean 'really / genuinely' (Das ist echt gut).

nominative.german: Das ist ein echter Diamant aus Südafrika.
nominative.english: That is a genuine diamond from South Africa.
nominative.hint: Predicate nominative after ist. Mixed declension: masculine ein takes no ending, so the adjective carries the strong ending -er: echter.

accusative.german: Er sucht eine echte Herausforderung im neuen Beruf.
accusative.english: He is looking for a real challenge in the new job.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sucht, so accusative. Feminine accusative eine; echte takes the mixed-declension ending -e; noun Herausforderung has no ending.

dative.german: Mit echtem Leder fühlt sich die neue Jacke viel besser an.
dative.english: With genuine leather the new jacket feels much better.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes the strong ending -em: echtem.

genitive.german: Der Wert eines echten Gemäldes steigt oft über die Jahre.
genitive.english: The value of a genuine painting often increases over the years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert. Neuter genitive eines; echten takes the weak ending -en; noun Gemälde adds genitive -s.

echt.proTip: In everyday spoken German, echt is the standard informal replacement for wirklich: Das ist echt schwer (That's really hard), Echt? (Really?). As an attributive adjective: echtes Gold (real gold), echte Perlen (real pearls).

mächtig.note: Adjective meaning 'powerful, mighty' (or colloquially 'massive / very'). Declines regularly before nouns according to the preceding determiner; stays uninflected when used predicatively or adverbially.

nominative.german: Ein mächtiger König regierte einst dieses weite Land.
nominative.english: A powerful king once ruled this vast land.
nominative.hint: Subject of regierte, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein takes no ending, so mächtiger carries the strong masculine nominative ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Konzern übt einen mächtigen Einfluss auf die Politik aus.
accusative.english: The corporation exerts a powerful influence on politics.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausüben, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; mächtigen takes the weak ending -en; Einfluss takes no ending.

dative.german: Die Bürger widersetzten sich dem mächtigen Herrscher.
dative.english: The citizens resisted the powerful ruler.
dative.hint: Dative required by sich widersetzen (+ dative). Masculine dative article dem; mächtigen takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Festung stand unter dem Schutz eines mächtigen Fürsten.
genitive.english: The fortress stood under the protection of a powerful prince.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Schutz. Masculine genitive eines; mächtigen takes weak ending -en; weak noun Fürst adds -en.

mächtig.proTip: Special grammatical idiom: einer Sprache / einer Sache mächtig sein (+ genitive) means 'to have command of a language / mastery of something': Er ist der deutschen Sprache mächtig. Colloquially, mächtig can mean 'very / enormously': Er hat sich mächtig geärgert.

bekannt.note: Adjective (originally the past participle of bekennen/bekannt machen) meaning 'known, well-known, familiar'. Declines regularly as an attributive adjective before a noun; uninflected as a predicate. When capitalized, ein Bekannter / eine Bekannte is an adjectival noun meaning 'an acquaintance'.

nominative.german: Ein bekannter Autor stellte gestern seinen neuen Roman vor.
nominative.english: A well-known author presented his new novel yesterday.
nominative.hint: Subject of stellte ... vor, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending, so bekannter takes the strong masculine nominative ending -er.

accusative.german: Ich habe einen bekannten Schauspieler auf der Straße getroffen.
accusative.english: I met a well-known actor on the street.
accusative.hint: Direct object of getroffen, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; bekannten takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Die Nachricht stammt von einem bekannten Wissenschaftler.
dative.english: The news comes from a well-known scientist.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Masculine dative einem; bekannten takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Melodie dieses bekannten Liedes kennt fast jedes Kind.
genitive.english: Almost every child knows the melody of this well-known song.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Melodie. Neuter genitive dieses; bekannten takes weak ending -en; noun Lied adds -es.

bekannt.proTip: Preposition patterns: bekannt für + accusative (famous for: Wien ist bekannt für seine Kaffeehauskultur); bekannt mit + dative (acquainted with someone). Note that the adjectival noun ein Bekannter (an acquaintance) keeps adjective endings: mit einem Bekannten.

gewaltig.note: Adjective meaning 'immense, tremendous, vast in scale or force'. Declines regularly before nouns; stays uninflected as an adverb or predicate.

nominative.german: Ein gewaltiger Sturm zerstörte mehrere Häuser im Dorf.
nominative.english: An immense storm destroyed several houses in the village.
nominative.hint: Subject of zerstörte, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein takes no ending, so gewaltiger takes the strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Explosion riss ein gewaltiges Loch in die dicke Mauer.
accusative.english: The explosion tore a huge hole into the thick wall.
accusative.hint: Direct object of riss, so accusative. Neuter accusative ein has no ending, so gewaltiges carries the strong neuter ending -es.

dative.german: Die Forscher standen vor einem gewaltigen Berg aus Eis.
dative.english: The researchers stood in front of an immense mountain of ice.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (location). Masculine dative einem; gewaltigen takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Ausmaße des gewaltigen Schadens sind noch immer unklar.
genitive.english: The extent of the immense damage is still unclear.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ausmaße. Masculine genitive des; gewaltigen takes weak ending -en; noun Schaden adds -s.

gewaltig.proTip: Although related to die Gewalt (force, power, violence), gewaltig usually refers to colossal size, scale, or degree without necessarily implying crime or harm: ein gewaltiger Unterschied (a huge difference), eine gewaltige Leistung (a tremendous achievement).

grundlegend.note: Adjective (present participle form) meaning 'fundamental, radical, foundational'. Declines regularly before nouns with standard endings; uninflected when used as an adverb or predicate.

nominative.german: Eine grundlegende Änderung ist in diesem Fall dringend nötig.
nominative.english: A fundamental change is urgently necessary in this case.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Mixed declension: feminine nominative eine; grundlegende takes the ending -e.

accusative.german: Wir brauchen ein grundlegendes Verständnis der Grammatikregeln.
accusative.english: We need a fundamental understanding of the grammar rules.
accusative.hint: Direct object of brauchen, so accusative. Neuter accusative ein has no ending; grundlegendes takes the strong neuter ending -es.

dative.german: Nach einer grundlegenden Renovierung erstrahlt das alte Haus neu.
dative.english: After a fundamental renovation the old house shines anew.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Feminine dative einer; grundlegenden takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Ursache des grundlegenden Problems liegt in der schlechten Planung.
genitive.english: The cause of the fundamental problem lies in the poor planning.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ursache. Neuter genitive des; grundlegenden takes weak ending -en; Problem adds genitive -s.

grundlegend.proTip: Frequently used as an adverb meaning 'fundamentally / from the ground up': Das hat meine Sichtweise grundlegend verändert (That changed my perspective fundamentally). Noun: die Grundlage (foundation / basis).

enorm.note: Adjective meaning 'enormous, tremendous'. Declines regularly when placed attributively before a noun; uninflected as an adverb (where it is very commonly used as an intensifier: enorm wichtig, enorm schnell).

nominative.german: Ein enormer Aufwand war für die Vorbereitung des Festes nötig.
nominative.english: An enormous effort was necessary for the preparation of the festival.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein takes no ending, so enormer takes the strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Das Unternehmen verzeichnete einen enormen Gewinn im letzten Quartal.
accusative.english: The company recorded an enormous profit in the last quarter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verzeichnete, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; enormen takes the weak ending -en.

dative.german: Mit enormem Fleiß schaffte sie die schwere Abschlussprüfung.
dative.english: With enormous diligence she passed the difficult final exam.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes the strong ending -em: enormem.

genitive.german: Wegen des enormen Drucks kündigte der leitende Angestellte.
genitive.english: Because of the enormous pressure the senior employee resigned.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive des; enormen takes weak ending -en; noun Druck adds -s.

enorm.proTip: In everyday modern German, enorm is predominantly heard as an intensifying adverb modifying adjectives: enorm wichtig (enormously important), enorm hilfreich (hugely helpful), enorm anstrengend (tremendously exhausting).

heutig.note: Temporal adjective meaning 'today's, present-day, current'. Derived from heute and almost exclusively used attributively before a noun, taking standard adjective declension endings.

nominative.german: Die heutige Jugend wächst ganz selbstverständlich mit Smartphones auf.
nominative.english: Today's youth naturally grows up with smartphones.
nominative.hint: Subject of wächst ... auf, so nominative. Weak declension: feminine definite article die; heutige takes the weak ending -e.

accusative.german: Hast du die heutige Ausgabe der Zeitung schon gelesen?
accusative.english: Have you already read today's edition of the newspaper?
accusative.hint: Direct object of gelesen, so accusative. Feminine accusative die; heutige takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In der heutigen Gesellschaft spielt digitale Vernetzung eine große Rolle.
dative.english: In today's society digital connectivity plays a major role.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location/state). Feminine dative article der; heutigen takes the weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Herausforderungen der heutigen Welt verlangen internationale Zusammenarbeit.
genitive.english: The challenges of today's world demand international cooperation.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Herausforderungen. Feminine genitive der; heutigen takes weak ending -en; noun Welt has no ending.

heutig.proTip: Distinguish the invariable adverb heute (today: Heute scheint die Sonne) from the attributive adjective heutig (der heutige Tag). Fixed phrase: bis zum heutigen Tag (to this day / right up to today).

einsam.note: Adjective meaning 'lonely' (experiencing isolation) or 'solitary, secluded' (of places). Declines regularly before nouns with standard endings; uninflected when used predicatively (Er ist einsam).

nominative.german: Ein einsamer Wolf durchstreifte den tief verschneiten Wald.
nominative.english: A solitary wolf roamed the deeply snow-covered forest.
nominative.hint: Subject of durchstreifte, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein takes no ending, so einsamer carries the strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Wir buchten eine einsame Hütte oben in den Schweizer Bergen.
accusative.english: We booked a secluded cabin up in the Swiss mountains.
accusative.hint: Direct object of buchten, so accusative. Feminine accusative eine; einsame takes the mixed-declension ending -e.

dative.german: Auf einer einsamen Insel verbrachte der Schriftsteller mehrere Monate.
dative.english: The writer spent several months on a deserted island.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the two-way preposition auf (location). Feminine dative einer; einsamen takes weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Stille des einsamen Tals half ihm beim konzentrierten Arbeiten.
genitive.english: The quiet of the solitary valley helped him during focused work.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Stille. Neuter genitive des; einsamen takes weak ending -en; noun Tal adds -s.

einsam.proTip: Distinguish einsam (emotionally lonely or secluded: Ich fühle mich einsam) from allein/alleine (simply physically on one's own without sadness: Ich bin allein zu Hause). Noun: die Einsamkeit (loneliness, solitude).

erstaunlich.note: Adjective meaning 'astonishing, remarkable, amazing'. Declines regularly as an attributive adjective before a noun; invariable as a predicate or modifying adverb (erstaunlich gut).

nominative.german: Ein erstaunlicher Fortschritt wurde in diesem Jahr erzielt.
nominative.english: An astonishing progress was achieved this year.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... erzielt, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending, so erstaunlicher takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Sie zeigte eine erstaunliche Geduld mit den lauten Schülern.
accusative.english: She showed an astonishing patience with the noisy students.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zeigte, so accusative. Feminine accusative eine; erstaunliche takes mixed ending -e.

dative.german: Mit erstaunlichem Mut rettete der Junge seinen Hund aus dem Fluss.
dative.english: With astonishing courage the boy saved his dog from the river.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em: erstaunlichem.

genitive.german: Trotz des erstaunlichen Erfolgs blieb die junge Künstlerin stets bescheiden.
genitive.english: Despite the astonishing success the young artist always remained modest.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive des; erstaunlichen takes weak ending -en; Erfolg adds genitive -s.

erstaunlich.proTip: Derived from the verb erstaunen (to amaze/astonish). Very frequently used adverbially: Das funktioniert erstaunlich gut (That works surprisingly/astonishingly well). Noun: das Erstaunen (astonishment).

eng.note: Adjective meaning 'narrow, tight' (spatial/physical) or 'close, intimate' (relationships, collaboration). Declines regularly before nouns with standard endings; uninflected as a predicate or adverb.

nominative.german: Der enge Durchgang führte direkt zum belebten Marktplatz.
nominative.english: The narrow passageway led directly to the busy marketplace.
nominative.hint: Subject of führte, so nominative. Weak declension: masculine article der; enge takes weak ending -e.

accusative.german: Wir pflegen einen engen Kontakt zu unseren internationalen Partnern.
accusative.english: We maintain close contact with our international partners.
accusative.hint: Direct object of pflegen, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; engen takes weak ending -en; Kontakt takes no ending.

dative.german: In einer engen Gasse parkte der kleine Lieferwagen.
dative.english: The small delivery van was parked in a narrow alley.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative einer; engen takes weak ending -en.

genitive.german: Aufgrund des engen Zeitplans mussten wir das Meeting leider verkürzen.
genitive.english: Due to the tight schedule we unfortunately had to shorten the meeting.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by aufgrund. Masculine genitive des; engen takes weak ending -en; Zeitplan adds genitive -s.

eng.proTip: Comparative forms take an umlaut: eng – enger – am engsten. Common collocations: im engsten Kreis (within the innermost circle / with closest friends), eng befreundet sein mit (to be close friends with).

entlegen.note: Adjective meaning 'remote, out-of-the-way, far-off'. Declines regularly as an attributive adjective before nouns; invariable when used as a predicate.

nominative.german: Ein entlegenes Dorf in den Alpen hat noch immer keine Mobilfunkabdeckung.
nominative.english: A remote village in the Alps still has no mobile phone coverage.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat, so nominative. Mixed declension: neuter ein takes no ending, so entlegenes takes the strong neuter ending -es.

accusative.german: Die Expedition erreichte einen entlegenen Winkel des Amazonasgebiets.
accusative.english: The expedition reached a remote corner of the Amazon region.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erreichte, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; entlegenen takes weak ending -en.

dative.german: In einem entlegenen Kloster fand der Philosoph seine innere Ruhe.
dative.english: In a remote monastery the philosopher found his inner peace.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative einem; entlegenen takes weak ending -en; Kloster takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Bewohner der entlegenen Region sind im Winter auf Hubschrauber angewiesen.
genitive.english: The inhabitants of the remote region rely on helicopters in winter.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bewohner. Feminine genitive der; entlegenen takes weak ending -en; Region takes no genitive -s.

entlegen.proTip: Etymologically related to ent- + liegen ('situated far away'). It carries a slightly formal or literary tone; everyday conversation often uses abgelegen or weit weg instead.

schlecht.note: Common adjective meaning 'bad, poor, defective'. Declines regularly with standard adjective endings before a noun (ein schlechter Tag, schlechtes Wetter). Used predicatively or adverbially, it stays uninflected (Das ist schlecht, Mir ist schlecht).

nominative.german: Ein schlechtes Gewissen plagte ihn die gesamte schlaflose Nacht.
nominative.english: A guilty conscience plagued him the entire sleepless night.
nominative.hint: Subject of plagte, so nominative. Mixed declension: neuter ein has no ending, so schlechtes takes the strong ending -es; Gewissen has no ending.

accusative.german: Ich habe gestern Nacht einen schlechten Traum gehabt.
accusative.english: I had a bad dream last night.
accusative.hint: Direct object of gehabt, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; schlechten takes the weak ending -en; noun Traum has no ending.

dative.german: Bei schlechtem Wetter fällt das geplante Sportfest leider aus.
dative.english: In bad weather the planned sports festival is unfortunately cancelled.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition bei. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes the strong ending -em: schlechtem.

genitive.german: Die gesundheitlichen Folgen schlechter Ernährung zeigen sich oft erst nach Jahren.
genitive.english: The health consequences of poor nutrition often only show after years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Strong declension without an article: feminine genitive takes the strong ending -er: schlechter; noun Ernährung adds no ending.

schlecht.proTip: Idioms: Mir ist schlecht (I feel sick/nauseous — notice dative experiencer mir!); schlechtes Gewissen (guilty conscience). Comparative forms are regular: schlecht – schlechter – am schlechtesten (unlike English bad – worse – worst).

dicht.note: Adjective meaning 'dense, thick, closely packed'. Used attributively before a noun it declines normally; used as an adverb it means 'closely, right up against' and takes no ending. It also has a second sense, 'sealed, watertight', which is normally predicative and therefore endingless.

nominative.german: Der dichte Nebel machte die Fahrt gefährlich.
nominative.english: The dense fog made the drive dangerous.
nominative.hint: Subject of machte, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e, since the definite article already marks the case.

accusative.german: Durch den dichten Flugverkehr ist die Belastung sehr hoch.
accusative.english: Because of the heavy air traffic the pollution is very high.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch, which always takes the accusative. Masculine den with the weak adjective ending -en on dichten.

dative.german: In dem dichten Wald verliert man schnell die Orientierung.
dative.english: In the dense forest you quickly lose your bearings.
dative.hint: Dative after the two-way preposition in, because the phrase states a location rather than a movement. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Wegen des dichten Verkehrs kamen wir viel zu spät.
genitive.english: Because of the heavy traffic we arrived far too late.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen, one of the everyday genitive prepositions. Masculine genitive des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's own genitive -s.

dicht.proTip: Attributive dicht declines (der dichte Wald); adverbial dicht does not and means 'right, closely': dicht neben mir, dicht hinter dem Haus. A separate sense is 'sealed' — Das Fenster ist dicht. Comparative dichter, superlative am dichtesten. Note that wegen takes the genitive in standard German, though you will hear wegen dem in speech.

chronisch.note: Adjective meaning 'chronic' — lasting a long time or recurring. Used attributively it declines like any adjective; used as an adverb it is invariable (chronisch krank). Watch the article-less plurals, which force the strong endings, since medical phrases often appear without an article.

nominative.german: Eine chronische Krankheit verändert das ganze Leben.
nominative.english: A chronic illness changes one's whole life.
nominative.hint: Subject of verändert, so nominative. Feminine eine is identical in nominative and accusative; the adjective takes the mixed-declension ending -e after an ein-word.

accusative.german: Der Arzt behandelt seit Monaten einen chronischen Husten.
accusative.english: The doctor has been treating a chronic cough for months.
accusative.hint: Direct object of behandeln, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

dative.german: Menschen mit chronischen Rückenschmerzen werden aktiv unterstützt.
dative.english: People with chronic back pain are actively supported.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by mit. There is no article, so the adjective must carry the case itself with the strong dative plural ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Behandlung einer chronischen Krankheit dauert oft Jahre.
genitive.english: The treatment of a chronic illness often takes years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Behandlung. Einer is the feminine genitive form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en; the noun adds no genitive -s.

chronisch.proTip: Attributive chronisch declines, adverbial chronisch does not: Er ist chronisch krank. Its medical opposite is akut. Colloquially it also works as a grumbling intensifier — chronisch pleite, chronisch unpünktlich. Stress falls on the second syllable: CHRO-nisch.

negativ.note: Adjective meaning 'negative' — expressing refusal, disapproval, or the absence of something. Attributively it declines like any adjective; predicatively and adverbially it takes no ending at all, which is the form you meet in test results: Der Test war negativ.

nominative.german: Das negative Ergebnis überraschte wirklich alle.
nominative.english: The negative result surprised absolutely everyone.
nominative.hint: Subject of überraschte, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Sie hat einen sehr negativen Eindruck bekommen.
accusative.english: She got a very negative impression.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bekommen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. The adverb sehr modifies the adjective and takes no ending.

dative.german: Mit negativer Kritik kann er nur schlecht umgehen.
dative.english: He copes only poorly with negative criticism.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine dative ending -er.

genitive.german: Die Folgen einer negativen Entwicklung sind deutlich spürbar.
genitive.english: The consequences of a negative development are clearly noticeable.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Einer is the feminine genitive form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en.

negativ.proTip: Stress the second-to-last syllable: neGAtiv. Attributive forms decline, predicative ones do not (Die Antwort war negativ). Its opposite is positiv, which behaves identically. Note the everyday medical use, where it is always endingless: Der Test ist negativ ausgefallen.

durchschnittlich.note: Two uses. As an attributive adjective it means 'average' and declines normally. As a sentence adverb it means 'on average' and is invariable, usually standing at the front of the clause. Both uses appear below; the adverb carries no ending in any position.

nominative.german: Der durchschnittliche Preis ist im letzten Jahr stark gestiegen.
nominative.english: The average price rose sharply last year.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist ... gestiegen, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Durchschnittlich geben Deutsche pro Monat etwa 2500 Euro aus.
accusative.english: On average Germans spend about 2,500 euros a month.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausgeben, so accusative. Euro stays uninflected after a number, so nothing visibly changes — the verb is what identifies the case. Here durchschnittlich is the invariable sentence adverb.

dative.german: Mit einem durchschnittlichen Einkommen ist das kaum zu bezahlen.
dative.english: On an average income that is hardly affordable.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Die Höhe des durchschnittlichen Gehalts ist längst bekannt.
genitive.english: The level of the average salary has long been known.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Höhe: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s.

durchschnittlich.proTip: Adjective declines, sentence adverb does not — compare der durchschnittliche Verbrauch with Durchschnittlich verbraucht das Auto sechs Liter. Related: der Durchschnitt and the equivalent phrase im Durchschnitt, which is often more natural than the adverb.

braun.note: Colour adjective meaning 'brown'. Like all colour adjectives in German it declines when it stands before a noun, but takes no ending at all when used predicatively after sein or werden: Der Mantel ist braun. That contrast is the main thing to master here.

nominative.german: Der braune Mantel hängt noch im Flur.
nominative.english: The brown coat is still hanging in the hall.
nominative.hint: Subject of hängt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e, since the definite article already shows the case.

accusative.german: Ich habe gestern einen braunen Tisch gekauft.
accusative.english: Yesterday I bought a brown table.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kaufen, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

dative.german: Sie kam mit einer großen braunen Tasche.
dative.english: She came with a large brown bag.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einer is the feminine dative form and both adjectives take the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Die Farbe des braunen Leders gefällt mir sehr.
genitive.english: I like the colour of the brown leather very much.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Farbe: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Mir is dative, required by gefallen.

braun.proTip: Attributive forms decline (ein brauner Schuh), predicative ones never do (Der Schuh ist braun). Capitalised, das Braun is the colour itself. Useful: braun werden (to tan), braune Augen. Be aware that in a political context braun refers to Nazism, so the word can carry that connotation.

sicher.note: Adjective meaning 'safe' and 'certain', and also a very common particle meaning 'certainly'. Attributively it declines — note that the -e- of the stem drops out: sicher becomes sichere, sicheren. Predicatively and as a particle it takes no ending. It also heads a genitive construction: sich einer Sache sicher sein.

nominative.german: Der sichere Weg dauert leider etwas länger.
nominative.english: The safe route unfortunately takes a little longer.
nominative.hint: Subject of dauert, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e; note that the stem loses its -e-, giving sichere rather than 'sichere­re'.

accusative.german: Wir suchen noch einen sicheren Platz für die Nacht.
accusative.english: We're still looking for a safe place for the night.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Für die Nacht is accusative too, governed by für.

dative.german: Mit einem sicheren Gefühl ging sie endlich nach Hause.
dative.english: With a feeling of safety she finally went home.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Einem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Ich bin mir meiner Sache ganz sicher.
genitive.english: I am quite certain of my case.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by the construction sich einer Sache sicher sein, which takes a genitive complement. Meiner is the feminine genitive form. Mir is a separate dative reflexive, and sicher is predicative here, so it has no ending.

sicher.proTip: Watch the dropped -e- in the declined forms: sicher → ein sicherer Ort, an einem sicheren Ort. The genitive frame sich einer Sache sicher sein is worth recognising, though modern German usually prefers sicher sein, dass ... As a particle sicher means 'certainly': Das schaffst du sicher.

theoretisch.note: Adjective meaning 'theoretical' — based on ideas rather than practice. Attributively it declines like any adjective. As an adverb it is invariable and very often carries an unspoken 'but in practice not', which is worth knowing: Theoretisch ist das möglich.

nominative.german: Die theoretische Prüfung findet schon nächste Woche statt.
nominative.english: The theory exam takes place as early as next week.
nominative.hint: Subject of findet ... statt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Nächste Woche is an accusative time expression.

accusative.german: Er hat den theoretischen Teil bereits bestanden.
accusative.english: He has already passed the theoretical part.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bestehen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: In einem theoretischen Modell funktioniert das ganz gut.
dative.english: In a theoretical model that works quite well.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location in an abstract sense rather than a movement. Einem shows the neuter dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en.

genitive.german: Die Grundlagen der theoretischen Physik sind ziemlich schwer.
genitive.english: The foundations of theoretical physics are quite difficult.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Grundlagen. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive -s.

theoretisch.proTip: Attributive theoretisch declines; as an adverb it is invariable and usually implies a contrast with reality — Theoretisch könnte das klappen. Its opposite praktisch works exactly the same way. Related: die Theorie, der Theoretiker.

bereit.note: Adjective meaning 'ready, prepared, willing'. It is used almost exclusively predicatively, after sein or werden, and predicative adjectives in German take no endings — so bereit is invariable in normal use. Its complement patterns are bereit zu + dative and bereit sein plus zu + infinitive.

nominative.german: Der neue Mitarbeiter ist sofort bereit.
nominative.english: The new employee is ready straight away.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative; masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Bereit stands after the verb as a predicate and takes no ending at all.

accusative.german: Sie ist bereit, für diese Stelle einen langen Weg zu fahren.
accusative.english: She is willing to travel a long way for this job.
accusative.hint: Accusative object of fahren in the infinitive clause: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Für diese Stelle is accusative too, governed by für.

dative.german: Er ist zu einem echten Kompromiss bereit.
dative.english: He is ready for a genuine compromise.
dative.hint: Dative required by zu, which always governs the dative — this is the standard complement of bereit. Einem shows the masculine dative -em and the adjective takes the weak -en.

genitive.german: Sie war bereit, die Folgen ihrer Entscheidung zu tragen.
genitive.english: She was ready to bear the consequences of her decision.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Ihrer is the feminine genitive form and the noun adds no genitive -s. Die Folgen is the accusative object of tragen.

bereit.proTip: Normally predicative, so no ending: Ich bin bereit. The patterns to learn are bereit zu + dative (zu allem bereit) and bereit sein zu + infinitive. Related words do decline or separate: bereitwillig, die Bereitschaft, and the separable verbs bereitstellen and bereithalten.

vermutlich.note: Most often a sentence adverb meaning 'presumably, probably', and in that use it is invariable. The same word also works as an attributive adjective meaning 'presumed, likely' (die vermutliche Ursache), where it declines normally. The genitive example below shows the adjective; the others show the adverb.

nominative.german: Vermutlich kommt der letzte Zug heute später.
nominative.english: The last train will presumably come later today.
nominative.hint: Subject of kommt, so nominative — it follows the verb because vermutlich fills first position. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Vermutlich hat er gestern einen anderen Weg genommen.
accusative.english: He presumably took a different route yesterday.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nehmen, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

dative.german: Vermutlich hat sie ihrem Chef davon nichts gesagt.
dative.english: She presumably said nothing about it to her boss.
dative.hint: Dative indirect object of sagen; ihrem shows the masculine dative -em. Nichts is the accusative object, and davon replaces a von-phrase.

genitive.german: Die vermutliche Ursache des Brandes ist inzwischen bekannt.
genitive.english: The presumed cause of the fire is now known.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ursache: masculine genitive des with the noun ending -es. In this sentence vermutliche is the attributive adjective, taking the weak ending -e.

vermutlich.proTip: Adverb invariable, attributive adjective declining — that is the whole story. Related: vermuten (to suspect, with an accusative object) and die Vermutung. Strength ranking among the neighbours: bestimmt and sicher are strongest, then wahrscheinlich and vermutlich, then wohl, then vielleicht.

fähig.note: Adjective meaning 'capable, able'. Attributively it declines like any adjective. What makes it worth studying is that it takes two different complements: the everyday zu + dative, and a more formal bare genitive — einer solchen Tat fähig. Both are shown below.

nominative.german: Der fähige Mitarbeiter löst wirklich jedes Problem.
nominative.english: The capable employee solves absolutely every problem.
nominative.hint: Subject of löst, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Jedes Problem is the accusative object.

accusative.german: Wir suchen für diese Stelle einen fähigen Nachfolger.
accusative.english: For this position we're looking for a capable successor.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en on fähigen.

dative.german: Er ist zu großen Leistungen durchaus fähig.
dative.english: He is thoroughly capable of great achievements.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by zu, which always governs the dative. With no article the adjective takes the strong dative plural ending -en, and the noun adds the dative plural -n.

genitive.german: Sie war einer solchen Tat einfach nicht fähig.
genitive.english: She was simply not capable of such a deed.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by fähig in its formal construction, which takes a bare genitive complement. Einer is the feminine genitive form and solchen takes the weak ending -en after it.

fähig.proTip: Two complements: everyday zu + dative (zu allem fähig) and formal genitive (keiner Lüge fähig). The suffix -fähig is enormously productive and always declines normally: arbeitsfähig, lernfähig, zahlungsfähig, kritikfähig. Related: die Fähigkeit, and the opposite unfähig.

unterschiedlich.note: Adjective meaning 'differing, varying' — not the same from one case to another. Attributively it declines like any adjective and is most often used in the plural, which means the article-less strong endings come up constantly. As an adverb it is invariable: Die Preise sind unterschiedlich hoch.

nominative.german: Die unterschiedlichen Meinungen führten schnell zum Streit.
nominative.english: The differing opinions quickly led to an argument.
nominative.hint: Subject of führten, so nominative plural. The plural article die is followed by the weak adjective ending -en, since the article already marks the case.

accusative.german: Wir haben damals ganz unterschiedliche Erfahrungen gemacht.
accusative.english: We had quite different experiences back then.
accusative.hint: Direct object of machen, so accusative plural. There is no article, so the adjective takes the strong plural ending -e; the adverb ganz modifies it and takes no ending.

dative.german: Mit unterschiedlichen Methoden kommt man trotzdem zum Ziel.
dative.english: With different methods you still reach the goal.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by mit. With no article the adjective carries the case itself with the strong dative plural ending -en, and the noun is already the plural Methoden.

genitive.german: Die Folgen unterschiedlicher Entscheidungen sind oft enorm.
genitive.english: The consequences of differing decisions are often enormous.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural expressing 'of' after Folgen. With no article the adjective takes the strong genitive plural ending -er.

unterschiedlich.proTip: Because it lives mostly in the plural, the strong endings matter here: unterschiedliche, unterschiedlichen, unterschiedlicher. Adverbially it is invariable. Related: der Unterschied, sich unterscheiden von + dative. Verschieden is a close synonym with the same behaviour.

unglaublich.note: Adjective meaning 'incredible, unbelievable'. Attributively it declines like any adjective. As an adverb it is invariable and works purely as an intensifier — unglaublich schnell — which is by far its most common use in speech.

nominative.german: Eine ziemlich unglaubliche Geschichte machte die Runde.
nominative.english: A rather incredible story went around.
nominative.hint: Subject of machte, so nominative. Feminine eine is identical in nominative and accusative; the adjective takes the mixed-declension ending -e, and the adverb ziemlich has no ending.

accusative.german: Er hat dabei einen wirklich unglaublichen Fehler gemacht.
accusative.english: In doing so he made a truly incredible mistake.
accusative.hint: Direct object of machen, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en. Wirklich is an adverb here and takes no ending.

dative.german: Mit unglaublicher Geduld erklärte sie alles noch einmal.
dative.english: With incredible patience she explained everything once more.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine dative ending -er.

genitive.german: Das war das Ergebnis einer wirklich unglaublichen Leistung.
genitive.english: That was the result of a truly incredible achievement.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ergebnis. Einer is the feminine genitive form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.
