unglaublich.proTip: Built from un- + glaublich, from glauben. Attributive forms decline; the intensifying adverb never does: unglaublich teuer, unglaublich gut. It belongs with a family of invariable intensifiers — unheimlich, wahnsinnig, irre — all of which are informal. On its own, Unglaublich! is a complete exclamation.

sogenannt.note: Adjective meaning 'so-called'. It is used only attributively, before a noun, which means it always carries an adjective ending — you will never meet it in its bare dictionary form. It comes from so + genannt, the past participle of nennen, and it declines exactly like any other adjective.

nominative.german: Der sogenannte Experte wusste erstaunlich wenig.
nominative.english: The so-called expert knew surprisingly little.
nominative.hint: Subject of wusste, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e. Experte is a weak (n-) noun, and the nominative singular is its one form without -n.

accusative.german: Wir benutzen im Labor das sogenannte neue Verfahren.
accusative.english: In the lab we use the so-called new procedure.
accusative.hint: Direct object of benutzen, so accusative. Neuter das is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; both adjectives take the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In dem sogenannten Ruhebereich war es erstaunlich laut.
dative.english: In the so-called quiet zone it was surprisingly noisy.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Masculine dative dem with the weak adjective ending -en on sogenannten.

genitive.german: Die Regeln des sogenannten freien Marktes sind sehr komplex.
genitive.english: The rules of the so-called free market are very complex.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Regeln: des, the weak ending -en on both adjectives, and the noun's own genitive -es.

sogenannt.proTip: Always attributive and always inflected: der sogenannte, ein sogenannter, dem sogenannten. In writing it is abbreviated sog. The tone can be neutral ('known as') or sceptical ('supposedly'), and only context tells you which — in speech the scepticism usually shows in the intonation.

endlos.note: Adjective meaning 'endless' — having no end or seeming to go on forever. Attributively it declines like any adjective; adverbially it is invariable (Es dauerte endlos). It is built with the very productive suffix -los, which corresponds to English '-less'.

nominative.german: Diese endlosen Diskussionen über Handys nerven mich wirklich.
nominative.english: These endless discussions about mobile phones really annoy me.
nominative.hint: Subject of nerven, so nominative plural — mich is the accusative object. Diese is a der-word carrying the plural ending -e, so the adjective drops to the weak ending -en.

accusative.german: Wir haben einen endlosen Nachmittag im Wartezimmer verbracht.
accusative.english: We spent an endless afternoon in the waiting room.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbringen, so accusative: einen shows the masculine accusative -en and the adjective takes the weak -en after it.

dative.german: Nach endlosem Warten kam endlich der richtige Bus.
dative.english: After endless waiting the right bus finally came.
dative.hint: Dative required by nach. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong neuter dative ending -em. Warten is a capitalised infinitive used as a neuter noun.

genitive.german: Am Ende der endlosen Straße stand ein kleines Haus.
genitive.english: At the end of the endless road stood a small house.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ende. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive -s.

endlos.proTip: The -los suffix is worth collecting, since all of these decline the same way: arbeitslos, hoffnungslos, kostenlos, sinnlos, erfolglos. Attributive endlos declines, adverbial endlos does not. For the mathematical sense 'infinite' German uses unendlich instead.

allgemein.note: Adjective meaning 'general' — true for most cases rather than specific. Attributively it declines like any adjective; adverbially it is invariable (allgemein bekannt). Note the fixed phrase im Allgemeinen, where the adjective is capitalised because it is being used as a noun.

nominative.german: Die allgemeine Meinung ist hier ganz anders.
nominative.english: The general opinion here is quite different.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e, since the article already marks the case.

accusative.german: Er hat zuerst einen allgemeinen Überblick gegeben.
accusative.english: He first gave a general overview.
accusative.hint: Direct object of geben, so accusative: einen with the masculine accusative -en and the weak adjective ending -en on allgemeinen.

dative.german: Mit allgemeinen Regeln kommt man hier nicht weiter.
dative.english: General rules won't get you any further here.
dative.hint: Dative plural required by mit. With no article the adjective takes the strong dative plural ending -en, and Regeln is already the plural form.

genitive.german: Das ist ein deutliches Zeichen allgemeiner Unsicherheit.
genitive.english: That is a clear sign of general uncertainty.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zeichen. With no article the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine genitive ending -er.

allgemein.proTip: Attributive forms decline, adverbial ones do not: allgemein bekannt, allgemein üblich. The fixed phrase im Allgemeinen capitalises the adjective because it functions as a noun there. Related: die Allgemeinheit, allgemeingültig, and the close synonym generell.

wahr.note: Adjective meaning 'true' — in accordance with the facts. Attributively it declines like any adjective; predicatively it takes no ending, and that is where you meet it most often: Das ist wahr. It also anchors several very common fixed expressions.

nominative.german: Die wahre Geschichte ist noch viel seltsamer.
nominative.english: The true story is even much stranger.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e. Seltsamer is a predicative comparative and takes no ending.

accusative.german: Endlich hat er uns den wahren Grund genannt.
accusative.english: At last he told us the real reason.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nennen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the adjective takes the weak ending -en. Uns is the dative indirect object.

dative.german: Von einer wahren Freundschaft erwartet man deutlich mehr.
dative.english: From a true friendship one expects considerably more.
dative.hint: Dative required by von, which always governs the dative. Einer is the feminine dative form and the adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

genitive.german: Der Kern der wahren Geschichte blieb lange unklar.
genitive.english: The core of the true story remained unclear for a long time.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kern. Feminine genitive article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun adds no genitive -s.

wahr.proTip: Attributive declines, predicative does not. Collect the fixed phrases, which are everywhere: nicht wahr? (isn't it?), wahr werden (to come true), es ist wahr, and das ist nicht wahr. Related: die Wahrheit and wahrscheinlich. Wahrnehmen (to perceive) shares the root but not the meaning.

-fach.note: This is a suffix, not an independent word — it never stands alone, so there is no case form of -fach itself. Attached to a number it builds a multiplicative: dreifach, zehnfach, mehrfach. The resulting word behaves like an ordinary adjective: invariable as an adverb, fully declining when attributive.

nominative.german: Der dreifache Preis ist für uns einfach zu hoch.
nominative.english: Triple the price is simply too high for us.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der with the weak adjective ending -e on dreifache — the whole formed word declines, not the suffix on its own.

accusative.german: Der Händler verlangt inzwischen den dreifachen Betrag.
accusative.english: The dealer is now demanding three times the amount.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verlangen, so accusative. Masculine der becomes den and the formed adjective takes the weak ending -en after it.

dative.german: Mit der zehnfachen Menge funktioniert das Rezept nicht mehr.
dative.english: With ten times the quantity the recipe no longer works.
dative.hint: Dative required by mit. Feminine dative article der with the weak adjective ending -en on zehnfachen.

genitive.german: Die Kosten des mehrfachen Versuchs waren am Ende hoch.
genitive.english: The costs of the repeated attempt were high in the end.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's own genitive -s.

-fach.proTip: Always written as one word with its number — dreifach, not 'drei fach'. As an adverb it is invariable (Der Umsatz ist dreifach gestiegen); attributively it declines fully. Useful members: mehrfach (repeated), vielfach (manifold), and einfach, which has drifted away to mean 'simple, easy'.

die Welt.note: Feminine noun meaning 'world'. Nouns decline for case, but a feminine noun never changes its own form in the singular — all four singular cases are Welt, and only the article or determiner shows the case. The plural die Welten exists but is rare outside science fiction and philosophy.

nominative.german: Die ganze Welt schaut gerade auf dieses kleine Land.
nominative.english: The whole world is currently watching this small country.
nominative.hint: Subject of schaut, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e; Welt itself takes no ending. Auf dieses kleine Land is accusative, as schauen auf requires.

accusative.german: Er will vor seinem dreißigsten Geburtstag die ganze Welt bereisen.
accusative.english: He wants to travel the whole world before his thirtieth birthday.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bereisen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; ganze takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In der modernen Welt geht einfach alles schneller.
dative.english: In the modern world everything simply moves faster.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Feminine dative article der with the weak adjective ending -en; the noun is still Welt.

genitive.german: Die Probleme der heutigen Welt sind wirklich komplex.
genitive.english: The problems of today's world are really complex.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Probleme. The feminine genitive article der is identical in form to the dative, so its position after the noun Probleme is what marks it as genitive.

die Welt.proTip: Feminine and unchanged through the whole singular. Collect the fixed phrases: auf der ganzen Welt (all over the world), zur Welt kommen (to be born), alle Welt (everybody). Compounds with Welt- are everywhere and stay feminine when Welt is the head: die Weltkarte, die Weltsprache.

das Gebiet.note: Neuter noun meaning 'area, region' and also 'field' in the sense of a subject or discipline. It adds -s or -es in the genitive singular (des Gebiets / des Gebietes) and -en in the dative plural; otherwise only the article changes. Plural: die Gebiete.

nominative.german: Das ganze Gebiet steht seit Jahren unter Naturschutz.
nominative.english: The whole area has been under nature protection for years.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das with the weak adjective ending -e; the noun takes no ending here.

accusative.german: Die Forscher haben ein sehr großes Gebiet untersucht.
accusative.english: The researchers investigated a very large area.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchen, so accusative. Neuter ein has no ending, so the adjective must carry the case with the strong ending -es. Neuter nominative and accusative look alike, so the verb identifies the case.

dative.german: Auf diesem Gebiet ist sie eine anerkannte Expertin.
dative.english: In this field she is a recognised expert.
dative.hint: Dative after auf — the 'field of knowledge' sense always uses auf + dative. Diesem shows the neuter dative -em. Eine anerkannte Expertin is a predicate nominative after sein.

genitive.german: Die Grenzen des besetzten Gebiets sind bis heute umstritten.
genitive.english: The borders of the occupied area are disputed to this day.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Grenzen: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Gebietes is the equally correct longer form.

das Gebiet.proTip: Two senses, one of which has a fixed preposition: a region of land, and a field of study, where German says auf dem Gebiet der Medizin. Compare der Bereich, which is very close, and die Gegend, which is a looser, more everyday 'area around here'.

die Masse.note: Feminine noun with two senses: physical 'mass' as in physics, and a 'crowd' or 'the masses' of people. Like all feminine nouns it never changes form in the singular — only the article shows the case. Plural: die Massen, with the usual dative plural -n already present.

nominative.german: Die große Masse wartete geduldig vor dem Stadion.
nominative.english: The large crowd waited patiently in front of the stadium.
nominative.hint: Subject of wartete, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die with the weak adjective ending -e; Masse itself takes no ending.

accusative.german: Der Redner erreichte die breite Masse an diesem Abend nicht.
accusative.english: The speaker did not reach the broad masses that evening.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erreichen, so accusative. Feminine die is identical in nominative and accusative, so the verb identifies the case; breite takes the weak ending -e.

dative.german: In der dichten Masse verlor ich sofort meine Freunde.
dative.english: In the dense crowd I immediately lost my friends.
dative.hint: Dative after in, because the phrase states a location. Feminine dative article der with the weak adjective ending -en. Meine Freunde is the accusative object.

genitive.german: Die Masse des kleinen Körpers ist inzwischen genau bekannt.
genitive.english: The mass of the small body is now precisely known.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Masse: des, the weak adjective ending -en, and the noun's genitive -s. Die Masse is the nominative subject here, in its physics sense.

die Masse.proTip: Feminine and unchanged in the singular. The fixed phrase die breite Masse means the general public. Keep three similar words apart: die Masse (mass, crowd), das Maß (measure, and in Bavaria a litre of beer), and die Menge, which is the usual word for 'a lot' or 'quantity'.

der Krebs.note: Masculine noun meaning 'cancer' (illness) or 'crab / crayfish' (crustacean). Nouns decline for case: in the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Krebses). Nominative, accusative, and dative rely on the article (der / den / dem Krebs). Plural: die Krebse.

nominative.german: Der Krebs wurde glücklicherweise frühzeitig entdeckt.
nominative.english: Fortunately the cancer was discovered early.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... entdeckt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; noun Krebs takes no ending.

accusative.german: Forscher bekämpfen den Krebs mit neuen Antikörpern.
accusative.english: Researchers are fighting cancer with new antibodies.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bekämpfen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; noun Krebs takes no accusative ending.

dative.german: Bei diesem Krebs schlagen herkömmliche Therapien oft nicht an.
dative.english: With this cancer conventional therapies often do not work.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition bei. Masculine dative determiner diesem; noun Krebs takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Früherkennung des Krebses rettet jedes Jahr viele Leben.
genitive.english: Early detection of cancer saves many lives every year.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Früherkennung. Masculine genitive article des; noun Krebs adds the genitive ending -es.

der Krebs.proTip: Krebs has two major meanings: the illness (cancer) and the animal (crab/crayfish), plus the astrological sign (Cancer). Notice the genitive des Krebses (with -es because Krebs ends in -s). Fixed phrase: an Krebs erkranken (to fall ill with cancer).

das Tier.note: Neuter noun meaning 'animal, creature'. Neuter nouns decline for case: in the singular, nominative and accusative are identical (das Tier), dative is dem Tier, and genitive adds -es (des Tieres) or -s (des Tiers). Plural: die Tiere.

nominative.german: Das Tier versteckte sich ängstlich im dichten Gebüsch.
nominative.english: The animal hid anxiously in the dense bushes.
nominative.hint: Subject of versteckte sich, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; noun Tier has no ending.

accusative.german: Der Tierarzt untersucht das verletzte Tier sehr vorsichtig.
accusative.english: The vet examines the injured animal very carefully.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersucht, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on verletzte.

dative.german: Wir gaben dem hungrigen Tier etwas frisches Wasser.
dative.english: We gave the hungry animal some fresh water.
dative.hint: Dative indirect object of gaben (to whom). Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on hungrigen.

genitive.german: Die Instinkte des Tieres sind erstaunlich gut ausgeprägt.
genitive.english: The instincts of the animal are astonishingly well developed.
genitive.hint: Genitive showing possession after Instinkte. Neuter genitive article des; noun Tier adds the genitive ending -es.

das Tier.proTip: Compound nouns ending in -tier are always neuter: das Haustier (pet), das Säugetier (mammal), das Raubtier (predator). Plural: die Tiere, dative plural: den Tieren.

das Alter.note: Neuter noun meaning 'age' (length of existence, or elderliness). In the singular, nominative and accusative are das Alter, dative is dem Alter, and genitive adds -s (des Alters). Plural is rare.

nominative.german: Das Alter spielt bei dieser Sportart überhaupt keine Rolle.
nominative.english: Age plays no role at all in this sport.
nominative.hint: Subject of spielt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; noun Alter takes no ending.

accusative.german: Man sieht ihm das hohe Alter kaum an.
accusative.english: You can hardly see the advanced age on him.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sieht ... an, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on hohe.

dative.german: In diesem Alter lernen Kinder eine neue Sprache spielerisch.
dative.english: At this age children learn a new language playfully.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition in (time/state). Neuter dative determiner diesem; noun Alter is unchanged.

genitive.german: Trotz des hohen Alters ist meine Großmutter geistig sehr fit.
genitive.english: Despite her advanced age my grandmother is very sharp mentally.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hohen; noun Alter adds genitive -s.

das Alter.proTip: Key prepositional idioms: im Alter von ... Jahren (at the age of ... years); bis ins hohe Alter (into old age). Colloquially, 'das Alter' is also used as a slang term of address ('Alter!' = 'Dude!').

die Energie.note: Feminine noun meaning 'energy' (physical force, power, stamina). Feminine nouns never add case endings in the singular — only the preceding article changes: die Energie (nom/acc), der Energie (dat/gen). Plural: die Energien.

nominative.german: Die erneuerbare Energie wird in Zukunft immer wichtiger.
nominative.english: Renewable energy will become increasingly important in the future.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on erneuerbare.

accusative.german: Wir müssen die verbrauchte Energie effizienter nutzen.
accusative.english: We need to use consumed energy more efficiently.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nutzen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on verbrauchte.

dative.german: Mit voller Energie begann sie ihr neues Studium.
dative.english: With full energy she began her new university degree.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes the strong ending -er on voller; noun Energie takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Kosten der Energie belasten viele Haushalte stark.
genitive.english: The cost of energy burdens many households heavily.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Feminine genitive article der; feminine noun Energie takes no ending.

die Energie.proTip: All nouns ending in -ie with stress on the last syllable are feminine: die Energie, die Philosophie, die Therapie. Common compounds: die Sonnenenergie (solar energy), die Windenergie (wind energy).

der Teenager.note: Masculine loanword from English meaning 'teenager'. It declines like native German masculine nouns in -er: only the genitive singular adds -s (des Teenagers). Plural remains die Teenager (dative plural: den Teenagern).

nominative.german: Der Teenager verbrachte viele Stunden vor seinem Computer.
nominative.english: The teenager spent many hours in front of his computer.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbrachte, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; noun Teenager takes no ending.

accusative.german: Die Eltern verstehen den rebellischen Teenager oft nicht.
accusative.english: The parents often don't understand the rebellious teenager.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verstehen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on rebellischen.

dative.german: Die Sozialarbeiterin half dem verzweifelten Teenager sofort.
dative.english: The social worker helped the desperate teenager immediately.
dative.hint: Dative required by the verb helfen. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on verzweifelten.

genitive.german: Das Zimmer des Teenagers war wie immer völlig unordentlich.
genitive.english: The teenager's room was completely messy as always.
genitive.hint: Genitive showing possession after Zimmer. Masculine genitive article des; noun Teenager adds genitive -s.

der Teenager.proTip: German native synonyms include der/die Jugendliche (declined as an adjectival noun) and der Heranwachsende. Plural form: die Teenager (no -s plural, unlike English!).

die Million.note: Feminine numeral noun meaning 'million'. Unlike plain numbers (eins, zwei), Million is a full feminine noun that takes plural -en (die Millionen). In the singular, it has no case ending on the noun itself.

nominative.german: Eine Million Euro wurde für das Projekt bewilligt.
nominative.english: One million euros was approved for the project.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... bewilligt, so nominative. Feminine nominative form of ein is eine; noun Million takes no singular ending.

accusative.german: Der glückliche Gewinner hat eine Million im Lotto gewonnen.
accusative.english: The lucky winner won a million in the lottery.
accusative.hint: Direct object of gewonnen, so accusative. Feminine accusative form eine; noun Million takes no ending.

dative.german: Mit einer Million Zuschauern war das Finale ein voller Erfolg.
dative.english: With one million viewers the final was a complete success.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article/numeral einer; Million takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Zinsen einer Million sind heute nicht mehr so hoch.
genitive.english: The interest on a million is no longer that high today.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zinsen. Feminine genitive article einer; Million adds no -s.

die Million.proTip: Million is always capitalized in German because it is a noun: drei Millionen (three million). Compare with small numbers, which are lowercase: drei, tausend.

der Ruhestand.note: Masculine compound noun (Ruhe + Stand) meaning 'retirement'. In the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Ruhestands / Ruhestandes); nominative, accusative, and dative use der, den, dem Ruhestand.

nominative.german: Der wohlverdiente Ruhestand beginnt für ihn nächsten Monat.
nominative.english: The well-deserved retirement begins for him next month.
nominative.hint: Subject of beginnt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on wohlverdiente.

accusative.german: Viele ältere Kollegen genießen den Ruhestand in vollen Zügen.
accusative.english: Many older colleagues enjoy retirement to the fullest.
accusative.hint: Direct object of genießen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; noun Ruhestand takes no ending.

dative.german: Seit seinem Ruhestand widmet er sich ganz der Gartenarbeit.
dative.english: Since his retirement he devotes himself entirely to gardening.
dative.hint: Dative governed by seit. Masculine dative possessive seinem; noun Ruhestand takes no ending.

genitive.german: Während des Ruhestands reisten die beiden um die ganze Welt.
genitive.english: During retirement the two traveled all around the world.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by während. Masculine genitive article des; noun Ruhestand adds genitive -s.

der Ruhestand.proTip: Common collocations: in den Ruhestand gehen / treten (to retire / enter retirement — accusative of direction); im Ruhestand sein (to be retired — dative of location). Synonym: die Rente / in Rente gehen.

die Milliarde.note: Feminine numeral noun meaning 'billion' (1,000,000,000). Declines like a regular feminine noun in the singular (die, die, der, der Milliarde); plural is die Milliarden.

nominative.german: Eine Milliarde Menschen hat keinen sicheren Zugang zu Trinkwasser.
nominative.english: One billion people have no reliable access to drinking water.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat, so nominative. Feminine nominative numeral eine; noun Milliarde takes no ending in the singular.

accusative.german: Der Staat investiert eine Milliarde in die Sanierung der Schulen.
accusative.english: The state is investing one billion in the renovation of schools.
accusative.hint: Direct object of investiert, so accusative. Feminine accusative eine; noun Milliarde has no ending.

dative.german: Bei einer Milliarde Euro liegt die geschätzte Gesamtsumme.
dative.english: The estimated total sum stands at one billion euros.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition bei. Feminine dative einer; noun Milliarde has no ending.

genitive.german: Der Verlust einer Milliarde brachte die Bank ins Wanken.
genitive.english: The loss of a billion caused the bank to falter.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Verlust. Feminine genitive einer; noun Milliarde takes no ending.

die Milliarde.proTip: False friend alert: German eine Milliarde is English 'one billion' (10^9). German eine Billion is English 'one trillion' (10^12)! Always capitalized: zwei Milliarden Euro.

die Weise.note: Feminine noun meaning 'way, manner, fashion'. Singular has no case endings: die, die, der, der Weise. Plural: die Weisen.

nominative.german: Diese besondere Weise zu malen gefällt mir sehr.
nominative.english: This special way of painting pleases me a lot.
nominative.hint: Subject of gefällt, so nominative. Feminine nominative demonstrative diese; weak adjective ending -e on besondere.

accusative.german: Er erklärte das Problem auf eine verständliche Weise.
accusative.english: He explained the problem in an understandable way.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition auf (manner). Feminine accusative eine; mixed adjective ending -e on verständliche.

dative.german: In gewisser Weise hat der Kollege völlig recht.
dative.english: In a certain way the colleague is completely right.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes the ending -er on gewisser; noun Weise is unchanged.

genitive.german: Die Einzigartigkeit ihrer Weise zu leben fasziniert mich.
genitive.english: The uniqueness of her way of living fascinates me.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Einzigartigkeit. Feminine genitive possessive ihrer; noun Weise takes no ending.

die Weise.proTip: Fixed idioms: auf diese Weise (in this way/manner — accusative after auf); in gewisser Weise (in a certain way — dative after in). Note suffix -weise forms adverbs: möglicherweise (possibly), beispielsweise (for example).

der Meter.note: Masculine (rarely neuter) noun meaning 'metre'. Only genitive singular adds -s (des Meters); nominative, accusative, dative remain Meter. After numbers, masculine units of measurement stay in the singular form (fünf Meter).

nominative.german: Der letzte Meter bis zum Gipfel war besonders steil.
nominative.english: The last metre to the summit was particularly steep.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on letzte.

accusative.german: Er sprang den entscheidenden Meter weiter als alle anderen.
accusative.english: He jumped the decisive metre further than anyone else.
accusative.hint: Accusative of measurement answering 'how much further'. Masculine accusative article den; weak ending -en on entscheidenden.

dative.german: Nach einem anstrengenden Meter im Schlamm rutschte er ab.
dative.english: After an exhausting metre in the mud he slipped.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en on anstrengenden.

genitive.german: Die Kosten des zusätzlichen Meters müssen wir selbst tragen.
genitive.english: We have to bear the cost of the additional metre ourselves.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Masculine genitive article des; weak ending -en on zusätzlichen; noun adds genitive -s.

der Meter.proTip: Measurement rule: masculine and neuter units of measurement retain their singular form after numbers: 100 Meter (never 100 Metere), 2 Kilo. Feminine units like Stunde or Meile take plural -n: zwei Meilen.

der Ring.note: Masculine noun meaning 'ring' (jewelry, circular band). In the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Rings / Ringes). Nominative: der Ring; accusative: den Ring; dative: dem Ring. Plural: die Ringe.

nominative.german: Der goldene Ring glänzte im hellen Sonnenlicht.
nominative.english: The golden ring shone in the bright sunlight.
nominative.hint: Subject of glänzte, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on goldene.

accusative.german: Er kaufte einen wunderschönen Ring für seine Verlobte.
accusative.english: He bought a gorgeous ring for his fiancée.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kaufte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; weak adjective ending -en on wunderschönen.

dative.german: Mit diesem wertvollen Ring machte er ihr einen Heiratsantrag.
dative.english: With this valuable ring he proposed to her.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on wertvollen.

genitive.german: Die Gravur des Rings war kaum noch lesbar.
genitive.english: The engraving of the ring was barely legible anymore.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gravur. Masculine genitive article des; noun Ring adds genitive -s (Ringes is also correct).

der Ring.proTip: Ring is used for jewelry (der Ehering = wedding ring), anatomy (der Augenring = dark circle under the eye), and traffic (der Innenstadtring = inner ring road). Plural: die Ringe.

der Ort.note: Masculine noun meaning 'place, location, town'. In the singular, only the genitive changes (des Ortes / des Orts); nominative der Ort, accusative den Ort, dative dem Ort. Plural: die Orte.

nominative.german: Der idyllische Ort liegt direkt an einem großen See.
nominative.english: The idyllic place lies directly on a large lake.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on idyllische.

accusative.german: Wir haben diesen historischen Ort zum ersten Mal besucht.
accusative.english: We visited this historic place for the first time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of besucht, so accusative. Masculine accusative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on historischen.

dative.german: An diesem ruhigen Ort kann man sich wunderbar erholen.
dative.english: In this quiet place one can relax wonderfully.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (location). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on ruhigen.

genitive.german: Die Geschichte des alten Ortes reicht bis ins Mittelalter zurück.
genitive.english: The history of the old town dates back to the Middle Ages.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Geschichte. Masculine genitive des; weak ending -en on alten; noun Ort adds -es.

der Ort.proTip: Key idioms: vor Ort sein (to be on site / locally present); an Ort und Stelle (on the spot / right then and there). Plural is regular: die Orte.

der Hang.note: Masculine noun meaning 'slope / hillside' (geography) or 'propensity / inclination' (figurative tendency). In the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Hangs / Hanges). Plural: die Hänge.

nominative.german: Der steile Hang war nach dem Regen sehr rutschig.
nominative.english: The steep slope was very slippery after the rain.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on steile.

accusative.german: Die Skifahrer fuhren den verschneiten Hang hinunter.
accusative.english: The skiers skied down the snow-covered slope.
accusative.hint: Accusative of path/direction with hinunterfahren. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on verschneiten.

dative.german: An dem sonnigen Hang wachsen besonders gute Weintrauben.
dative.english: On the sunny hillside particularly good grapes grow.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (location). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on sonnigen.

genitive.german: Wegen der Steilheit des Hangs mussten wir vorsichtig klettern.
genitive.english: Because of the steepness of the slope we had to climb carefully.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Steilheit. Masculine genitive article des; noun Hang adds genitive -s.

der Hang.proTip: Two distinct meanings: physical hillside/slope (der Abhang, Skihang) and mental inclination/tendency (der Hang zu + dative: Sie hat einen Hang zur Perfektion). Plural takes an umlaut: die Hänge.

der Kern.note: Masculine noun meaning 'core, kernel, seed, nucleus'. In the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Kerns / des Kernes). Plural: die Kerne.

nominative.german: Der feste Kern des Atoms enthält Protonen und Neutronen.
nominative.english: The solid nucleus of the atom contains protons and neutrons.
nominative.hint: Subject of enthält, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on feste.

accusative.german: Er hat den harten Kern des Pfirsichs versehentlich verschluckt.
accusative.english: He accidentally swallowed the hard pit of the peach.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verschluckt, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on harten.

dative.german: In seinem innersten Kern ist das Problem rein organisatorischer Natur.
dative.english: In its innermost core the problem is of purely organizational nature.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location/state). Masculine dative possessive seinem; weak adjective ending -en on innersten.

genitive.german: Die Spaltung des Kerns setzt gewaltige Energiemengen frei.
genitive.english: The splitting of the core releases vast amounts of energy.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Spaltung. Masculine genitive article des; noun Kern adds genitive -s.

der Kern.proTip: Common idioms: der harte Kern (the hard core / inner circle); der Kern der Sache (the heart of the matter); im Kern (at core / essentially). Fruit pits and stone kernels are Kerne; small seeds like apples also Kerne; berries have Samen.

der Druck.note: Masculine noun meaning 'pressure' (physical or psychological) or 'printing'. In the singular, only the genitive changes (des Drucks / Druckes). Nominative der Druck, accusative den Druck, dative dem Druck. Plural: die Drücke (physical forces) or die Drucke (prints).

nominative.german: Der psychische Druck auf die Angestellten war enorm hoch.
nominative.english: The psychological pressure on the employees was enormously high.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on psychische.

accusative.german: Die Chefin übt einen großen Druck auf das Team aus.
accusative.english: The boss exerts great pressure on the team.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausüben, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; weak adjective ending -en on großen.

dative.german: Unter starkem Druck trifft man oft unüberlegte Entscheidungen.
dative.english: Under strong pressure one often makes rash decisions.
dative.hint: Dative governed by unter (condition). Strong declension without article: masculine dative takes ending -em on starkem.

genitive.german: Wegen des hohen Drucks barst das alte Wasserrohr.
genitive.english: Because of the high pressure the old water pipe burst.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hohen; noun Druck adds genitive -s.

der Druck.proTip: Idioms: unter Druck stehen (to be under pressure); jemanden unter Druck setzen (to put pressure on someone); Druck ausüben auf + accusative. Note verb: drucken (to print) vs. drücken (to press/squeeze).

die Größe.note: Feminine noun meaning 'size, height, greatness, magnitude'. In the singular, feminine nouns take no case ending: die, die, der, der Größe. Plural: die Größen.

nominative.german: Die genaue Größe des Zimmers steht im Mietvertrag.
nominative.english: The exact size of the room is stated in the lease agreement.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on genaue.

accusative.german: Die Gutachter prüfen die tatsächliche Größe des Schadens.
accusative.english: The assessors are examining the actual extent of the damage.
accusative.hint: Direct object of prüfen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on tatsächliche.

dative.german: Bei dieser beachtlichen Größe passt der Schrank nicht durch die Tür.
dative.english: With this considerable size the wardrobe will not fit through the door.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on beachtlichen.

genitive.german: Trotz der enormen Größe des Flugzeugs war der Flug sehr ruhig.
genitive.english: Despite the enormous size of the aircraft the flight was very calm.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on enormen; noun Größe takes no ending.

die Größe.proTip: Größe corresponds to both 'size' (clothing: Welche Größe haben Sie?) and 'height' of a person (Körpergröße). It can also mean mathematical magnitude or a famous personality ('eine historische Größe').

die Gefahr.note: Feminine noun meaning 'danger, hazard, risk'. Feminine nouns do not decline in the singular: die Gefahr (nom/acc), der Gefahr (dat/gen). Plural: die Gefahren.

nominative.german: Die drohende Gefahr wurde von den Behörden unterschätzt.
nominative.english: The impending danger was underestimated by the authorities.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... unterschätzt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on drohende.

accusative.german: Wir erkannten die ernste Gefahr erst im allerletzten Moment.
accusative.english: We only recognized the serious danger at the very last moment.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erkannten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on ernste.

dative.german: In dieser großen Gefahr hielten die Dorfbewohner fest zusammen.
dative.english: In this great danger the villagers held closely together.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (state). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on großen.

genitive.german: Aus Angst vor den Folgen der Gefahr verließen viele die Stadt.
genitive.english: For fear of the consequences of the danger many left the city.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Feminine genitive article der; feminine noun Gefahr takes no ending.

die Gefahr.proTip: Key idioms: in Gefahr sein / schweben (to be in danger); jemanden in Gefahr bringen (to put someone in danger); auf eigene Gefahr (at one's own risk).

die Tiefe.note: Feminine noun meaning 'depth, deepness' (physical depth or emotional/intellectual profundity). In the singular, it has no endings: die, die, der, der Tiefe. Plural: die Tiefen.

nominative.german: Die gemessene Tiefe des Bergsees beträgt über zweihundert Meter.
nominative.english: The measured depth of the mountain lake is over two hundred metres.
nominative.hint: Subject of beträgt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on gemessene.

accusative.german: Der Taucher liebte die geheimnisvolle Tiefe des Ozeans.
accusative.english: The diver loved the mysterious depth of the ocean.
accusative.hint: Direct object of liebte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on geheimnisvolle.

dative.german: In dieser schwindelerregenden Tiefe herrscht völlige Dunkelheit.
dative.english: In this dizzying depth complete darkness prevails.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on schwindelerregenden.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung der unergründlichen Tiefe erfordert Spezialausrüstung.
genitive.english: The exploration of the unfathomable depth requires specialized equipment.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on unergründlichen.

die Tiefe.proTip: Used literally (die Wassertiefe = water depth) and figuratively (die Tiefe eines Gedichts = the depth of a poem; in die Tiefe gehen = to go into depth / explore in detail). Plural expression: Höhen und Tiefen (ups and downs).

die Studie.note: Feminine noun meaning 'study' (scientific report, empirical investigation). Feminine nouns take no endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Studie. Plural: die Studien.

nominative.german: Eine neue wissenschaftliche Studie belegt den positiven Effekt von Sport.
nominative.english: A new scientific study proves the positive effect of exercise.
nominative.hint: Subject of belegt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on neue and wissenschaftliche.

accusative.german: Die Forscher veröffentlichten eine umfassende Studie zum Klimawandel.
accusative.english: The researchers published a comprehensive study on climate change.
accusative.hint: Direct object of veröffentlichten, so accusative. Feminine accusative eine; mixed adjective ending -e on umfassende.

dative.german: Laut einer aktuellen Studie schlafen die meisten Menschen zu wenig.
dative.english: According to a current study most people sleep too little.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition laut. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on aktuellen.

genitive.german: Die Ergebnisse der langjährigen Studie überraschten selbst die Experten.
genitive.english: The results of the multi-year study surprised even the experts.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ergebnisse. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on langjährigen.

die Studie.proTip: Distinguish die Studie (the research paper / investigation: eine Studie durchführen) from das Studium (university degree / academic study: ein Studium beginnen). Plural of Studie is die Studien.

die Macht.note: Feminine noun meaning 'power, authority, might'. In the singular, no case endings are added: die, die, der, der Macht. Plural: die Mächte (with umlaut).

nominative.german: Die politische Macht liegt in einer Demokratie beim Volk.
nominative.english: In a democracy political power lies with the people.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on politische.

accusative.german: Der Diktator wollte die absolute Macht um jeden Preis behalten.
accusative.english: The dictator wanted to keep absolute power at all costs.
accusative.hint: Direct object of behalten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on absolute.

dative.german: Mit großer Macht kommt auch eine große Verantwortung.
dative.english: With great power comes great responsibility as well.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes the strong ending -er on großer.

genitive.german: Der Missbrauch der Macht führte schließlich zum Sturz der Regierung.
genitive.english: The abuse of power ultimately led to the overthrow of the government.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Missbrauch. Feminine genitive article der; feminine noun Macht takes no ending.

die Macht.proTip: Key idioms: an der Macht sein (to be in power — dative of location); an die Macht kommen (to come to power — accusative of direction); an die Macht gelangen. Plural takes an umlaut: die Großmächte (the superpowers).

der Vorfahr.note: Weak masculine noun (n-noun) meaning 'ancestor, forebear'. Weak masculine nouns add -(e)n in all singular cases except the nominative: der Vorfahr (nom), den Vorfahren (acc), dem Vorfahren (dat), des Vorfahren (gen). Plural: die Vorfahren.

nominative.german: Ein entfernter Vorfahr unserer Familie wanderte vor vielen Jahren nach Amerika aus.
nominative.english: A distant ancestor of our family emigrated to America many years ago.
nominative.hint: Subject of wanderte ... aus, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending; entfernter takes strong ending -er; Vorfahr has no ending in the nominative singular.

accusative.german: Der Genealoge erforscht einen berühmten Vorfahren des Schriftstellers.
accusative.english: The genealogist is researching a famous ancestor of the writer.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erforscht, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; weak adjective ending -en; weak noun Vorfahr adds -en.

dative.german: Das antike Schwert gehörte einst einem tapferen Vorfahren der Familie.
dative.english: The antique sword once belonged to a brave ancestor of the family.
dative.hint: Dative governed by gehören. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en; weak noun adds -en.

genitive.german: Die Traditionen dieses Vorfahren werden bis heute gepflegt.
genitive.english: The traditions of this ancestor are preserved to this day.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Traditionen. Masculine genitive dieses; weak noun Vorfahr adds -en (not -s!).

der Vorfahr.proTip: Vorfahr is a weak masculine noun (n-noun): it takes -en in accusative, dative, and genitive singular (des Vorfahren, never des Vorfahr(e)s). Female ancestor is die Vorfahrin (plural: die Vorfahrinnen).

der Körper.note: Masculine noun ending in -er meaning 'body, physique'. It declines regularly: in the singular only the genitive adds -s (des Körpers). Nominative der Körper, accusative den Körper, dative dem Körper. Plural remains die Körper.

nominative.german: Der menschliche Körper besteht zu einem großen Teil aus Wasser.
nominative.english: The human body consists largely of water.
nominative.hint: Subject of besteht, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on menschliche.

accusative.german: Regelmäßiges Schwimmen stärkt den gesamten Körper effektiv.
accusative.english: Regular swimming strengthens the entire body effectively.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stärkt, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

dative.german: Mit einem gesunden Körper bewältigt man den Alltag viel leichter.
dative.english: With a healthy body one copes with everyday life much more easily.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en on gesunden.

genitive.german: Die Abwehrkräfte des Körpers bekämpfen die Krankheitserreger.
genitive.english: The body's defenses fight the pathogens.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Abwehrkräfte. Masculine genitive article des; noun Körper adds genitive -s.

der Körper.proTip: Idioms: am ganzen Körper zittern (to tremble all over / with one's whole body); der Fremdkörper (foreign body / object). Plural is unchanged: die Körper.

die Gemeinschaft.note: Feminine noun ending in -schaft meaning 'community, fellowship'. Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Gemeinschaft. Plural: die Gemeinschaften.

nominative.german: Eine lebendige Gemeinschaft unterstützt ihre schwächeren Mitglieder.
nominative.english: A lively community supports its weaker members.
nominative.hint: Subject of unterstützt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on lebendige.

accusative.german: Wir wollen die europäische Gemeinschaft in Krisenzeiten stärken.
accusative.english: We want to strengthen the European community in times of crisis.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stärken, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on europäische.

dative.german: In dieser engen Gemeinschaft fühlt sich jeder Neubürger willkommen.
dative.english: In this close community every new citizen feels welcome.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on engen.

genitive.german: Das Wohlergehen der Gemeinschaft steht im Mittelpunkt der Politik.
genitive.english: The well-being of the community is at the center of politics.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wohlergehen. Feminine genitive article der; noun Gemeinschaft takes no ending.

die Gemeinschaft.proTip: All German nouns ending in -schaft are feminine: die Gemeinschaft, die Mannschaft (team), die Freundschaft (friendship), die Wissenschaft (science).

die Kraft.note: Feminine noun meaning 'power, strength, force' (or 'employee / worker' in Arbeitskraft). No singular endings: die, die, der, der Kraft. Plural: die Kräfte (with umlaut).

nominative.german: Die körperliche Kraft des Athleten war wirklich beeindruckend.
nominative.english: The athlete's physical strength was truly impressive.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on körperliche.

accusative.german: Der Gewichtheber mobilisierte seine letzte Kraft für den Versuch.
accusative.english: The weightlifter mobilized his last strength for the attempt.
accusative.hint: Direct object of mobilisierte, so accusative. Feminine possessive seine; mixed adjective ending -e on letzte.

dative.german: Mit voller Kraft zog die Mannschaft das schwere Boot an Land.
dative.english: With full strength the team pulled the heavy boat ashore.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes the strong ending -er on voller.

genitive.german: Trotz der schwindenden Kraft kämpfte der Marathonläufer bis zum Ziel.
genitive.english: Despite fading strength the marathon runner fought to the finish.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on schwindenden; noun Kraft takes no ending.

die Kraft.proTip: Key legal and organizational idioms: in Kraft treten (to come into effect / force — accusative); außer Kraft setzen (to repeal / invalidate); aus eigener Kraft (under one's own steam). Plural takes an umlaut: die Kräfte.

die Zurückweisung.note: Feminine noun ending in -ung meaning 'rejection, repudiation, rebuff'. Feminine nouns take no endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Zurückweisung. Plural: die Zurückweisungen.

nominative.german: Eine schroffe Zurückweisung verletzte den jungen Bewerber tief.
nominative.english: A blunt rejection hurt the young applicant deeply.
nominative.hint: Subject of verletzte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on schroffe.

accusative.german: Er konnte die unerwartete Zurückweisung nur schwer verkraften.
accusative.english: He could only cope with the unexpected rejection with difficulty.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verkraften, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on unerwartete.

dative.german: Nach dieser schmerzhaften Zurückweisung zog er sich tagelang zurück.
dative.english: After this painful rejection he withdrew for days.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on schmerzhaften.

genitive.german: Die Gründe der Zurückweisung wurden dem Kläger nicht mitgeteilt.
genitive.english: The reasons for the rejection were not disclosed to the plaintiff.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gründe. Feminine genitive article der; noun Zurückweisung takes no ending.

die Zurückweisung.proTip: Derived from the separable verb zurückweisen (to reject/turn away). Nouns ending in -ung are invariably feminine: die Zurückweisung, die Einladung, die Hoffnung.

die Natur.note: Feminine noun meaning 'nature' (the natural physical world, or character/disposition). In the singular, no case endings are added: die, die, der, der Natur. Plural: die Naturen (rare, mostly for characters).

nominative.german: Die unberührte Natur lockt jedes Jahr unzählige Wanderer an.
nominative.english: Untouched nature attracts countless hikers every year.
nominative.hint: Subject of lockt ... an, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on unberührte.

accusative.german: Wir müssen die verletzliche Natur vor weiterer Zerstörung schützen.
accusative.english: We must protect vulnerable nature from further destruction.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schützen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on verletzliche.

dative.german: Im Urlaub verbringen wir die meiste Zeit draußen in der freien Natur.
dative.english: On holiday we spend most of our time outside in the great outdoors.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on freien.

genitive.german: Die Gesetze der Natur lassen sich durch Technik nicht aufheben.
genitive.english: The laws of nature cannot be suspended by technology.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gesetze. Feminine genitive article der; feminine noun Natur takes no ending.

die Natur.proTip: Idioms: in freier Natur (in the wild / outdoors); von Natur aus (by nature / naturally: Er ist von Natur aus neugierig); reine Natur (pure nature).

das Gas.note: Neuter noun meaning 'gas' (matter state, or fuel). Neuter nouns decline for case: nominative and accusative are das Gas, dative is dem Gas, and genitive adds -es (des Gases). Plural: die Gase.

nominative.german: Das austretende Gas roch stechend nach verfaulten Eiern.
nominative.english: The escaping gas smelled pungently of rotten eggs.
nominative.hint: Subject of roch, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on austretende.

accusative.german: Die Feuerwehrleute pumpten das giftige Gas vorsichtig ab.
accusative.english: The firefighters carefully pumped out the poisonous gas.
accusative.hint: Direct object of pumpten ... ab, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on giftige.

dative.german: Mit verflüssigtem Gas werden immer mehr moderne Schiffe angetrieben.
dative.english: With liquefied gas more and more modern ships are powered.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes ending -em on verflüssigtem; noun Gas takes no ending.

genitive.german: Wegen des entweichenden Gases wurde das gesamte Gebäude evakuiert.
genitive.english: Because of the escaping gas the entire building was evacuated.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on entweichenden; noun Gas adds -es.

das Gas.proTip: Everyday idiom: Gas geben (literally to step on the gas pedal; figuratively to speed up / hurry up: Wir müssen Gas geben!). Note genitive singular des Gases (adds -es because Gas ends in -s).

der Tod.note: Masculine noun meaning 'death'. In the singular, only the genitive adds an ending (des Todes / des Tods). Nominative der Tod, accusative den Tod, dative dem Tod. Usually singular (no plural).

nominative.german: Der plötzliche Tod des Sängers schockierte die Musikwelt.
nominative.english: The singer's sudden death shocked the music world.
nominative.hint: Subject of schockierte, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on plötzliche.

accusative.german: Der mutige Polizist fand den Tod im Einsatz für andere.
accusative.english: The brave police officer met his death in the line of duty for others.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fand, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; noun Tod takes no ending.

dative.german: Nach dem tragischen Tod ihres Vaters übernahm sie das Familienunternehmen.
dative.english: After the tragic death of her father she took over the family business.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on tragischen.

genitive.german: Die genaue Ursache des Todes konnte der Gerichtsmediziner feststellen.
genitive.english: The coroner was able to determine the exact cause of death.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ursache. Masculine genitive article des; noun Tod adds genitive ending -es.

der Tod.proTip: Spelling alert: der Tod (noun, meaning 'death', with d) vs. tot (adjective, meaning 'dead', with t: Er ist tot). Compound nouns: die Todesursache (cause of death), das Todesurteil (death sentence).

die Art.note: Feminine noun meaning 'kind, species, type, manner'. In the singular, it has no endings: die, die, der, der Art. Plural: die Arten.

nominative.german: Diese seltene Art von Orchidee wächst nur im Hochgebirge.
nominative.english: This rare species of orchid grows only in high mountain ranges.
nominative.hint: Subject of wächst, so nominative. Feminine nominative demonstrative diese; weak adjective ending -e on seltene.

accusative.german: Ich schätze seine ruhige und besonnene Art sehr.
accusative.english: I value his calm and thoughtful manner very much.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schätze, so accusative. Feminine possessive seine; mixed adjective ending -e on ruhige and besonnene.

dative.german: Mit dieser Art von Humor kann leider nicht jeder etwas anfangen.
dative.english: Unfortunately not everyone can relate to this kind of humor.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative determiner dieser; noun Art is unchanged in the singular.

genitive.german: Der Schutz der bedrohten Art hat für die Umweltschützer oberste Priorität.
genitive.english: The protection of the endangered species has top priority for the environmentalists.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Schutz. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on bedrohten; noun Art takes no ending.

die Art.proTip: Art has two primary meanings: biological species/kind (eine bedrohte Tierart) and personal manner/way of acting (seine freundliche Art). Fixed idiom: auf diese Art und Weise (in this manner).

das Werkzeug.note: Neuter compound noun (Werk + Zeug) meaning 'tool, implement, instrument'. Neuter nouns decline for case: nominative/accusative das Werkzeug, dative dem Werkzeug, genitive des Werkzeugs. Plural: die Werkzeuge.

nominative.german: Das richtige Werkzeug erleichtert die handwerkliche Arbeit ungemein.
nominative.english: The right tool makes manual work immensely easier.
nominative.hint: Subject of erleichtert, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on richtige.

accusative.german: Der Handwerker legte das schwere Werkzeug zurück in den Koffer.
accusative.english: The craftsman put the heavy tool back into the toolbox.
accusative.hint: Direct object of legte, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on schwere.

dative.german: Mit diesem praktischen Werkzeug kann man Schrauben mühelos lösen.
dative.english: With this practical tool you can loosen screws effortlessly.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on praktischen.

genitive.german: Die Qualität des Werkzeugs entscheidet über die Haltbarkeit des Möbelstücks.
genitive.english: The quality of the tool determines the durability of the piece of furniture.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Qualität. Neuter genitive article des; noun Werkzeug adds genitive -s.

das Werkzeug.proTip: All nouns ending in -zeug are neuter: das Werkzeug, das Flugzeug (airplane), das Fahrzeug (vehicle), das Spielzeug (toy). Zeug originally meant 'equipment / gear'.

die Veränderung.note: Feminine noun ending in -ung meaning 'change, alteration, transformation'. No singular case endings: die, die, der, der Veränderung. Plural: die Veränderungen.

nominative.german: Eine spürbare Veränderung des Klimas ist weltweit zu beobachten.
nominative.english: A noticeable change in the climate can be observed worldwide.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist ... zu beobachten, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on spürbare.

accusative.german: Die Firma plant eine grundlegende Veränderung ihrer Organisationsstruktur.
accusative.english: The company is planning a fundamental change to its organizational structure.
accusative.hint: Direct object of plant, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on grundlegende.

dative.german: Nach dieser tiefgreifenden Veränderung brauchten die Mitarbeiter etwas Eingewöhnungszeit.
dative.english: After this profound change the employees needed some time to settle in.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on tiefgreifenden.

genitive.german: Die Notwendigkeit der Veränderung wurde allen Beteiligten schnell klar.
genitive.english: The necessity of the change quickly became clear to everyone involved.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Notwendigkeit. Feminine genitive article der; noun Veränderung takes no ending.

die Veränderung.proTip: Derived from the verb verändern (to change/alter). Feminine suffix -ung forms nouns from verbs: verändern -> die Veränderung. Fixed collocation: eine Veränderung vornehmen (to make a change).

die Umgebung.note: Feminine noun ending in -ung meaning 'surroundings, vicinity, environment'. Singular has no endings: die, die, der, der Umgebung. Plural: die Umgebungen.

nominative.german: Die malerische Umgebung unseres Hotels lädt zu langen Spaziergängen ein.
nominative.english: The picturesque surroundings of our hotel invite long walks.
nominative.hint: Subject of lädt ... ein, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on malerische.

accusative.german: Die Kinder erkundeten die neue Umgebung mit großer Neugier.
accusative.english: The children explored the new environment with great curiosity.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erkundeten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

dative.german: In einer ruhigen Umgebung kann man sich wesentlich besser konzentrieren.
dative.english: In quiet surroundings one can concentrate much better.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on ruhigen.

genitive.german: Der Lärm der lauten Umgebung störte die Patienten im Krankenhaus.
genitive.english: The noise of the loud surroundings disturbed the patients in the hospital.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Lärm. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on lauten; noun Umgebung takes no ending.

die Umgebung.proTip: Common idiom: in der näheren Umgebung (in the immediate vicinity / surrounding area). Distinguish die Umgebung (immediate physical surroundings/vicinity) from die Umwelt (the natural ecological environment).

die Fähigkeit.note: Feminine noun ending in -keit meaning 'ability, skill, capability'. Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Fähigkeit. Plural: die Fähigkeiten.

nominative.german: Die Fähigkeit zur Teamarbeit wird in diesem Beruf besonders geschätzt.
nominative.english: The ability to work in a team is particularly valued in this profession.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird ... geschätzt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; noun Fähigkeit takes no ending.

accusative.german: Der Schüler besitzt eine bemerkenswerte Fähigkeit im Kopfrechnen.
accusative.english: The student possesses a remarkable ability in mental arithmetic.
accusative.hint: Direct object of besitzt, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on bemerkenswerte.

dative.german: Mit dieser besonderen Fähigkeit löste die Ingenieurin das technische Problem.
dative.english: With this special skill the female engineer solved the technical problem.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on besonderen.

genitive.german: Der Ausbau der eigenen Fähigkeiten erfordert viel Übung und Geduld.
genitive.english: The development of one's own abilities requires much practice and patience.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural expressing 'of' after Ausbau. Genitive plural article der; weak adjective ending -en on eigenen; plural noun adds -en.

die Fähigkeit.proTip: Nouns ending in -keit and -heit are always feminine: die Fähigkeit, die Möglichkeit (possibility), die Genauigkeit (precision). Preposition pattern: die Fähigkeit zu + dative (the ability to do sth).

die Hilfe.note: Feminine noun meaning 'help, assistance, aid'. In the singular, no endings are added: die, die, der, der Hilfe. Plural: die Hilfen (usually financial or practical aids).

nominative.german: Die schnelle Hilfe der Nachbarn rettete das brennende Gartenhaus.
nominative.english: The neighbors' prompt help saved the burning garden shed.
nominative.hint: Subject of rettete, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on schnelle.

accusative.german: Er brauchte dringend die professionelle Hilfe eines Fachanwalts.
accusative.english: He urgently needed the professional help of a specialist lawyer.
accusative.hint: Direct object of brauchte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on professionelle.

dative.german: Mit deiner freundlichen Hilfe konnten wir den Umzug rechtzeitig beenden.
dative.english: With your kind help we were able to finish the move in time.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative possessive deiner; weak adjective ending -en on freundlichen.

genitive.german: Wegen der fehlenden Hilfe scheiterte das ehrgeizige Projekt schließlich.
genitive.english: Because of the lacking help the ambitious project ultimately failed.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on fehlenden; noun Hilfe takes no ending.

die Hilfe.proTip: Key idioms: Erste Hilfe leisten (to administer first aid); zu Hilfe eilen / kommen (to rush/come to sb's aid); mit Hilfe / mithilfe + genitive (with the help of / by means of).

der Experte.note: Weak masculine noun (n-noun) ending in -e meaning 'expert, specialist'. All cases except the nominative singular add -n: der Experte (nom), den Experten (acc), dem Experten (dat), des Experten (gen). Plural: die Experten.

nominative.german: Ein anerkannter Experte auf diesem Gebiet hielt einen spannenden Vortrag.
nominative.english: A recognized expert in this field gave an exciting presentation.
nominative.hint: Subject of hielt, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending; anerkannter takes strong ending -er; Experte has no ending in the nominative singular.

accusative.german: Die Redaktion befragte den bekannten Experten zur aktuellen Wirtschaftslage.
accusative.english: The editorial team interviewed the well-known expert on the current economic situation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of befragte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en; weak noun Experte adds -n.

dative.german: Wir vertrauen dem erfahrenen Experten bei der Auswahl der richtigen Strategie.
dative.english: We trust the experienced expert in choosing the right strategy.
dative.hint: Dative required by vertrauen. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en; weak noun Experte adds -n.

genitive.german: Die Einschätzung des unabhängigen Experten erwies sich als völlig zutreffend.
genitive.english: The independent expert's assessment proved to be completely accurate.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Einschätzung. Masculine genitive article des; weak ending -en on unabhängigen; weak noun Experte adds -n (not -s!).

der Experte.proTip: Experte is a classic weak masculine noun: masculine humans ending in -e (der Experte, der Kollege, der Junge, der Zeuge) decline with -n in accusative, dative, and genitive singular. Female counterpart: die Expertin.

das Bedürfnis.note: Neuter noun ending in -nis meaning 'need, requirement, urge'. Neuter nouns in -nis double the s before endings: des Bedürfnisses (genitive singular), die Bedürfnisse (plural). Nominative/accusative: das Bedürfnis; dative: dem Bedürfnis.

nominative.german: Das grundlegende Bedürfnis nach Sicherheit teilt jeder Mensch.
nominative.english: Every human shares the fundamental need for security.
nominative.hint: Subject of teilt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on grundlegende.

accusative.german: Sie verspürte das dringende Bedürfnis nach einer kurzen Pause.
accusative.english: She felt the urgent need for a short break.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verspürte, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on dringende.

dative.german: Die Schule kommt dem besonderen Bedürfnis behinderter Kinder entgegen.
dative.english: The school accommodates the special need of disabled children.
dative.hint: Dative governed by entgegenkommen. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on besonderen; noun Bedürfnis takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Befriedigung des seelischen Bedürfnisses stand für den Therapeuten im Vordergrund.
genitive.english: The satisfaction of the emotional need was paramount for the therapist.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Befriedigung. Neuter genitive article des; weak ending -en on seelischen; noun doubles the s and adds -es: Bedürfnisses.

das Bedürfnis.proTip: Spelling rule: nouns ending in -nis double the -s- before vowel endings: das Bedürfnis -> des Bedürfnisses (genitive), die Bedürfnisse (plural). Preposition pattern: ein Bedürfnis nach + dative (a need for).

der Haufen.note: Masculine noun belonging to the mixed/special weak declension (originally der Haufe). In modern standard German, nominative is der Haufen, accusative den Haufen, dative dem Haufen, and genitive adds -s: des Haufens. Plural: die Haufen.

nominative.german: Ein riesiger Haufen von Steinen blockierte die schmale Landstraße.
nominative.english: A huge pile of stones blocked the narrow country road.
nominative.hint: Subject of blockierte, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending; riesiger takes strong ending -er; noun Haufen has no ending.

accusative.german: Die Gärtner fegten den großen Haufen aus trockenem Laub zusammen.
accusative.english: The gardeners swept together the large pile of dry leaves.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fegten ... zusammen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on großen.

dative.german: Unter diesem unordentlichen Haufen alter Zeitungen lag mein Ausweis.
dative.english: Under this messy pile of old newspapers lay my identity card.
dative.hint: Dative governed by unter (location). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on unordentlichen.

genitive.german: Wegen des riesigen Haufens aus Bauschutt konnte niemand parken.
genitive.english: Because of the huge pile of rubble nobody could park.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on riesigen; noun Haufen adds genitive -s.

der Haufen.proTip: Idioms: über den Haufen werfen (to throw into disarray / overturn plans); ein Haufen Geld (a heap / ton of money — informal quantifier); über den Haufen rennen (to knock someone over).

die Generation.note: Feminine noun of Latin origin ending in -tion meaning 'generation'. Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Generation. Plural: die Generationen.

nominative.german: Die jüngere Generation blickt oft mit Sorge in die Zukunft.
nominative.english: The younger generation often looks into the future with concern.
nominative.hint: Subject of blickt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on jüngere.

accusative.german: Dieses zeitlose Buch begeistert schon die dritte Generation von Lesern.
accusative.english: This timeless book has already been delighting the third generation of readers.
accusative.hint: Direct object of begeistert, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on dritte.

dative.german: Von einer neuen Generation verlangt die Arbeitswelt völlig neue Kompetenzen.
dative.english: From a new generation the working world demands completely new skills.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on neuen.

genitive.german: Die Lebensweise der heutigen Generation unterscheidet sich stark von der früheren.
genitive.english: The lifestyle of today's generation differs greatly from that of earlier ones.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Lebensweise. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on heutigen; noun Generation takes no ending.

die Generation.proTip: All nouns ending in -tion are feminine and take plural -en: die Generation, die Information, die Tradition. Common collocation: der Generationenkonflikt (generation conflict).

die Menschheit.note: Feminine collective noun ending in -heit meaning 'humanity, mankind' (all human beings collectively). Feminine nouns take no endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Menschheit. Used almost exclusively in the singular.

nominative.german: Die gesamte Menschheit steht vor historischen ökologischen Herausforderungen.
nominative.english: All of humanity faces historic ecological challenges.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on gesamte.

accusative.german: Wissenschaftler wollen die Menschheit vor gefährlichen Seuchen schützen.
accusative.english: Scientists want to protect humanity from dangerous epidemics.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schützen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; noun Menschheit takes no ending.

dative.german: Diese bahnbrechende Erfindung brachte der Menschheit unermesslichen Nutzen.
dative.english: This groundbreaking invention brought immeasurable benefit to humanity.
dative.hint: Dative indirect object of brachte (to whom). Feminine dative article der; noun Menschheit takes no ending.

genitive.german: Das kulturelle Erbe der Menschheit muss für zukünftige Generationen bewahrt werden.
genitive.english: The cultural heritage of humanity must be preserved for future generations.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erbe. Feminine genitive article der; noun Menschheit takes no ending.

die Menschheit.proTip: All nouns ending in -heit are feminine: die Menschheit, die Gesundheit (health), die Freiheit (freedom). Distinguish die Menschheit (humanity/mankind as a species) from die Menschlichkeit (humaneness / compassion).

die Reise.note: Feminine noun meaning 'journey, trip, voyage, travel'. In the singular, no case endings are added: die, die, der, der Reise. Plural: die Reisen.

nominative.german: Die lange Reise durch Skandinavien war ein unvergessliches Erlebnis.
nominative.english: The long journey through Scandinavia was an unforgettable experience.
nominative.hint: Subject of war, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on lange.

accusative.german: Wir buchten gestern eine zweiwöchige Reise nach Italien.
accusative.english: Yesterday we booked a two-week trip to Italy.
accusative.hint: Direct object of buchten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on zweiwöchige.

dative.german: Vor dieser weiten Reise prüfte er den Zustand seines Autos genau.
dative.english: Before this long journey he checked the condition of his car carefully.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (time). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on weiten.

genitive.german: Der Höhepunkt der abenteuerlichen Reise war die Überquerung des Passes.
genitive.english: The highlight of the adventurous journey was crossing the mountain pass.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Höhepunkt. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on abenteuerlichen; noun Reise takes no ending.

die Reise.proTip: Idioms: eine Reise antreten (to embark on a journey); auf Reisen sein (to be traveling / on a trip); Gute Reise! (Have a good trip!). Verb: reisen.

die Dunkelheit.note: Feminine noun ending in -heit meaning 'darkness, obscurity'. Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Dunkelheit. Used almost exclusively in the singular.

nominative.german: Die plötzliche Dunkelheit überraschte die Wanderer im dichten Wald.
nominative.english: The sudden darkness surprised the hikers in the dense forest.
nominative.hint: Subject of überraschte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on plötzliche.

accusative.german: Die Taschenlampe durchbrach die tiefe Dunkelheit der Höhle.
accusative.english: The flashlight pierced the deep darkness of the cave.
accusative.hint: Direct object of durchbrach, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on tiefe.

dative.german: In der völligen Dunkelheit konnte man die eigene Hand nicht sehen.
dative.english: In complete darkness one could not see one's own hand.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location/state). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on völligen.

genitive.german: Die Schatten der Dunkelheit wirkten auf das Kind sehr bedrohlich.
genitive.english: The shadows of the darkness seemed very threatening to the child.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Schatten. Feminine genitive article der; noun Dunkelheit takes no ending.

die Dunkelheit.proTip: Nouns ending in -heit are always feminine: die Dunkelheit, die Klarheit (clarity), die Wahrheit (truth). Idioms: im Schutz der Dunkelheit (under cover of darkness); bei Dunkelheit (after dark / at nightfall).

die Eltern.note: Plural-only noun (plural tantum) meaning 'parents'. It has no singular form in standard German (use der Vater, die Mutter, or ein Elternteil). In the plural: nominative die Eltern, accusative die Eltern, dative den Eltern (already ending in -n), genitive der Eltern.

nominative.german: Die besorgten Eltern warteten die ganze Nacht am Telefon.
nominative.english: The worried parents waited by the phone all night.
