das Uran.note: Neuter noun (chemical element U) meaning 'uranium'. In the singular, nominative and accusative are das Uran, dative is dem Uran, and genitive adds -s: des Urans. Uncountable.

nominative.german: Das angereicherte Uran dient als Brennstoff in zivilen Kernkraftwerken.
nominative.english: Enriched uranium serves as fuel in civilian nuclear power plants.
nominative.hint: Subject of dient, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on angereicherte.

accusative.german: Die Fabrik verarbeitet das geförderte Uran zu fertigen Brennelementen.
accusative.english: The factory processes the mined uranium into finished fuel assemblies.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verarbeitet, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on geförderte.

dative.german: Mit natürlichem Uran allein lässt sich keine Kettenreaktion in Gang halten.
dative.english: With natural uranium alone a chain reaction cannot be sustained.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on natürlichem.

genitive.german: Der radioaktive Zerfall des Urans dauert viele Millionen Jahre.
genitive.english: The radioactive decay of uranium takes many millions of years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zerfall. Neuter genitive article des; noun Uran adds genitive -s.

das Uran.proTip: Most chemical metals and elements ending in -ium or -an are neuter: das Uran, das Helium, das Eisen, das Gold, das Platin.

das Neuron.note: Neuter noun of Greek origin meaning 'neuron / nerve cell'. In the singular, nominative and accusative are das Neuron, dative is dem Neuron, and genitive adds -s: des Neurons. Plural: die Neuronen (or die Neurone).

nominative.german: Ein einzelnes Neuron kann Signale an Tausende benachbarte Zellen weiterleiten.
nominative.english: A single neuron can forward signals to thousands of neighboring cells.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann ... weiterleiten, so nominative. Mixed declension: neuter ein has no ending; einzelnes takes strong ending -es; Neuron takes no ending.

accusative.german: Forscher stimulierten das isolierte Neuron mit winzigen Elektroden.
accusative.english: Researchers stimulated the isolated neuron with tiny electrodes.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stimulierten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on isolierte.

dative.german: Zwischen dem aktivierten Neuron und der Muskelzelle fließt ein elektrischer Impuls.
dative.english: An electrical impulse flows between the activated neuron and the muscle cell.
dative.hint: Dative governed by zwischen (location). Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on aktivierten.

genitive.german: Die Struktur des menschlichen Neurons ist hochgradig spezialisiert.
genitive.english: The structure of the human neuron is highly specialized.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Struktur. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on menschlichen; noun Neuron adds genitive -s.

das Neuron.proTip: Greek neuter nouns ending in -on (das Neuron, das Elektron, das Proton) take -s in the genitive singular (des Neurons) and -en in the plural (die Neuronen).

die Erdkruste.note: Feminine compound noun (Erde + Kruste) meaning 'Earth's crust' (outermost solid geological layer). Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Erdkruste. Plural: die Erdkrusten (rare).

nominative.german: Die feste Erdkruste schwimmt auf dem heißen, zähflüssigen Erdmantel.
nominative.english: The solid Earth's crust floats on the hot, viscous mantle.
nominative.hint: Subject of schwimmt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on feste.

accusative.german: Geologen durchbohren die dünne Erdkruste bei Tiefseebohrungen um mehrere Kilometer.
accusative.english: Geologists drill through the thin Earth's crust by several kilometers during deep-sea drilling.
accusative.hint: Direct object of durchbohren, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on dünne.

dative.german: Tief in der kontinentalen Erdkruste entstehen unter gewaltigem Druck wertvolle Diamanten.
dative.english: Deep in the continental Earth's crust valuable diamonds form under enormous pressure.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on kontinentalen.

genitive.german: Die tektonischen Bewegungen der Erdkruste lösen schwere Erdbeben und Vulkanausbrüche aus.
genitive.english: The tectonic movements of the Earth's crust trigger severe earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bewegungen. Feminine genitive article der; noun Erdkruste takes no ending.

die Erdkruste.proTip: Kruste means 'crust' (also used for bread: die Brotkruste). All compound nouns ending in -kruste are feminine: die Erdkruste, die Salzkruste.

die Superintelligenz.note: Feminine compound noun (Super- + Intelligenz) meaning 'superintelligence' (artificial intelligence vastly surpassing human cognitive capability). Feminine nouns take no endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Superintelligenz.

nominative.german: Eine künstliche Superintelligenz könnte die Menschheit vor unvorhersehbare Probleme stellen.
nominative.english: An artificial superintelligence could confront humanity with unpredictable problems.
nominative.hint: Subject of könnte ... stellen, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on künstliche.

accusative.german: Viele Philosophen betrachten die hypothetische Superintelligenz sowohl als Chance als auch als Risiko.
accusative.english: Many philosophers regard hypothetical superintelligence both as an opportunity and as a risk.
accusative.hint: Direct object of betrachten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on hypothetische.

dative.german: Vor einer unkontrollierbaren Superintelligenz warnten bereits renommierte Informatiker und Physiker.
dative.english: Renowned computer scientists and physicists already warned against an uncontrollable superintelligence.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (warnen vor + dative). Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on unkontrollierbaren.

genitive.german: Die Entwicklung einer echten Superintelligenz erfordert strenge internationale Sicherheitsstandards.
genitive.english: The development of a true superintelligence requires strict international safety standards.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Entwicklung. Feminine genitive article einer; weak adjective ending -en on echten; noun takes no ending.

die Superintelligenz.proTip: All nouns ending in -enz are feminine: die Intelligenz, die Superintelligenz, die Konferenz, die Existenz. Super- is an intensifying prefix in German.

das Erdbeben.note: Neuter compound noun (Erde + Beben) meaning 'earthquake'. Neuter nouns decline for case: nominative/accusative das Erdbeben, dative dem Erdbeben, genitive des Erdbebens. Plural remains die Erdbeben.

nominative.german: Ein schweres Erdbeben erschütterte die Küstenregion am frühen Morgen.
nominative.english: A severe earthquake shook the coastal region early in the morning.
nominative.hint: Subject of erschütterte, so nominative. Mixed declension: neuter ein has no ending; schweres takes strong ending -es; Erdbeben takes no ending.

accusative.german: Die seismischen Stationen registrierten das unerwartete Erdbeben sofort.
accusative.english: The seismic stations registered the unexpected earthquake immediately.
accusative.hint: Direct object of registrierten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on unerwartete.

dative.german: Bei dem verheerenden Erdbeben wurden Hunderte historische Gebäude zerstört.
dative.english: In the devastating earthquake hundreds of historic buildings were destroyed.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on verheerenden.

genitive.german: Die Stärke des nächtlichen Erdbebens lag bei 6,8 auf der Richterskala.
genitive.english: The magnitude of the nighttime earthquake was 6.8 on the Richter scale.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Stärke. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on nächtlichen; noun adds genitive -s.

das Erdbeben.proTip: Derived from beben (to tremble / shake). Compounds ending in -beben are neuter: das Beben, das Seebeben (seaquake/tsunami trigger), das Nachbeben (aftershock). Plural is unchanged: die Erdbeben.

die Denkaufgabe.note: Feminine compound noun (Denken + Aufgabe) meaning 'cognitive task, brain teaser, mental problem'. Feminine nouns take no case endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Denkaufgabe. Plural: die Denkaufgaben.

nominative.german: Diese knifflige Denkaufgabe verlangte den Schülern viel Geduld ab.
nominative.english: This tricky brain teaser demanded a lot of patience from the students.
nominative.hint: Subject of verlangte ... ab, so nominative. Feminine nominative demonstrative diese; weak adjective ending -e on knifflige.

accusative.german: Der Lehrer stellte den Kindern eine spannende Denkaufgabe zum logischen Schließen.
accusative.english: The teacher gave the children an exciting cognitive task on logical reasoning.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stellte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on spannende.

dative.german: Bei dieser schwierigen Denkaufgabe rauchten den Teilnehmern förmlich die Köpfe.
dative.english: With this difficult thinking task the participants' heads were literally smoking.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on schwierigen.

genitive.german: Die Lösung der mathematischen Denkaufgabe fiel ihm nach einer kurzen Denkpause ein.
genitive.english: The solution to the mathematical problem came to him after a brief pause for thought.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Lösung. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on mathematischen; noun takes no ending.

die Denkaufgabe.proTip: All compounds ending in -aufgabe are feminine: die Aufgabe, die Hausaufgabe (homework), die Denkaufgabe. Idiom: jemandem eine Aufgabe stellen (to give someone a task).

die Bombe.note: Feminine noun of Italian/French origin meaning 'bomb' (explosive device). Feminine nouns take no endings in the singular: die, die, der, der Bombe. Plural: die Bomben.

nominative.german: Eine alte Bombe aus dem Zweiten Weltkrieg wurde gestern bei Bauarbeiten gefunden.
nominative.english: An old bomb from the Second World War was found yesterday during construction work.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... gefunden, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on alte.

accusative.german: Sprengstoffexperten entschärften die gefährliche Bombe am späten Abend erfolgreich.
accusative.english: Explosives experts successfully defused the dangerous bomb late in the evening.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entschärften, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on gefährliche.

dative.german: Bei einer unentdeckten Bombe besteht für Bauarbeiter stets akute Lebensgefahr.
dative.english: With an undiscovered bomb there is always acute mortal danger for construction workers.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on unentdeckten.

genitive.german: Die Detonation der Bombe riss einen tiefen Krater in den Erdboden.
genitive.english: The detonation of the bomb tore a deep crater into the ground.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Detonation. Feminine genitive article der; feminine noun Bombe takes no ending.

die Bombe.proTip: Colloquial German idiom: einschlagen wie eine Bombe (to have a sensational impact / create a huge stir); Bombenstimmung (fantastic atmosphere / great party mood); bombensicher (bombproof / completely safe).

das Schach.note: Neuter noun (from Persian shah = king) meaning 'chess' (board game). It declines for case: nominative/accusative das Schach, dative dem Schach, genitive des Schachs. Plural is not used.

nominative.german: Das königliche Schach erfordert strategische Weitsicht und tiefe Konzentration.
nominative.english: Royal chess requires strategic foresight and deep concentration.
nominative.hint: Subject of erfordert, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on königliche.

accusative.german: Mein Großvater brachte mir das anspruchsvolle Schach schon im Kindesalter bei.
accusative.english: My grandfather taught me demanding chess back in my childhood.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beibringen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on anspruchsvolle.

dative.german: Bei dem traditionellen Schach gelten auf Turnieren strenge Zeitregeln.
dative.english: In traditional chess strict time rules apply at tournaments.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on traditionellen.

genitive.german: Die Faszination des Schachs liegt in der unendlichen Vielfalt möglicher Züge.
genitive.english: The fascination of chess lies in the endless variety of possible moves.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Faszination. Neuter genitive article des; noun Schach adds genitive -s.

das Schach.proTip: Key game terms: Schach! (Check!), Schachmatt! (Checkmate!). Idioms: jemanden in Schach halten (to hold someone in check / keep someone under control); Schach spielen (to play chess — usually without an article).

aufgeben.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to give up, surrender, abandon' (or 'to check in baggage / post a letter'). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Aufgeben requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object. The examples below show case in sentences containing aufgeben.

nominative.german: Der erschöpfte Läufer gab das Rennen trotz aller Schmerzen niemals auf.
nominative.english: The exhausted runner never gave up the race despite all the pain.
nominative.hint: Subject of gab ... auf, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erschöpfte.

accusative.german: Sie wollte ihre lang gehegte Hoffnung auf Heilung nicht aufgeben.
accusative.english: She did not want to give up her long-cherished hope for a cure.
accusative.hint: Direct object of aufgeben, so accusative. Feminine possessive ihre; mixed adjective ending -e on gehegte.

dative.german: Nach dem bitteren Rückschlag gab der Unternehmer seine Pläne dennoch nicht auf.
dative.english: After the bitter setback the entrepreneur nevertheless did not give up his plans.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on bitteren.

genitive.german: Wegen des großen Drucks der Öffentlichkeit musste der Politiker sein Amt aufgeben.
genitive.english: Because of great public pressure the politician had to give up his office.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on großen; noun Druck adds -s.

aufgeben.proTip: Aufgeben is strong and separable: aufgeben – gab auf – hat aufgegeben (er gibt auf). Multiple meanings: 1. to give up (die Hoffnung aufgeben), 2. to assign homework (eine Aufgabe aufgeben), 3. to check in luggage (Gepäck aufgeben), 4. to post a letter/ad (einen Brief / eine Anzeige aufgeben).

begreifen.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix be- meaning 'to grasp, comprehend, fully understand'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Begreifen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was begreift man?).

nominative.german: Das kleine Kind begreift den Unterschied zwischen Richtig und Falsch erstaunlich früh.
nominative.english: The small child grasps the difference between right and wrong astonishingly early.
nominative.hint: Subject of begreift, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on kleine.

accusative.german: Ich kann diesen mathematischen Beweis einfach nicht begreifen.
accusative.english: I simply cannot comprehend this mathematical proof.
accusative.hint: Direct object of begreifen, so accusative. Masculine accusative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on mathematischen.

dative.german: Mit ihrem wachen Verstand half sie mir, das Phänomen zu begreifen.
dative.english: With her sharp mind she helped me comprehend the phenomenon.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative possessive ihrem; weak adjective ending -en on wachen.

genitive.german: Die Tiefe des Textes ist ohne Vorkenntnisse kaum zu begreifen.
genitive.english: The depth of the text is hardly comprehensible without prior knowledge.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Tiefe. Masculine genitive article des; noun Text adds genitive -es.

begreifen.proTip: Inseparable prefix be- never takes ge- in the past participle: begreifen – begriff – hat begriffen. Etymologically from greifen (to grasp with hands) -> begreifen (to grasp with the mind). Related noun: der Begriff (concept/term), schwer von Begriff sein (to be slow on the uptake).

kriegen.note: Weak verb meaning 'to get, receive, catch'. Colloquial in spoken German, corresponding to standard bekommen or erhalten. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline. Kriegen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was kriegt man?).

nominative.german: Der fleißige Junge kriegt zum Geburtstag ein neues Fahrrad.
nominative.english: The hardworking boy gets a new bicycle for his birthday.
nominative.hint: Subject of kriegt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on fleißige; Junge is a weak noun (n-noun).

accusative.german: Ich kriege diesen hartnäckigen Fleck einfach nicht aus dem Hemd.
accusative.english: I simply cannot get this stubborn stain out of the shirt.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kriege, so accusative. Masculine accusative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on hartnäckigen.

dative.german: Von meiner netten Kollegin kriege ich morgen die fehlenden Unterlagen.
dative.english: From my nice colleague I will get the missing documents tomorrow.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Feminine dative possessive meiner; weak adjective ending -en on netten.

genitive.german: Trotz des schlechten Wetters kriegte sie gute Laune bei dem Spaziergang.
genitive.english: Despite the bad weather she got into a good mood during the walk.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on schlechten; noun Wetter adds -s.

kriegen.proTip: Register alert: kriegen is very common in everyday spoken German, but should generally be replaced by bekommen or erhalten in formal writing. Idioms: jemanden zu fassen kriegen (to catch someone); einen Schreck kriegen (to get a fright); Ärger kriegen (to get into trouble).

schenken.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to give as a gift, present'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline. Schenken typically takes a nominative subject, a dative indirect object (the recipient: wem?), and an accusative direct object (the gift: was?).

nominative.german: Die Großmutter schenkt ihren Enkeln jedes Jahr tolle Bücher.
nominative.english: The grandmother gives her grandchildren great books every year as a present.
nominative.hint: Subject of schenkt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; noun Großmutter takes no ending.

accusative.german: Er schenkte seiner Freundin eine wunderschöne Halskette zum Jubiläum.
accusative.english: He gave his girlfriend a gorgeous necklace for their anniversary.
accusative.hint: Direct object (the gift) of schenkte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on wunderschöne.

dative.german: Wir schenken dem braven Hund einen saftigen Knochen zu Weihnachten.
dative.english: We give the well-behaved dog a juicy bone for Christmas.
dative.hint: Indirect object (the recipient) of schenken, so dative. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on braven.

genitive.german: Wegen des runden Geburtstags schenkten die Kollegen ihm einen Reisegutschein.
genitive.english: Because of the milestone birthday the colleagues gave him a travel voucher.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on runden; noun adds genitive -s.

schenken.proTip: Classic dative-accusative verb: jemanden (dative) etwas (accusative) schenken (to give someone something). Idioms: jemandem Glauben schenken (to believe someone / give credence to); geschenkt! (colloquial for 'never mind / forget about it!').

entspannen.note: Regular weak verb with inseparable prefix ent- meaning 'to relax, ease, unwind'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Often used reflexively: sich entspannen. Transitive use: etwas entspannen (to relax muscles/tensions). The examples show case on noun and pronoun phrases in sentences containing entspannen.

nominative.german: Der gestresste Manager entspannt sich am Wochenende im Garten.
nominative.english: The stressed manager relaxes in the garden on the weekend.
nominative.hint: Subject of entspannt sich, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on gestresste.

accusative.german: Ein warmes Schaumbad entspannt die verspannten Muskeln spürbar.
accusative.english: A warm bubble bath noticeably relaxes the tense muscles.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entspannt, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en; noun Muskeln ends in -n.

dative.german: Mit beruhigender Musik entspannte sie sich nach dem langen Arbeitstag.
dative.english: With soothing music she relaxed after the long workday.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on beruhigender; noun Musik takes no ending.

genitive.german: Das Ziel des entspannenden Urlaubs war die vollständige Erholung.
genitive.english: The goal of the relaxing vacation was complete recovery.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ziel. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on entspannenden; noun Urlaub adds genitive -s.

entspannen.proTip: Reflexive vs. non-reflexive: 'Ich entspanne mich' (I am relaxing) vs. 'Das entspannt meinen Nacken' (That relaxes my neck). Inseparable prefix ent- never takes ge- in the past participle: hat entspannt.

würfeln.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to roll dice' (in a game) or 'to dice' (cutting food into small cubes). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Intransitive in board games, transitive when cutting vegetables. Sentences demonstrate case on surrounding phrases.

nominative.german: Der jüngste Spieler würfelt immer als Erster in der Runde.
nominative.english: The youngest player always rolls the dice first in the round.
nominative.hint: Subject of würfelt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on jüngste.

accusative.german: Der Koch würfelt die geschälten Karotten in gleichmäßige Stücke.
accusative.english: The chef dices the peeled carrots into uniform pieces.
accusative.hint: Direct object of würfelt, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on geschälten.

dative.german: Mit einem glücklichen Wurf würfelte er eine rettende Sechs.
dative.english: With a lucky roll he rolled a saving six.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en on glücklichen.

genitive.german: Trotz des schlechten Würfelns gewann das Kind das spannende Brettspiel.
genitive.english: Despite the unlucky rolling of dice the child won the exciting board game.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on schlechten; nominalized infinitive Würfeln adds genitive -s.

würfeln.proTip: Famous quote attributed to Einstein: 'Gott würfelt nicht' (God does not play dice). The noun for die/dice is der Würfel (also meaning geometric cube).

fließen.note: Strong intransitive verb meaning 'to flow, run' (liquids, traffic, money). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Fließen takes a nominative subject and takes NO accusative direct object (it forms its perfect with sein: ist geflossen).

nominative.german: Der breite Fluss fließt ruhig durch das grüne Tal.
nominative.english: The wide river flows calmly through the green valley.
nominative.hint: Subject of fließt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on breite.

accusative.german: Ein Großteil des Gehalts fließt jeden Monat in die Miete.
accusative.english: A large part of the salary flows into rent every month.
accusative.hint: Subject of fließt, so nominative; masculine ein has no ending. Notice in die Miete is accusative showing direction.

dative.german: Das Wasser fließt aus einem tiefen Brunnen im Dorfzentrum.
dative.english: The water flows from a deep well in the village center.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus, which always requires dative. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en on tiefen.

genitive.german: Die Geschwindigkeit des fließenden Wassers trieb die alte Mühle an.
genitive.english: The speed of the flowing water powered the old mill.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Geschwindigkeit. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on fließenden; noun Wasser adds -s.

fließen.proTip: Strong verb forms: fließen – floss – ist geflossen (with double s in past, sharp ß in present: er fließt). Figurative expression: fließt in Strömen (is flowing in torrents / pouring down).

anziehen.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to put on / dress' (clothing) or 'to attract' (gravity, magnets, interest). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. In clothing contexts: sich (dative) etwas (accusative) anziehen. In attraction contexts: etwas/jemanden (accusative) anziehen.

nominative.german: Die besorgte Mutter zieht dem Kind eine warme Jacke an.
nominative.english: The worried mother puts a warm jacket on the child.
nominative.hint: Subject of zieht ... an, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on besorgte.

accusative.german: Der Magnet zieht den eisernen Nagel mühelos an.
accusative.english: The magnet attracts the iron nail effortlessly.
accusative.hint: Direct object of anziehen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on eisernen.

dative.german: Ich ziehe mir heute meinen neuen Wintermantel an.
dative.english: I am putting on my new winter coat today.
dative.hint: Dative reflexive pronoun indicating the beneficiary (on myself); meinen neuen Wintermantel is the accusative direct object.

genitive.german: Die Kraft des Anziehens hält die Planeten in ihren Umlaufbahnen.
genitive.english: The force of attraction keeps the planets in their orbits.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kraft. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Anziehen adds genitive -s.

anziehen.proTip: Vowel change and principal parts: anziehen – zog an – hat angezogen (er zieht an). Reflexive usage: 'Ich ziehe mich an' (I get dressed) vs. 'Ich ziehe mir den Pullover an' (I put on the sweater — note dative mir!).

nachgehen.note: Separable strong intransitive verb meaning 'to pursue, follow up on, investigate' (a clue/hobby) or 'to go slow' (of a watch). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Nachgehen strictly governs a DATIVE object (jemandem/einer Sache nachgehen).

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Kommissar geht jedem verdächtigen Hinweis sorgfältig nach.
nominative.english: The experienced detective follows up carefully on every suspicious clue.
nominative.hint: Subject of geht ... nach, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Wir müssen diesen ganzen Tag nutzen, um unseren Interessen nachzugehen.
accusative.english: We must use this whole day to pursue our interests.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long' with nutzen; nachzugehen in the infinitive clause governs the dative unseren Interessen.

dative.german: In den Ferien kann jeder endlich seinem geliebten Hobby nachgehen.
dative.english: In the holidays everyone can finally pursue their beloved hobby.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by nachgehen. Neuter dative possessive seinem; weak adjective ending -en on geliebten.

genitive.german: Das Nachgehen der Spuren erforderte die Mithilfe eines Spürhundes.
genitive.english: Following up on the tracks required the assistance of a tracking dog.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Mithilfe. Masculine genitive indefinite article eines; noun Spürhund adds genitive -es.

nachgehen.proTip: Verb government alert: nachgehen ALWAYS takes the dative: einer Beschäftigung nachgehen (to go about a job/occupation); einem Verdacht nachgehen (to investigate a suspicion). For clocks: 'Meine Uhr geht fünf Minuten nach' (My watch is 5 minutes slow).

festhalten.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to hold tight, grip firmly' or reflexively 'to hold on' (sich festhalten an + dative). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Festhalten takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was hält man fest?).

nominative.german: Der kleine Junge hielt den bunten Luftballon ganz fest.
nominative.english: The little boy held the colorful balloon very tightly.
nominative.hint: Subject of hielt ... fest, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on kleine; Junge is a weak noun (n-noun).

accusative.german: Bitte halte das Geländer beim Treppensteigen gut fest!
accusative.english: Please hold the handrail firmly when climbing stairs!
accusative.hint: Direct object of festhalten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; noun Geländer takes no ending.

dative.german: Die verängstigte Passagierin hielt sich an dem Sicherheitsgurt fest.
dative.english: The frightened passenger held on tightly to the seatbelt.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (two-way preposition showing location of grip). Masculine dative article dem; noun takes no ending.

genitive.german: Trotz des Festhaltens an alten Traditionen modernisierte die Firma ihre Technik.
genitive.english: Despite holding on to old traditions the company modernized its technology.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Festhalten adds genitive -s.

festhalten.proTip: Vowel change in present: ich halte fest, du hältst fest, er hält fest (strong: festhalten – hielt fest – hat festgehalten). Figurative idiom: an einer Meinung festhalten (to stick to / cling to an opinion).

beantworten.note: Regular weak transitive verb with inseparable prefix be- meaning 'to answer, reply to' (a question, email, letter). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Beantworten takes a nominative subject and requires an ACCUSATIVE direct object (die Frage beantworten).

nominative.german: Der Pressesprecher beantwortet alle kritischen Fragen der Journalisten sachlich.
nominative.english: The press spokesman answers all critical questions from journalists objectively.
nominative.hint: Subject of beantwortet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; noun Pressesprecher takes no ending.

accusative.german: Die Ministerin beantwortete den dringenden Brief der Bürgerinitiative sofort.
accusative.english: The minister answered the urgent letter from the citizens' initiative immediately.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beantwortete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on dringenden.

dative.german: Mit großer Ausführlichkeit beantwortete die Expertin die gestellte Aufgabe.
dative.english: With great detail the expert answered the set task.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on großer.

genitive.german: Die Frist des Beantwortens der Umfrage endet am kommenden Freitag.
genitive.english: The deadline for answering the survey ends next Friday.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Frist. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Beantworten adds genitive -s.

beantworten.proTip: Crucial distinction: beantworten is transitive and takes an accusative question (Ich beantworte deine Frage). Antworten takes a dative person or auf + accusative (Ich antworte dir / Ich antworte auf deine Frage). Never say 'Ich beantworte dir'!

ansteigen.note: Separable strong intransitive verb meaning 'to rise, increase, climb' (temperatures, prices, roads). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Ansteigen takes a nominative subject and takes NO accusative direct object (it forms its perfect with sein: ist angestiegen).

nominative.german: Die durchschnittliche Temperatur steigt im Sommer stetig an.
nominative.english: The average temperature rises steadily in summer.
nominative.hint: Subject of steigt ... an, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on durchschnittliche.

accusative.german: Die Wanderer spürten den steilen Anstieg, als der Weg ungemütlich anstieg.
accusative.english: The hikers felt the steep incline as the path rose uncomfortably.
accusative.hint: Direct object of spürten, so accusative; anstieg in the subordinate clause has the nominative subject der Weg.

dative.german: Bei stark ansteigendem Wasserstand sperrte die Feuerwehr die Uferstraße.
dative.english: With sharply rising water levels the fire brigade closed the riverside road.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on ansteigendem.

genitive.german: Wegen des stetigen Ansteigens der Rohstoffpreise mussten die Produkte verteuert werden.
genitive.english: Because of the steady rise in raw material prices the products had to be made more expensive.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on stetigen; nominalized verb adds -s.

ansteigen.proTip: Strong verb forms: ansteigen – stieg an – ist angestiegen (no vowel change in present: es steigt an). Related noun: der Anstieg (rise/increase). Contrast with sinken / fallen (to drop/fall).

antworten.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to reply, answer'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Antworten takes a nominative subject and a DATIVE person (wem antwortet man?), and takes auf + accusative for the topic (auf die Frage antworten).

nominative.german: Der Schüler antwortet der Lehrerin stets höflich und präzise.
nominative.english: The student always replies to the teacher politely and precisely.
nominative.hint: Subject of antwortet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; noun Schüler takes no ending.

accusative.german: Er antwortete sofort auf die wichtige E-Mail seines Vorgesetzten.
accusative.english: He replied immediately to the important email from his superior.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition auf. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on wichtige.

dative.german: Sie antwortete dem neugierigen Journalisten nur mit einem knappen Lächeln.
dative.english: She replied to the curious journalist with only a terse smile.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by antworten (to whom). Masculine dative article dem; weak noun Journalist takes -en.

genitive.german: Das Zögern des Antwortenden verriet seine große Unsicherheit.
genitive.english: The respondent's hesitation betrayed his great insecurity.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing possession after Zögern. Masculine genitive des; adjectival noun Antwortender takes weak ending -en.

antworten.proTip: Antworten + dative person: 'Ich antworte dir' (I answer you). For the matter answered: 'Ich antworte auf deine Frage' (I reply to your question). Do not confuse with transitive beantworten: 'Ich beantworte deine Frage'.

strömen.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to stream, flow, pour, flock' (liquids, crowd of people, air). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Strömen takes a nominative subject and forms its perfect tense with sein: ist geströmt.

nominative.german: Das kalte Wasser strömt mit hoher Geschwindigkeit aus dem Rohr.
nominative.english: The cold water streams out of the pipe at high speed.
nominative.hint: Subject of strömt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on kalte.

accusative.german: Tausende begeisterte Fans strömten den ganzen Nachmittag in das Stadion.
accusative.english: Thousands of enthusiastic fans streamed into the stadium the whole afternoon.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; strömten is intransitive with the prepositional phrase in das Stadion (accusative of direction).

dative.german: Aus dem brennenden Gebäude strömte dicker schwarzer Rauch.
dative.english: Thick black smoke streamed out of the burning building.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on brennenden.

genitive.german: Das Rauschen des strömenden Regens wiegte das Kind in den Schlaf.
genitive.english: The rushing sound of the pouring rain lulled the child to sleep.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Rauschen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on strömenden; noun Regen adds -s.

strömen.proTip: Used for liquids ('Der Regen strömt'), air/gases ('Gas strömt aus'), and crowds of people ('Massen strömten auf den Platz'). Perfect with sein: 'Die Menschen sind ins Kino geströmt'.

spüren.note: Regular weak transitive verb meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive' (physical sensation or intuitive perception). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Spüren requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was spürt man?).

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Bergführer spürt den nahenden Wetterumschwung schon frühzeitig.
nominative.english: The experienced mountain guide senses the approaching change in weather early on.
nominative.hint: Subject of spürt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Ich spüre eine leichte Besserung meiner Erkältungssymptome.
accusative.english: I feel a slight improvement in my cold symptoms.
accusative.hint: Direct object of spüre, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on leichte.

dative.german: Mit feinen Sinnen spürte der Jagdhund die Beute im Gebüsch auf.
dative.english: With keen senses the hunting dog detected the prey in the bushes.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension plural: dative plural takes ending -en on feinen; noun Sinn adds -en in dative plural.

genitive.german: Trotz des tauben Gefühls spürte der Patient die Berührung der Nadel.
genitive.english: Despite the numb feeling the patient felt the touch of the needle.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on tauben; noun Gefühl adds -s.

spüren.proTip: Distinguish spüren (to physically/intuitively sense: Ich spüre Schmerz / den Wind) from fühlen (more emotional: Ich fühle mich glücklich). Collocation: am eigenen Leib spüren (to feel firsthand / experience the hard way).

herrschen.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to rule, reign' (over a country) or 'to prevail, exist widespread' (silence, chaos, cold). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. For ruling: herrschen über + accusative. For prevailing: an intransitive use taking a nominative subject.

nominative.german: Ein weiser König herrschte viele Jahrzehnte lang über das wohlhabende Reich.
nominative.english: A wise king ruled over the prosperous empire for many decades.
nominative.hint: Subject of herrschte, so nominative. Mixed declension: masculine ein has no ending; weiser takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Der grausame Herrscher regierte das Volk und herrschte über das gesamte Territorium.
accusative.english: The cruel ruler governed the people and ruled over the entire territory.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by über in the sense of ruling over. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on gesamte.

dative.german: In diesem abgelegenen Bergdorf herrscht eine absolute Stille.
dative.english: In this remote mountain village an absolute silence prevails.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on abgelegenen.

genitive.german: Während des strengen Herrschens der Militärjunta gab es keine Pressefreiheit.
genitive.english: During the strict rule of the military junta there was no freedom of the press.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by während. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on strengen; nominalized verb adds -s.

herrschen.proTip: Very common in the sense of 'to prevail / exist': Es herrscht Chaos (Chaos reigns / prevails); Es herrscht Stille (Silence prevails); Hier herrscht Rauchverbot (Smoking is prohibited here). Noun: der Herrscher.

explodieren.note: Regular verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to explode, detonate, burst violently'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Explodieren is intransitive: it takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with sein: ist explodiert.

nominative.german: Die alte Gasflasche explodierte plötzlich im Keller des Hauses.
nominative.english: The old gas cylinder suddenly exploded in the basement of the house.
nominative.hint: Subject of explodierte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on alte.

accusative.german: Die Schaulustigen beobachteten den ganzen Abend, wie Feuerwerkskörper am Himmel explodierten.
accusative.english: The onlookers watched the whole evening as fireworks exploded in the sky.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; explodierten in the subordinate clause is intransitive.

dative.german: Bei einer explodierenden Bombe entsteht eine gewaltige Druckwelle.
dative.english: With an exploding bomb a tremendous blast wave is produced.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on explodierenden.

genitive.german: Die gewaltige Wucht des explodierten Sprengstoffs zerstörte die Brücke.
genitive.english: The tremendous force of the exploded explosive destroyed the bridge.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wucht. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on explodierten; noun adds -s.

explodieren.proTip: Verbs in -ieren never take ge- in the past participle: explodieren – explodierte – ist explodiert. Figurative use: Die Preise explodieren (Prices are skyrocketing/exploding); Er ist vor Wut explodiert (He blew his top with anger).

stören.note: Regular weak transitive verb meaning 'to disturb, interrupt, bother, annoy'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Stören takes a nominative subject and requires an ACCUSATIVE direct object (wen oder was stört man?).

nominative.german: Der laute Straßenlärm stört meine Konzentration bei der Arbeit.
nominative.english: The loud traffic noise disturbs my concentration at work.
nominative.hint: Subject of stört, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on laute.

accusative.german: Bitte stören Sie den schlafenden Patienten jetzt nicht!
accusative.english: Please do not disturb the sleeping patient now!
accusative.hint: Direct object of stören, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak noun Patient adds -en.

dative.german: An diesem unpassenden Verhalten störten sich viele Gäste des Hotels.
dative.english: Many guests of the hotel took offense at this inappropriate behavior.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an in the reflexive idiom sich stören an + dative (to be bothered by / take offense at).

genitive.german: Wegen des ständigen Störens durch den Schüler schickte der Lehrer ihn vor die Tür.
genitive.english: Because of the student's constant disruption the teacher sent him outside.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ständigen; nominalized verb adds -s.

stören.proTip: Reflexive pattern: sich stören an + dative means 'to be bothered by': Ich störe mich nicht daran (I don't mind that). Polite phrase: 'Störe ich?' (Am I disturbing you? / Do you have a moment?).

schleudern.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to hurl, fling, fling away' (transitive) or 'to skid, spin out of control' (intransitive, of vehicles). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Sentences demonstrate case on accompanying phrases.

nominative.german: Der wütende Riese schleuderte einen gewaltigen Felsbrocken ins Meer.
nominative.english: The angry giant hurled a huge boulder into the sea.
nominative.hint: Subject of schleuderte, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on wütende; Riese is a weak noun.

accusative.german: Der Vulkan schleuderte glühende Asche kilometerweit in die Luft.
accusative.english: The volcano hurled glowing ash kilometers high into the air.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schleuderte, so accusative. Feminine accusative without an article: strong ending -e on glühende.

dative.german: Auf der vereisten Fahrbahn geriet der Wagen plötzlich ins Schleudern.
dative.english: On the iced-over roadway the car suddenly started skidding.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on vereisten.

genitive.german: Die Fliehkräfte des schnellen Schleuderns pressten die Fahrer in die Sitze.
genitive.english: The centrifugal forces of the rapid spinning pressed the drivers into their seats.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Fliehkräfte. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on schnellen; noun adds -s.

schleudern.proTip: Dual meaning: 1. to throw violently (Steine schleudern); 2. to skid/spin (Das Auto schleuderte in den Graben). Also used for washing machines: die Schleuder / Wäsche schleudern (to spin-dry laundry).

quetschen.note: Regular weak transitive verb meaning 'to squeeze, crush, bruise' (an object or body part). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Quetschen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (was quetscht man?). Reflexively: sich (dative) den Finger quetschen.

nominative.german: Die schwere Eisentür quetschte ihm den Daumen beim Zufallen.
nominative.english: The heavy iron door crushed his thumb as it slammed shut.
nominative.hint: Subject of quetschte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on schwere.

accusative.german: Er hat sich gestern den linken Zeigefinger in der Schublade gequetscht.
accusative.english: He pinched his left index finger in the drawer yesterday.
accusative.hint: Direct object (body part) of gequetscht, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on linken.

dative.german: Mit einer mechanischen Presse quetschte der Bauer den Saft aus den Äpfeln.
dative.english: With a mechanical press the farmer squeezed the juice from the apples.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on mechanischen.

genitive.german: Die Folgen des schmerzhaften Quetschens waren blaue Flecken an der Hand.
genitive.english: The consequences of the painful bruising were blue bruises on the hand.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on schmerzhaften; noun adds -s.

quetschen.proTip: Common reflexive pattern with body parts: sich (dative) den Finger / den Fuß quetschen (to pinch/crush one's finger/foot). Idiom: sich in die Bahn quetschen (to squeeze/crowd into the train).

verlassen.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to leave, depart from, abandon' (a place, a partner). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Verlassen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object. Reflexively: sich verlassen auf + accusative (to rely on).

nominative.german: Der letzte Fahrgast verlässt den Zug am Endbahnhof.
nominative.english: The last passenger leaves the train at the terminus station.
nominative.hint: Subject of verlässt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on letzte.

accusative.german: Viele junge Menschen verlassen ihr heimatliches Dorf für eine Ausbildung in der Stadt.
accusative.english: Many young people leave their native village for an apprenticeship in the city.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verlassen, so accusative. Neuter possessive ihr has no ending; heimatliches takes strong ending -es.

dative.german: Auf meinen besten Freund kann ich mich in jeder Notlage blind verlassen.
dative.english: I can rely blindly on my best friend in any emergency.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (state). Feminine dative determiner jeder; noun Notlage takes no ending.

genitive.german: Wegen des überstürzten Verlassens der Wohnung vergaß er seinen Haustürschlüssel.
genitive.english: Because of hastily leaving the apartment he forgot his front door key.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on überstürzten; nominalized verb adds -s.

verlassen.proTip: Strong verb forms: verlassen – verließ – hat verlassen (vowel change in present: er verlässt). Reflexive idiom: sich verlassen auf + accusative = to rely/depend on: 'Auf mich kannst du dich verlassen' (You can count on me).

schweben.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to hover, float, glide' (in air or water without sinking). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Schweben takes a nominative subject and takes NO accusative direct object. Forms perfect with sein (or haben when emphasizing state).

nominative.german: Eine weiße Wolke schwebt langsam über den Berggipfel.
nominative.english: A white cloud hovers slowly over the mountain peak.
nominative.hint: Subject of schwebt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on weiße.

accusative.german: Die Raumsonde schwebte den weiten Weg durch die Schwerelosigkeit völlig geräuschlos.
accusative.english: The space probe drifted the long way through weightlessness completely silently.
accusative.hint: Accusative of distance/path traversed answering 'which way / how far'; schweben itself is intransitive.

dative.german: In eisiger Höhe schwebte der Adler lautlos im Aufwind.
dative.english: At an icy height the eagle soared silently in the updraft.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on eisiger.

genitive.german: Der Zauber des lautlosen Schwebens faszinierte die Zuschauer im Zirkus.
genitive.english: The magic of silent hovering fascinated the spectators in the circus.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zauber. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on lautlosen; noun adds -s.

schweben.proTip: Common idioms: auf Wolke sieben schweben (to be on cloud nine / deeply in love); in Lebensgefahr schweben (to be in mortal danger); im Ungewissen schweben (to be up in the air / uncertain).

heizen.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to heat' (a room/building) or colloquially 'to drive very fast / speed'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Transitive: eine Wohnung heizen (accusative object). Intransitive: mit Gas heizen (to heat with gas).

nominative.german: Die moderne Wärmepumpe heizt das gesamte Haus äußerst energieeffizient.
nominative.english: The modern heat pump heats the entire house extremely energy-efficiently.
nominative.hint: Subject of heizt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on moderne.

accusative.german: Wir heizen das große Wohnzimmer im Winter nur mit Holz.
accusative.english: We only heat the large living room with wood in winter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of heizen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on große.

dative.german: Mit umweltfreundlicher Fernwärme heizen immer mehr Bürger ihre Wohnungen.
dative.english: With environmentally friendly district heating more and more citizens heat their apartments.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on umweltfreundlicher.

genitive.german: Die hohen Kosten des Heizens belasten viele Familien in der kalten Jahreszeit.
genitive.english: The high cost of heating burdens many families in the cold season.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Heizen adds genitive -s.

heizen.proTip: Related noun: die Heizung (the heating system / radiator). Colloquial slang meaning: über die Autobahn heizen (to tear down / speed down the autobahn).

betreffen.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix be- meaning 'to concern, affect, relate to'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Betreffen takes a nominative subject and requires an ACCUSATIVE direct object (wen oder was betrifft es?).

nominative.german: Die neue Gesetzgebung betrifft alle mittelständischen Unternehmen im Land.
nominative.english: The new legislation affects all medium-sized enterprises in the country.
nominative.hint: Subject of betrifft, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

accusative.german: Diese wichtige Entscheidung betrifft jeden einzelnen Mitarbeiter der Abteilung.
accusative.english: This important decision affects every single employee of the department.
accusative.hint: Direct object of betrifft, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner jeden; weak adjective ending -en on einzelnen.

dative.german: In diesem konkreten Fall betrifft die Änderung nur Personen mit doppeltem Wohnsitz.
dative.english: In this specific case the change concerns only persons with dual residence.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location/situation). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on konkreten.

genitive.german: Die Frage des Betroffenseins hängt von den individuellen Lebensumständen ab.
genitive.english: The question of being affected depends on individual life circumstances.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Frage. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized phrase adds genitive -s.

betreffen.proTip: Strong verb forms: betreffen – betraf – hat betroffen (vowel change in present: es betrifft). Common idioms: was mich betrifft (as far as I am concerned); die betroffene Person (the person affected / concerned).

folgen.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to follow' (physically or logically). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Folgen strictly governs a DATIVE object (jemandem/einer Sache folgen) and forms its perfect with sein: ist gefolgt.

nominative.german: Der treue Hund folgt seinem Besitzer auf Schritt und Tritt.
nominative.english: The faithful dog follows its owner every step of the way.
nominative.hint: Subject of folgt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on treue.

accusative.german: Die Touristen folgten den ganzen Tag den Anweisungen des Bergführers.
accusative.english: The tourists followed the mountain guide's instructions the whole day.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; the verb folgten governs the dative object den Anweisungen.

dative.german: Wir folgen dem erfahrenen Reiseleiter durch die engen Gassen.
dative.english: We follow the experienced tour guide through the narrow alleys.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by folgen (jemandem folgen). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on erfahrenen.

genitive.german: Infolge des Nichtbeachtens der Regeln verirrte sich die Gruppe.
genitive.english: As a result of failing to observe the rules the group lost its way.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by infolge. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized verb adds genitive -s.

folgen.proTip: Crucial rule: folgen ALWAYS takes dative (jemandem folgen, NOT 'jemanden folgen'): 'Ich folge dir' (I follow you). Perfect with sein: 'Ich bin ihm gefolgt'. Figurative: aus etwas folgen (to result from something).

zerfallen.note: Strong intransitive verb with inseparable prefix zer- meaning 'to disintegrate, decay, fall to pieces'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Zerfallen takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with sein: ist zerfallen.

nominative.german: Die alte Burgmauer zerfällt nach vielen Jahrhunderten allmählich zu Staub.
nominative.english: The old castle wall gradually disintegrates into dust after many centuries.
nominative.hint: Subject of zerfällt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on alte.

accusative.german: Der Wissenschaftler untersuchte den schnellen Zerfall des radioaktiven Elements.
accusative.english: The scientist investigated the rapid decay of the radioactive element.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on schnellen.

dative.german: In diesem zerfallenen Gebäude darf niemand mehr wohnen.
dative.english: No one is allowed to live in this dilapidated building anymore.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on past participle zerfallenen.

genitive.german: Wegen des fortschreitenden Zerfallens des Denkmals wurde der Platz gesperrt.
genitive.english: Because of the advancing disintegration of the monument the square was closed.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on fortschreitenden; nominalized infinitive Zerfallen adds -s.

zerfallen.proTip: Principal parts: zerfallen – zerfiel – ist zerfallen (3rd person singular: es zerfällt). The prefix zer- always indicates destruction or separation into parts (zerreißen, zerstören, zerbrechen).

verschlingen.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to devour, gulp down, swallow whole' (food, or figuratively books/money). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Verschlingen takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object.

nominative.german: Das hungrige Raubtier verschlingt die gefangene Beute in wenigen Minuten.
nominative.english: The hungry predator devours the captured prey in a few minutes.
nominative.hint: Subject of verschlingt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on hungrige.

accusative.german: Der Schüler verschlang den spannenden Abenteuerroman an einem einzigen Abend.
accusative.english: The student devoured the exciting adventure novel in a single evening.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verschlang, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on spannenden.

dative.german: Mit unersättlichem Appetit verschlang der Hund das Fleisch aus dem Napf.
dative.english: With insatiable appetite the dog devoured the meat from the bowl.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes ending -em on unersättlichem.

genitive.german: Die Gefahr des Verschlingens durch wilde Bestien ängstigte die Forscher.
genitive.english: The danger of being devoured by wild beasts frightened the researchers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gefahr. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verschlingen adds genitive -s.

verschlingen.proTip: Principal parts: verschlingen – verschlang – hat verschlungen. Figurative usage: 'Sie hat das Buch verschlungen' (She devoured the book / read it avidly); 'Das Projekt verschlingt Unmengen an Geld' (The project eats up huge sums of money).

erleuchten.note: Regular weak transitive verb with inseparable prefix er- meaning 'to illuminate, light up' (physically or spiritually/intellectually). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Erleuchten requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas erleuchten).

nominative.german: Der helle Mondschein erleuchtet den nächtlichen Waldweg.
nominative.english: The bright moonlight illuminates the nighttime forest path.
nominative.hint: Subject of erleuchtet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on helle.

accusative.german: Hunderte Kerzen erleuchteten den prächtigen Festsaal im Schloss.
accusative.english: Hundreds of candles illuminated the magnificent banquet hall in the castle.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erleuchteten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on prächtigen.

dative.german: Mit warmem Licht erleuchtete die kleine Lampe das gemütliche Zimmer.
dative.english: With warm light the small lamp illuminated the cozy room.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on warmem.

genitive.german: Während des Erleuchtens des Weihnachtsbaums sangen alle Kinder ein Lied.
genitive.english: During the lighting up of the Christmas tree all the children sang a song.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by während. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Erleuchten adds genitive -s.

erleuchten.proTip: Weak verb: erleuchten – erleuchtete – hat erleuchtet. Root leuchten means 'to shine' (intransitive), whereas prefix er- makes it transitive: 'Die Lampe leuchtet' vs. 'Die Lampe erleuchtet den Raum'. Noun: die Erleuchtung (illumination / enlightenment).

vorfinden.note: Separable strong transitive verb meaning 'to find on arrival, discover upon reaching a place'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Vorfinden requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas vorfinden).

nominative.german: Die neuen Mieter fanden eine völlig renovierte Wohnung vor.
nominative.english: The new tenants found a completely renovated apartment upon arrival.
nominative.hint: Subject of fanden ... vor, so nominative plural. Plural nominative article die; weak adjective ending -en on neuen.

accusative.german: Der Ermittler fand am Tatort einen entscheidenden Hinweis vor.
accusative.english: The investigator found a crucial clue at the crime scene.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vorfinden, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on entscheidenden.

dative.german: Bei unserer späten Ankunft fanden wir das Hotel verschlossen vor.
dative.english: Upon our late arrival we found the hotel locked.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative possessive unserer; weak adjective ending -en on späten.

genitive.german: Trotz des Vorfindens vieler Dokumente blieb der Fall vorerst ungelöst.
genitive.english: Despite finding many documents the case remained unsolved for now.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Vorfinden adds genitive -s.

vorfinden.proTip: Conjugation: vorfinden – fand vor – hat vorgefunden (er findet vor). Used specifically when coming to a place and seeing what state it is in: 'Wir fanden das Haus verlassen vor' (We found the house deserted upon our arrival).

anlocken.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 'to lure, entice, attract' (animals with food, customers with discounts). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Anlocken requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden/etwas anlocken).

nominative.german: Der süße Duft frischer Blumen lockt viele Bienen an.
nominative.english: The sweet scent of fresh flowers attracts many bees.
nominative.hint: Subject of lockt ... an, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on süße.

accusative.german: Das Geschäft lockte einen neuen Kunden mit verlockenden Rabatten an.
accusative.english: The shop attracted a new customer with enticing discounts.
accusative.hint: Direct object of anlocken, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; weak adjective ending -en on neuen; Kunde is a weak noun (n-noun: den Kunden).

dative.german: Mit frischem Futter lockte der Bauer die scheuen Hühner in den Stall.
dative.english: With fresh feed the farmer lured the shy chickens into the coop.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on frischem.

genitive.german: Das Ziel des Anlockens von Touristen war die Belebung der Wirtschaft.
genitive.english: The goal of attracting tourists was reviving the economy.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ziel. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Anlocken adds genitive -s.

anlocken.proTip: Separable weak verb: anlocken – lockte an – hat angelockt. Related words: der Köder (bait), anziehend (attractive). Difference: anlocken implies using bait or a deliberate enticement, while anziehen can be passive/physical attraction.

verwirren.note: Regular weak transitive verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to confuse, bewilder, disorient' (a person or thoughts). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Verwirren requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden verwirren).

nominative.german: Die komplizierte Wegbeschreibung verwirrt die ausländischen Gäste.
nominative.english: The complicated directions confuse the foreign guests.
nominative.hint: Subject of verwirrt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on komplizierte.

accusative.german: Diese widersprüchlichen Aussagen verwirrten den vorsichtigen Richter.
accusative.english: These contradictory statements confused the cautious judge.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verwirrten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on vorsichtigen.

dative.german: Mit einer überraschenden Frage verwirrte die Schülerin den Lehrer völlig.
dative.english: With a surprise question the female student completely confused the teacher.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on überraschenden.

genitive.german: Die Absicht des Verwirrens der gegnerischen Mannschaft gelang perfekt.
genitive.english: The intention of confusing the opposing team succeeded perfectly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Absicht. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verwirren adds genitive -s.

verwirren.proTip: Regular forms: verwirren – verwirrte – hat verwirrt (past participle verwirrt is also used as an adjective: 'Ich bin verwirrt' = I am confused). Related noun: die Verwirrung (confusion).

angreifen.note: Separable strong transitive verb meaning 'to attack, assault' (physically, verbally, or militarily). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Angreifen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden/etwas angreifen).

nominative.german: Das wilde Tier greift die Wanderer im Wald plötzlich an.
nominative.english: The wild animal suddenly attacks the hikers in the forest.
nominative.hint: Subject of greift ... an, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on wilde.

accusative.german: Die gegnerische Armee griff die befestigte Stadt im Morgengrauen an.
accusative.english: The opposing army attacked the fortified city at dawn.
accusative.hint: Direct object of angreifen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on befestigte.

dative.german: Nach einem überraschenden Angriff zog sich der Feind schnell zurück.
dative.english: After a surprise attack the enemy quickly retreated.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on überraschenden.

genitive.german: Die Verteidiger rechneten mit der Gefahr des Angreifens durch die Rebellen.
genitive.english: The defenders reckoned with the danger of an attack by the rebels.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gefahr. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Angreifen adds genitive -s.

angreifen.proTip: Principal parts: angreifen – griff an – hat angegriffen (er greift an). Figurative use: 'Die Säure greift das Metall an' (The acid corrodes the metal); 'Das hat seine Gesundheit stark angegriffen' (That took a heavy toll on his health).

sich aneignen.note: Separable reflexive verb meaning 'to acquire, master, pick up' (knowledge, skills, or habits). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Grammatically, the reflexive pronoun is DATIVE (sich etwas aneignen), while the acquired skill or item is the ACCUSATIVE direct object.

nominative.german: Der fleißige Student eignet sich die neue Sprache in wenigen Monaten an.
nominative.english: The hardworking student acquires the new language in a few months.
nominative.hint: Subject of eignet ... an, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on fleißige.

accusative.german: Sie hat sich fundiertes Wissen über die deutsche Grammatik angeeignet.
accusative.english: She has acquired in-depth knowledge of German grammar.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sich aneignen, so accusative. Strong declension without an article: neuter accusative takes strong ending -es on fundiertes.

dative.german: Ich eigne mir diese nützliche Fertigkeit durch tägliches Üben an.
dative.english: I acquire this useful skill through daily practice.
dative.hint: Dative reflexive pronoun indicating the beneficiary (to myself). In sich aneignen, the person is in the dative (mir/dir/sich/uns/euch/sich).

genitive.german: Der Prozess des Aneignens einer Fremdsprache erfordert viel Geduld.
genitive.english: The process of acquiring a foreign language requires a lot of patience.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Prozess. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Aneignen adds genitive -s.

sich aneignen.proTip: Watch the pronoun case! The reflexivpronomen is DATIVE because the skill is the accusative direct object: 'Ich eigne MIR (dat) Deutsch (akk) an', 'Du eignest DIR (dat) Wissen an'. Never say 'Ich eigne mich an'!

erkennen.note: Mixed verb with inseparable prefix er- meaning 'to recognise, identify, perceive' (a person, sign, truth). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Erkennen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden/etwas erkennen), often combined with an + dative (erkennen an + dat).

nominative.german: Der alte Lehrer erkennt seine ehemaligen Schüler sofort an der Stimme.
nominative.english: The old teacher recognizes his former students immediately by their voice.
nominative.hint: Subject of erkennt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on alte.

accusative.german: Ich erkannte meinen alten Schulfreund trotz der langen Trennung auf Anhieb.
accusative.english: I recognized my old school friend immediately despite the long separation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erkannte, so accusative. Masculine accusative possessive meinen; weak adjective ending -en on alten.

dative.german: Man erkennt den echten Diamanten an seiner außergewöhnlichen Härte.
dative.english: One recognizes the real diamond by its exceptional hardness.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition an (recognize by). Feminine dative possessive seiner; weak adjective ending -en on außergewöhnlichen.

genitive.german: Das Problem des Nicht-Erkennens der Symptome führte zu Komplikationen.
genitive.english: The problem of failing to recognize the symptoms led to complications.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Problem. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized verb adds genitive -s.

erkennen.proTip: Mixed verb forms: erkennen – erkannte – hat erkannt (present: er erkennt). Key preposition pattern: jemanden/etwas an (+ Dativ) erkennen: 'Woran hast du ihn erkannt? – An seiner Stimme!'

kosten.note: Regular weak verb meaning 'to cost' (require payment, effort, lives) or 'to taste/sample' (food). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. In modern German, kosten usually takes an accusative person and an accusative amount (etwas kostet jemanden [akk] etwas [akk]), though dative person is also seen in colloquial regional usage.

nominative.german: Das neue Smartphone kostet mehrere hundert Euro im Geschäft.
nominative.english: The new smartphone costs several hundred euros in the shop.
nominative.hint: Subject of kostet, so nominative. Neuter nominative article das; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

accusative.german: Diese unüberlegte Entscheidung kostete den jungen Mann viel Geld.
accusative.english: This rash decision cost the young man a lot of money.
accusative.hint: Direct personal object of kostete, taking accusative in standard German. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on jungen.

dative.german: Bei so hohen Kosten überlegen sich viele Kunden den Kauf gründlich.
dative.english: With such high costs many customers reconsider the purchase thoroughly.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Plural dative takes ending -en on adjective hohen; noun Kosten is plural-only (Pluraletantum).

genitive.german: Die Begleichung der Kosten des Aufenthalts erfolgte über die Kreditkarte.
genitive.english: Settlement of the costs of the stay took place via credit card.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Begleichung. Plural genitive article der; noun Kosten takes no additional ending.

kosten.proTip: Double accusative in standard German: 'Das kostet mich (akk) einen Euro (akk)' (though colloquially 'Das kostet mir' is sometimes heard, standard Duden grammar prefers the accusative). Also means 'to taste/sample': 'Darf ich mal kosten?'

betragen.note: Strong verb with inseparable prefix be- meaning 'to amount to, total' (numbers, prices, distances) or reflexively sich betragen ('to behave'). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. In the mathematical sense, betragen takes a nominative subject and an accusative measure/amount.

nominative.german: Die monatliche Miete für das Apartment beträgt achthundert Euro.
nominative.english: The monthly rent for the apartment amounts to eight hundred euros.
nominative.hint: Subject of beträgt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on monatliche.

accusative.german: Die Gesamtsumme der Rechnung beträgt einen beträchtlichen Betrag.
accusative.english: The grand total of the bill amounts to a considerable sum.
accusative.hint: Accusative complement specifying the amount after beträgt. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on beträchtlichen.

dative.german: Bei einem Betrag von über tausend Euro ist eine Ratenzahlung möglich.
dative.english: For an amount exceeding one thousand euros payment by installments is possible.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; noun Betrag takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die Überprüfung des genauen Betragens der Differenz dauerte zwei Tage.
genitive.english: The verification of the exact amount of the difference took two days.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Überprüfung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on genauen; nominalized verb adds -s.

betragen.proTip: Strong verb forms: betragen – betrug – hat betragen (er beträgt with umlaut!). Common synonyms: sich belaufen auf (+ akk), ausmachen. In older/formal language, sich betragen means 'to behave' (noun: das Betragen = conduct/behavior).

beweisen.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix be- meaning 'to prove, demonstrate, establish' (innocence, guilt, a theory). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Beweisen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas/jemandem etwas beweisen) or a dass-clause.

nominative.german: Der engagierte Anwalt beweist die Unschuld seines Mandanten vor Gericht.
nominative.english: The dedicated lawyer proves the innocence of his client in court.
nominative.hint: Subject of beweist, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on engagierte.

accusative.german: Die Zeugenaussage bewies den mutmaßlichen Tathergang zweifelsfrei.
accusative.english: The witness testimony proved the suspected course of events beyond doubt.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bewies, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on mutmaßlichen.

dative.german: Mit stichhaltigen Argumenten bewies die Forscherin ihre kühne Hypothese.
dative.english: With sound arguments the researcher proved her bold hypothesis.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural dative takes ending -en on adjective stichhaltigen and noun Argumenten.

genitive.german: Wegen des Fehlens eines klaren Beweises wurde der Angeklagte freigesprochen.
genitive.english: Because of the lack of a clear proof the accused was acquitted.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by the noun Fehlens. Masculine genitive article eines; mixed adjective ending -en on klaren; noun Beweis adds -es.

beweisen.proTip: Strong verb: beweisen – bewies – hat bewiesen (er beweist). Dative beneficiary possible: 'Er hat mir seine Treue bewiesen' (He proved his loyalty to me). Noun: der Beweis (proof/evidence).

isolieren.note: Regular weak verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to isolate, insulate' (electrical wire, buildings against heat/cold, patients). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Isolieren takes a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas/jemanden isolieren).

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Handwerker isoliert das gesamte Dachgeschoss fachgerecht.
nominative.english: The experienced craftsman insulates the entire attic professionally.
nominative.hint: Subject of isoliert, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Die Arbeiter isolierten das freiliegende Stromkabel sorgfältig.
accusative.english: The workers insulated the exposed power cable carefully.
accusative.hint: Direct object of isolierten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on freiliegende.

dative.german: Mit speziellem Dämmmaterial isolierte der Bauherr die kalte Außenwand.
dative.english: With special insulation material the builder insulated the cold exterior wall.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on speziellem.

genitive.german: Die Kosten des Isolierens alter Wohnhäuser amortisieren sich rasch.
genitive.english: The costs of insulating old residential houses pay off quickly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Isolieren adds genitive -s.

isolieren.proTip: Weak verb in -ieren: isolieren – isolierte – hat isoliert (no ge- prefix!). Dual meaning: physical thermal/electrical insulation (das Rohr isolieren) and social/medical quarantine/isolation (den Patienten isolieren).

gelten.note: Strong intransitive verb meaning 'to be valid, apply, count' (rules, tickets, laws) or 'to be considered as' (gelten als + nominative). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Gelten takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and commonly governs für + accusative or a dative person.

nominative.german: Dieser ermäßigte Fahrschein gilt für alle öffentlichen Verkehrsmittel der Stadt.
nominative.english: This discounted ticket is valid for all public transport in the city.
nominative.hint: Subject of gilt, so nominative. Masculine nominative determiner Dieser; weak adjective ending -e on ermäßigte.

accusative.german: Die neuen Vorschriften gelten für den gesamten Betrieb ab nächster Woche.
