accusative.english: The new regulations apply to the entire company starting next week.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition für. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

dative.german: Sein freundliches Lächeln galt der jungen Dame an der Kasse.
dative.english: His friendly smile was meant for the young lady at the checkout.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by gelten (jemandem gelten = to be aimed at / meant for someone). Feminine dative article der.

genitive.german: Die Dauer des Geltens der behördlichen Verordnung beträgt sechs Monate.
genitive.english: The duration of validity of the official ordinance is six months.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Dauer. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Gelten adds genitive -s.

gelten.proTip: Stem change: gelten – galt – hat gegolten (er/sie/es GILT). Construction note: 'gelten als' takes NOMINATIVE (predicate noun): 'Er gilt als ein fähiger Arzt' (not accusative!). 'Gelten für' takes accusative: 'Das gilt für dich'.

hungern.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to go hungry, starve' (or figuratively 'to yearn/crave': hungern nach + dative). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Hungern takes a nominative subject (or impersonal es hungert mich [akk]) and forms its perfect with haben: hat gehungert.

nominative.german: Die arme Bevölkerung hungerte während der langanhaltenden Dürreperiode.
nominative.english: The poor population went hungry during the prolonged drought period.
nominative.hint: Subject of hungerte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on arme.

accusative.german: Die gestrandeten Seeleute hungerten viele schwere Tage auf der Insel.
accusative.english: The stranded sailors went hungry for many hard days on the island.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; hungerten is intransitive.

dative.german: Nach tagelangem Hungern freute sich der Wanderer über eine warme Suppe.
dative.english: After days of going hungry the hiker was glad to have warm soup.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on tagelangem.

genitive.german: Trotz des Hungerns verlor die tapfere Mannschaft nicht ihren Lebensmut.
genitive.english: Despite starving the brave crew did not lose their courage to live.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Hungern adds genitive -s.

hungern.proTip: Weak verb: hungern – hungerte – hat gehungert. Figurative idiom: hungern nach + dative (to crave/starve for): 'Sie hungern nach Anerkennung' (They crave recognition). Compare with verhungern (to starve to death, perfect with sein!).

überholen.note: Inseparable strong transitive verb (with stress on -hol-: überhólen) meaning 'to overtake, pass' (a car, runner, rival). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Überholen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden/etwas überholen).

nominative.german: Der schnelle Sportwagen überholt den langsamen Lastwagen auf der Autobahn.
nominative.english: The fast sports car overtakes the slow truck on the motorway.
nominative.hint: Subject of überholt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on schnelle.

accusative.german: Der Radfahrer überholte einen älteren Fußgänger auf dem Waldweg.
accusative.english: The cyclist overtook an older pedestrian on the forest path.
accusative.hint: Direct object of überholte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on älteren.

dative.german: Mit hoher Geschwindigkeit überholte der Rennfahrer das Führungsauto.
dative.english: At high speed the racing driver overtook the lead car.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on hoher.

genitive.german: Wegen des riskanten Überholens im Nebel verlor der Fahrer seinen Führerschein.
genitive.english: Because of the risky overtaking in fog the driver lost his driving licence.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on riskanten; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

überholen.proTip: Stress matters! Inseparable überhólen (stress on hol) = to overtake / to overhaul a machine: er überholt, überholte, hat überholt. Separable überholen (stress on über) is rare/specialized in sailing (to fetch across).

vermeiden.note: Strong transitive verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to avoid, prevent, steer clear of' (risks, mistakes, conflict). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Vermeiden requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas vermeiden).

nominative.german: Ein umsichtiger Autofahrer vermeidet unnötige Risiken im dichten Verkehr.
nominative.english: A prudent driver avoids unnecessary risks in heavy traffic.
nominative.hint: Subject of vermeidet, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative ein; strong adjective ending -er on umsichtiger.

accusative.german: Wir müssen diesen fatalen Fehler beim nächsten Mal unbedingt vermeiden.
accusative.english: We must by all means avoid this fatal mistake next time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vermeiden, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner diesen; weak adjective ending -en on fatalen.

dative.german: Mit guter Planung lassen sich viele Missverständnisse leicht vermeiden.
dative.english: With good planning many misunderstandings can be easily avoided.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on guter.

genitive.german: Zur Vermeidung des Entstehens von Konflikten wurden klare Regeln aufgestellt.
genitive.english: To avoid the occurrence of conflicts clear rules were set up.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vermeidung. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Entstehen adds genitive -s.

vermeiden.proTip: Strong verb forms: vermeiden – vermied – hat vermieden (er vermeidet). Frequently followed by an infinitive with zu: 'Er vermied es, ihr direkt in die Augen zu schauen' (He avoided looking her straight in the eye). Noun: die Vermeidung.

produzieren.note: Regular weak transitive verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to produce, manufacture, create' (goods, energy, films). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Produzieren requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas produzieren).

nominative.german: Die moderne Fabrik produziert tausende Elektrofahrzeuge pro Monat.
nominative.english: The modern factory produces thousands of electric vehicles per month.
nominative.hint: Subject of produziert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on moderne.

accusative.german: Das neue Solarkraftwerk produziert sauberen Strom für die ganze Region.
accusative.english: The new solar power plant produces clean electricity for the entire region.
accusative.hint: Direct object of produziert, so accusative. Strong declension without an article: masculine accusative takes strong ending -en on sauberen.

dative.german: Mit modernster Technik produziert das Unternehmen hochwertige Präzisionswerkzeuge.
dative.english: With state-of-the-art technology the enterprise produces high-quality precision tools.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on modernster.

genitive.german: Die Kosten des Produzierens von Solarmodulen sind in den letzten Jahren stark gesunken.
genitive.english: The costs of producing solar modules have fallen sharply in recent years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Produzieren adds genitive -s.

produzieren.proTip: Verbs ending in -ieren do not take the ge- prefix in the past participle: produzieren – produzierte – hat produziert. Related noun: die Produktion / das Produkt. Reflexive idiom: sich produzieren (to show off / posture in public).

meiden.note: Strong transitive verb meaning 'to shun, avoid, steer clear of' (a person, place, or food). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Meiden requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (jemanden/etwas meiden).

nominative.german: Der vorsichtige Spaziergänger meidet den dunklen Waldweg in der Nacht.
nominative.english: The cautious stroller avoids the dark forest path at night.
nominative.hint: Subject of meidet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on vorsichtige.

accusative.german: Der Allergiker mied jeglichen Kontakt mit tierischen Haaren konsequent.
accusative.english: The allergy sufferer consistently avoided any contact with animal hair.
accusative.hint: Direct object of mied, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner jeglichen.

dative.german: Aus gutem Grund meidet die scheue Katze den lauten Staubsauger.
dative.english: For good reason the shy cat steers clear of the loud vacuum cleaner.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on gutem.

genitive.german: Die Gründe des Meidens bestimmter Lebensmittel lagen in ihren Unverträglichkeiten.
genitive.english: The reasons for avoiding certain foods lay in her intolerances.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gründe. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Meiden adds genitive -s.

meiden.proTip: Strong verb: meiden – mied – hat gemieden (er meidet). Nuance difference: meiden means deliberate, habitual avoidance or shunning of persons/places/foods ('Sie meidet Zucker', 'Er meidet schlechte Gesellschaft'), whereas vermeiden emphasizes preventing an error, accident, or specific action.

loslegen.note: Separable weak intransitive verb meaning 'to get going, start enthusiastically without delay'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Loslegen takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and often combines with mit + dative (mit der Arbeit loslegen).

nominative.german: Das motivierte Team legt sofort mit der Umsetzung des Projekts los.
nominative.english: The motivated team gets going immediately with the implementation of the project.
nominative.hint: Subject of legt ... los, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on motivierte.

accusative.german: Nach einer kurzen Pause legten die Handwerker den ganzen Nachmittag richtig los.
accusative.english: After a short break the craftsmen really got going for the whole afternoon.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; loslegen is an intransitive verb.

dative.german: Mit großem Eifer legten die Sportler beim Training los.
dative.english: With great eagerness the athletes got going during training.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on großem.

genitive.german: Der Zeitpunkt des Loslegens wurde von der Projektleitung genau festgelegt.
genitive.english: The timing of getting going was precisely determined by project management.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zeitpunkt. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Loslegen adds genitive -s.

loslegen.proTip: Colloquial and energetic: 'Worauf wartest du? Leg los!' (What are you waiting for? Get cracking!). Common construction: mit etwas (dative) loslegen. Forms: loslegen – legte los – hat losgelegt.

verschmelzen.note: Strong verb with inseparable prefix ver- meaning 'to fuse, melt together, merge' (metals, cultures, ideas). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Intransitive with sein (ist verschmolzen: two things merge), transitive with haben (hat verschmolzen: to melt something together). Commonly governs mit + dative.

nominative.german: Tradition und Moderne verschmelzen in dieser pulsierenden Metropole zu einer Einheit.
nominative.english: Tradition and modernity merge into a single entity in this vibrant metropolis.
nominative.hint: Compound nominative subject of verschmelzen. Nouns without articles functioning as subjects in the nominative.

accusative.german: Der Künstler verschmolz verschiedene Stilelemente zu einem faszinierenden Gesamtkunstwerk.
accusative.english: The artist fused various stylistic elements into a fascinating total work of art.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verschmolz (transitive use), so accusative plural. Strong plural ending -e on verschiedene.

dative.german: Bei extrem hoher Hitze verschmilzt das Metall mit dem beigemischten Kupfer.
dative.english: At extremely high heat the metal fuses with the blended copper.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on hoher.

genitive.german: Das Phänomen des Verschmelzens zweier Galaxien fasziniert Astronomen weltweit.
genitive.english: The phenomenon of two galaxies merging fascinates astronomers worldwide.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Phänomen. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verschmelzen adds genitive -s.

verschmelzen.proTip: Strong verb forms: verschmelzen – verschmolz – ist/hat verschmolzen (3rd person singular: es verschmilzt). Intransitive: 'Die Firmen sind verschmolzen' (The companies merged). Transitive: 'Der Schmied hat das Gold verschmolzen'.

anpassen.note: Separable weak verb meaning 'to adapt, adjust, customize'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Transitive: etwas (akk) an etwas (akk) anpassen. Reflexive: sich (akk) an etwas (akk) anpassen (to adapt oneself to something).

nominative.german: Ein fähiger Entwickler passt die Software an die Wünsche der Kunden an.
nominative.english: A capable developer adapts the software to the wishes of the customers.
nominative.hint: Subject of passt ... an, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative ein; strong adjective ending -er on fähiger.

accusative.german: Das Unternehmen muss seine Strategie schnell an die veränderte Marktlage anpassen.
accusative.english: The company must quickly adapt its strategy to the changed market situation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of anpassen, so accusative. Feminine accusative possessive seine.

dative.german: Mit großer Flexibilität passten sich die Mitarbeiter der neuen Arbeitssituation an.
dative.english: With great flexibility the employees adapted to the new work situation.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on großer.

genitive.german: Die Notwendigkeit des ständigen Anpassens bereitet vielen traditionellen Betrieben Mühe.
genitive.english: The necessity of constant adaptation causes trouble for many traditional businesses.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Notwendigkeit. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ständigen; nominalized verb adds -s.

anpassen.proTip: Two-way preposition rule: 'anpassen an' ALWAYS takes ACCUSATIVE (showing target/direction of adjustment): 'Er passt sich an die Situation (akk) an'. Regular forms: anpassen – passte an – hat angepasst.

zusammenhalten.note: Separable strong verb meaning 'to hold together, stick together' (family, glue, team). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Transitive: etwas (akk) zusammenhalten. Intransitive / reflexive: fest zusammenhalten (to stick together).

nominative.german: Eine starke Gemeinschaft hält auch in schweren Zeiten fest zusammen.
nominative.english: A strong community sticks firmly together even in difficult times.
nominative.hint: Subject of hält ... zusammen, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative eine; weak adjective ending -e on starke.

accusative.german: Dieser spezielle Klebstoff hält die zerbrochenen Teile dauerhaft zusammen.
accusative.english: This special adhesive holds the broken pieces together permanently.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zusammenhalten, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on zerbrochenen.

dative.german: Mit unerschütterlicher Loyalität hielt die Familie in der Krise zusammen.
dative.english: With unshakeable loyalty the family held together in the crisis.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on unerschütterlicher.

genitive.german: Die Bedeutung des familiären Zusammenhaltens zeigt sich besonders in Notlagen.
genitive.english: The importance of family solidarity shows itself especially in emergencies.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bedeutung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on familiären; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

zusammenhalten.proTip: Strong verb forms: zusammenhalten – hielt zusammen – hat zusammengehalten (er hält zusammen). Noun: der Zusammenhalt (solidarity, cohesion): 'Der Zusammenhalt im Team ist hervorragend'.

anwachsen.note: Separable strong intransitive verb meaning 'to grow, swell, accumulate, rise to' (debts, population, water levels). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Anwachsen takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with sein: ist angewachsen (anwachsen zu / auf + akk).

nominative.german: Der Schuldenberg wächst durch die Zinsen von Monat zu Monat an.
nominative.english: The mountain of debt grows from month to month due to interest.
nominative.hint: Subject of wächst ... an, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; compound noun Schuldenberg.

accusative.german: Die Summe wuchs über die Jahre auf einen beträchtlichen Betrag an.
accusative.english: Over the years the sum grew to a considerable amount.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition auf (showing target level). Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on beträchtlichen.

dative.german: Bei rasch anwachsendem Hochwasser müssen die Anwohner rechtzeitig evakuiert werden.
dative.english: With rapidly rising floodwaters the residents must be evacuated in good time.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on anwachsendem.

genitive.german: Wegen des kontinuierlichen Anwachsens der Bevölkerung benötigt die Stadt neue Schulen.
genitive.english: Because of the continuous growth of the population the city needs new schools.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on kontinuierlichen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

anwachsen.proTip: Principal parts: anwachsen – wuchs an – ist angewachsen (vowel change: er/sie/es wächst an). Perfect with sein! Prepositions: 'anwachsen auf + akk' (grow to a figure: auf eine Million anwachsen) or 'anwachsen zu + dat' (grow into a threat).

sammeln.note: Regular weak transitive verb meaning 'to collect, gather, amass' (stamps, experiences, money) or reflexively sich sammeln ('to gather / collect one's thoughts'). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Sammeln requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas sammeln).

nominative.german: Der leidenschaftliche Sammler besitzt hunderte seltene Münzen aus aller Welt.
nominative.english: The passionate collector owns hundreds of rare coins from all over the world.
nominative.hint: Subject of besitzt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on leidenschaftliche.

accusative.german: Die Kinder sammeln bunte Blätter und Kastanien im herbstlichen Park.
accusative.english: The children collect colorful leaves and chestnuts in the autumnal park.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sammeln, so accusative plural. Strong declension without an article: plural accusative takes ending -e on bunte.

dative.german: Mit großem Fleiß sammelte die Hilfsorganisation Spenden für Bedürftige.
dative.english: With great diligence the aid organisation collected donations for those in need.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on großem.

genitive.german: Die Freude des Sammelns antiker Uhren begleitet ihn schon seit seiner Jugend.
genitive.english: The joy of collecting antique watches has accompanied him since his youth.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Freude. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Sammeln adds genitive -s.

sammeln.proTip: Spelling note: verbs ending in -eln drop the -e- in the ich-form: 'ich sammle' (or colloquial 'ich sammele'), du sammelst, er sammelt. Past: sammelte, hat gesammelt. Reflexive: 'sich sammeln' = to gather / compose oneself.

erhalten.note: Inseparable strong transitive verb with dual meaning: 1. 'to receive, get' (a letter, award); 2. 'to preserve, maintain' (buildings, peace, nature). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Erhalten takes a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas erhalten).

nominative.german: Der verdiente Wissenschaftler erhält einen prestigeträchtigen Forschungspreis.
nominative.english: The deserving scientist receives a prestigious research prize.
nominative.hint: Subject of erhält, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on verdiente.

accusative.german: Ich habe gestern einen wichtigen Brief von meiner Bank erhalten.
accusative.english: I received an important letter from my bank yesterday.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erhalten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on wichtigen.

dative.german: Nach langem Warten erhielt der Antragsteller endlich die ersehnte Genehmigung.
dative.english: After a long wait the applicant finally received the longed-for approval.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on langem.

genitive.german: Die Kosten des Erhaltens historischer Baudenkmäler sind oft enorm hoch.
genitive.english: The costs of preserving historic architectural monuments are often enormously high.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Erhalten adds genitive -s.

erhalten.proTip: Strong verb: erhalten – erhielt – hat erhalten (vowel change: er/sie/es erhält). Two main meanings: 'Ich habe deine Nachricht erhalten' (received) vs. 'Den Denkmalschutz erhalten' (preserve/maintain). Noun: der Erhalt (receipt) / die Erhaltung (preservation).

detonieren.note: Regular weak intransitive verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to detonate, explode with high velocity' (bombs, explosive charges). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Detonieren takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with haben or sein (Duden lists both: hat/ist detoniert).

nominative.german: Die alte Fliegerbombe detonierte bei der kontrollierten Entschärfung auf dem Feld.
nominative.english: The old aerial bomb detonated during the controlled defusal in the field.
nominative.hint: Subject of detonierte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on alte.

accusative.german: Die Einsatzkräfte sperrten den gesamten Gefahrenbereich weiträumig ab, bevor die Sprengladung detonierte.
accusative.english: The emergency forces cordoned off the entire danger zone widely before the explosive charge detonated.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sperrten ... ab, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

dative.german: Bei einer plötzlich detonierenden Granate zählt jede Sekunde für die Soldaten.
dative.english: With a suddenly detonating grenade every second counts for the soldiers.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on detonierenden.

genitive.german: Die Druckwelle des Detonierens der Sprengladung zerstörte mehrere Fenster.
genitive.english: The blast wave of the detonating of the explosive charge destroyed several windows.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Druckwelle. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Detonieren adds genitive -s.

detonieren.proTip: Verbs ending in -ieren take no ge- in the Partizip II: detonieren – detonierte – hat/ist detoniert. Distinguish: detonieren is sudden supersonic chemical detonation; explodieren is general explosion; platzen is bursting/popping.

ausführen.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 'to carry out, execute, perform' (plans, orders, commands) or 'to walk' (a dog) or 'to export' (goods). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Ausführen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas/jemanden ausführen).

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Meister führt den schwierigen Auftrag mit höchster Präzision aus.
nominative.english: The experienced master craftsman carries out the difficult assignment with utmost precision.
nominative.hint: Subject of führt ... aus, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Das Programm führt den komplexen Befehl in wenigen Millisekunden aus.
accusative.english: The program executes the complex command in a few milliseconds.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausführen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on komplexen.

dative.german: Mit größter Sorgfalt führte die Chirurgin die anspruchsvolle Operation aus.
dative.english: With the greatest care the surgeon carried out the demanding operation.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on größter.

genitive.german: Die Verantwortung des fehlerfreien Ausführens des Plans lag beim Projektleiter.
genitive.english: The responsibility for faultless execution of the plan lay with the project manager.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Verantwortung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on fehlerfreien; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

ausführen.proTip: Multiple meanings to know: 1. Carry out/execute: 'einen Plan ausführen'; 2. Walk a pet: 'den Hund ausführen'; 3. Export goods: 'Waren ins Ausland ausführen'; 4. Explain at length: 'einen Gedanken näher ausführen'. Noun: die Ausführung.

abwerfen.note: Separable strong transitive verb meaning 'to drop / release from above' (bombs, cargo, rider thrown from a horse) or financially 'to yield, bring in' (profit, returns). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Abwerfen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas abwerfen).

nominative.german: Das Transportflugzeug wirft dringend benötigte Hilfsgüter über dem Katastrophengebiet ab.
nominative.english: The transport aircraft drops urgently needed relief supplies over the disaster area.
nominative.hint: Subject of wirft ... ab, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; noun Transportflugzeug takes no ending.

accusative.german: Das nervöse Pferd warf den unvorsichtigen Reiter im hohen Bogen ab.
accusative.english: The nervous horse threw off the careless rider in a wide arc.
accusative.hint: Direct object of abwerfen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on unvorsichtigen.

dative.german: Mit diesem erfolgreichen Geschäft warf das Unternehmen beachtliche Gewinne ab.
dative.english: With this successful business the company yielded considerable profits.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on erfolgreichen.

genitive.german: Der genaue Ort des Abwerfens der Notfallpakete war auf der Karte markiert.
genitive.english: The exact location of the dropping of the emergency packages was marked on the map.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ort. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Abwerfen adds genitive -s.

abwerfen.proTip: Strong verb with vowel change: abwerfen – warf ab – hat abgeworfen (er/sie/es wirft ab). Financial collocation: 'Gewinn abwerfen' (to yield a profit) — 'Die Investition wirft gute Zinsen ab'.

aufsteigen.note: Separable strong intransitive verb meaning 'to ascend, rise up, climb' (smoke, balloons, climbers, careers). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Aufsteigen takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with sein: ist aufgestiegen.

nominative.german: Der bunte Heißluftballon steigt langsam in den blauen Himmel auf.
nominative.english: The colorful hot-air balloon rises slowly into the blue sky.
nominative.hint: Subject of steigt ... auf, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on bunte.

accusative.german: Die Wanderer stiegen den steilen Pfad hinauf, bis dichter Nebel aufstieg.
accusative.english: The hikers climbed up the steep path until dense fog rose up.
accusative.hint: Direct object of hinaufsteigen, so accusative. In the subordinate clause, aufstieg has the nominative subject dichter Nebel.

dative.german: Aus dem tiefen Tal stieg dichter weißer Rauch auf.
dative.english: Dense white smoke rose up out of the deep valley.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on tiefen.

genitive.german: Das Geräusch des Aufsteigens der Flugzeuge war kilometerweit zu hören.
genitive.english: The sound of the ascending of the airplanes could be heard miles away.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Geräusch. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Aufsteigen adds genitive -s.

aufsteigen.proTip: Strong verb: aufsteigen – stieg auf – ist aufgestiegen (no vowel change in present: er steigt auf). Sports/career meaning: to be promoted / rise to a higher league: 'Die Mannschaft ist in die Bundesliga aufgestiegen' (The team was promoted to the Bundesliga). Noun: der Aufstieg.

nachbauen.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 'to replicate, recreate, reconstruct, build a model/copy of'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Nachbauen requires a nominative subject and an accusative direct object (etwas nachbauen).

nominative.german: Der begabte Modellbauer baut historische Segelschiffe originalgetreu nach.
nominative.english: The talented model builder replicates historic sailing ships true to the original.
nominative.hint: Subject of baut ... nach, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on begabte.

accusative.german: Die Schüler bauten das antike römische Kastell aus Karton nach.
accusative.english: The students recreated the ancient Roman fort out of cardboard.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nachbauen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective endings -e on antike and römische.

dative.german: Nach genauen Bauplänen baute der Ingenieur die historische Dampfmaschine nach.
dative.english: According to exact blueprints the engineer replicated the historic steam engine.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Plural dative takes ending -en on adjective genauen and noun Bauplänen.

genitive.german: Die Herausforderung des Nachbauens einer solchen Anlage liegt im Detail.
genitive.english: The challenge of replicating such a facility lies in the detail.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Herausforderung. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Nachbauen adds genitive -s.

nachbauen.proTip: Separable weak verb: nachbauen – baute nach – hat nachgebaut. Prefix nach- often carries the meaning of copying or reproducing an original: nachmachen, nachahmen, nachahmen, nachbauen. Noun: der Nachbau.

vorgehen.note: Separable strong intransitive verb meaning 1. 'to proceed, take action, act according to a method' (gegen etwas vorgehen); 2. 'to take precedence, come first' (Sicherheit geht vor); 3. 'to run fast' (of a watch). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Vorgehen takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect with sein: ist vorgegangen.

nominative.german: Die örtliche Polizei geht entschlossen gegen die organisierte Kriminalität vor.
nominative.english: The local police proceed decisively against organized crime.
nominative.hint: Subject of geht ... vor, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on örtliche.

accusative.german: Der Ausschuss ging die ganze Woche über streng nach dem Protokoll vor.
accusative.english: The committee proceeded strictly according to protocol throughout the entire week.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long'; vorgehen is an intransitive verb.

dative.german: Nach einem durchdachten Plan gingen die Spezialisten bei der Untersuchung vor.
dative.english: According to a well-thought-out plan the specialists proceeded during the investigation.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on durchdachten.

genitive.german: Die Rechtmäßigkeit des Vorgehens der Behörden wurde vom Gericht bestätigt.
genitive.english: The legality of the approach of the authorities was confirmed by the court.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Rechtmäßigkeit. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Vorgehen adds genitive -s.

vorgehen.proTip: Strong verb: vorgehen – ging vor – ist vorgegangen. Common meanings: 1. 'Wie sollen wir vorgehen?' (How should we proceed?); 2. 'Sicherheit geht vor' (Safety comes first); 3. 'Meine Uhr geht 5 Minuten vor' (My watch is 5 minutes fast). Noun: das Vorgehen (procedure/approach).

sich ereignen.note: Inseparable regular reflexive verb with prefix er- meaning 'to occur, happen, take place' (events, accidents, tragedies). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. The subject is nominative (was ereignet sich?), the reflexive pronoun sich is ACCUSATIVE, and the perfect is formed with haben: hat sich ereignet.

nominative.german: Ein folgenschwerer Verkehrsunfall ereignete sich gestern auf der nassen Autobahn.
nominative.english: A serious traffic accident occurred yesterday on the wet motorway.
nominative.hint: Subject of ereignete sich, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative ein; strong adjective ending -er on folgenschwerer.

accusative.german: Der Vorfall ereignete sich genau in jenem Moment, den niemand vorhersehen konnte.
accusative.english: The incident occurred at the exact moment that no one could foresee.
accusative.hint: Relative clause in accusative modifying Moment (den is the accusative direct object of vorhersehen).

dative.german: Bei diesem tragischen Unglück ereigneten sich dramatische Szenen.
dative.english: In this tragic disaster dramatic scenes took place.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on tragischen.

genitive.german: Der genaue Zeitpunkt des Ereignens der Katastrophe ließ sich nicht rekonstruieren.
genitive.english: The exact time of the catastrophe's occurrence could not be reconstructed.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zeitpunkt. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Ereignen adds genitive -s.

sich ereignen.proTip: Reflexive verb: sich ereignen – ereignete sich – hat sich ereignet. Elevating/formal synonym for passieren or geschehen: 'Was hat sich ereignet?' (What occurred?). Related noun: das Ereignis (event / occurrence, plural: die Ereignisse).

besiegen.note: Inseparable weak transitive verb with prefix be- meaning 'to defeat, conquer, overcome' (an opponent, an illness, fears). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Besiegen requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (jemanden/etwas besiegen).

nominative.german: Die tapfere Heldin besiegt den furchterregenden Drachen im Märchen.
nominative.english: The brave heroine defeats the terrifying dragon in the fairy tale.
nominative.hint: Subject of besiegt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on tapfere.

accusative.german: Unsere Mannschaft besiegte den amtierenden Meister mit drei zu null Toren.
accusative.english: Our team defeated the reigning champion by three goals to nil.
accusative.hint: Direct object of besiegte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on amtierenden.

dative.german: Mit überlegener Taktik besiegte die Spielerin ihre erfahrene Konkurrentin.
dative.english: With superior tactics the player defeated her experienced rival.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on überlegener.

genitive.german: Nach dem Triumph des Besiegens des Gegners feierten alle ausgelassen.
genitive.english: After the triumph of defeating the opponent everyone celebrated exuberantly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Triumph. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Besiegen adds genitive -s.

besiegen.proTip: Regular weak forms: besiegen – besiegte – hat besiegt. Can be used for enemies in battle/sports, but also abstract foes: 'seine Angst besiegen' (to conquer one's fear), 'eine schwere Krankheit besiegen' (to beat a severe disease). Noun: der Sieg (victory).

verdampfen.note: Regular weak verb with prefix ver- meaning 'to vaporise, evaporate' (turn from liquid into gas/steam). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Intransitive (water evaporates): takes nominative subject, no direct object, perfect with sein (ist verdampft). Transitive (to evaporate something): takes accusative object, perfect with haben (hat verdampft).

nominative.german: Das kochende Wasser verdampft bei hundert Grad Celsius vollständig.
nominative.english: The boiling water vaporises completely at one hundred degrees Celsius.
nominative.hint: Subject of verdampft, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on kochende.

accusative.german: Die intensive Hitze verdampfte den letzten Tropfen Feuchtigkeit aus dem Boden.
accusative.english: The intense heat vaporised the last drop of moisture from the ground.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verdampfte (transitive use), so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on letzten; Tropfen is a weak noun (n-noun).

dative.german: Aus der kochenden Flüssigkeit stieg heißer Dampf mit hoher Geschwindigkeit auf.
dative.english: Hot steam rose at high speed out of the boiling liquid.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on kochenden.

genitive.german: Der Vorgang des Verdampfens entzieht der Umgebung eine beträchtliche Wärmemenge.
genitive.english: The process of vaporisation extracts a considerable amount of heat from the surroundings.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vorgang. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verdampfen adds genitive -s.

verdampfen.proTip: Weak verb forms: verdampfen – verdampfte – ist verdampft (intransitive) / hat verdampft (transitive). Distinguish verdampfen (boiling evaporation at high temperature) from verdunsten (passive evaporation at ambient temperature below boiling point).

trainieren.note: Regular weak verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to train, coach, practice, work out'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Intransitive (to work out) or transitive with an ACCUSATIVE direct object (einen Muskel / eine Mannschaft / eine Fähigkeit trainieren).

nominative.german: Die ehrgeizige Athletin trainiert täglich mehrere Stunden für den Marathon.
nominative.english: The ambitious athlete trains several hours daily for the marathon.
nominative.hint: Subject of trainiert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on ehrgeizige.

accusative.german: Der Trainer trainierte die neue Mannschaft intensiv vor der Meisterschaft.
accusative.english: The coach trained the new team intensively before the championship.
accusative.hint: Direct object of trainierte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

dative.german: Mit eisernem Willen trainiert der Sportler jeden frühen Morgen im Fitnessstudio.
dative.english: With iron will the athlete works out every early morning in the gym.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on eisernem; weak noun Wille adds -n in dative.

genitive.german: Die positiven Effekte des regelmäßigen Trainierens stärken das Immunsystem nachhaltig.
genitive.english: The positive effects of regular training sustainably strengthen the immune system.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Effekte. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on regelmäßigen; nominalized verb adds -s.

trainieren.proTip: No ge- prefix in Partizip II: trainieren – trainierte – hat trainiert. Both transitive ('Er trainiert den Hund / die Mannschaft') and intransitive ('Ich trainiere dreimal pro Woche'). Related nouns: das Training, der Trainer / die Trainerin.

verbergen.note: Inseparable strong verb with prefix ver- meaning 'to conceal, hide' (secrets, feelings, objects) or reflexively sich verbergen ('to hide oneself / lie hidden'). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Transitive: etwas/jemanden (akk) vor jemandem (dat) verbergen.

nominative.german: Die dichte Nebelwand verbirgt die majestätischen Berggipfel vor den Blicken der Wanderer.
nominative.english: The dense wall of fog conceals the majestic mountain peaks from the hikers' view.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbirgt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on dichte.

accusative.german: Er verbarg seine wahren Gefühle hinter einer kühlen Maske.
accusative.english: He concealed his true feelings behind a cool mask.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbarg, so accusative plural. Plural accusative possessive seine; weak adjective ending -en on wahren.

dative.german: Sie verbarg das wertvolle Schmuckstück vor den neugierigen Blicken der Gäste.
dative.english: She concealed the valuable piece of jewelry from the curious gazes of the guests.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (conceal from). Plural dative article den; weak adjective ending -en on neugierigen; noun Blick adds -en in dative plural.

genitive.german: Der Sinn des Verbergens der Wahrheit erschloss sich den Ermittlern erst später.
genitive.english: The point of concealing the truth became clear to the investigators only later.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Sinn. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verbergen adds genitive -s.

verbergen.proTip: Strong verb with vowel change: verbergen – verbarg – hat verborgen (er/sie/es verbirgt). Key preposition: 'etwas vor (+ Dativ) verbergen': 'Du musst nichts vor mir verbergen' (You don't have to hide anything from me).

zusammenfassen.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 'to summarise, sum up, synthesize' (main points, findings) or 'to combine / group together' (departments, forces). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Zusammenfassen requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas zusammenfassen).

nominative.german: Der Dozent fasst die Kernaussagen der Vorlesung am Ende kurz zusammen.
nominative.english: The lecturer briefly summarizes the key statements of the lecture at the end.
nominative.hint: Subject of fasst ... zusammen, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; noun Dozent takes no ending in nominative.

accusative.german: Die Studentin fasste den langen wissenschaftlichen Artikel präzise zusammen.
accusative.english: The student summarized the long scientific article precisely.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zusammenfassen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective endings -en on langen and wissenschaftlichen.

dative.german: In wenigen klaren Sätzen fasste der Redner die Ergebnisse zusammen.
dative.english: In a few clear sentences the speaker summarized the results.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in. Strong declension plural without an article: dative plural ending -en on wenigen and klaren; noun Satz adds -en in dative plural.

genitive.german: Die Kunst des präzisen Zusammenfassens erfordert analytisches Denken.
genitive.english: The art of precise summarizing requires analytical thinking.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kunst. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on präzisen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

zusammenfassen.proTip: Regular weak forms: zusammenfassen – fasste zusammen – hat zusammengefasst. Noun: die Zusammenfassung (summary). Essential phrase for presentations and exams: 'Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass...' (In summary, it can be said that...).

interessieren.note: Regular weak verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to interest, concern'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Active transitive: etwas interessiert jemanden (accusative direct object). Reflexive: sich (accusative) für etwas (accusative) interessieren.

nominative.german: Das spannende Thema interessiert viele Studierende an der Universität.
nominative.english: The exciting topic interests many students at the university.
nominative.hint: Subject of interessiert, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on spannende.

accusative.german: Die neuen wissenschaftlichen Erkenntnisse interessieren den jungen Forscher brennend.
accusative.english: The new scientific findings interest the young researcher intensely.
accusative.hint: Direct object of interessieren (wen interessiert es?), so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on jungen.

dative.german: Mit großem Interesse verfolgte das Publikum den Vortrag des Wissenschaftlers.
dative.english: With great interest the audience followed the scientist's lecture.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on großem.

genitive.german: Trotz des offensichtlichen Interesses der Investoren platzte das geplante Geschäft.
genitive.english: Despite the obvious interest of the investors the planned deal fell through.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on offensichtlichen; noun Interesse adds -s.

interessieren.proTip: Case watch with interessieren: 1. Transitive: 'Das interessiert MICH' (accusative!). 2. Reflexive with für: 'Ich interessiere MICH (akk) für (akk) Kunst'. Do NOT confuse with dative 'interessiert sein an + dat': 'Ich bin an dem Projekt interessiert'.

überfluten.note: Inseparable weak transitive verb with prefix über- (stress on -flu-: überflúten) meaning 'to flood, inundate, overflow' (land, streets, or figuratively markets). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Überfluten requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas überfluten).

nominative.german: Der reißende Fluss überflutet die tiefer gelegenen Straßen der Altstadt.
nominative.english: The torrential river floods the lower-lying streets of the old town.
nominative.hint: Subject of überflutet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on reißende.

accusative.german: Die gewaltige Flutwelle überflutete den gesamten Stadtteil innerhalb weniger Minuten.
accusative.english: The enormous tidal wave flooded the entire district within a few minutes.
accusative.hint: Direct object of überflutete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

dative.german: Nach der verheerenden Überschwemmung stand das Wasser meterhoch in den Kellern.
dative.english: After the devastating inundation the water stood meters high in the basements.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on verheerenden.

genitive.german: Wegen des plötzlichen Überflutens der Deiche musste das Dorf evakuiert werden.
genitive.english: Because of the sudden flooding of the dykes the village had to be evacuated.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on plötzlichen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

überfluten.proTip: Stress on root flu: überflúten – überflutete – hat überflutet (inseparable, no ge-!). Figurative usage: 'Billige Importe überfluten den Markt' (Cheap imports flood the market).

herstellen.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 'to manufacture, produce' (goods) or 'to establish, create' (order, contact, connection). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Herstellen requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas herstellen).

nominative.german: Das traditionsreiche Familienunternehmen stellt hochwertige Holzmöbel in Handarbeit her.
nominative.english: The traditional family company manufactures high-quality wooden furniture by hand.
nominative.hint: Subject of stellt ... her, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on traditionsreiche.

accusative.german: Die Fabrik stellt einen neuen Typ von Solarzellen für den Weltmarkt her.
accusative.english: The factory manufactures a new type of solar cells for the world market.
accusative.hint: Direct object of herstellen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on neuen.

dative.german: Mit modernsten Maschinen stellt die Firma mikroskopisch kleine Bauteile her.
dative.english: With state-of-the-art machines the firm manufactures microscopic components.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension plural without an article: dative plural ending -en on modernsten and Maschinen.

genitive.german: Die Gesamtkosten des Herstellens eines Prototyps belaufen sich auf zehntausend Euro.
genitive.english: The total costs of manufacturing a prototype amount to ten thousand euros.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gesamtkosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Herstellen adds genitive -s.

herstellen.proTip: Separable weak verb: herstellen – stellte her – hat hergestellt. Abstract collocations: 'Kontakt herstellen' (establish contact); 'Ordnung herstellen' (restore order); 'eine Verbindung herstellen' (establish a connection). Noun: der Hersteller (manufacturer).

kopieren.note: Regular weak transitive verb ending in -ieren meaning 'to copy, duplicate, photocopy, replicate'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Kopieren requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas kopieren).

nominative.german: Die fleißige Praktikantin kopiert die vertraulichen Unterlagen für die Besprechung.
nominative.english: The hardworking intern copies the confidential documents for the meeting.
nominative.hint: Subject of kopiert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on fleißige.

accusative.german: Könnten Sie bitte diesen wichtigen Vertrag für meine Akten kopieren?
accusative.english: Could you please copy this important contract for my files?
accusative.hint: Direct object of kopieren, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner diesen; weak adjective ending -en on wichtigen.

dative.german: Mit dem neuen Farbkopierer lassen sich hochwertige Duplikate schnell erstellen.
dative.english: With the new color photocopier high-quality duplicates can be created quickly.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on neuen.

genitive.german: Das unerlaubte Kopieren des geschützten Computerprogramms ist strafbar.
genitive.english: Unauthorized copying of the protected computer program is punishable.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kopieren. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on geschützten; noun adds -s.

kopieren.proTip: Verbs ending in -ieren do not take the ge- prefix in the past participle: kopieren – kopierte – hat kopiert. Noun: die Kopie (copy / photocopy) vs. das Original (original).

abbauen.note: Separable weak transitive verb meaning 1. 'to mine / quarry / extract' (coal, ores); 2. 'to dismantle / take down' (scaffolding, tents); 3. 'to reduce / shed' (stress, debts, jobs). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Abbauen requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object.

nominative.german: Das Bergbauunternehmen baut wertvolles Lithium im Tagebau ab.
nominative.english: The mining enterprise extracts valuable lithium in open-cast mining.
nominative.hint: Subject of baut ... ab, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; compound noun Bergbauunternehmen.

accusative.german: Der Konzern muss in der Krise viele Arbeitsplätze im Werk abbauen.
accusative.english: In the crisis the corporation must cut many jobs at the plant.
accusative.hint: Direct object of abbauen, so accusative plural. Strong declension without an article: plural accusative ending -e on viele.

dative.german: Mit gezielten Übungen baut der Sportler überschüssigen Stress im Alltag ab.
dative.english: With targeted exercises the athlete breaks down excess stress in everyday life.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural dative takes ending -en on adjective gezielten and noun Übungen.

genitive.german: Die Genehmigung des Abbaus von Rohstoffen unterliegt strengen Umweltauflagen.
genitive.english: The permit for mining raw materials is subject to strict environmental regulations.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Genehmigung. Masculine genitive article des; noun Abbau adds genitive -s.

abbauen.proTip: Separable weak verb: abbauen – baute ab – hat abgebaut. Versatile meanings: 'Zelte abbauen' (take down tents); 'Schulden abbauen' (reduce debts); 'Alkohol abbauen' (metabolize alcohol). Antonym: aufbauen (build up / erect).

verhungern.note: Regular weak intransitive verb with prefix ver- meaning 'to starve, die of hunger'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Verhungern takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect strictly with SEIN: ist verhungert.

nominative.german: Viele unschuldige Tiere verhungern im strengen Winter ohne menschliche Hilfe.
nominative.english: Many innocent animals starve in the harsh winter without human help.
nominative.hint: Subject of verhungern, so nominative plural. Plural nominative ending -e on viele and unschuldige.

accusative.german: Die Eingeschlossenen litten wochenlang, bis die Retter die drohende Hungersnot abwendeten.
accusative.english: The trapped people suffered for weeks until rescuers averted the threatening famine.
accusative.hint: Direct object of abwendeten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on drohende.

dative.german: Vor quälendem Hunger verlor der Verirrte im Schnee fast den Verstand.
dative.english: From agonizing hunger the lost person in the snow almost lost his mind.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (cause/emotion). Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on quälendem.

genitive.german: Die tragische Gefahr des Verhungerns bedrohte die gesamte Mannschaft auf dem Schiff.
genitive.english: The tragic danger of starving threatened the entire crew on the ship.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gefahr. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Verhungern adds genitive -s.

verhungern.proTip: Auxiliary alert: verhungern takes SEIN because it indicates a change of state ending in death: 'Die Vögel sind im Winter verhungert'. Contrast with hungern (to simply feel hungry/go hungry, perfect with haben: hat gehungert). Colloquial exaggeration: 'Ich verhungere gleich!' (I'm starving!).

versorgen.note: Inseparable weak transitive verb with prefix ver- meaning 'to supply, provide, take care of, cater for'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Grammatical pattern: jemanden/etwas (akk) mit etwas (dat) versorgen.

nominative.german: Die fürsorgliche Krankenschwester versorgt den verletzten Patienten auf der Station.
nominative.english: The caring nurse looks after the injured patient on the ward.
nominative.hint: Subject of versorgt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on fürsorgliche.

accusative.german: Das Kraftwerk versorgt die gesamte Stadt zuverlässig mit elektrischem Strom.
accusative.english: The power plant supplies the entire city reliably with electrical power.
accusative.hint: Direct object of versorgt, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on gesamte.

dative.german: Die Hilfsorganisation versorgte die Flüchtlinge mit warmer Kleidung und sauberem Wasser.
dative.english: The aid organisation provided the refugees with warm clothing and clean water.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the preposition mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on warmer.

genitive.german: Die Gewährleistung des sicheren Versorgens der Bevölkerung ist Aufgabe des Staates.
genitive.english: Guaranteeing the reliable supplying of the population is the duty of the state.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gewährleistung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on sicheren; nominalized verb adds -s.

versorgen.proTip: Key preposition pattern: 'jemanden MIT (+ Dativ) versorgen': 'Wir versorgen das Spital mit Medikamenten'. Weak forms: versorgen – versorgte – hat versorgt. Noun: die Versorgung (supply / care / healthcare).

altern.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to age, grow old, mature'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Altern takes a nominative subject, NO accusative direct object, and forms its perfect tense with SEIN: ist gealtert.

nominative.german: Die menschliche Haut altert durch intensive Sonneneinstrahlung deutlich schneller.
nominative.english: Human skin ages noticeably faster through intensive sun exposure.
nominative.hint: Subject of altert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on menschliche.

accusative.german: Der Wissenschaftler untersuchte den normalen Alterungsprozess des Körpers über viele Jahre.
accusative.english: The scientist investigated the normal aging process of the body over many years.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on normalen.

dative.german: In diesem kühlen Weinkeller altert der edle Tropfen unter optimalen Bedingungen.
dative.english: In this cool wine cellar the fine wine matures under optimal conditions.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on kühlen.

genitive.german: Die biologischen Ursachen des Alterns sind Gegenstand intensiver medizinischer Forschung.
genitive.english: The biological causes of aging are the subject of intensive medical research.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ursachen. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Altern adds genitive -s.

altern.proTip: Auxiliary alert: altern forms its perfect with SEIN because it expresses an irreversible process of change of state: 'Er ist in den letzten Jahren kaum gealtert' (He has hardly aged in recent years). Noun: das Altern / das Alter.

beenden.note: Inseparable weak transitive verb with prefix be- meaning 'to end, finish, conclude, terminate' (work, a meeting, a relationship). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Beenden requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object (etwas beenden).

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Schiedsrichter beendet das spannende Fußballspiel nach vier Minuten Nachspielzeit.
nominative.english: The experienced referee ends the exciting football match after four minutes of stoppage time.
nominative.hint: Subject of beendet, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Die Diplomaten beendeten die schwierigen Verhandlungen mit einem tragfähigen Kompromiss.
accusative.english: The diplomats concluded the difficult negotiations with a sustainable compromise.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beendeten, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on schwierigen.

dative.german: Mit einer kurzen Zusammenfassung beendete die Professorin ihren Vortrag.
dative.english: With a short summary the professor concluded her lecture.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on kurzen.

genitive.german: Nach dem Beenden des Studiums trat die Absolventin eine Stelle im Ministerium an.
genitive.english: After finishing her studies the graduate took up a post in the ministry.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Beenden. Neuter genitive article des; noun Studium ends in -s.

beenden.proTip: Transitive vs. intransitive: BEENDEN is transitive and needs an object: 'Ich beende die Arbeit' (I finish the work). ENDEN is intransitive: 'Die Arbeit endet um fünf' (Work ends at five). Never say 'Ich ende die Arbeit'!

enden.note: Regular weak intransitive verb meaning 'to end, finish, terminate, draw to a close'. Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Enden takes a nominative subject, NO direct object, and forms its perfect with haben: hat geendet (or regional sein: ist geendet).

nominative.german: Die offizielle Anmeldefrist für den Kurs endet am kommenden Freitagabend.
nominative.english: The official registration deadline for the course ends next Friday evening.
nominative.hint: Subject of endet, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on offizielle.

accusative.german: Das Theaterstück dauerte den ganzen Abend und endete erst um Mitternacht.
accusative.english: The play lasted the whole evening and only ended at midnight.
accusative.hint: Accusative of duration answering 'how long' with dauerte; endete in the coordinating clause is intransitive.

dative.german: Der spannende Kriminalroman endete mit einer völlig unerwarteten Wendung.
dative.english: The exciting crime novel ended with a completely unexpected twist.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on unerwarteten.

genitive.german: Das plötzliche Enden der Musik überraschte die tanzenden Paare im Saal.
genitive.english: The sudden ending of the music surprised the dancing couples in the hall.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Enden. Feminine genitive article der; noun Musik takes no ending.

enden.proTip: Enden is strictly intransitive (etwas endet: 'Der Film endet'). To express bringing something to an end, use beenden ('Wir beenden den Film'). Prepositions: 'enden auf + akk' (words ending in a letter: endet auf ein 'e') or 'enden mit + dat' (end with something: endet mit einem Sieg).

spritzen.note: Regular weak verb meaning 1. 'to splash, squirt, spray' (water, mud); 2. 'to inject' (medicine). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Intransitive with sein (ist gespritzt: liquid splashes), transitive with haben (hat gespritzt: doctor injects medicine, gardener sprays plants).

nominative.german: Das schmutzige Wasser spritzt bei jedem vorbeifahrenden Auto auf den Gehweg.
nominative.english: The dirty water splashes onto the pavement with every passing car.
nominative.hint: Subject of spritzt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on schmutzige.

accusative.german: Die Ärztin spritzte dem erkrankten Kind ein wirksames Schmerzmittel.
accusative.english: The doctor injected an effective painkiller into the sick child.
accusative.hint: Direct object of spritzte, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on wirksames.

dative.german: Der Arzt verabreichte die rettende Impfung mit einer sterilen Nadel.
dative.english: The doctor administered the life-saving vaccination with a sterile needle.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on sterilen.

genitive.german: Das laute Geräusch des Spritzens des Wassers weckte die schlafende Katze auf.
genitive.english: The loud sound of the splashing of the water woke up the sleeping cat.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Geräusch. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Spritzen adds genitive -s.

spritzen.proTip: Dual usage: medical injection (eine Spritze geben / Insulin spritzen: transitive with dative recipient: 'Ich spritze DIR (dat) ein Mittel (akk)') vs. splashing liquids ('Wasser ist an die Wand gespritzt'). Noun: die Spritze (syringe / injection).

betreiben.note: Inseparable strong transitive verb with prefix be- meaning 'to operate, run, manage' (a business, website, plant) or 'to conduct, pursue' (research, sports, politics). Verbs conjugate; they do not decline for case. Betreiben requires a nominative subject and an ACCUSATIVE direct object.

nominative.german: Der geschäftstüchtige Gastronom betreibt drei erfolgreiche Restaurants im Stadtzentrum.
nominative.english: The enterprising restaurateur runs three successful restaurants in the city center.
nominative.hint: Subject of betreibt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on geschäftstüchtige.

accusative.german: Die Forscher betreiben aufwendige Grundlagenforschung auf dem Gebiet der Quantenphysik.
accusative.english: The researchers conduct elaborate basic research in the field of quantum physics.
accusative.hint: Direct object of betreiben, so accusative. Strong declension without an article: feminine accusative takes ending -e on aufwendige.

dative.german: Mit großer Leidenschaft betreibt die junge Frau ihr eigenes kleines Café.
dative.english: With great passion the young woman runs her own small café.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on großer.

genitive.german: Die laufenden Kosten des Betreibens einer solchen Anlage sind beträchtlich.
genitive.english: The operating costs of running such a facility are considerable.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Betreiben adds genitive -s.

betreiben.proTip: Strong verb forms: betreiben – betrieb – hat betrieben (er betreibt). Nouns: der Betrieb (enterprise, business, operation) / der Betreiber (operator). Collocations: 'Sport betreiben' (do sports); 'Forschung betreiben' (conduct research); 'Aufwand betreiben' (make an effort).

erwachsen.note: Adjective meaning 'grown-up, adult, mature'. When used attributively before a noun or nominalized as a noun (der Erwachsene, ein Erwachsener), it inflects according to German adjective declension rules. Can also function as a strong verb (erwachsen aus + dat = to arise/grow from).

nominative.german: Ein erwachsener Mensch trägt die volle Verantwortung für sein eigenes Handeln.
nominative.english: An adult human bears full responsibility for his own actions.
nominative.hint: Subject of trägt, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension: indefinite article ein has no ending; erwachsener takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Film richtet sich an ein erwachsenes Publikum und ist nicht für Kinder geeignet.
accusative.english: The film is aimed at an adult audience and is not suitable for children.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition an. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on erwachsenes.

dative.german: Bei einem erwachsenen Patienten wird die Dosierung des Medikaments entsprechend erhöht.
dative.english: In an adult patient the dosage of the medication is increased accordingly.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; weak adjective ending -en on erwachsenen; Patient is a weak noun (n-noun).

genitive.german: Die typischen Merkmale eines erwachsenen Wolfes unterscheiden sich deutlich vom Welpen.
genitive.english: The typical characteristics of an adult wolf differ clearly from the cub.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Merkmale. Masculine genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on erwachsenen; noun Wolf adds -es.

erwachsen.proTip: Adjectival noun: 'der Erwachsene' (the adult, weak declension), 'ein Erwachsener' (an adult, mixed declension), 'viele Erwachsene' (many adults). Also a strong verb: 'Aus kleinen Fehlern erwachsen oft große Probleme' (From small mistakes, big problems often arise; erwachsen – erwuchs – ist erwachsen).

wunderschön.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'beautiful, gorgeous, exquisite, magnificent' (intensified schön with wunder-). Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun, and remains uninflected when used predicatively or adverbially.

nominative.german: Ein wunderschöner Regenbogen erschien nach dem Sommergewitter am östlichen Himmel.
nominative.english: A gorgeous rainbow appeared in the eastern sky after the summer thunderstorm.
nominative.hint: Subject of erschien, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension: ein has no ending; wunderschöner takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Wir verbrachten einen wunderschönen Urlaub an den idyllischen Stränden Portugals.
accusative.english: We spent a gorgeous holiday on the idyllic beaches of Portugal.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbrachten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on wunderschönen.

dative.german: In diesem wunderschönen Garten blühen hunderte verschiedene Rosenarten.
dative.english: In this gorgeous garden hundreds of different rose varieties bloom.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on wunderschönen.

genitive.german: Wegen des wunderschönen Wetters strömten tausende Menschen an den Badesee.
genitive.english: Because of the gorgeous weather thousands of people flocked to the swimming lake.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on wunderschönen; noun Wetter adds -s.

wunderschön.proTip: Compound of Wunder (wonder) + schön (beautiful). Cannot take comparative *-er in everyday German (since it is already an absolute superlative in meaning: 'extremely beautiful'), though occasionally colloquial 'noch wunderschöner' is heard. Uninflected as adverb: 'Sie singt wunderschön'.

ernst.note: Adjective meaning 'serious, grave, solemn' (person, situation, look). Declines when used attributively before a noun. Can also be a masculine noun: der Ernst (seriousness, gravity; collocations: im Ernst, es ist mein Ernst).

nominative.german: Die ernste Lage in den Überschwemmungsgebieten erfordert sofortiges Handeln der Regierung.
nominative.english: The serious situation in the flood zones requires immediate action by the government.
nominative.hint: Subject of erfordert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on ernste.

accusative.german: Der Arzt warf der Familie einen ernsten Blick zu, bevor er sprach.
accusative.english: The doctor cast a serious look at the family before he spoke.
accusative.hint: Direct object of warf ... zu, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on ernsten.

dative.german: Mit ernstem Gesichtsausdruck verkündete die Richterin das endgültige Urteil.
dative.english: With a serious facial expression the judge announced the final verdict.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on ernstem.

genitive.german: Angesichts des ernsten Zustands des Patienten blieben die Angehörigen im Krankenhaus.
genitive.english: In view of the serious condition of the patient the relatives stayed at the hospital.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by angesichts. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ernsten; noun Zustand adds -s.

ernst.proTip: Essential collocations: 'etwas ernst nehmen' (to take something seriously); 'Das ist mein voller Ernst' (I'm deadly serious); 'Im Ernst?' (Seriously?). Comparative forms: ernster (or ernster/ernster), am ernstesten.

unwirtlich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'inhospitable, desolate, bleak, harsh' (climate, landscape, weather). Formed with the negative prefix un- and the root Wirt (host). Declines according to regular German adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Die unwirtliche Polarlandschaft bietet extrem schwierige Lebensbedingungen für Tiere.
nominative.english: The inhospitable polar landscape offers extremely difficult living conditions for animals.
nominative.hint: Subject of bietet, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on unwirtliche.

accusative.german: Die mutigen Forscher durchquerten ein unwirtliches Wüstengebiet ohne Wasserquellen.
accusative.english: The brave researchers crossed an inhospitable desert area without water sources.
accusative.hint: Direct object of durchquerten, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on unwirtliches.

dative.german: In diesem unwirtlichen Gebirge überleben nur wenige hochspezialisierte Pflanzen.
dative.english: In these inhospitable mountains only a few highly specialized plants survive.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on unwirtlichen.

genitive.german: Wegen des unwirtlichen Klimas ist die abgelegene Insel vollkommen unbewohnt.
genitive.english: Because of the inhospitable climate the remote island is completely uninhabited.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on unwirtlichen; noun Klima adds -s.

unwirtlich.proTip: Root connection: related to der Wirt (host / innkeeper) and gastfreundlich / wirtlich (hospitable). Thus unwirtlich literally means 'inhospitable / not welcoming to guests'. Antonym: einladend, gastfreundlich.

ungefähr.note: Adverb meaning 'approximately, roughly, about, around'. As an adverb, ungefähr is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples demonstrate case declension on noun phrases modified by or appearing alongside ungefähr.

nominative.german: Ungefähr dreihundert begeisterte Gäste besuchten die feierliche Eröffnung des Museums.
nominative.english: Approximately three hundred enthusiastic guests attended the ceremonial opening of the museum.
nominative.hint: Subject of besuchten, so nominative plural. Adverb ungefähr modifies the numeral dreihundert; plural ending -e on begeisterte.

accusative.german: Der Handwerker schätzte den ungefähr doppelten Preis für die Reparatur des Dachs.
accusative.english: The craftsman estimated roughly double the price for the repair of the roof.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schätzte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on doppelten.

dative.german: In ungefähr fünfzehn Minuten erreicht der ICE-Zug den Hauptbahnhof.
dative.english: In approximately fifteen minutes the ICE train reaches the central station.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (time span). Plural noun Minuten ends in -n in dative plural.

genitive.german: Trotz des ungefähr gleichen Werts beider Gemälde wählte der Käufer das Landschaftsbild.
genitive.english: Despite the approximately equal value of both paintings the buyer chose the landscape.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gleichen; noun Wert adds -s.

ungefähr.proTip: Ungefähr functions as an adverb/particle modifying numbers or adjectives: 'Es kostet ungefähr 20 Euro'. Idiom: 'von ungefähr kommen' (to come about by chance): 'Das kommt nicht von ungefähr' (That's no coincidence / that didn't happen by accident).

bewohnt.note: Adjective derived from the past participle of bewohnen, meaning 'inhabited, occupied, lived-in'. Declines when placed before a noun according to standard German adjective endings. Antonym: unbewohnt (uninhabited).

nominative.german: Das malerische Schloss ist seit über zweihundert Jahren durchgehend bewohnt.
nominative.english: The picturesque castle has been continuously inhabited for over two hundred years.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on malerische; bewohnt is the predicate adjective.

accusative.german: Die Archäologen betraten den bis heute bewohnten Flügel der alten Burganlage.
accusative.english: The archaeologists entered the wing of the old castle complex that is inhabited to this day.
accusative.hint: Direct object of betraten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on bewohnten.

dative.german: Auf dieser dauerhaft bewohnten Insel gibt es eine kleine Schule für dreißig Kinder.
dative.english: On this permanently inhabited island there is a small school for thirty children.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on bewohnten.

genitive.german: Wegen des bewohnten Zustands des Gebäudes durften die Abrissarbeiten nicht beginnen.
genitive.english: Because of the inhabited state of the building the demolition work was not allowed to begin.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on bewohnten; noun Zustand adds -s.

bewohnt.proTip: Can be used attributively ('ein bewohntes Haus') or predicatively ('Das Haus ist bewohnt'). From bewohnen (transitive: 'Sie bewohnen das Haus'). Negative prefix: unbewohnt ('eine unbewohnte Insel' = an uninhabited island).

inklusive.note: Preposition meaning 'including, inclusive of'. In formal and standard written German, inklusive strictly governs the GENITIVE case (e.g. inklusive der Steuern, inklusive des Frühstücks). When used with a masculine or neuter noun without an article or adjective, dative or uninflected form is also permitted by Duden.

nominative.german: Der gesamte Preis inklusive aller Nebenkosten beträgt zweihundert Euro.
nominative.english: The entire price including all incidental costs amounts to two hundred euros.
nominative.hint: Subject of beträgt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on gesamte.

accusative.german: Wir buchten das komplette Urlaubspaket inklusive eines reichhaltigen Frühstücksbuffets.
accusative.english: We booked the complete holiday package including a rich breakfast buffet.
accusative.hint: Direct object of buchten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on komplette.

dative.german: Zu einem fairen Pauschalpreis inklusive der Anreise bietet das Hotel diesen Kurzurlaub an.
dative.english: At a fair all-inclusive price including travel the hotel offers this short break.
dative.hint: Dative governed by zu. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on fairen.

genitive.german: Das Zimmer kostet hundert Euro pro Nacht inklusive des reichhaltigen Frühstücks.
genitive.english: The room costs one hundred euros per night including the rich breakfast.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by the preposition inklusive. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on reichhaltigen; noun Frühstück adds -s.

inklusive.proTip: Preposition grammar rule: inklusive is a GENITIVE preposition: 'inklusive des Versands' (including shipping); 'inklusive aller Gebühren' (inclusive of all fees). Antonym: exklusive (excluding, also governs genitive). Common abbreviation in business: inkl.

organisch.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'organic' (chemistry, agriculture, biology, or natural structural growth). Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Organischer Abfall aus der Küche eignet sich hervorragend für den heimischen Komposthaufen.
nominative.english: Organic waste from the kitchen is outstandingly suitable for the domestic compost heap.
