nominative.hint: Subject of eignet sich, so nominative. Strong declension without an article: masculine nominative takes strong ending -er on Organischer.

accusative.german: Die Bauern verwenden ausschließlich organischen Dünger auf ihren Feldern.
accusative.english: The farmers exclusively use organic fertilizer on their fields.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verwenden, so accusative. Strong declension without an article: masculine accusative takes strong ending -en on organischen.

dative.german: Mit organischem Material lässt sich die Bodenqualität im Garten nachhaltig verbessern.
dative.english: With organic material soil quality in the garden can be sustainably improved.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on organischem.

genitive.german: Die langsame Zersetzung des organischen Mülls erzeugt wertvollen Humus.
genitive.english: The slow decomposition of organic garbage produces valuable humus.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zersetzung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on organischen; noun Müll adds -s.

organisch.proTip: Multiple contexts: 1. Environmental/agricultural: organische Abfälle (organic waste); 2. Chemistry: organische Chemie (organic chemistry = carbon compounds); 3. Figurative/organizational: organisches Wachstum (organic/natural growth). Antonym: anorganisch (inorganic).

endlich.note: Adverb meaning 'finally, at last' (expressing relief or long-awaited outcome), or adjective meaning 'finite, limited' (mathematics, philosophy). As an adverb, it does not decline; as an adjective, it declines according to standard adjective rules.

nominative.german: Der lang ersehnte Sommerurlaub beginnt endlich nach Monaten harter Arbeit.
nominative.english: The long-awaited summer holiday finally begins after months of hard work.
nominative.hint: Subject of beginnt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on ersehnte; adverb endlich modifies the clause.

accusative.german: Nach stundenlangem Suchen fand der Mechaniker den lange vermissten Schraubenschlüssel endlich.
accusative.english: After hours of searching the mechanic finally found the long-missing wrench.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fand, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on vermissten.

dative.german: Nach einer endlos scheinenden Wartezeit traf der verspätete Zug endlich am Bahnhof ein.
dative.english: After an endless-seeming wait the delayed train finally arrived at the station.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on scheinenden.

genitive.german: Die Anerkennung des endlichen Charakters menschlicher Ressourcen ist für den Klimaschutz essenziell.
genitive.english: Recognition of the finite character of human resources is essential for climate protection.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Anerkennung. Adjectival use of endlich (finite): masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on endlichen; noun adds -s.

endlich.proTip: Two distinct roles: 1. Adverb: 'Endlich bist du da!' (Finally you are here! — expresses relief); 2. Adjective meaning finite: 'Die Ressourcen der Erde sind endlich' (The earth's resources are finite). Antonym of the adjective is unendlich (infinite / endless).

bewegungslos.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'motionless, still, immobile'. Formed from Bewegung (movement) + suffix -los (-less). Declines according to standard adjective endings when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used predicatively or adverbially.

nominative.german: Die kleine Eidechse verharrt bewegungslos auf dem sonnengewärmten Stein.
nominative.english: The little lizard remains motionless on the sun-warmed stone.
nominative.hint: Subject of verharrt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e on kleine; bewegungslos functions adverbially/predicatively.

accusative.german: Der Jäger beobachtete den bewegungslosen Rehbock am Waldrand durch das Fernglas.
accusative.english: The hunter observed the motionless roebuck at the edge of the forest through binoculars.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beobachtete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on bewegungslosen.

dative.german: In bewegungslosem Zustand verharrte die Schlange viele Minuten lang.
dative.english: In a motionless state the snake remained for many minutes.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (state/condition). Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on bewegungslosem.

genitive.german: Wegen des bewegungslosen Verharrens des Tiers bemerkte der Wanderer es zunächst nicht.
genitive.english: Because of the animal's motionless pausing the hiker did not notice it at first.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on bewegungslosen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

bewegungslos.proTip: Suffix -los corresponds to English '-less' and turns nouns into negative adjectives: bewegungslos (motionless), schlaflos (sleepless), harmlos (harmless). Uninflected in predicate position: 'Der Patient lag bewegungslos im Bett'.

unwahrscheinlich.note: Adjective meaning 'unlikely, improbable' (odds, events) or colloquially 'incredible, extraordinary' (huge effort/talent). Declines according to regular adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein solcher Zufall ist im Alltag extrem unwahrscheinlich.
nominative.english: Such a coincidence is extremely unlikely in everyday life.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; adjective/determiner solcher; unwahrscheinlich is the predicate adjective.

accusative.german: Der Experte schloss ein derart unwahrscheinliches Szenario von vornherein aus.
accusative.english: The expert ruled out such an unlikely scenario from the outset.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schloss ... aus, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on unwahrscheinliches.

dative.german: Bei einem so unwahrscheinlichen Ausgang der Wahl wären alle Analysten überrascht.
dative.english: With such an unlikely outcome of the election all analysts would be surprised.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; weak adjective ending -en on unwahrscheinlichen.

genitive.german: Trotz des unwahrscheinlichen Erfolgs investierte der Unternehmer mutig in das Startup.
genitive.english: Despite the unlikely success the entrepreneur boldly invested in the startup.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on unwahrscheinlichen; noun Erfolg adds -s.

unwahrscheinlich.proTip: Two distinct registers: 1. Formal probability: 'Es ist höchst unwahrscheinlich, dass...' (It is highly improbable that...); 2. Colloquial intensifier meaning 'immense / incredible': 'Wir hatten unwahrscheinlich viel Glück' (We had incredible luck!).

aktiv.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'active, dynamic, participatory' (sports, volcanoes, participation). Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used predicatively.

nominative.german: Ein aktiver Vulkan auf der Insel stößt regelmäßig heiße Gase und Asche aus.
nominative.english: An active volcano on the island regularly spews hot gases and ash.
nominative.hint: Subject of stößt ... aus, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension: indefinite article ein has no ending; aktiver takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Schule fördert einen aktiven Lebensstil durch tägliche Sportstunden.
accusative.english: The school promotes an active lifestyle through daily sports lessons.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fördert, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on aktiven.

dative.german: Mit aktiver Teilnahme an den Seminaren sichern sich die Studierenden wichtige Bonuspunkte.
dative.english: With active participation in the seminars the students secure important bonus points.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on aktiver.

genitive.german: Die Vorteile eines aktiven Lebens sind durch zahlreiche Studien wissenschaftlich belegt.
genitive.english: The benefits of an active life are scientifically proven by numerous studies.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vorteile. Neuter genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on aktiven; noun Leben adds -s.

aktiv.proTip: Antonym: passiv (passive). Fixed grammar terminology: das Aktiv (the active voice) vs. das Passiv (the passive voice). Collocation: 'aktiv werden' (to take action / get active).

intelligent.note: Descriptive adjective of foreign origin (ending in -ent) meaning 'intelligent, clever, bright, smart' (persons, algorithms, solutions). Declines according to regular adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Der hochgradig intelligente Schüler löst die komplizierte mathematische Aufgabe mühelos.
nominative.english: The highly intelligent student solves the complicated mathematical problem effortlessly.
nominative.hint: Subject of löst, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on intelligente.

accusative.german: Die Ingenieure entwickelten eine intelligente Lösung für die effiziente Energiespeicherung.
accusative.english: The engineers developed an intelligent solution for efficient energy storage.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwickelten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on intelligente.

dative.german: Mit einem intelligenten Stromnetz lassen sich Stromausfälle im Winter zuverlässig verhindern.
dative.english: With a smart power grid blackouts in winter can be reliably prevented.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on intelligenten.

genitive.german: Das Verhalten eines intelligenten Tieres unterscheidet sich deutlich von reinen Reflexen.
genitive.english: The behavior of an intelligent animal differs clearly from pure reflexes.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Verhalten. Neuter genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on intelligenten; noun Tier adds -es.

intelligent.proTip: Comparative: intelligenter, am intelligentesten. Related noun: die Intelligenz (intelligence). Modern technical collocations: 'künstliche Intelligenz' (artificial intelligence); 'intelligente Haushaltsgeräte' (smart household appliances).

subjektiv.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'subjective, personal, biased' (opinions, evaluations). Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun. Antonym: objektiv (objective).

nominative.german: Eine rein subjektive Wahrnehmung kann die objektive Realität der Lage verzerren.
nominative.english: A purely subjective perception can distort the objective reality of the situation.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann verzerren, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on subjektive.

accusative.german: Der Kritiker äußerte ein sehr subjektives Urteil über die Ausstellung moderner Kunst.
accusative.english: The critic expressed a very subjective verdict on the exhibition of modern art.
accusative.hint: Direct object of äußerte, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on subjektives.

dative.german: Nach meinem rein subjektiven Empfinden war die Prüfung schwieriger als im Vorjahr.
dative.english: According to my purely subjective feeling the exam was more difficult than the previous year.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Neuter dative possessive meinem; weak adjective ending -en on subjektiven.

genitive.german: Wegen des subjektiven Charakters der Bewertung verlangten die Schüler eine zweite Korrektur.
genitive.english: Because of the subjective character of the evaluation the students demanded a second grading.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on subjektiven; noun Charakter adds -s.

subjektiv.proTip: Core philosophical/scientific pair: subjektiv (based on personal perspective) vs. objektiv (fact-based, neutral). Adverbial use: 'Das sehe ich ganz subjektiv' (I see that completely subjectively).

rational.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'rational, logical, reasonable' (decisions, arguments, behavior). Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun. Antonym: irrational (irrational).

nominative.german: Ein rational denkender Mensch analysiert die Fakten gründlich vor einer Entscheidung.
nominative.english: A rationally thinking person analyzes the facts thoroughly before making a decision.
nominative.hint: Subject of analysiert, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; participle/adjective ending -er on denkender; rational functions adverbially.

accusative.german: Die Geschäftsführung traf eine rationale Entscheidung zum Wohl des gesamten Unternehmens.
accusative.english: The management made a rational decision for the welfare of the entire company.
accusative.hint: Direct object of traf, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on rationale.

dative.german: Mit rein rationalem Denken lassen sich manche emotionale Probleme nicht vollständig lösen.
dative.english: With purely rational thinking some emotional problems cannot be completely solved.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on rationalem.

genitive.german: Die Vorzüge eines rationalen Handelns liegen in der verlässlichen Planbarkeit von Projekten.
genitive.english: The advantages of rational action lie in the reliable predictability of projects.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vorzüge. Neuter genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on rationalen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

rational.proTip: In economics and mathematics: 'rationale Zahlen' (rational numbers). In psychology/philosophy: 'rational' contrasts with 'emotional' or 'intuitiv'. Related noun: die Rationalität / das Rationale.

empfänglich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'receptive, susceptible, open' (to ideas, suggestions, flattery, or diseases). Declines according to regular adjective declension. Commonly governs für + accusative (empfänglich für etwas sein).

nominative.german: Ein offener Geist ist stets empfänglich für neue Ideen und kreative Vorschläge.
nominative.english: An open mind is always receptive to new ideas and creative suggestions.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on offener; empfänglich is the predicate adjective.

accusative.german: Die Werbung zielt besonders auf ein leicht empfängliches Publikum im jugendlichen Alter ab.
accusative.english: Advertising aims especially at an easily receptive audience in teenage years.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the preposition auf. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on empfängliches.

dative.german: Bei einem für Infektionen empfänglichen Körper ist eine gesunde Ernährung besonders wichtig.
dative.english: With a body susceptible to infections a healthy diet is particularly important.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; weak adjective ending -en on empfänglichen.

genitive.german: Die Beeinflussbarkeit eines überaus empfänglichen Gemüts wurde von den Betrügern ausgenutzt.
genitive.english: The suggestibility of an exceedingly receptive disposition was exploited by the fraudsters.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Beeinflussbarkeit. Neuter genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on empfänglichen; noun Gemüt adds -s.

empfänglich.proTip: Fixed preposition pattern: 'empfänglich für (+ Akkusativ) sein': 'Er ist für Schmeicheleien sehr empfänglich' (He is very susceptible to flattery). Medical: 'empfänglich für Krankheiten' (susceptible to diseases).

neuronal.note: Technical scientific adjective meaning 'neural, relating to nerve cells or the nervous system'. Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun. Widely used in neuroscience, medicine, and machine learning.

nominative.german: Ein künstliches neuronales Netz lernt durch wiederholtes Training an großen Datenmengen.
nominative.english: An artificial neural network learns through repeated training on large datasets.
nominative.hint: Subject of lernt, so nominative. Neuter mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective endings -es on künstliches and neuronales.

accusative.german: Die Forscher analysierten die neuronale Aktivität im Gehirn während des Schlafens.
accusative.english: The researchers analyzed the neural activity in the brain during sleep.
accusative.hint: Direct object of analysierten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on neuronale.

dative.german: Mit hochentwickelten neuronalen Netzwerken lassen sich komplexe Muster präzise erkennen.
dative.english: With highly developed neural networks complex patterns can be precisely identified.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension plural without an article: dative plural ending -en on hochentwickelten and neuronalen; noun Netzwerk adds -en.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung des neuronalen Systems liefert bahnbrechende Erkenntnisse für die Medizin.
genitive.english: Research into the neural system provides groundbreaking insights for medicine.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on neuronalen; noun System adds -s.

neuronal.proTip: Prominent modern technical term in AI: 'neuronale Netze' (neural networks) / 'ein künstliches neuronales Netzwerk' (an artificial neural network). In biology/medicine: 'neuronale Verbindungen' (neural connections / synapses).

biologisch.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'biological, organic, biodegradable'. Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially or predicatively.

nominative.german: Biologischer Landbau schont die Umwelt und verzichtet auf chemische Pflanzenschutzmittel.
nominative.english: Organic farming protects the environment and dispenses with chemical pesticides.
nominative.hint: Subject of schont, so nominative. Strong declension without an article: masculine nominative takes strong ending -er on Biologischer.

accusative.german: Immer mehr Verbraucher kaufen biologische Lebensmittel aus der regionalen Erzeugung.
accusative.english: More and more consumers buy organic groceries from regional production.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kaufen, so accusative plural. Strong declension without an article: plural accusative takes ending -e on biologische.

dative.german: Aus biologischem Anbau schmeckt das frische Gemüse den meisten Menschen besser.
dative.english: From organic cultivation the fresh vegetables taste better to most people.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on biologischem.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung des biologischen Abbaus von Kunststoffen ist eine dringliche Aufgabe.
genitive.english: Research into the biological decomposition of plastics is an urgent task.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on biologischen; noun Abbau adds -s.

biologisch.proTip: Colloquially shortened to 'Bio-': 'Bio-Gemüse', 'Bio-Eier', 'im Bio-Laden'. Note environmental term: 'biologisch abbaubar' (biodegradable).

verwandt.note: Adjective meaning 'related, kindred, affiliated' (by family blood/kinship, or linguistically/intellectually). Declines when used before a noun. Often used as an adjectival noun: der Verwandte / ein Verwandter (relative/kin). Commonly takes mit + dative (verwandt mit + dat).

nominative.german: Die beiden ostslawischen Sprachen sind eng miteinander verwandt.
nominative.english: The two East Slavic languages are closely related to one another.
nominative.hint: Subject of sind, so nominative plural. Plural nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -en on beiden and ostslawischen; verwandt is predicate adjective.

accusative.german: Der Forscher untersuchte einen nah verwandten Dialekt in den Alpenregionen.
accusative.english: The researcher investigated a closely related dialect in the Alpine regions.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on verwandten.

dative.german: Zu einem weit entfernten Verwandten hatte die Familie seit Jahrzehnten keinen Kontakt.
dative.english: The family had had no contact with a distant relative for decades.
dative.hint: Dative governed by zu. Masculine dative article einem; weak adjective endings -en on entfernten and adjectival noun Verwandten.

genitive.german: Der Besuch eines wohlhabenden Verwandten aus Übersee sorgte für große Aufregung.
genitive.english: The visit of a wealthy relative from overseas caused great excitement.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Besuch. Masculine genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on wohlhabenden and adjectival noun Verwandten.

verwandt.proTip: Watch out for adjectival noun declension: 'mein Verwandter' (nom), 'meinen Verwandten' (akk), 'meinem Verwandten' (dat), 'meines Verwandten' (gen). Key construction: 'verwandt mit (+ Dativ) sein': 'Er ist mit mir verwandt' (He is related to me).

neutral.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'neutral, impartial, unbiased' (politics, chemistry, linguistics). Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used predicatively.

nominative.german: Ein neutraler Beobachter dokumentiert den ordnungsgemäßen Ablauf der Wahlen.
nominative.english: A neutral observer documents the orderly conduct of the elections.
nominative.hint: Subject of dokumentiert, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension: indefinite article Ein has no ending; neutraler takes strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Schweiz wahrte eine neutrale Haltung während beider Weltkriege.
accusative.english: Switzerland maintained a neutral stance during both world wars.
accusative.hint: Direct object of wahrte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on neutrale.

dative.german: Auf neutralem Boden trafen sich die beiden Konfliktparteien zu Friedensgesprächen.
dative.english: The two conflicting parties met on neutral ground for peace talks.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on neutralem.

genitive.german: Die Bestätigung des neutralen Standpunkts des Vermittlers war für alle Beteiligten wichtig.
genitive.english: Confirmation of the mediator's neutral point of view was important for all parties involved.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bestätigung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on neutralen; noun Standpunkt adds -s.

neutral.proTip: Contexts: 1. Political: neutrale Staaten (neutral states); 2. Chemistry: eine neutrale Lösung (pH 7); 3. Physics: elektrisch neutral (electrically neutral). Adverbial: 'sich neutral verhalten' (to remain neutral).

kostenlos.note: Adjective and adverb meaning 'free of charge, complimentary, gratis'. Formed from Kosten (costs) + suffix -los (-less). Declines when placed before a noun; uninflected as an adverb.

nominative.german: Ein kostenloser Shuttlebus bringt die Fluggäste alle zehn Minuten zum Terminal.
nominative.english: A free shuttle bus takes passengers to the terminal every ten minutes.
nominative.hint: Subject of bringt, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on kostenloser.

accusative.german: Der Verlag bietet einen kostenlosen Download der ersten drei Kapitel des Buchs an.
accusative.english: The publisher offers a free download of the first three chapters of the book.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bietet ... an, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on kostenlosen.

dative.german: Mit kostenlosem WLAN locken viele moderne Cafés neue Kundschaft an.
dative.english: With free Wi-Fi many modern cafés attract new clientele.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on kostenlosem.

genitive.german: Die Bereitstellung eines kostenlosen Parkplatzes ist ein großer Vorteil des Hotels.
genitive.english: The provision of a free parking space is a big advantage of the hotel.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bereitstellung. Masculine genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on kostenlosen; noun Parkplatz adds -es.

kostenlos.proTip: Synonyms: gratis, kostenfrei, umsonst. Note subtle distinction: 'umsonst' can mean both 'free of charge' and 'in vain' ('Ich habe umsonst gewartet' = I waited in vain), whereas 'kostenlos' unambiguously means without cost.

doppelt.note: Numerical adjective and adverb meaning 'double, twofold, twice'. Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Die doppelte Menge an Mehl wird für das große Festtagsbrot benötigt.
nominative.english: Double the amount of flour is required for the big celebration bread.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird benötigt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on doppelte.

accusative.german: Der hungrige Gast bestellte den doppelten Espresso am Tresen.
accusative.english: The hungry guest ordered the double espresso at the counter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bestellte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on doppelten.

dative.german: Mit doppeltem Boden sicherte der Zauberkünstler seine geheimnisvolle Kiste ab.
dative.english: With a false bottom the magician secured his mysterious box.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on doppeltem.

genitive.german: Wegen des doppelten Gewinns im letzten Quartal zahlte der Chef eine Sonderprämie aus.
genitive.english: Because of the double profit in the last quarter the boss paid out a special bonus.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on doppelten; noun Gewinn adds -s.

doppelt.proTip: Adverbial usage: 'doppelt so viel' (twice as much); 'doppelt gemoppelt' (colloquial: tautological / redundant). Idiom: 'ein doppelter Boden' (a false bottom / safety net).

gern.note: Modal adverb meaning 'gladly, willingly, with pleasure, like to'. As an adverb, gern (or gerne) is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing gern. Comparative: lieber (rather / prefer to); superlative: am liebsten (most of all).

nominative.german: Der hilfsbereite Nachbar leiht gern sein neues Werkzeug an Freunde aus.
nominative.english: The helpful neighbor gladly lends his new tools to friends.
nominative.hint: Subject of leiht ... aus, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on hilfsbereite; gern is a modal adverb.

accusative.german: Ich trinke jeden Morgen gern einen frisch gebrühten Kaffee zum Frühstück.
accusative.english: I gladly drink a freshly brewed coffee every morning with breakfast.
accusative.hint: Direct object of trinke, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on gebrühten.

dative.german: Mit großem Vergnügen hilft sie ihren jüngeren Geschwistern gern bei den Hausaufgaben.
dative.english: With great pleasure she gladly helps her younger siblings with their homework.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by helfen (jemandem helfen). Plural dative possessive ihren; weak adjective ending -en on jüngeren; noun ends in -n.

genitive.german: Wegen des hervorragenden Geschmacks essen viele Touristen die lokale Spezialität besonders gern.
genitive.english: Because of the outstanding taste many tourists eat the local specialty particularly gladly.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hervorragenden; noun Geschmack adds -s.

gern.proTip: In German, 'gern' is an adverb used with verbs to express 'to like doing something': 'Ich lese gern' = I like reading; 'Ich koche gern' = I like cooking. Do not use 'mögen' for activities; use verb + gern! Both 'gern' and 'gerne' are completely interchangeable and correct.

gelb.note: Color adjective meaning 'yellow'. Declines according to standard German adjective endings when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used predicatively.

nominative.german: Ein gelber Kanarienvogel singt wunderschöne Lieder auf dem Balkon.
nominative.english: A yellow canary sings beautiful songs on the balcony.
nominative.hint: Subject of singt, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on gelber.

accusative.german: Der Postbote warf die Briefe in den gelben Briefkasten an der Straßenecke.
accusative.english: The postman dropped the letters into the yellow postbox at the street corner.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by in (direction/destination). Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gelben.

dative.german: Mit einer leuchtend gelben Warnweste ist der Fahrradfahrer im Nebel gut sichtbar.
dative.english: With a bright yellow high-visibility vest the cyclist is clearly visible in the fog.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on gelben.

genitive.german: Die intensive Farbe des gelben Löwenzahns leuchtet über die gesamte Frühlingswiese.
genitive.english: The intense color of the yellow dandelion shines across the entire spring meadow.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Farbe. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gelben; noun Löwenzahn adds -s.

gelb.proTip: Idioms with gelb: 'das Gelbe vom Ei' (the best part / the cream of the crop; often negative: 'Das ist nicht gerade das Gelbe vom Ei' = That's not ideal); 'gelb vor Neid' (green/yellow with envy). In soccer: 'die Gelbe Karte' (the yellow card).

verbreitet.note: Adjective derived from the past participle of verbreiten, meaning 'widespread, common, prevalent, widely circulated'. Declines when placed before a noun according to regular adjective declension.

nominative.german: Ein weit verbreiteter Irrglaube besagt, dass Fledermäuse völlig blind seien.
nominative.english: A widespread misconception states that bats are completely blind.
nominative.hint: Subject of besagt, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on verbreiteter.

accusative.german: Der Dozent widerlegte das weit verbreitete Vorurteil anhand zahlreicher empirischer Daten.
accusative.english: The lecturer refuted the widespread prejudice using numerous empirical data.
accusative.hint: Direct object of widerlegte, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on verbreitete.

dative.german: In vielen weit verbreiteten Mundarten wird das Wort ganz anders ausgesprochen.
dative.english: In many widespread dialects the word is pronounced completely differently.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Plural dative determiner vielen; weak adjective ending -en on verbreiteten; noun Mundart adds -en.

genitive.german: Trotz des weit verbreiteten Zweifels setzte die Forscherin ihre Studien unermüdlich fort.
genitive.english: Despite widespread doubt the researcher continued her studies tirelessly.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on verbreiteten; noun Zweifel adds -s.

verbreitet.proTip: Frequently combined with weit: 'weit verbreitet' (widespread). Verb: verbreiten (to spread, circulate: 'Nachrichten verbreiten'). Reflexive: sich verbreiten ('Das Virus verbreitet sich rasch').

massereich.note: Technical and scientific adjective meaning 'massive, having high mass' (used in astrophysics for stars and black holes, or nuclear physics). Formed from Masse (mass) + suffix -reich (rich in). Declines according to regular adjective declension.

nominative.german: Ein extrem massereicher Stern explodiert am Ende seines Lebens als Supernova.
nominative.english: An extremely massive star explodes as a supernova at the end of its life.
nominative.hint: Subject of explodiert, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on massereicher.

accusative.german: Die Astrophysiker entdeckten ein supermassereiches Schwarzes Loch im Zentrum der Galaxie.
accusative.english: The astrophysicists discovered a supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entdeckten, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on supermassereiches.

dative.german: Bei einem extrem massereichen Stern herrschen im Kern unvorstellbare Druckverhältnisse.
dative.english: In an extremely massive star unimaginable pressure conditions prevail in the core.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; weak adjective ending -en on massereichen.

genitive.german: Die gewaltige Gravitation eines massereichen Objekts krümmt den umgebenden Raum spürbar.
genitive.english: The enormous gravitation of a massive object noticeably curves the surrounding space.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gravitation. Neuter genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on massereichen; noun Objekt adds -s.

massereich.proTip: Distinguish from massiv: 'massereich' specifically means possessing huge physical mass in physics/astronomy (massereiche Sterne), while 'massiv' means physically solid/heavy or figuratively severe/massive (massive Kritik / massives Holz).

maschinell.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'mechanical, machine-made, by machine, automated'. Formed from Maschine (machine) + suffix -ell. Declines when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially. Antonym: manuell / von Hand (manual / by hand).

nominative.german: Die maschinelle Bearbeitung von Metallteilen garantiert eine gleichbleibend hohe Qualität.
nominative.english: The mechanical processing of metal parts guarantees consistently high quality.
nominative.hint: Subject of garantiert, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on maschinelle.

accusative.german: Die moderne Weberei ersetzte die mühsame Handarbeit durch einen vollautomatischen maschinellen Prozess.
accusative.english: The modern weaving mill replaced laborious handwork with a fully automatic mechanical process.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by durch. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective endings -en on vollautomatischen and maschinellen.

dative.german: Mit maschineller Unterstützung können die Arbeiter schwere Lasten mühelos bewegen.
dative.english: With mechanical support the workers can move heavy loads effortlessly.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on maschineller.

genitive.german: Die Umstellung auf die Kosten der maschinellen Fertigung hat sich für den Betrieb schnell bezahlt gemacht.
genitive.english: Switching to the costs of machine production paid off quickly for the enterprise.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on maschinellen.

maschinell.proTip: Adverbial usage: 'maschinell hergestellt' (manufactured by machine) vs. 'handgefertigt' (handmade). Contrast: 'mechanisch' refers to the laws of mechanics/physics, whereas 'maschinell' refers specifically to machines doing work.

grob.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 1. 'coarse, rough' (sand, fabric, surface); 2. 'rough, approximate' (estimate, overview); 3. 'crude, rude' (behavior); 4. 'gross, severe' (negligence, error: grobe Fahrlässigkeit). Declines regularly, but takes umlaut in comparative: gröber, am gröbsten.

nominative.german: Ein grober Fehler in der Software führte zum Absturz des gesamten Serversystems.
nominative.english: A gross error in the software led to the crash of the entire server system.
nominative.hint: Subject of führte, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on grober.

accusative.german: Der Polizist ahndete das grobe Fehlverhalten des rücksichtslosen Autofahrers streng.
accusative.english: The police officer punished the gross misconduct of the reckless driver severely.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ahndete, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on grobe.

dative.german: Mit einem groben Pinselstrich vollendete der Maler den Hintergrund der Landschaft.
dative.english: With a broad brushstroke the painter completed the background of the landscape.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on groben.

genitive.german: Wegen grober Fahrlässigkeit lehnte die Versicherung die Übernahme der Schäden ab.
genitive.english: Because of gross negligence the insurance rejected coverage of the damages.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Strong declension without an article: feminine genitive takes strong ending -er on grober.

grob.proTip: Legal and professional collocation: 'grobe Fahrlässigkeit' (gross negligence). Texture: 'grober Sand' (coarse sand) vs. 'feiner Sand' (fine sand). Approximate: 'eine grobe Schätzung' (a rough estimate). Comparative: gröber, am gröbsten.

mittlerweile.note: Temporal adverb meaning 'meanwhile, by now, in the meantime'. As an adverb, mittlerweile does not inflect for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing mittlerweile.

nominative.german: Die renommierte Universität zählt mittlerweile zu den besten Hochschulen Europas.
nominative.english: The renowned university is by now counted among the best universities in Europe.
nominative.hint: Subject of zählt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on renommierte; mittlerweile is a temporal adverb.

accusative.german: Die junge Firma beherrscht mittlerweile den gesamten Inlandsmarkt für Elektrofahrräder.
accusative.english: The young firm by now dominates the entire domestic market for electric bicycles.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beherrscht, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

dative.german: Mit großer Selbstverständlichkeit nutzen mittlerweile auch Senioren moderne Smartphones.
dative.english: With great naturalness seniors also by now use modern smartphones.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on großer.

genitive.german: Trotz des mittlerweile hohen Alters arbeitet der berühmte Dirigent weiterhin mit voller Energie.
genitive.english: Despite his by now advanced age the famous conductor continues to work with full energy.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hohen; noun Alter adds -s.

mittlerweile.proTip: Synonyms: inzwischen, unterdessen, mit der Zeit. Indicates the result of a progression over time up to the present or reference point: 'Er ist mittlerweile Vater geworden' (He has by now become a father).

übrig.note: Predicate adjective and adverb meaning 'left over, remaining, residual' (übrig sein / übrig bleiben) or attributive adjective (das übrige Geld = the remaining money). Attributive uses decline according to regular adjective declension.

nominative.german: Das übrige Essen vom Festessen wurde sorgfältig im Kühlschrank aufbewahrt.
nominative.english: The leftover food from the feast was carefully stored in the refrigerator.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde aufbewahrt, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on übrige.

accusative.german: Der sparsame Student sparte den ganzen übrigen Betrag für Notfälle.
accusative.english: The thrifty student saved the entire remaining amount for emergencies.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sparte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective endings -en on ganzen and übrigen.

dative.german: Von dem übrigen Kuchen gab die Mutter den Nachbarskindern ein großes Stück ab.
dative.english: From the remaining cake the mother gave the neighbor's children a big piece.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on übrigen.

genitive.german: Die Aufteilung des übrigen Vermögens des Erblassers erfolgte nach dem Testament.
genitive.english: The distribution of the remaining estate of the testator took place according to the will.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Aufteilung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on übrigen; noun Vermögen adds -s.

übrig.proTip: Common idioms: 'übrig bleiben' (to remain / be left over: 'Es bleibt nichts übrig'); 'übrig haben' (to have to spare: 'Hast du etwas Geld für mich übrig?'); 'im Übrigen' (incidentally / moreover).

überall.note: Local adverb meaning 'everywhere, all over, in all places'. As an adverb, überall is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples demonstrate case declension on noun phrases in sentences containing überall.

nominative.german: Die bunte Blumenpracht blüht im Frühling überall in den städtischen Parks.
nominative.english: The colorful floral splendor blooms everywhere in the municipal parks in spring.
nominative.hint: Subject of blüht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on bunte; überall is a local adverb.

accusative.german: Die Reisenden suchten überall in der fremden Stadt ein gemütliches Restaurant für das Abendessen.
accusative.english: The travelers searched everywhere in the unfamiliar city for a cozy restaurant for dinner.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchten, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on gemütliches.

dative.german: Mit neugierigen Blicken suchten die Kinder überall nach den versteckten Ostereiern.
dative.english: With curious looks the children searched everywhere for the hidden Easter eggs.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension plural without an article: dative plural ending -en on neugierigen; noun Blick adds -en.

genitive.german: Die Spuren des überall sichtbaren Verfalls der alten Fabrik stimmten die Besucher traurig.
genitive.english: The traces of the everywhere visible decay of the old factory made the visitors sad.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Spuren. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on sichtbaren; noun Verfall adds -s.

überall.proTip: Adverb pairs: überall (everywhere) vs. nirgends / nirgendwo (nowhere). Fixed expressions: 'überall auf der Welt' (all over the world); 'überall und nirgends' (here, there, and everywhere / nowhere in particular).

beachtlich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'considerable, remarkable, substantial, noteworthy' (amount, achievement, size). Formed from beachten (to pay attention to) + suffix -lich. Declines according to standard adjective endings when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein beachtlicher Erfolg krönte die jahrelange Forschungsarbeit des Teams.
nominative.english: A considerable success crowned the years of research work of the team.
nominative.hint: Subject of krönte, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on beachtlicher.

accusative.german: Die Sportlerin erzielte eine beachtliche Leistungssteigerung im Vergleich zum Vorjahr.
accusative.english: The athlete achieved a remarkable increase in performance compared to the previous year.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erzielte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on beachtliche.

dative.german: Mit beachtlichem Aufwand renovierte die Familie das denkmalgeschützte Bauernhaus.
dative.english: With considerable effort the family renovated the heritage-listed farmhouse.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on beachtlichem.

genitive.german: Trotz des beachtlichen Gewinns hielten die Investoren an ihrem Sparkurs fest.
genitive.english: Despite the considerable profit the investors stuck to their austerity course.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on beachtlichen; noun Gewinn adds -s.

beachtlich.proTip: Synonyms: beträchtlich, bemerkenswert, respektabel. Adverbial use: 'Die Zuschauerzahl ist beachtlich gewachsen' (The number of spectators grew considerably). Related verb: beachten (to observe / pay attention to).

unendlich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'infinite, endless, boundless, perpetual'. Formed with the negative prefix un- and the adjective endlich (finite). Declines according to regular adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Die unendliche Weite des Weltalls übersteigt das menschliche Vorstellungsvermögen.
nominative.english: The infinite expanse of outer space exceeds human power of imagination.
nominative.hint: Subject of übersteigt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on unendliche.

accusative.german: Der Dichter beschrieb den unendlichen Ozean in seinen berühmtesten Versen.
accusative.english: The poet described the infinite ocean in his most famous verses.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beschrieb, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on unendlichen.

dative.german: In unendlicher Geduld hörte der alte Meister den Fragen seiner Schüler zu.
dative.english: In infinite patience the old master listened to the questions of his students.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (manner). Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on unendlicher.

genitive.german: Die Faszination des unendlichen Himmels zieht Astronomen seit Jahrtausenden in ihren Bann.
genitive.english: The fascination of the infinite sky has captivated astronomers for millennia.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Faszination. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on unendlichen; noun Himmel adds -s.

unendlich.proTip: Noun: die Unendlichkeit (infinity). Mathematics: das Unendliche / das Unendlich-Zeichen (∞, the infinity symbol). Colloquial intensifier: 'Das hat unendlich viel Spaß gemacht!' (That was endlessly fun!).

geballt.note: Adjective derived from the past participle of ballen, meaning 'concentrated, dense, massed, clenched' (geballte Kraft, geballte Ladung, geballte Faust). Declines according to standard adjective rules when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Geballte Fachkompetenz versammelte sich auf der internationalen Fachtagung für Medizin.
nominative.english: Concentrated specialist expertise gathered at the international medical symposium.
nominative.hint: Subject of versammelte sich, so nominative. Strong declension without an article: feminine nominative takes strong ending -e on Geballte.

accusative.german: Das neue Fachbuch bündelt das geballte Wissen führender Ökonomen unserer Zeit.
accusative.english: The new textbook bundles the concentrated knowledge of leading economists of our time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bündelt, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on geballte.

dative.german: Mit geballter Kraft stemmten die Feuerwehrleute den umgestürzten Baumstamm vom Auto.
dative.english: With concentrated strength the firefighters hoisted the overturned tree trunk off the car.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on geballter.

genitive.german: Wegen des geballten Auftretens von Stürmen wurden viele Flüge vorsorglich gestrichen.
genitive.english: Because of the concentrated occurrence of storms many flights were cancelled as a precaution.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on geballten; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

geballt.proTip: Physical vs. abstract collocations: 1. Physical: 'mit geballter Faust' (with clenched fist); 2. Abstract/figurative: 'geballte Energie' (concentrated energy); 'eine geballte Ladung Information' (a concentrated blast of information).

aufeinander.note: Reciprocal pronominal adverb meaning 'on top of one another, upon each other, consecutively'. As an adverb, aufeinander is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing aufeinander.

nominative.german: Die schweren Holzklötze liegen ordentlich aufeinander gestapelt in der Werkstatt.
nominative.english: The heavy wooden blocks lie neatly stacked on top of one another in the workshop.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegen, so nominative plural. Plural nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -en on schweren; aufeinander is a pronominal adverb.

accusative.german: Die Bauarbeiter stapelten die flachen Steine sorgfältig aufeinander an der Wand.
accusative.english: The construction workers stacked the flat stones carefully on top of one another by the wall.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stapelten, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on flachen.

dative.german: Nach mehreren aufeinander folgenden Niederlagen trennte sich der Verein vom Trainer.
dative.english: After several consecutive defeats the club parted ways with the coach.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Plural dative determiner mehreren; ending -en on folgenden and Niederlagen.

genitive.german: Die Ursache des Aufeinandertreffens der beiden Fahrzeuge konnte schnell geklärt werden.
genitive.english: The cause of the collision of the two vehicles could be clarified quickly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ursache. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized compound adds genitive -s.

aufeinander.proTip: Formed from preposition auf + reciprocal pronoun einander: aufeinander (on each other). Analogous compounds: voneinander (from each other), miteinander (with each other), nacheinander (one after another), zueinander (to each other).

umliegend.note: Adjective derived from the present participle of umliegen, meaning 'surrounding, neighboring, adjoining, adjacent' (villages, countryside, mountains). Declines according to standard German adjective endings when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Die umliegenden Dörfer wurden durch die schwere Überschwemmung von der Außenwelt abgeschnitten.
nominative.english: The surrounding villages were cut off from the outside world by the severe flooding.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurden abgeschnitten, so nominative plural. Plural nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -en on umliegenden.

accusative.german: Die Touristen erkundeten das umliegende Bergland auf gut markierten Wanderwegen.
accusative.english: The tourists explored the surrounding mountain country on well-marked hiking trails.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erkundeten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on umliegende.

dative.german: Aus den umliegenden Gemeinden pendeln täglich tausende Beschäftigte in das Wirtschaftszentrum.
dative.english: From the surrounding municipalities thousands of employees commute daily into the economic center.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Plural dative article den; weak adjective ending -en on umliegenden; noun Gemeinde adds -n.

genitive.german: Die Bürgermeister der umliegenden Orte trafen sich zur gemeinsamen Krisensitzung im Rathaus.
genitive.english: The mayors of the surrounding localities met for a joint crisis session in the town hall.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bürgermeister. Plural genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on umliegenden.

umliegend.proTip: Almost exclusively used in attributive position: 'die umliegenden Gemeinden' (the surrounding communities); 'das umliegende Gelände' (the surrounding terrain). Related preposition: um ... herum (around).

rapide.note: Descriptive adjective and adverb of French origin meaning 'rapid, swift, precipitous' (growth, decline, changes). Declines according to regular adjective declension when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Ein rapider Anstieg der Energiekosten belastet viele kleine und mittlere Betriebe schwer.
nominative.english: A rapid increase in energy costs places a heavy burden on many small and medium-sized businesses.
nominative.hint: Subject of belastet, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on rapider.

accusative.german: Der Meteorologe prognostizierte einen rapiden Temperaturabfall für die kommenden Tage.
accusative.english: The meteorologist forecast a rapid drop in temperature for the coming days.
accusative.hint: Direct object of prognostizierte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on rapiden.

dative.german: Mit rapider Geschwindigkeit breitete sich das Lauffeuer im ausgetrockneten Nadelwald aus.
dative.english: At rapid speed the wildfire spread in the parched coniferous forest.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on rapider.

genitive.german: Wegen des rapiden Verfalls der Währung verloren viele Sparer ihr gesamtes Vermögen.
genitive.english: Because of the rapid collapse of the currency many savers lost their entire fortune.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on rapiden; noun Verfall adds -s.

rapide.proTip: Synonyms: rasch, schnell, rasant, blitzschnell. Often used for dramatic statistical changes: 'rapide zunehmen' (to increase rapidly); 'rapide sinken' (to plummet / drop rapidly).

buchstäblich.note: Adjective and adverb meaning 'literal, literally, verbatim'. Formed from Buchstabe (letter of alphabet) + suffix -lich. Declines when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially to emphasize that a statement is meant word-for-word.

nominative.german: Die buchstäbliche Bedeutung des Begriffs weicht oft vom allgemeinen Sprachgebrauch ab.
nominative.english: The literal meaning of the term often deviates from general linguistic usage.
nominative.hint: Subject of weicht ... ab, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on buchstäbliche.

accusative.german: Der Übersetzer wählte eine buchstäbliche Übersetzung für das alte Sprichwort.
accusative.english: The translator chose a literal translation for the old proverb.
accusative.hint: Direct object of wählte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on buchstäbliche.

dative.german: In buchstäblichem Sinne ging das Schiff samt seiner gesamten Fracht im Sturm unter.
dative.english: In a literal sense the ship went down in the storm together with its entire cargo.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on buchstäblichem.

genitive.german: Die Beachtung des buchstäblichen Wortlauts des Vertrages verhinderte juristische Streitigkeiten.
genitive.english: Observance of the literal wording of the contract prevented legal disputes.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Beachtung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on buchstäblichen; noun Wortlaut adds -s.

buchstäblich.proTip: Root: der Buchstabe (letter of the alphabet). Adverbial use corresponds to English 'literally': 'Er stand buchstäblich vor dem Nichts' (He literally stood with nothing left / faced total ruin).

nett.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'nice, friendly, kind, pleasant' (people, gesture, greeting). Declines according to standard German adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein netter Kollege aus dem Büro half der neuen Mitarbeiterin bei der Einarbeitung.
nominative.english: A nice colleague from the office helped the new employee during onboarding.
nominative.hint: Subject of half, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on netter.

accusative.german: Die Nachbarin schrieb einen netten Brief zum Geburtstag der alten Dame.
accusative.english: The neighbor wrote a nice letter for the old lady's birthday.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schrieb, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on netten.

dative.german: Mit einer netten Geste bedankte sich der Gast beim aufmerksamen Kellner.
dative.english: With a nice gesture the guest thanked the attentive waiter.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on netten.

genitive.german: Wegen des netten Umgangs der Pflegekräfte fühlte sich die Patientin sehr wohl.
genitive.english: Because of the nice manner of the nursing staff the patient felt very comfortable.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on netten; noun Umgang adds -s.

nett.proTip: Comparative: netter, am nettesten. German idiom/proverb caveat: 'Nett ist die kleine Schwester von...' (German popular saying cautioning that 'nett' can sometimes sound lukewarm or faint praise: 'Er ist ganz nett' can imply 'He's okay, but not impressive').

massiv.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 1. 'massive, solid, sturdy' (walls, wood, gold); 2. 'severe, heavy, substantial' (criticism, pressure, increase). Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Eine massive Mauer aus Granitsteinen schützt die alte Festung vor feindlichen Angriffen.
nominative.english: A massive wall made of granite stones protects the old fortress from enemy attacks.
nominative.hint: Subject of schützt, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on massive.

accusative.german: Die Opposition übte massive Kritik an den vorgeschlagenen Sparmaßnahmen der Regierung.
accusative.english: The opposition exercised massive criticism of the government's proposed austerity measures.
accusative.hint: Direct object of übte, so accusative. Strong declension without an article: feminine accusative takes ending -e on massive.

dative.german: In einem massiven Gebäude aus Stahlbeton sind die wertvollen Archive sicher untergebracht.
dative.english: In a solid building made of reinforced concrete the valuable archives are safely housed.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on massiven.

genitive.german: Wegen des massiven Schneefalls mussten mehrere Passstraßen in den Bergen gesperrt werden.
genitive.english: Because of the massive snowfall several mountain pass roads had to be closed.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on massiven; noun Schneefall adds -s.

massiv.proTip: Dual usage: 1. Material (pure/solid, not hollow or plated): 'massives Gold' (solid gold), 'massives Eichenholz' (solid oak); 2. Intensifier for negative/critical events: 'massive Probleme' (severe problems), 'massive Vorwürfe' (heavy accusations).

erstmal.note: Colloquial temporal adverb / particle (short for erst einmal) meaning 'first of all, for now, for the time being, to begin with'. As an adverb, it does not inflect for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing erstmal.

nominative.german: Der müde Wanderer ruht sich nach dem steilen Aufstieg erstmal auf der Bank aus.
nominative.english: The tired hiker rests on the bench for now after the steep climb.
nominative.hint: Subject of ruht sich ... aus, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on müde; erstmal is a temporal particle.

accusative.german: Wir trinken nach der anstrengenden Fahrt erstmal ein kühles Glas Wasser.
accusative.english: After the exhausting drive we drink a cool glass of water first of all.
accusative.hint: Direct object of trinken, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on kühles.

dative.german: Mit einer heißen Tasse Tee entspannte sich die Reisende nach der Ankunft erstmal.
dative.english: With a hot cup of tea the traveler relaxed for now after arrival.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on heißen.

genitive.german: Trotz des anfänglichen Zögerns wagte der Unternehmer erstmal einen kleinen Testlauf.
genitive.english: Despite initial hesitation the entrepreneur dared a small trial run for now.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on anfänglichen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

erstmal.proTip: Colloquial contraction of 'erst einmal'. In formal written German, prefer 'zunächst', 'vorerst', or 'erst einmal'. Meaning: 'Let's do this first before thinking about the next step'.

gigantisch.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'gigantic, colossal, gargantuan, immense' (size, project, scale). Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Ein gigantischer Frachtkahn transportiert tausende Tonnen Sand auf dem Rhein.
nominative.english: A gigantic freight barge transports thousands of tons of sand on the Rhine.
nominative.hint: Subject of transportiert, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on gigantischer.

accusative.german: Die Baufirma errichtete einen gigantischen Wolkenkratzer mitten im Bankenviertel.
accusative.english: The construction company erected a gigantic skyscraper in the middle of the banking district.
accusative.hint: Direct object of errichtete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on gigantischen.

dative.german: Mit gigantischem finanziellem Aufwand wurde das historische Opernhaus saniert.
dative.english: With gigantic financial expense the historic opera house was renovated.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on gigantischem and finanziellem.

genitive.german: Die Dimensionen des gigantischen Bauwerks versetzten alle Besucher in ungläubiges Staunen.
genitive.english: The dimensions of the gigantic structure filled all visitors with incredulous astonishment.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Dimensionen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gigantischen; noun Bauwerk adds -s.

gigantisch.proTip: Synonyms: riesig, kolossal, monumental, gewaltig. Derives from the Giants of Greek mythology (die Giganten). Often used as a colloquial intensifier: 'Das war eine gigantische Show!'.

zumindest.note: Modal adverb and particle meaning 'at least, at any rate' (setting a minimum expectation or condition). Uninflected, does not decline for case. The examples demonstrate case on noun phrases in sentences containing zumindest.

nominative.german: Zumindest ein erfahrener Mitarbeiter muss während der gesamten Nachtschicht anwesend sein.
nominative.english: At least one experienced employee must be present during the entire night shift.
nominative.hint: Subject of muss sein, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative ein; strong adjective ending -er on erfahrener; zumindest is a limiting particle.

accusative.german: Die Schülerin forderte zumindest eine faire Chance beim mündlichen Vortrag.
accusative.english: The student demanded at least a fair chance during the oral presentation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of forderte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on faire.

dative.german: Mit zumindest etwas Geduld lassen sich auch schwierige Puzzlespiele erfolgreich lösen.
dative.english: With at least some patience even difficult puzzle games can be solved successfully.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Geduld is an uncountable noun preceded by the indeclinable quantifier etwas.

genitive.german: Trotz des Ausbleibens des Hauptgewinns freute sich der Lottospieler über zumindest einen kleinen Teilerfolg.
genitive.english: Despite the failure to win the jackpot the lottery player was happy about at least a small partial success.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Ausbleiben adds genitive -s.

zumindest.proTip: Synonyms: wenigstens, mindestens. Subtlety: 'mindestens' is preferred with precise numbers ('mindestens 5 Euro'), while 'zumindest' and 'wenigstens' are frequently used for concessions or subjective minimum conditions ('Es hat zumindest nicht geregnet').

eben.note: Dual grammatical category: 1. Descriptive adjective meaning 'flat, even, level' (surface, terrain, ground); 2. Modal particle / temporal adverb meaning 'just, precisely, simply' (Das ist eben so = That's just the way it is; Er ist eben angekommen = He just arrived). When used as an attributive adjective, it declines.

nominative.german: Eine vollkommen ebene Fläche erleichtert das Verlegen von Fliesen im Badezimmer.
nominative.english: A completely flat surface makes laying tiles in the bathroom easier.
nominative.hint: Subject of erleichtert, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on ebene.

accusative.german: Die Sportler suchten einen ebenen Weg durch den dichten Wald für ihren Dauerlauf.
accusative.english: The athletes looked for a flat path through the dense forest for their continuous run.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on ebenen.

dative.german: Auf ebenem Gelände lässt sich das große Zelt ohne Schwierigkeiten aufbauen.
dative.english: On level ground the large tent can be pitched without difficulty.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on ebenem.

genitive.german: Wegen des ebenen Verlaufs der Strecke eignet sich die Radtour hervorragend für Familien.
genitive.english: Because of the flat course of the route the cycling tour is ideally suited for families.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ebenen; noun Verlauf adds -s.

eben.proTip: Very high frequency particle in spoken German: 'Das ist eben Pech' (That's just bad luck); 'Ich habe ihn eben gesehen' (I just saw him a moment ago); 'Eben!' (Exactly! / My point precisely!). As an adjective: die Ebene (the plain / level).

potenziell.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'potential, prospective, possible'. Also spelled potentiell according to traditional orthography (Duden recommends potenziell). Declines according to standard adjective rules when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein potenzieller Investor prüft den detaillierten Geschäftsplan des neuen Startups sorgfältig.
nominative.english: A potential investor examines the detailed business plan of the new startup carefully.
nominative.hint: Subject of prüft, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on potenzieller.

accusative.german: Die Bank analysiert das potenzielle Risiko des Kredits vor der Bewilligung genau.
accusative.english: The bank analyzes the potential risk of the loan precisely before approval.
accusative.hint: Direct object of analysiert, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on potenzielle.

dative.german: Bei einem potenziellen Notfall müssen alle Rettungswege im Gebäude freigehalten werden.
dative.english: In a potential emergency all escape routes in the building must be kept clear.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on potenziellen.

genitive.german: Die Identifizierung eines potenziellen Schadens hilft bei der Vermeidung teurer Reparaturen.
genitive.english: Identifying potential damage helps to avoid costly repairs.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Identifizierung. Masculine genitive article eines; weak adjective ending -en on potenziellen; noun Schaden adds -s.

potenziell.proTip: Related noun: das Potenzial (potential). Common collocations: 'potenzielle Kunden' (prospective customers); 'potenzielle Gefahren' (potential dangers); 'potenzielle Käufer' (potential buyers).

bisschen.note: Indeclinable indefinite pronoun / noun used with 'ein' (ein bisschen = a little bit, a small amount of). Functions as a quantifier before nouns or as an adverb modifying adjectives/verbs. It does not decline for case. The noun modified by 'ein bisschen' takes the case required by the clause.

nominative.german: Ein bisschen Sonnenschein hebt die Laune der Spaziergänger an kalten Wintertagen sofort.
nominative.english: A little bit of sunshine immediately lifts the walkers' spirits on cold winter days.
nominative.hint: Subject of hebt, so nominative. Quantifier ein bisschen modifying masculine noun Sonnenschein.

accusative.german: Könnten Sie mir bitte ein bisschen Geduld entgegenbringen?
accusative.english: Could you please show me a little bit of patience?
accusative.hint: Direct object of entgegenbringen, so accusative. Indeclinable quantifier ein bisschen modifying Geduld.

dative.german: Mit ein bisschen handwerklichem Geschick lässt sich das alte Holzregal leicht reparieren.
dative.english: With a little bit of craftsmanship skill the old wooden shelf can be easily repaired.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative adjective Geschick takes strong ending -em on handwerklichem after ein bisschen.

genitive.german: Wegen des großen Erfolgs dieses Projekts feierten die Mitarbeiter mit ein bisschen Sekt.
genitive.english: Because of the great success of this project the employees celebrated with a little bit of champagne.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on großen; noun Erfolg adds -s; the clause contains the indeclinable quantifier ein bisschen.

bisschen.proTip: Spelling note: 'ein bisschen' is written lowercase with double s (formerly 'ein bischen' or capitalized 'ein Bisschen' in archaic German; current Duden standard: always 'ein bisschen'). Synonym: ein wenig.

erfüllend.note: Descriptive adjective derived from the present participle of erfüllen, meaning 'fulfilling, satisfying, rewarding' (work, hobby, task). Declines according to standard German adjective endings when placed before a noun; uninflected when used predicatively or adverbially.

nominative.german: Eine erfüllende Arbeit im sozialen Bereich gibt dem Leben einen tieferen Sinn.
nominative.english: A fulfilling job in the social sector gives life a deeper meaning.
nominative.hint: Subject of gibt, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on erfüllende.

accusative.german: Viele Menschen suchen eine erfüllende Aufgabe für ihren Ruhestand.
accusative.english: Many people seek a fulfilling task for their retirement.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on erfüllende.

dative.german: Mit einer zutiefst erfüllenden Tätigkeit vergeht der Arbeitstag wie im Flug.
dative.english: With a deeply fulfilling occupation the workday flies by.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on erfüllenden.

genitive.german: Das Gefühl des erfüllenden Arbeitens im Garten entspannt Geist und Körper.
genitive.english: The feeling of fulfilling work in the garden relaxes mind and body.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gefühl. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on erfüllenden; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

erfüllend.proTip: Formed as the Partizip I (present participle) of erfüllen: erfüllen + -d = erfüllend. Describes an activity that provides inner fulfilment: 'ein erfüllendes Hobby', 'ein erfüllendes Berufsleben'. Antonym: frustrierend (frustrating).

vorne.note: Local adverb meaning 'in front, at the front, ahead, forward'. As an adverb, vorne (also vorn) is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing vorne.

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Kapitän steht vorne auf der Brücke des Kreuzfahrtschiffs.
nominative.english: The experienced captain stands at the front on the bridge of the cruise ship.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene; vorne is a local adverb.

accusative.german: Die Lehrerin bat den unruhigen Schüler, sich ganz nach vorne zu setzen.
accusative.english: The teacher asked the restless student to sit right at the front.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bat, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on unruhigen; noun Schüler takes no ending.

dative.german: In der ersten Reihe ganz vorne saßen die Ehrengäste des festlichen Konzerts.
dative.english: In the first row right at the front sat the guests of honor of the festive concert.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on ersten.

genitive.german: Trotz des lauten Lärms ganz vorne genossen die Fans den Auftritt der Rockband.
genitive.english: Despite the loud noise right at the front the fans enjoyed the performance of the rock band.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on lauten; noun Lärm adds -s.

vorne.proTip: Both 'vorne' and 'vorn' are standard German. Direction vs. location: 'nach vorne' (motion towards front: 'Komm nach vorne!'); 'vorne' (stationary location at the front: 'Ich sitze vorne'). Antonym: hinten (at the back).

enttäuscht.note: Adjective derived from the past participle of enttäuschen, meaning 'disappointed, disillusioned'. Declines when placed before a noun according to standard adjective rules; uninflected when used predicatively. Often combines with von + dative or über + accusative.

nominative.german: Ein enttäuschter Kunde forderte an der Kasse die sofortige Rückerstattung seines Geldes.
nominative.english: A disappointed customer demanded the immediate refund of his money at the checkout.
nominative.hint: Subject of forderte, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on enttäuschter.

accusative.german: Der Trainer tröstete den sichtlich enttäuschten Spieler nach der bitteren Niederlage.
accusative.english: The coach consoled the visibly disappointed player after the bitter defeat.
accusative.hint: Direct object of tröstete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on enttäuschten.

dative.german: Mit enttäuschter Miene verließ der Bewerber das Büro des Personalchefs.
dative.english: With a disappointed expression the applicant left the HR manager's office.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on enttäuschter.

genitive.german: Wegen des enttäuschten Gesichts des Kindes kaufte der Vater ihm doch noch ein Eis.
genitive.english: Because of the child's disappointed face the father bought him an ice cream after all.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on enttäuschten; noun Gesicht adds -s.

enttäuscht.proTip: Preposition patterns: 'enttäuscht sein von (+ Dativ)' (disappointed by a person: 'Ich bin von dir enttäuscht'); 'enttäuscht sein über (+ Akkusativ)' (disappointed about a circumstance: 'Er ist über das Ergebnis enttäuscht').

dahin.note: Directional adverb meaning 'to there, thither' (indicating motion toward a distant point), or predicate adjective meaning 'gone, ruined, perished' (dahin sein). As an adverb, dahin does not decline for case. The examples demonstrate case on noun phrases in sentences containing dahin.

nominative.german: Die schönste Zeit des Sommers ist nun leider unwiederbringlich dahin.
nominative.english: The most beautiful time of summer is now unfortunately irretrievably gone.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist dahin, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak superlative adjective ending -e on schönste; dahin is a predicate adverb meaning 'gone'.

accusative.german: Der Busfahrer brachte die aufgeregten Schüler pünktlich dahin, wo das Zeltlager stattfand.
accusative.english: The bus driver brought the excited students punctually to there where the camp was held.
accusative.hint: Direct object of brachte, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on aufgeregten.

dative.german: Mit dem schnellen Schnellzug fuhren die Geschäftsleute direkt dahin zur Konferenz.
dative.english: With the fast express train the business people traveled directly to there for the conference.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on schnellen.

genitive.german: Wegen des Dahinscheidens des alten Königs versammelten sich die Bürger in tiefer Trauer.
genitive.english: Because of the passing away of the old king the citizens gathered in deep mourning.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized verb based on dahin + scheiden adds genitive -s.

dahin.proTip: Directional adverb with two main meanings: 1. Spatial target: 'Geh nicht dahin!' (Don't go there!); 2. Loss / ruin: 'Alle Hoffnungen sind dahin' (All hopes are gone/lost). Fixed idiom: 'bis dahin' (until then / by then).

gemeinsam.note: Adjective and adverb meaning 'joint, common, shared, mutual, together'. Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Ein gemeinsamer Spaziergang durch den herbstlichen Wald entspannt die ganze Familie.
nominative.english: A joint walk through the autumnal forest relaxes the entire family.
nominative.hint: Subject of entspannt, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on gemeinsamer.

accusative.german: Die beiden Partner verfolgen ein gemeinsames Ziel im neuen Geschäftsjahr.
accusative.english: The two partners pursue a common goal in the new business year.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verfolgen, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on gemeinsames.

dative.german: Mit gemeinsamer Anstrengung schaffte das Team den fristgerechten Projektabschluss.
dative.english: With mutual effort the team achieved project completion on schedule.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on gemeinsamer.

genitive.german: Die Früchte des gemeinsamen Erfolgs teilten die Gründer zu gleichen Teilen untereinander auf.
genitive.english: The founders divided the fruits of their joint success equally among themselves.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Früchte. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gemeinsamen; noun Erfolg adds -s.
