gemeinsam.proTip: High-frequency adverb: 'gemeinsam essen' (eat together), 'gemeinsam arbeiten' (work together). Attributive noun collocations: 'das gemeinsame Sorgerecht' (joint custody); 'gemeinsame Interessen' (shared interests). Synonyms: zusammen, gemeinschaftlich.

dahinter.note: Pronominal adverb (prepositional adverb) meaning 'behind it, behind that' or figuratively 'behind the scenes / the motive behind something'. As an adverb, dahinter is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing dahinter.

nominative.german: Die riesige Scheune verdeckt das Haus, und der bunte Garten liegt direkt dahinter.
nominative.english: The huge barn conceals the house, and the colorful garden lies directly behind it.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on bunte; dahinter is a pronominal adverb.

accusative.german: Die Detektive vermuteten eine gerissene Betrügerbande dahinter und leiteten Ermittlungen ein.
accusative.english: The detectives suspected a cunning gang of fraudsters behind it and initiated investigations.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vermuteten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on gerissene.

dative.german: Mit geschultem Scharfsinn erkannte die Journalistin die wahren Absichten dahinter.
dative.english: With trained acumen the journalist recognized the true intentions behind it.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on geschultem.

genitive.german: Die Aufdeckung des Geheimnisses dahinter sorgte für großes Aufsehen in den Medien.
genitive.english: The uncovering of the secret behind it caused a great sensation in the media.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Aufdeckung. Neuter genitive article des; noun Geheimnis adds -es; dahinter modifies the phrase.

dahinter.proTip: Formed from da + hinter (behind that/it). Idioms: 'dahinterkommen' (to find out / uncover a secret: 'Ich bin dahintergekommen'); 'dahinterstecken' (to be behind something: 'Wer steckt dahinter?'); 'sich dahinterklemmen' (to buckle down / put serious effort into something).

uralt.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'ancient, age-old, primordial' (traditions, trees, legends). Formed with the intensifying prefix ur- (ancient/original) + alt (old). Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Eine uralte Eiche spendet den rastenden Wanderern an heißen Tagen kühlen Schatten.
nominative.english: An ancient oak provides cool shade to resting hikers on hot days.
nominative.hint: Subject of spendet, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on uralte.

accusative.german: Die Forscher entdeckten einen uralten Tempel tief im undurchdringlichen Dschungel.
accusative.english: The researchers discovered an ancient temple deep in the impenetrable jungle.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entdeckten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on uralten.

dative.german: Nach einem uralten Brauch zünden die Dorfbewohner im Frühling ein großes Feuer an.
dative.english: According to an ancient custom the villagers light a large fire in spring.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on uralten.

genitive.german: Die geheimnisvolle Inschrift der uralten Steintafel konnte von Experten entziffert werden.
genitive.english: The mysterious inscription on the ancient stone tablet could be deciphered by experts.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Inschrift. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on uralten.

uralt.proTip: The prefix ur- denotes primordial origin or ancient age (die Urzeit = prehistory, der Ursprung = origin, urplötzlich = out of nowhere). Does not normally take comparative/superlative forms since 'uralt' is already an absolute intensifier of 'alt'.

herab.note: Directional adverb meaning 'down, downward' (from a higher position towards the speaker/observer). As an adverb, herab is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing herab.

nominative.german: Kaltes Quellwasser fließt in sanftem Lauf vom hohen Berggipfel herab.
nominative.english: Cold spring water flows in a gentle course down from the high mountain summit.
nominative.hint: Subject of fließt, so nominative. Strong declension without an article: neuter nominative takes strong ending -es on Kaltes; herab is a directional adverb.

accusative.german: Die Wanderer blickten den steilen Abhang hinab, während Steine laut herab polterten.
accusative.english: The hikers looked down the steep slope while stones rumbled loudly downwards.
accusative.hint: Direct object / directional accusative of blickten ... hinab. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on steilen.

dative.german: Von der hohen Klippe stürzte der tosende Wasserfall brausend herab.
dative.english: From the high cliff the roaring waterfall crashed loudly downward.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on hohen.

genitive.german: Wegen des Herabfallens schwerer Dachziegel sperrte die Polizei den Gehweg vor dem Haus.
genitive.english: Because of the falling down of heavy roof tiles the police cordoned off the pavement in front of the house.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized compound Herabfallen adds genitive -s.

herab.proTip: Her- indicates movement toward the speaker (herab = down toward here), while hin- indicates movement away from the speaker (hinab = down away from here). Idiom: 'von oben herab' (condescendingly): 'Er behandelt seine Mitarbeiter von oben herab'.

ständig.note: Descriptive adjective and adverb meaning 'constant, permanent, continuous, perpetual, chronic'. Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Der ständige Straßenlärm vor dem Schlafzimmerfenster raubt den Anwohnern den Schlaf.
nominative.english: The constant traffic noise outside the bedroom window robs the residents of sleep.
nominative.hint: Subject of raubt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on ständige.

accusative.german: Das kleine Kind stellte den ganzen Nachmittag lang ständige Fragen über die Welt.
accusative.english: The little child asked continuous questions about the world the entire afternoon long.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stellte, so accusative plural. Strong declension without an article: plural accusative takes ending -e on ständige.

dative.german: Unter ständigem Zeitdruck machen selbst erfahrene Mitarbeiter vermehrt Fehler.
dative.english: Under constant time pressure even experienced employees make increased mistakes.
dative.hint: Dative governed by unter (condition). Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on ständigem.

genitive.german: Wegen des ständigen Wechsels der Abteilungsleiter verlor das Team seine Orientierung.
genitive.english: Because of the constant change of department heads the team lost its orientation.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ständigen; noun Wechsel adds -s.

ständig.proTip: High-frequency adverb: 'Er beschwert sich ständig' (He complains constantly). Official title: 'der Ständige Vertreter' (the Permanent Representative / chargé d'affaires). Synonyms: dauernd, permanent, ununterbrochen.

wiederum.note: Modal and connective adverb meaning 'in turn, on the other hand, again, conversely'. As an adverb, wiederum is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing wiederum.

nominative.german: Der neue Vorschlag des Bürgermeisters stieß wiederum auf heftigen Widerstand im Stadtrat.
nominative.english: The mayor's new proposal in turn met with fierce resistance in the city council.
nominative.hint: Subject of stieß, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on neue; wiederum is a connective adverb.

accusative.german: Die Geschäftsleitung billigte diesen riskanten Plan, der wiederum große Risiken barg.
accusative.english: The management approved this risky plan, which in turn harbored great risks.
accusative.hint: Direct object of billigte, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner diesen; weak adjective ending -en on riskanten.

dative.german: Mit dieser unvorhergesehenen Wendung eröffnete sich wiederum eine völlig neue Perspektive.
dative.english: With this unforeseen turn of events a completely new perspective opened up in turn.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on unvorhergesehenen.

genitive.german: Trotz des wiederum sinkenden Aktienkurses behielten die optimistischen Anleger ihre Wertpapiere.
genitive.english: Despite the once again falling share price the optimistic investors kept their securities.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on sinkenden; noun Aktienkurs adds -es; modified by adverb wiederum.

wiederum.proTip: Two nuances: 1. Repetition: 'Er kam wiederum zu spät' (He was late once again); 2. Contrast/consequence: 'Das senkt die Kosten, was wiederum den Gewinn steigert' (That lowers costs, which in turn increases profit). Synonyms: seinerseits, andererseits, abermals.

spannend.note: Descriptive adjective derived from the present participle of spannen, meaning 'exciting, gripping, suspenseful, thrilling' (novel, match, debate). Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein spannender Kriminalfilm fesselte das gesamte Publikum bis zur letzten Minute.
nominative.english: A gripping crime thriller captivated the entire audience until the last minute.
nominative.hint: Subject of fesselte, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on spannender.

accusative.german: Die Schüler lasen eine überaus spannende Geschichte über mittelalterliche Ritter.
accusative.english: The students read an exceedingly exciting story about medieval knights.
accusative.hint: Direct object of lasen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on spannende.

dative.german: Bei einem so spannenden Spiel saß kein einziger Zuschauer mehr ruhig auf seinem Platz.
dative.english: At such an exciting match not a single spectator was sitting quietly in their seat.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on spannenden.

genitive.german: Wegen des spannenden Verlaufs der Partie blieb der Ausgang bis zum Abpfiff völlig offen.
genitive.english: Because of the thrilling course of the match the outcome remained completely open until the final whistle.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on spannenden; noun Verlauf adds -s.

spannend.proTip: Comparative: spannender, am spannendsten. Collocations: 'hochspannend' (highly gripping); 'es bleibt spannend' (the suspense continues / it remains exciting). Antonym: langweilig (boring).

daran.note: Pronominal adverb (prepositional adverb) meaning 'on it, at it, about it, to it' (representing an + prepositional object). As an adverb, daran (short form dran) is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples show case on noun phrases in sentences containing daran.

nominative.german: Der erfahrene Mechaniker erinnert sich noch gut daran, wie der Motor repariert wurde.
nominative.english: The experienced mechanic still remembers well how the engine was repaired.
nominative.hint: Subject of erinnert sich, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene; daran is a pronominal adverb.

accusative.german: Wir müssen diesen wichtigen Termin im Kalender notieren, um rechtzeitig daran zu denken.
accusative.english: We must note this important appointment in the calendar to remember it in time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of notieren, so accusative. Masculine accusative determiner diesen; weak adjective ending -en on wichtigen.

dative.german: Mit großem Fleiß arbeiteten die Studenten wochenlang daran, das Projekt abzuschließen.
dative.english: With great diligence the students worked on it for weeks to complete the project.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on großem.

genitive.german: Wegen des Fehlens wichtiger Ersatzteile scheiterte der Versuch, rechtzeitig daran weiterzubauen.
genitive.english: Because of the lack of important spare parts the attempt to continue building on it in time failed.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized infinitive Fehlen adds genitive -s.

daran.proTip: Compound of da(r) + an. Used with verbs that govern the preposition an + case: denken an (daran denken = think of it); arbeiten an (daran arbeiten = work on it); zweifeln an (daran zweifeln = doubt it). Spoken colloquial form: 'dran' ('Ich bin dran' = It's my turn).

wissenschaftlich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'scientific, academic, scholarly'. Formed from Wissenschaft (science) + suffix -lich. Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Eine wissenschaftliche Studie belegt die Wirksamkeit der neuen medizinischen Behandlung.
nominative.english: A scientific study proves the effectiveness of the new medical treatment.
nominative.hint: Subject of belegt, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on wissenschaftliche.

accusative.german: Die Studentin verfasste einen wissenschaftlichen Aufsatz über erneuerbare Energien.
accusative.english: The student wrote a scientific essay on renewable energies.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verfasste, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on wissenschaftlichen.

dative.german: Mit wissenschaftlicher Präzision untersuchte das Labor die unbekannten Wasserproben.
dative.english: With scientific precision the laboratory examined the unknown water samples.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative takes strong ending -er on wissenschaftlicher.

genitive.german: Die strengen Kriterien des wissenschaftlichen Arbeitens müssen von allen Forschern eingehalten werden.
genitive.english: The strict criteria of scientific work must be observed by all researchers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kriterien. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on wissenschaftlichen; nominalized infinitive adds -s.

wissenschaftlich.proTip: Collocations: 'wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter' (research associate); 'wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse' (scientific findings); 'wissenschaftliche Arbeit' (academic paper / research). Antonym: unwissenschaftlich.

neben.note: Two-way preposition (Wechselpräposition) meaning 'next to, beside' or figuratively 'besides, in addition to'. Governs DATIVE when indicating a static location (Wo? an der Wand neben dem Schrank), and ACCUSATIVE when indicating direction or motion to a place alongside (Wohin? Er stellt den Stuhl neben das Fenster).

nominative.german: Der alte Parkplatz neben dem modernen Bürogebäude wird bald komplett umgebaut.
nominative.english: The old parking lot next to the modern office building will soon be completely rebuilt.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird umgebaut, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on alte; neben dem modernen Bürogebäude is a prepositional modifier.

accusative.german: Der Kellner stellte den bequemen Stuhl direkt neben den festlich gedeckten Tisch.
accusative.english: The waiter placed the comfortable chair directly next to the festively laid table.
accusative.hint: Accusative governed by the two-way preposition neben expressing destination/direction (Wohin?). Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Die kleine Bäckerei befindet sich direkt neben dem historischen Rathaus der Stadt.
dative.english: The small bakery is located directly next to the historic town hall of the city.
dative.hint: Dative governed by the two-way preposition neben expressing stationary location (Wo?). Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on historischen.

genitive.german: Wegen des Baus einer Tiefgarage neben der alten Kirche traten Risse im Gemäuer auf.
genitive.english: Because of the construction of an underground garage next to the old church cracks appeared in the masonry.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; noun Bau adds genitive -s; contains the prepositional phrase neben der alten Kirche.

neben.proTip: Wechselpräposition rule: 'neben + Dativ' for location (Wo? 'Er sitzt neben MIR' [dat]); 'neben + Akkusativ' for direction (Wohin? 'Setz dich neben MICH' [akk]). Figurative use 'in addition to': 'Neben seinem Studium arbeitet er' (Alongside his studies he works).

täglich.note: Temporal adjective and adverb meaning 'daily, every day, quotidian'. Formed from Tag (day) with umlaut + suffix -lich. Declines according to gender, number, and case when used attributively before a noun; uninflected when used adverbially.

nominative.german: Der tägliche Morgenspaziergang an der frischen Luft hält Körper und Geist fit.
nominative.english: The daily morning walk in the fresh air keeps body and mind fit.
nominative.hint: Subject of hält, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on tägliche.

accusative.german: Viele Menschen lesen die tägliche Zeitung schon früh morgens beim Frühstück.
accusative.english: Many people read the daily newspaper early in the morning with breakfast.
accusative.hint: Direct object of lesen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on tägliche.

dative.german: Mit täglichem Training erzielte die fleißige Schwimmerin enorme Leistungsfortschritte.
dative.english: With daily training the hardworking swimmer achieved enormous performance progress.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative takes strong ending -em on täglichem.

genitive.german: Die Bewältigung der Herausforderungen des täglichen Lebens erfordert Gelassenheit und Geduld.
genitive.english: Coping with the challenges of daily life requires composure and patience.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Herausforderungen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on täglichen; noun Leben adds -s.

täglich.proTip: Series of time adjectives: täglich (daily), wöchentlich (weekly), monatlich (monthly), jährlich (annually). As an adverb: 'Ich laufe täglich fünf Kilometer' (I run 5 km daily).

jener.note: Demonstrative determiner and pronoun meaning 'that, that one, those' (referring to something more distant in time or space, or already mentioned). Inflects for all four cases like the definite article der/die/das: jener (masc nom), jenen (masc akk), jenem (masc/neut dat), jener (fem dat/gen, pl gen), jenes (neut nom/akk, masc/neut gen).

nominative.german: Jener erfahrene Bergsteiger warnte die Gruppe eindringlich vor dem nahenden Unwetter.
nominative.english: That experienced mountaineer warned the group urgently about the approaching storm.
nominative.hint: Subject of warnte, so nominative. Masculine nominative demonstrative Jener; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Die Ermittler überprüften jenen verdächtigen Koffer am Flughafen sehr genau.
accusative.english: The investigators examined that suspicious suitcase at the airport very closely.
accusative.hint: Direct object of überprüften, so accusative. Masculine accusative demonstrative jenen; weak adjective ending -en on verdächtigen.

dative.german: In jenem abgelegenen Dorf am Waldrand scheint die Zeit stillzustehen.
dative.english: In that remote village at the edge of the forest time seems to stand still.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative demonstrative jenem; weak adjective ending -en on abgelegenen.

genitive.german: Die Erinnerung jenes denkwürdigen Tages blieb allen Beteiligten ein Leben lang im Gedächtnis.
genitive.english: The memory of that memorable day remained in the memory of all involved for a lifetime.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erinnerung. Masculine genitive demonstrative jenes; weak adjective ending -en on denkwürdigen; noun Tag adds -es.

jener.proTip: Contrast pair: dieser (this, near) vs. jener (that, distant). Jener is more literary/formal than 'dieser dort' or 'der da' in modern everyday German. Followed by weak adjective endings (just like after der/die/das).

unmöglich.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'impossible, unfeasible' (task, feat) or colloquially 'outrageous, intolerable, improper' (behavior, manners). Formed from möglich (possible) + negative prefix un-. Declines according to standard adjective endings when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Eine unlösbare und unmögliche Aufgabe frustriert selbst die ehrgeizigsten Schüler.
nominative.english: An unsolvable and impossible task frustrates even the most ambitious students.
nominative.hint: Subject of frustriert, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on unlösbare and unmögliche.

accusative.german: Der Chef forderte das schier Unmögliche von seinem völlig überlasteten Team.
accusative.english: The boss demanded the sheer impossible from his completely overburdened team.
accusative.hint: Direct object of forderte, so accusative. Nominalized neuter adjective with definite article das; weak ending -e on Unmögliche.

dative.german: Unter solch unmöglichen Bedingungen konnte das Experiment im Labor nicht gelingen.
dative.english: Under such impossible conditions the experiment in the laboratory could not succeed.
dative.hint: Dative governed by unter. Plural dative takes ending -en on unmöglichen and Bedingungen.

genitive.german: Die Erkenntnis des Unmöglichen eines solchen Vorhabens bewahrte die Firma vor dem Ruin.
genitive.english: Recognition of the impossibility of such an undertaking saved the company from ruin.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erkenntnis. Neuter genitive article des; nominalized adjective takes weak ending -en.

unmöglich.proTip: Idiom: 'ein unmögliches Benehmen' (outrageous/unacceptable behavior). Predicate: 'Das ist ein Ding der Unmöglichkeit' (That is a total impossibility / out of the question). Antonym: möglich (possible).

jeweils.note: Distributive adverb meaning 'in each case, respectively, each, at a time'. As an adverb, jeweils is uninflected and does not decline for case. The examples demonstrate case on noun phrases in sentences containing jeweils.

nominative.german: Jeweils zwei erfahrene Taucher bilden ein Team bei der Unterwassererkundung.
nominative.english: In each case two experienced divers form a team during the underwater exploration.
nominative.hint: Subject of bilden, so nominative plural. Plural nominative ending -e on erfahrene; jeweils is a distributive adverb.

accusative.german: Die Teilnehmer erhalten jeweils ein gedrucktes Exemplar des neuen Leitfadens.
accusative.english: The participants each receive a printed copy of the new guideline.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erhalten, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on gedrucktes.

dative.german: An jeweils einem festen Wochentag findet die Sprechstunde des Professors statt.
dative.english: On each respective fixed day of the week the professor's consultation hours take place.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (time/day). Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on festen.

genitive.german: Die genaue Dauer der jeweils ersten Phase des Programms beträgt vier Wochen.
genitive.english: The exact duration of each respective first phase of the program is four weeks.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Dauer. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on ersten; adverb jeweils modifies the phrase.

jeweils.proTip: Distributive use: specifies that an amount or condition applies individually to each item: 'Die Eintrittskarten kosten jeweils 15 Euro' (The tickets cost 15 euros each). Synonyms: je, im Einzelfall, einzeln.

eiförmig.note: Descriptive compound adjective meaning 'egg-shaped, oval, ovoid'. Formed from Ei (egg) + suffix -förmig (-shaped). Declines according to regular adjective declension when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Ein eiförmiger Kieselstein liegt glatt geschliffen am Ufer des Gebirgsbachs.
nominative.english: An egg-shaped pebble lies smoothly ground on the bank of the mountain stream.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Masculine mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -er on eiförmiger.

accusative.german: Der Goldschmied fertigte einen eiförmigen Anhänger aus reinem Silber an.
accusative.english: The goldsmith crafted an egg-shaped pendant out of pure silver.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fertigte ... an, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on eiförmigen.

dative.german: Mit einem eiförmigen Werkzeug glättete der Töpfer die feuchte Oberfläche der Tonschale.
dative.english: With an egg-shaped tool the potter smoothed the moist surface of the clay bowl.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on eiförmigen.

genitive.german: Wegen des eiförmigen Querschnitts besitzt die Betonröhre eine besonders hohe Stabilität.
genitive.english: Because of the egg-shaped cross-section the concrete pipe possesses particularly high stability.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on eiförmigen; noun Querschnitt adds -s.

eiförmig.proTip: Productive suffix -förmig forms adjectives indicating geometric or object shape: kreisförmig (circular), herzförmig (heart-shaped), keilförmig (wedge-shaped), sternförmig (star-shaped). Synonym: oval.

euer.note: Possessive determiner and pronoun for 2nd person plural informal (belonging to ihr / you all). Inflects for gender, number, and case: euer (masc nom, neut nom/akk), euren (masc akk, dat pl), eurem (masc/neut dat), eurer (fem dat/gen, pl gen), eures (masc/neut gen). The stem vowel -e- in euer is regularly dropped before endings beginning with a vowel (eure, euren, eurem, eures).

nominative.german: Euer neuer Sportlehrer leitet heute das Training in der großen Turnhalle.
nominative.english: Your new PE teacher is leading the training in the large gymnasium today.
nominative.hint: Subject of leitet, so nominative. Masculine possessive determiner Euer (has no ending in masc nom); strong adjective ending -er on neuer.

accusative.german: Habt ihr euren alten Schulranzen noch im Keller aufbewahrt?
accusative.english: Have you still kept your old school satchel in the basement?
accusative.hint: Direct object of aufbewahrt, so accusative. Masculine accusative possessive euren (drops stem -e- before ending -en); weak adjective ending -en on alten.

dative.german: Die Großmutter schenkte eurem kleinen Bruder ein spannendes Bilderbuch.
dative.english: The grandmother gave your little brother an exciting picture book.
dative.hint: Indirect dative object of schenkte (to whom). Masculine dative possessive eurem; weak adjective ending -en on kleinen.

genitive.german: Wegen des Umzugs eures besten Freundes war die ganze Klasse traurig.
genitive.english: Because of the move of your best friend the whole class was sad.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Umzugs. Masculine genitive possessive eures; weak adjective ending -en on besten; noun Freund adds -es.

euer.proTip: Contraction rule: whenever an ending is added to euer, the stem vowel 'e' usually drops out: eur- + -e = eure (not *euere); eur- + -en = euren; eur- + -em = eurem; eur- + -es = eures. Distinguish plural informal 'euer' from polite 'Ihr/Ihre'.

vulkanisch.note: Descriptive adjective meaning 'volcanic, produced by volcanoes'. Derived from Vulkan (volcano) + suffix -isch. Declines according to gender, number, and case when placed before a noun.

nominative.german: Vulkanische Asche verdunkelte den Himmel über der Insel für mehrere Tage.
nominative.english: Volcanic ash darkened the sky over the island for several days.
nominative.hint: Subject of verdunkelte, so nominative. Strong declension without an article: feminine nominative takes strong ending -e on Vulkanische.

accusative.german: Die Geologen untersuchten das vulkanische Gestein auf seine mineralische Zusammensetzung.
accusative.english: The geologists examined the volcanic rock for its mineral composition.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchten, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on vulkanische.

dative.german: Auf vulkanischem Boden wachsen besonders ertragreiche Weinstöcke und Olivenbäume.
dative.english: On volcanic soil particularly high-yielding grapevines and olive trees grow.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Strong declension without an article: masculine dative takes strong ending -em on vulkanischem.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung des vulkanischen Ursprungs der Inselgruppe lieferte überraschende Ergebnisse.
genitive.english: Research into the volcanic origin of the archipelago provided surprising results.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on vulkanischen; noun Ursprung adds -s.

vulkanisch.proTip: Scientific and geographical collocations: 'vulkanischer Boden' (fertile volcanic soil); 'vulkanische Aktivität' (volcanic activity); 'vulkanische Gase' (volcanic gases); 'vulkanischer Tuff' (tuff rock). Noun: der Vulkan (volcano, pl. die Vulkane).

der Moment.note: Masculine noun meaning 'the moment, instant, brief period' (plural: die Momente). Strong declension: der Moment, den Moment, dem Moment, des Moments (or des Momentes). (In physics/mechanics, das Moment means momentum/factor).

nominative.german: Der entscheidende Moment des Rennens kam in der letzten Kurve vor dem Ziel.
nominative.english: The decisive moment of the race came in the last bend before the finish.
nominative.hint: Subject of kam, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on entscheidende; noun Moment.

accusative.german: Wir müssen genau den richtigen Moment für den Start der Rakete abpassen.
accusative.english: We must catch exactly the right moment for the launch of the rocket.
accusative.hint: Direct object of abpassen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on richtigen.

dative.german: In diesem glücklichen Moment vergaßen die Freunde alle Sorgen des Alltags.
dative.english: In this happy moment the friends forgot all the worries of everyday life.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (time). Masculine dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on glücklichen.

genitive.german: Die Einzigartigkeit des flüchtigen Moments berührte die Herzen aller Anwesenden.
genitive.english: The uniqueness of the fleeting moment touched the hearts of all present.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Einzigartigkeit. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on flüchtigen; noun Moment adds -s.

der Moment.proTip: Gender watch: DER Moment (masculine) = moment of time ('einen Moment bitte!'). DAS Moment (neuter) = impetus, factor, or torque/momentum in physics and sociology ('ein wichtiges Moment in der Verhandlung').

die Einöde.note: Feminine noun meaning 'wasteland, wilderness, desolate solitude, barren expanse' (plural: die Einöden). As a feminine noun, it takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der).

nominative.german: Die karge Einöde erstreckt sich über hunderte Kilometer bis zum fernen Horizont.
nominative.english: The barren wasteland extends over hundreds of kilometers to the distant horizon.
nominative.hint: Subject of erstreckt sich, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on karge.

accusative.german: Die mutigen Pioniere durchquerten die lebensfeindliche Einöde zu Fuß und mit Maultieren.
accusative.english: The brave pioneers crossed the hostile wasteland on foot and with mules.
accusative.hint: Direct object of durchquerten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on lebensfeindliche.

dative.german: In der abgelegenen Einöde des Hochlands fand der Einsiedler vollkommene Ruhe.
dative.english: In the remote wilderness of the highlands the hermit found complete tranquility.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on abgelegenen.

genitive.german: Wegen der drückenden Einsamkeit der Einöde kehrten die Reisenden bald in die Stadt zurück.
genitive.english: Because of the oppressive loneliness of the wasteland the travelers soon returned to the city.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Einsamkeit. Feminine genitive article der; noun Einöde takes no ending.

die Einöde.proTip: Etymology: composed of ein (alone, single, as in einsam) + suffix -öde (desolate/barren). Describes uninhabited, desolate tracts of land (desert, tundra, desolate wilderness). Plural: die Einöden.

die Anzahl.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the number, quantity, count' (plural: die Anzahlen). As a feminine noun, it takes no ending in the singular: die Anzahl (nom/akk), der Anzahl (dat/gen). Often combined with an + dative or followed by a genitive/appositional plural noun.

nominative.german: Die genaue Anzahl der Teilnehmer steht erst morgen nach dem Anmeldeschluss fest.
nominative.english: The exact number of participants will only be certain tomorrow after the registration deadline.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht ... fest, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on genaue.

accusative.german: Die Wissenschaftler ermittelten die tatsächliche Anzahl der gefährdeten Tierarten im Nationalpark.
accusative.english: The scientists determined the actual number of endangered animal species in the national park.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ermittelten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on tatsächliche.

dative.german: Bei einer großen Anzahl von Beschwerden muss der Hersteller das Produkt nachbessern.
dative.english: With a large number of complaints the manufacturer must improve the product.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on großen; noun Anzahl takes no ending.

genitive.german: Wegen der steigenden Anzahl von Krankheitsfällen schloss das Gesundheitsamt die Schule.
genitive.english: Because of the increasing number of illnesses the health authority closed the school.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on steigenden; noun Anzahl takes no ending.

die Anzahl.proTip: Usage note: 'eine große Anzahl an (+ Dativ)' or with genitive: 'eine Anzahl von (+ Dativ)' / 'eine Anzahl der Teilnehmer'. Synonym: die Zahl (number/figure) or die Menge (quantity/amount).

die Pflanze.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the plant' (plural: die Pflanzen). Takes no inflectional ending in the singular (die, die, der, der) and adds -n in the plural (die Pflanzen, den Pflanzen).

nominative.german: Die exotische Pflanze gedeiht im feuchtwarmen Klima des tropischen Gewächshauses prächtig.
nominative.english: The exotic plant thrives splendidly in the warm and humid climate of the tropical greenhouse.
nominative.hint: Subject of gedeiht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on exotische.

accusative.german: Der Gärtner goss die empfindliche Pflanze jeden Morgen mit lauwarmem Regenwasser.
accusative.english: The gardener watered the sensitive plant every morning with lukewarm rainwater.
accusative.hint: Direct object of goss, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on empfindliche.

dative.german: Auf der grünen Pflanze saß ein kleiner Marienkäfer und sonnte sich.
dative.english: On the green plant sat a little ladybird, basking in the sun.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on grünen.

genitive.german: Die leuchtenden Blüten der seltenen Pflanze ziehen zahlreiche Schmetterlinge an.
genitive.english: The radiant blossoms of the rare plant attract numerous butterflies.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Blüten. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on seltenen.

die Pflanze.proTip: Related words: das Pflanzenreich (plant kingdom), pflanzlich (plant-based / vegetable: 'pflanzliche Ernährung' = plant-based diet), einpflanzen (to plant). Verb: pflanzen (to plant).

das Zeitalter.note: Neuter compound noun meaning 'the age, era, epoch' (plural: die Zeitalter). Formed from Zeit (time) + Alter (age). Follows strong neuter declension: das Zeitalter (nom/akk), dem Zeitalter (dat), des Zeitalters (gen).

nominative.german: Das digitale Zeitalter verändert die Kommunikation und die Arbeitswelt grundlegend.
nominative.english: The digital age is fundamentally changing communication and the working world.
nominative.hint: Subject of verändert, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on digitale.

accusative.german: Die Historiker erforschen das goldene Zeitalter der europäischen Renaissance mit großem Interesse.
accusative.english: Historians investigate the golden age of the European Renaissance with great interest.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erforschen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on goldene.

dative.german: In jenem fernen Zeitalter lebten die Menschen noch als Jäger und Sammler.
dative.english: In that distant age people still lived as hunter-gatherers.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (time/epoch). Neuter dative demonstrative jenem; weak adjective ending -en on fernen.

genitive.german: Die bahnbrechenden Erfindungen des industriellen Zeitalters prägen unsere moderne Zivilisation.
genitive.english: The groundbreaking inventions of the industrial age shape our modern civilization.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erfindungen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on industriellen; noun Zeitalter adds -s.

das Zeitalter.proTip: Important historical eras: 'das Atomzeitalter' (atomic age), 'das Weltraumzeitalter' (space age), 'das Informationszeitalter' (information age), 'das Industriezeitalter' (industrial age). Synonym: die Epoche / die Ära.

die Alge.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the alga / seaweed' (plural: die Algen = algae). As a feminine noun, it takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der) and adds -n in the plural (die Algen, den Algen).

nominative.german: Die mikroskopisch kleine Alge betreibt Photosynthese und erzeugt lebenswichtigen Sauerstoff.
nominative.english: The microscopic alga conducts photosynthesis and produces vital oxygen.
nominative.hint: Subject of betreibt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on kleine; Alge is singular.

accusative.german: Die Biologin untersuchte die grüne Alge unter dem hochauflösenden Mikroskop.
accusative.english: The female biologist examined the green alga under the high-resolution microscope.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on grüne.

dative.german: Mit dieser nahrhaften Alge lassen sich hochwertige Nahrungsergänzungsmittel herstellen.
dative.english: With this nutritious alga high-quality dietary supplements can be produced.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on nahrhaften.

genitive.german: Die rasante Vermehrung der blaugrünen Alge gefährdet das biologische Gleichgewicht im Badesee.
genitive.english: The rapid proliferation of the blue-green alga endangers the biological balance in the swimming lake.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Vermehrung. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on blaugrünen.

die Alge.proTip: Commonly encountered in the plural: 'die Algen' (algae / seaweed). Notable compounds: die Rotalge (red alga), die Grünalge (green alga), die Algenblüte (algal bloom). In cooking: Nori-Algen (seaweed sheets for sushi).

die Kontrolle.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the control, inspection, check, supervision' (plural: die Kontrollen). Takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der) and adds -n in the plural.

nominative.german: Die strenge Kontrolle am Grenzübergang verzögerte die Weiterfahrt der Reisenden erheblich.
nominative.english: The strict inspection at the border crossing delayed the travelers' onward journey considerably.
nominative.hint: Subject of verzögerte, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on strenge.

accusative.german: Der erfahrene Pilot behielt die volle Kontrolle über das Flugzeug während des Sturms.
accusative.english: The experienced pilot kept full control over the airplane during the storm.
accusative.hint: Direct object of behielt, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on volle.

dative.german: Bei der routinemäßigen Kontrolle entdeckten die Beamten gefälschte Ausweispapiere.
dative.english: During the routine check the officers discovered forged identity documents.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on routinemäßigen.

genitive.german: Wegen des Verlusts der Kontrolle über das Fahrzeug geriet der Wagen ins Schleudern.
genitive.english: Because of the loss of control over the vehicle the car went into a skid.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Verlusts. Feminine genitive article der; noun Kontrolle takes no ending.

die Kontrolle.proTip: False friend alert: German 'die Kontrolle' very often means 'inspection / check' ('Fahrkartenkontrolle' = ticket inspection, 'Passkontrolle' = passport check), not just dominion/command over something ('die Kontrolle verlieren' = to lose control).

die Bakterie.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the bacterium' (plural: die Bakterien). In technical German, das Bakterium (neuter, pl. Bakterien) is also common; die Bakterie is feminine and inflects die Bakterie (nom/akk), der Bakterie (dat/gen).

nominative.german: Die winzige Bakterie vermehrt sich unter feuchten und warmen Bedingungen rasend schnell.
nominative.english: The tiny bacterium multiplies at lightning speed under moist and warm conditions.
nominative.hint: Subject of vermehrt sich, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on winzige.

accusative.german: Der Arzt identifizierte die krankheitserregende Bakterie im Labor nach wenigen Stunden.
accusative.english: The doctor identified the pathogenic bacterium in the laboratory after a few hours.
accusative.hint: Direct object of identifizierte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on krankheitserregende.

dative.german: Mit einer neuartigen Bakterie reinigen Forscher kontaminiertes Grundwasser im Tagebau.
dative.english: With a novel bacterium researchers purify contaminated groundwater in open-cast mining.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on neuartigen.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung des Erbguts der resistenten Bakterie ermöglicht die Entwicklung neuer Antibiotika.
genitive.english: Research into the genetic material of the resistant bacterium enables the development of new antibiotics.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erbguts. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on resistenten.

die Bakterie.proTip: Duden recognizes both feminine 'die Bakterie' and neuter 'das Bakterium' (both take plural 'die Bakterien'). In medicine and biochemistry, the plural 'die Bakterien' is by far the most frequent form. Adjective: bakteriell (bacterial).

die Kommunikation.note: Feminine noun ending in -ion meaning 'the communication, exchange of information' (plural: die Kommunikationen). Feminine nouns ending in -ion are always feminine, take no ending in the singular, and take -en in the plural.

nominative.german: Eine offene Kommunikation zwischen Mitarbeitern und Vorgesetzten fördert das Betriebsklima.
nominative.english: Open communication between employees and superiors promotes the working atmosphere.
nominative.hint: Subject of fördert, so nominative. Feminine mixed nominative Eine; weak adjective ending -e on offene.

accusative.german: Das Management verbesserte die interne Kommunikation durch regelmäßige Teambesprechungen.
accusative.english: Management improved internal communication through regular team meetings.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verbesserte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on interne.

dative.german: Bei der direkten Kommunikation von Angesicht zu Angesicht entstehen seltener Missverständnisse.
dative.english: In direct face-to-face communication misunderstandings arise less frequently.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on direkten.

genitive.german: Die Kunst der diplomatischen Kommunikation erfordert großes Einfühlungsvermögen und Taktgefühl.
genitive.english: The art of diplomatic communication requires great empathy and tact.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kunst. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on diplomatischen.

die Kommunikation.proTip: All German nouns ending in -ion are feminine without exception: die Kommunikation, die Nation, die Tradition, die Station. Verb: kommunizieren (to communicate); adjective: kommunikativ.

das Ökosystem.note: Neuter compound noun meaning 'the ecosystem' (plural: die Ökosysteme). Formed from Öko- (ecological) + System. Follows strong neuter declension: das Ökosystem (nom/akk), dem Ökosystem (dat), des Ökosystems (gen).

nominative.german: Ein intaktes Ökosystem reguliert den Wasserhaushalt und schützt vor Bodenerosion.
nominative.english: An intact ecosystem regulates the water balance and protects against soil erosion.
nominative.hint: Subject of reguliert, so nominative. Neuter mixed nominative Ein; strong adjective ending -es on intaktes.

accusative.german: Der Klimawandel bedroht das empfindliche Ökosystem der tropischen Korallenriffe massiv.
accusative.english: Climate change massively threatens the sensitive ecosystem of tropical coral reefs.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bedroht, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on empfindliche.

dative.german: In diesem einzigartigen Ökosystem leben tausende seltene Tier- und Pflanzenarten.
dative.english: In this unique ecosystem thousands of rare animal and plant species live.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter dative determiner diesem; weak adjective ending -en on einzigartigen.

genitive.german: Der Zusammenbruch des arktischen Ökosystems hätte verheerende globale Folgen.
genitive.english: The collapse of the Arctic ecosystem would have devastating global consequences.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zusammenbruch. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on arktischen; noun Ökosystem adds -s.

das Ökosystem.proTip: Compound of Öko- (from Greek oikos = house/habitat) + System. Prefix Öko- appears in many green/environmental terms: der Ökostrom (green electricity), die Ökologie (ecology), ökologisch (ecological).

das System.note: Neuter noun of Greek/Latin origin meaning 'the system, organized scheme, network' (plural: die Systeme). Strong neuter declension: das System (nom/akk), dem System (dat), des Systems (gen).

nominative.german: Das neue System zur Datensicherung läuft vollautomatisch jede Nacht ab.
nominative.english: The new system for data backup runs fully automatically every night.
nominative.hint: Subject of läuft ... ab, so nominative. Neuter nominative article Das; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

accusative.german: Die Ingenieure installierten ein hochmodernes System zur Überwachung der Luftqualität.
accusative.english: The engineers installed a state-of-the-art system for monitoring air quality.
accusative.hint: Direct object of installierten, so accusative. Neuter mixed accusative ein; strong adjective ending -es on hochmodernes.

dative.german: Mit dem bewährten System ließen sich Produktionsfehler frühzeitig erkennen und beheben.
dative.english: With the proven system production errors could be recognized and resolved early on.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on bewährten.

genitive.german: Die Anfälligkeit des veralteten Systems führte zu häufigen Serverabstürzen.
genitive.english: The vulnerability of the obsolete system led to frequent server crashes.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Anfälligkeit. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on veralteten; noun System adds -s.

das System.proTip: Adjective: systematisch (systematic). Frequent compounds: das Betriebssystem (operating system / OS); das Sonnensystem (solar system); das Immunsystem (immune system); das Bildungssystem (education system).

der Meeresgrund.note: Masculine compound noun meaning 'the seabed, seafloor, ocean floor'. Formed from Meer (sea) + -es- + Grund (ground/bottom). Strong masculine declension: der Meeresgrund (nom), den Meeresgrund (akk), dem Meeresgrund / Meeresgrunde (dat), des Meeresgrunds / Meeresgrundes (gen).

nominative.german: Der dunkle Meeresgrund birgt bis heute viele unerforschte Geheimnisse der Tiefsee.
nominative.english: The dark seabed conceals many unexplored secrets of the deep sea to this day.
nominative.hint: Subject of birgt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on dunkle.

accusative.german: Das Spezial-U-Boot erforschte den felsigen Meeresgrund in dreitausend Metern Tiefe.
accusative.english: The special submarine explored the rocky seabed at a depth of three thousand meters.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erforschte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on felsigen.

dative.german: Auf dem sandigen Meeresgrund ruht das Wrack des gesunkenen Segelschiffs seit Jahrhunderten.
dative.english: On the sandy seabed rests the wreck of the sunken sailing ship for centuries.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (location). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on sandigen.

genitive.german: Die geologische Beschaffenheit des Meeresgrunds verrät viel über die Kontinentalverschiebung.
genitive.english: The geological nature of the seabed reveals a lot about continental drift.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Beschaffenheit. Masculine genitive article des; noun Meeresgrund adds -s.

der Meeresgrund.proTip: Synonyms: der Meeresboden, der Seegrund, der Meeresgrund. Contrast with der Grund (reason / ground). Note compound composition: das Meer + Fugenelement -es- + der Grund.

die Wirtschaft.note: Feminine noun meaning 1. 'the economy, business sector'; 2. 'inn, pub, tavern' (colloquial Gasthaus). Plural: die Wirtschaften. Feminine singular takes no case endings (die, die, der, der).

nominative.german: Die deutsche Wirtschaft erholt sich nach der Krise allmählich wieder.
nominative.english: The German economy is gradually recovering again after the crisis.
nominative.hint: Subject of erholt sich, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on deutsche.

accusative.german: Die Regierung will die regionale Wirtschaft durch steuerliche Anreize gezielt stärken.
accusative.english: The government intends to strengthen the regional economy specifically through tax incentives.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stärken, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on regionale.

dative.german: In der modernen Wirtschaft spielen digitale Technologien eine entscheidende Rolle.
dative.english: In the modern economy digital technologies play a decisive role.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (domain/location). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on modernen.

genitive.german: Das Wachstum der heimischen Wirtschaft übertraf alle Erwartungen der Analysten.
genitive.english: The growth of the domestic economy exceeded all expectations of the analysts.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wachstum. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on heimischen.

die Wirtschaft.proTip: Two distinct meanings: 1. Economy / business: 'die freie Marktwirtschaft' (free market economy), 'die Wirtschaftswissenschaft' (economics); 2. Pub / tavern (in southern Germany and Austria): 'Gehen wir in die Wirtschaft ein Bier trinken?' (Shall we go to the pub for a beer?).

der Kontinentalhang.note: Masculine compound noun meaning 'the continental slope' (the steep slope from the continental shelf to the deep ocean basin). Formed from kontinental (continental) + Hang (slope). Strong masculine declension: der Kontinentalhang (nom), den Kontinentalhang (akk), dem Kontinentalhang (dat), des Kontinentalhangs (gen).

nominative.german: Der steile Kontinentalhang fällt mehrere tausend Meter in die Tiefsee ab.
nominative.english: The steep continental slope drops several thousand meters into the deep sea.
nominative.hint: Subject of fällt ... ab, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on steile.

accusative.german: Das Forschungsschiff kartierte den zerklüfteten Kontinentalhang mithilfe moderner Echolote.
accusative.english: The research vessel mapped the rugged continental slope using modern sonar.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kartierte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on zerklüfteten.

dative.german: An dem steil abfallenden Kontinentalhang entstehen gewaltige unterseeische Erdrutsche.
dative.english: On the steeply sloping continental slope enormous undersea landslides occur.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (location). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on abfallenden.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung des Kontinentalhangs liefert wichtige Einblicke in marine Strömungsmuster.
genitive.english: Research into the continental slope provides important insights into marine current patterns.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. Masculine genitive article des; noun Kontinentalhang adds -s.

der Kontinentalhang.proTip: Key oceanographic term: situated between der Kontinentalschelf (continental shelf, shallow) and der Ozeanboden / das Tiefseebecken (deep sea floor). Root noun: der Hang (slope / hillside).

die Forschung.note: Feminine noun meaning 'the research, investigation, scientific study' (plural: die Forschungen). Derived from forschen (to research) + suffix -ung. As a feminine noun, it takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der).

nominative.german: Die medizinische Forschung macht bei der Krebstherapie stetig bedeutende Fortschritte.
nominative.english: Medical research is steadily making significant progress in cancer therapy.
nominative.hint: Subject of macht, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on medizinische.

accusative.german: Die Universität fördert die angewandte Forschung durch großzügige Stipendien.
accusative.english: The university promotes applied research through generous scholarships.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fördert, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on angewandte.

dative.german: In der wissenschaftlichen Forschung müssen alle Experimente reproduzierbar sein.
dative.english: In scientific research all experiments must be reproducible.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (domain). Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on wissenschaftlichen.

genitive.german: Die Ergebnisse der jahrelangen Forschung wurden in einem renommierten Fachjournal veröffentlicht.
genitive.english: The results of years of research were published in a renowned peer-reviewed journal.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ergebnisse. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on jahrelangen.

die Forschung.proTip: Nouns ending in -ung are ALWAYS feminine: die Forschung, die Hoffnung, die Übung, die Wohnung. Key compounds: die Grundlagenforschung (basic research), die Weltraumforschung (space research), das Forschungsinstitut (research institute).

der Tintenfisch.note: Masculine compound noun meaning 'the squid, cuttlefish, inkfish' (cephalopod). Formed from Tinte (ink) + Fisch (fish). Strong masculine declension: der Tintenfisch (nom), den Tintenfisch (akk), dem Tintenfisch (dat), des Tintenfischs (gen).

nominative.german: Der scheue Tintenfisch tarnt sich meisterhaft auf dem felsigen Meeresboden.
nominative.english: The shy cuttlefish camouflages itself masterfully on the rocky seafloor.
nominative.hint: Subject of tarnt sich, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on scheue.

accusative.german: Die Taucher beobachteten einen bunten Tintenfisch beim Jagen von kleinen Krabben.
accusative.english: The divers observed a colorful cuttlefish hunting small crabs.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beobachteten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on bunten.

dative.german: Bei Gefahr entkommt das Raubtier dem flinken Tintenfisch nur mit Mühe.
dative.english: In danger the predator escapes from the nimble squid only with difficulty.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by entkommen (jemandem entkommen). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on flinken.

genitive.german: Die dunkle Tinte des bedrohten Tintenfischs vernebelt dem Angreifer die Sicht.
genitive.english: The dark ink of the threatened squid clouds the attacker's view.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Tinte. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on bedrohten; noun Tintenfisch adds -s.

der Tintenfisch.proTip: Colloquial collective term: 'Tintenfisch' is used in German for cuttlefish, squids (Kalmare), and octopuses (Kraken). In culinary contexts: 'gegrillter Tintenfisch' (calamari / grilled squid).

die Gesellschaft.note: Feminine noun with suffix -schaft meaning 1. 'society, community, public'; 2. 'company, corporation' (GmbH); 3. 'company, social gathering' (Gesellschaft leisten = to keep someone company). Plural: die Gesellschaften. Takes no inflectional ending in the singular (die, die, der, der).

nominative.german: Die moderne Gesellschaft steht vor gewaltigen ökologischen und technologischen Herausforderungen.
nominative.english: Modern society faces enormous ecological and technological challenges.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht vor, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on moderne.

accusative.german: Der Soziologe erforscht die multikulturelle Gesellschaft der europäischen Großstädte.
accusative.english: The sociologist researches the multicultural society of European major cities.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erforscht, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on multikulturelle.

dative.german: In einer gerechten Gesellschaft sollten alle Kinder die gleichen Bildungschancen haben.
dative.english: In a just society all children should have the same educational opportunities.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location/concept). Feminine dative article einer; weak adjective ending -en on gerechten.

genitive.german: Der Zusammenhalt der gesamten Gesellschaft hängt vom gegenseitigen Vertrauen der Bürger ab.
genitive.english: The cohesion of the entire society depends on the mutual trust of the citizens.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zusammenhalt. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten.

die Gesellschaft.proTip: Nouns ending in -schaft are ALWAYS feminine: die Gesellschaft, die Freundschaft, die Mannschaft. Idiom: 'jemandem Gesellschaft leisten' (to keep someone company). Business: 'die Aktiengesellschaft' (AG = stock corporation), 'die Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung' (GmbH = LLC).

der Raubfisch.note: Masculine compound noun meaning 'predatory fish, predator fish' (pike, shark, barracuda). Formed from Raub (robbery/prey) + Fisch. Strong masculine declension: der Raubfisch (nom), den Raubfisch (akk), dem Raubfisch (dat), des Raubfischs / Raubfisches (gen).

nominative.german: Der hungrige Raubfisch lauert regungslos im dichten Schilf auf unvorsichtige Beute.
nominative.english: The hungry predatory fish lurks motionlessly in the dense reeds for careless prey.
nominative.hint: Subject of lauert, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on hungrige.

accusative.german: Der Sportangler fing einen riesigen Raubfisch im tiefen Bergsee.
accusative.english: The angler caught a huge predatory fish in the deep mountain lake.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fing, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on riesigen.

dative.german: Die kleinen Beutefische konnten dem pfeilschnellen Raubfisch nicht mehr entkommen.
dative.english: The small prey fish could no longer escape from the lightning-fast predatory fish.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by entkommen (jemandem entkommen). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on pfeilschnellen.

genitive.german: Die scharfen Zähne des gefährlichen Raubfischs hinterließen tiefe Kratzer im Kescher.
genitive.english: The sharp teeth of the dangerous predatory fish left deep scratches in the landing net.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zähne. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gefährlichen; noun Raubfisch adds -s.

der Raubfisch.proTip: Formed with Raub- (indicating predator/predatory behavior): das Raubtier (predator/carnivore), der Raubvogel (bird of prey), der Raubzug (raid). Typical freshwater Raubfische in Germany: der Hecht (pike), der Zander (pike-perch), der Barsch (perch).

der Schluss.note: Masculine noun meaning 1. 'the end, close, conclusion, termination'; 2. 'logical inference / deduction' (einen Schluss ziehen). Plural: die Schlüsse. Strong masculine declension with short vowel: der Schluss, den Schluss, dem Schluss, des Schlusses.

nominative.german: Der feierliche Schluss der Veranstaltung wurde mit langem Applaus belohnt.
nominative.english: The ceremonial conclusion of the event was rewarded with long applause.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde belohnt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on feierliche.

accusative.german: Die Kommissarin zog aus den gefundenen Indizien den richtigen Schluss.
accusative.english: The detective drew the right conclusion from the clues found.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zog, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on richtigen.

dative.german: Zum Schluss der feierlichen Rede bedankte sich der Präsident bei allen Helfern.
dative.english: At the end of the ceremonial speech the president thanked all helpers.
dative.hint: Dative governed by zu (contracted zum = zu dem). Masculine dative article dem; noun Schluss takes no ending.

genitive.german: Die logische Herleitung des logischen Schlusses überzeugte alle Anwesenden im Seminar.
genitive.english: The logical deduction of the logical conclusion convinced everyone present in the seminar.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Herleitung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on logischen; noun Schluss adds -es.

der Schluss.proTip: Idiomatic expressions: 'zum Schluss' (at the end / in conclusion); 'Schluss machen' (to end / break up a relationship); 'Schluss jetzt!' (Stop it right now! / That's enough!); 'einen Schlussstrich ziehen' (to draw a line under something).

die Seegurke.note: Feminine compound noun meaning 'the sea cucumber' (echinoderm). Formed from See (sea) + Gurke (cucumber). Takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der) and adds -n in the plural (die Seegurken).

nominative.german: Die stachelige Seegurke bewegt sich extrem langsam über den weichen Meeresboden.
nominative.english: The spiny sea cucumber moves extremely slowly across the soft ocean floor.
nominative.hint: Subject of bewegt sich, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on stachelige.

accusative.german: Der Meeresbiologe fotografierte eine seltene Seegurke in den Tiefen des Pazifiks.
accusative.english: The marine biologist photographed a rare sea cucumber in the depths of the Pacific.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fotografierte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; mixed adjective ending -e on seltene.

dative.german: Bei dieser ungewöhnlichen Seegurke dient der gesamte Körper als natürlicher Wasserfilter.
dative.english: In this unusual sea cucumber the entire body serves as a natural water filter.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on ungewöhnlichen.

genitive.german: Die Regenerationsfähigkeit der erstaunlichen Seegurke fasziniert Wissenschaftler weltweit.
genitive.english: The regenerative ability of the astonishing sea cucumber fascinates scientists worldwide.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Regenerationsfähigkeit. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on erstaunlichen.

die Seegurke.proTip: Marine biology and cuisine: in Asian gastronomy, sea cucumbers are considered a luxury delicacy (known in German trade as Trepang). Derived from die Gurke (cucumber).

die Lebenszeit.note: Feminine compound noun meaning 'the lifetime, life span' (plural: die Lebenszeiten). Formed from Leben (life) + -s- + Zeit (time). Takes no ending in the singular (die, die, der, der).

nominative.german: Die durchschnittliche Lebenszeit des Menschen ist im letzten Jahrhundert deutlich gestiegen.
nominative.english: The average human lifetime has risen noticeably in the last century.
nominative.hint: Subject of ist gestiegen, so nominative. Feminine nominative article Die; weak adjective ending -e on durchschnittliche.

accusative.german: Der Philosoph nutzte seine kostbare Lebenszeit für das unermüdliche Streben nach Weisheit.
accusative.english: The philosopher used his precious lifetime for the tireless pursuit of wisdom.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nutzte, so accusative. Feminine accusative possessive seine; weak adjective ending -e on kostbare.

dative.german: In seiner relativ kurzen Lebenszeit schuf der Komponist unsterbliche Meisterwerke.
dative.english: In his relatively short lifetime the composer created immortal masterpieces.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (time). Feminine dative possessive seiner; weak adjective ending -en on kurzen.

genitive.german: Die Verlängerung der gesunden Lebenszeit ist das Hauptziel moderner medizinischer Forschung.
genitive.english: Extending healthy lifespan is the main goal of modern medical research.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Verlängerung. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on gesunden.

die Lebenszeit.proTip: Idiom: 'auf Lebenszeit' (for life / tenure): 'Er wurde zum Richter auf Lebenszeit ernannt' (He was appointed judge for life). Synonym: die Lebensdauer (lifespan, especially of machines/products).

der Oktopus.note: Masculine noun of Greek origin meaning 'the octopus' (plural: die Oktopusse or die Oktopoden). Strong masculine declension: der Oktopus (nom), den Oktopus (akk), dem Oktopus (dat), des Oktopus (gen, without -es ending according to standard Duden usage for foreign -us nouns).

nominative.german: Der hochentwickelte Oktopus besitzt drei Herzen und blaues Blut.
nominative.english: The highly developed octopus possesses three hearts and blue blood.
nominative.hint: Subject of besitzt, so nominative. Masculine nominative article Der; weak adjective ending -e on hochentwickelte.

accusative.german: Das Kamerateam filmte einen getarnten Oktopus beim geschickten Öffnen einer Muschel.
accusative.english: The camera crew filmed a camouflaged octopus cleverly opening a mussel.
accusative.hint: Direct object of filmte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on getarnten.

dative.german: Mit seinen acht Fangarmen entkam das Meerestier dem neugierigen Oktopus nur knapp.
dative.english: With its eight tentacles the sea creature escaped from the curious octopus only narrowly.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by entkommen (jemandem entkommen). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on neugierigen.

genitive.german: Die erstaunliche Intelligenz des lernfähigen Oktopus überrascht Biologen immer wieder.
genitive.english: The astonishing intelligence of the adaptive octopus surprises biologists time and again.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Intelligenz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on lernfähigen; noun Oktopus retains its form without ending.

der Oktopus.proTip: From Greek okto (eight) + pous (foot). Synonyms: der Krake (masculine n-noun: der Krake, den Kraken). Plural forms in German: die Oktopusse (most common) or die Oktopoden (Greek scholarly plural).

höchstwahrscheinlich.note: Adverb meaning 'most likely, very probably', formed from höchst (most) + wahrscheinlich (probable). As an adverb it is invariable and never takes case endings; the case in each example below is demonstrated on a different noun phrase in the sentence.

nominative.german: Höchstwahrscheinlich wird der neue Manager das Projekt übernehmen.
nominative.english: The new manager will most likely take over the project.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird ... übernehmen, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e on neue. Höchstwahrscheinlich itself stays unchanged.

accusative.german: Höchstwahrscheinlich gewinnt unsere Mannschaft den entscheidenden Wettkampf.
accusative.english: Our team will most likely win the decisive competition.
accusative.hint: Direct object of gewinnt, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on entscheidenden.

dative.german: Höchstwahrscheinlich hilft die Regierung den betroffenen Familien schnell.
dative.english: The government will most likely help the affected families quickly.
dative.hint: Dative required by helfen. Plural dative article den; weak adjective ending -en on betroffenen; plural noun adds -n.

genitive.german: Höchstwahrscheinlich ist sich der Zeuge seiner Aussage völlig sicher.
genitive.english: The witness is most likely completely sure of his testimony.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by the idiom sich einer Sache sicher sein. Feminine possessive seiner takes the weak genitive ending -er; noun Aussage takes no ending.

höchstwahrscheinlich.proTip: Höchstwahrscheinlich is an invariable adverb; it never takes case endings itself, so always look for a real noun or pronoun phrase elsewhere in the sentence to demonstrate case.

hochtechnisiert.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'highly technological, highly advanced technologically', from hoch (highly) + technisiert (technicalized, past participle of technisieren). It declines like a regular adjective, agreeing with the noun it modifies.

nominative.german: Eine hochtechnisierte Fabrik produziert die Bauteile vollautomatisch.
nominative.english: A highly technological factory produces the components fully automatically.
nominative.hint: Subject of produziert, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Das Unternehmen baute eine hochtechnisierte Anlage in nur einem Jahr.
accusative.english: The company built a highly technological facility in just one year.
accusative.hint: Direct object of baute, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: In dieser hochtechnisierten Umgebung fühlen sich viele Mitarbeiter überfordert.
dative.english: In this highly technological environment, many employees feel overwhelmed.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine dative determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on hochtechnisierten.

genitive.german: Die Kosten der hochtechnisierten Ausrüstung überstiegen das Budget deutlich.
genitive.english: The costs of the highly technological equipment significantly exceeded the budget.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on hochtechnisierten.

hochtechnisiert.proTip: Hochtechnisiert typically describes industries, societies, or environments that rely heavily on advanced technology, e.g. eine hochtechnisierte Gesellschaft.

hochwertig.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'high-quality', from hoch (high) + Wert (value) + -ig. It declines regularly like any descriptive adjective.

nominative.german: Dieses hochwertige Material hält viele Jahre lang.
nominative.english: This high-quality material lasts for many years.
nominative.hint: Subject of hält, so nominative. Neuter weak declension after dieses: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Kunde bestellte ein hochwertiges Produkt aus heimischer Produktion.
accusative.english: The customer ordered a high-quality product from domestic production.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bestellte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit hochwertigem Werkzeug arbeitet man deutlich präziser.
dative.english: With high-quality tools one works significantly more precisely.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on hochwertigem.

genitive.german: Die Herstellung hochwertiger Möbel erfordert viel Erfahrung.
genitive.english: The production of high-quality furniture requires a lot of experience.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Herstellung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on hochwertiger.

hochwertig.proTip: Hochwertig commonly modifies Material, Produkt, or Inhaltsstoffe; avoid the redundant collocation 'hochwertige Qualität' since Qualität already implies value.

hörbar.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'audible', from hören (to hear) + -bar (able to be...). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein hörbares Seufzen ging durch den Saal.
nominative.english: An audible sigh went through the hall.
nominative.hint: Subject of ging, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Die Mikrofone nahmen ein deutlich hörbares Rauschen auf.
accusative.english: The microphones picked up a clearly audible hum.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nahmen ... auf, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit hörbarem Erstaunen reagierte das Publikum auf die Nachricht.
dative.english: The audience reacted to the news with audible astonishment.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on hörbarem.

genitive.german: Trotz des kaum hörbaren Knackens bemerkte niemand den Fehler.
genitive.english: Despite the barely audible crackling, nobody noticed the fault.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hörbaren; noun Knacken adds genitive -s.

hörbar.proTip: Hörbar is the opposite of unhörbar (inaudible); it describes sounds that reach the ear, whether faint or clear.

hundertprozentig.note: Adjective/adverb meaning 'one hundred percent, fully, completely'. As an attributive adjective before a noun it takes normal adjective endings (eine hundertprozentige Garantie); used adverbially before a verb it stays invariable (sich hundertprozentig verlassen). The examples below show the attributive, case-marked use.

nominative.german: Eine hundertprozentige Garantie kann hier leider niemand geben.
nominative.english: Unfortunately nobody can give a hundred percent guarantee here.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann ... geben, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Trainer verlangt von seinem Team einen hundertprozentigen Einsatz.
accusative.english: The coach demands one hundred percent commitment from his team.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verlangt, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit hundertprozentiger Konzentration meisterte sie die Prüfung.
dative.english: With one hundred percent concentration she mastered the exam.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on hundertprozentiger.

genitive.german: Die Qualität der hundertprozentigen Baumwolle überzeugt selbst empfindliche Haut.
genitive.english: The quality of the hundred percent cotton convinces even sensitive skin.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Qualität. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on hundertprozentigen.

hundertprozentig.proTip: Check whether hundertprozentig precedes a noun (it declines: eine hundertprozentige Garantie) or a verb/adjective (it stays invariable: hundertprozentig sicher sein).

ideell.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'idealistic, non-material', often contrasted with materiell (material). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein ideeller Wert zählt für sie mehr als Geld.
nominative.english: A non-material value matters more to her than money.
nominative.hint: Subject of zählt, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Verein verfolgt einen rein ideellen Zweck.
accusative.english: The association pursues a purely idealistic purpose.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verfolgt, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit ideellem Engagement unterstützt er die Nachbarschaftshilfe.
dative.english: With idealistic commitment he supports the neighborhood assistance group.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on ideellem.

genitive.german: Die Bedeutung des ideellen Gewinns übersteigt oft den finanziellen.
genitive.english: The significance of the non-material gain often exceeds the financial one.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bedeutung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ideellen; noun Gewinn adds genitive -s.

ideell.proTip: Ideell (non-material, idealistic) has a double -ll; do not confuse it with ideal (ideal, perfect), which is spelled with a single -l.

immens.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'immense'. It declines like a regular adjective and often intensifies nouns like Aufwand, Summe, or Schaden.

nominative.german: Ein immenser Aufwand steckte hinter der Organisation des Festivals.
nominative.english: Immense effort lay behind the organization of the festival.
nominative.hint: Subject of steckte, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Firma investierte eine immense Summe in die neue Technologie.
accusative.english: The company invested an immense sum in the new technology.
