accusative.hint: Direct object of investierte, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit immenser Geduld erklärte die Lehrerin den Stoff erneut.
dative.english: With immense patience the teacher explained the material again.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on immenser.

genitive.german: Angesichts des immensen Schadens wurde sofort Hilfe geschickt.
genitive.english: In view of the immense damage, help was sent immediately.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by angesichts. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on immensen; noun Schaden adds genitive -s.

immens.proTip: Immens is a near-synonym of gewaltig or riesig, used to intensify abstract or measurable nouns such as effort, sums, or damage.

inakzeptabel.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'unacceptable'. Like other adjectives ending in -abel, it drops the e before an ending: inakzeptabel -> inakzeptable, never 'inakzeptabele'.

nominative.german: Eine inakzeptable Verzögerung brachte den ganzen Zeitplan durcheinander.
nominative.english: An unacceptable delay threw the whole schedule into disarray.
nominative.hint: Subject of brachte ... durcheinander, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e (the -abel drops its e before the ending).

accusative.german: Der Kunde beanstandete eine inakzeptable Wartezeit am Schalter.
accusative.english: The customer complained about an unacceptable waiting time at the counter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beanstandete, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit einer inakzeptablen Ausrede versuchte er sich zu rechtfertigen.
dative.english: With an unacceptable excuse he tried to justify himself.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine mixed declension after einer: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Wegen des inakzeptablen Verhaltens wurde der Spieler vom Platz gestellt.
genitive.english: Because of the unacceptable behavior, the player was sent off the field.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on inakzeptablen; noun Verhalten adds genitive -s.

inakzeptabel.proTip: Adjectives ending in -abel/-ibel drop the e before any ending: inakzeptabel -> eine inakzeptable Ausrede (never 'inakzeptabele').

inbegriffen.note: Past-participle adjective meaning 'included'. It most often appears predicatively and unchanged after sein (das Frühstück ist inbegriffen), but declines like a regular adjective when placed attributively before a noun, as shown below.

nominative.german: Die inbegriffene Verpflegung überraschte alle Gäste positiv.
nominative.english: The included catering pleasantly surprised all the guests.
nominative.hint: Subject of überraschte, so nominative. Feminine weak declension after die: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Das Hotel bietet eine inbegriffene Halbpension für alle Zimmer.
accusative.english: The hotel offers included half-board for all rooms.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bietet, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Neben dem inbegriffenen Frühstück gibt es einen kostenlosen Shuttleservice.
dative.english: Besides the included breakfast there is a free shuttle service.
dative.hint: Dative governed by neben. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on inbegriffenen.

genitive.german: Der Umfang des inbegriffenen Services variiert je nach Tarif.
genitive.english: The scope of the included service varies depending on the tariff.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Umfang. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on inbegriffenen; loanword Service adds genitive -s.

inbegriffen.proTip: Inbegriffen most commonly stays unchanged in predicate position (im Preis inbegriffen) but declines normally when it precedes a noun, e.g. die inbegriffenen Getränke.

individuell.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'individual, personal', describing something tailored to a single person or case. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein individueller Plan passt sich den Bedürfnissen jedes Schülers an.
nominative.english: An individual plan adapts to the needs of each student.
nominative.hint: Subject of passt ... an, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Beraterin erstellt für jeden Kunden eine individuelle Lösung.
accusative.english: The consultant creates an individual solution for every customer.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erstellt, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit individueller Betreuung erreichen die Schüler bessere Ergebnisse.
dative.english: With individual support the students achieve better results.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on individueller.

genitive.german: Die Berücksichtigung individueller Wünsche steht im Mittelpunkt des Konzepts.
genitive.english: Taking individual wishes into account is at the heart of the concept.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Berücksichtigung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on individueller.

individuell.proTip: Individuell contrasts with allgemein (general) or standardisiert (standardized); common collocations include individuelle Betreuung and individueller Plan.

innig.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'intimate, close, deep' (of feelings or relationships). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine innige Freundschaft verband die beiden seit der Kindheit.
nominative.english: A close friendship connected the two of them since childhood.
nominative.hint: Subject of verband, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Sie pflegte eine innige Beziehung zu ihrer Großmutter.
accusative.english: She maintained a deep relationship with her grandmother.
accusative.hint: Direct object of pflegte, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit inniger Zuneigung kümmerte sich die Tante um die Kinder.
dative.english: With deep affection the aunt looked after the children.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on inniger.

genitive.german: Die Kraft dieser innigen Verbundenheit half ihnen durch schwere Zeiten.
genitive.english: The strength of this deep bond helped them through hard times.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kraft. Feminine genitive determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on innigen.

innig.proTip: Innig describes emotional depth or closeness (innige Liebe, innige Freundschaft); distinguish it from intim, which more often implies physical or private closeness.

integrativ.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'integrative', describing approaches that bring different groups or elements together. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein integrativer Ansatz verbindet unterschiedliche Fachrichtungen.
nominative.english: An integrative approach combines different disciplines.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbindet, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Schule verfolgt ein integratives Konzept für alle Kinder.
accusative.english: The school pursues an integrative concept for all children.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verfolgt, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit einem integrativen Unterricht profitieren auch schwächere Schüler.
dative.english: With integrative teaching, weaker students also benefit.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine mixed declension after einem: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Erfolg des integrativen Modells überzeugte viele Lehrkräfte.
genitive.english: The success of the integrative model convinced many teachers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erfolg. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on integrativen; noun Modell adds genitive -s.

integrativ.proTip: Integrativ is common in education (integrativer Unterricht) and medicine (integrative Medizin), describing methods that unite different elements or groups.

interaktiv.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'interactive', describing technology or activities that respond to user input. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein interaktives Spiel hält die Kinder stundenlang beschäftigt.
nominative.english: An interactive game keeps the children occupied for hours.
nominative.hint: Subject of hält ... beschäftigt, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Der Lehrer nutzt eine interaktive Tafel im Unterricht.
accusative.english: The teacher uses an interactive whiteboard in class.
accusative.hint: Direct object of nutzt, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit interaktiven Übungen lernen die Schüler viel schneller.
dative.english: With interactive exercises the students learn much faster.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: plural dative ending -en on interaktiven.

genitive.german: Die Beliebtheit interaktiver Apps steigt bei jungen Nutzern stetig.
genitive.english: The popularity of interactive apps is steadily rising among young users.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Beliebtheit. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on interaktiver.

interaktiv.proTip: Interaktiv describes anything that responds to user input; common collocations include interaktives Whiteboard and interaktive Landkarte.

interkulturell.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'intercultural' (inter- + kulturell), describing exchange or relations between different cultures. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein interkultureller Austausch bereichert beide Seiten enorm.
nominative.english: An intercultural exchange enriches both sides enormously.
nominative.hint: Subject of bereichert, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Universität fördert eine interkulturelle Zusammenarbeit zwischen den Fakultäten.
accusative.english: The university promotes intercultural cooperation between the faculties.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fördert, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit interkultureller Kompetenz meistert sie schwierige Verhandlungen im Ausland.
dative.english: With intercultural competence she masters difficult negotiations abroad.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on interkultureller.

genitive.german: Das Ziel des interkulturellen Projekts war gegenseitiges Verständnis.
genitive.english: The goal of the intercultural project was mutual understanding.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ziel. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on interkulturellen; noun Projekt adds genitive -s.

interkulturell.proTip: Interkulturell is frequent in education and business contexts, especially in the fixed phrase interkulturelle Kompetenz (intercultural competence).

internetbasiert.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'internet-based' (Internet + basiert, from basieren auf). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine internetbasierte Plattform erlaubt Zugriff von überall her.
nominative.english: An internet-based platform allows access from anywhere.
nominative.hint: Subject of erlaubt, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Das Unternehmen entwickelte eine internetbasierte Lösung für den Kundenservice.
accusative.english: The company developed an internet-based solution for customer service.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwickelte, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit einem internetbasierten System sparen die Mitarbeiter viel Zeit.
dative.english: With an internet-based system the employees save a lot of time.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter mixed declension after einem: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Sicherheit des internetbasierten Zahlungssystems wird regelmäßig geprüft.
genitive.english: The security of the internet-based payment system is checked regularly.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Sicherheit. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on internetbasierten; noun Zahlungssystem adds genitive -s.

internetbasiert.proTip: Internetbasiert is a modern compound meaning something that runs on or relies on the internet; common in technology and business vocabulary.

intim.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'intimate', describing close, private, or personal closeness. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein intimes Gespräch entwickelte sich zwischen den beiden alten Freunden.
nominative.english: An intimate conversation developed between the two old friends.
nominative.hint: Subject of entwickelte sich, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Sie teilte mit ihm ein sehr intimes Geheimnis.
accusative.english: She shared a very intimate secret with him.
accusative.hint: Direct object of teilte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: In einer intimen Atmosphäre fühlten sich die Gäste sehr wohl.
dative.english: In an intimate atmosphere the guests felt very comfortable.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Feminine mixed declension after einer: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Details dieser intimen Begegnung blieben unter den Freunden geheim.
genitive.english: The details of this intimate encounter remained secret among the friends.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Details. Feminine genitive determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on intimen.

intim.proTip: Intim describes personal or emotional closeness, often private in nature; distinguish it from privat (private, not necessarily emotionally close).

irgendein/e/r.note: Indefinite determiner/pronoun meaning 'some (or other), any', built on irgend- + ein. Unlike a descriptive adjective, it declines exactly like ein itself for gender and case, both before a noun and standing alone as a pronoun.

nominative.german: Irgendeiner wird das Problem schon lösen.
nominative.english: Someone or other will solve the problem eventually.
nominative.hint: Subject of wird ... lösen, so nominative. Used as a pronoun (no noun follows), it takes the strong masculine nominative ein-word ending -er.

accusative.german: Sie hat sich irgendeinen Regenschirm aus dem Fundbüro geliehen.
accusative.english: She borrowed some umbrella or other from the lost-and-found office.
accusative.hint: Direct object of geliehen (hat ... geliehen), so accusative. Masculine ein-word ending -en on irgendeinen.

dative.german: Er vertraut irgendeinem Fremden aus dem Internet zu schnell.
dative.english: He trusts some stranger from the internet too quickly.
dative.hint: Dative required by vertrauen. Masculine ein-word ending -em on irgendeinem.

genitive.german: Die Bemerkung irgendeines Zuschauers brachte ihn völlig aus der Fassung.
genitive.english: Some spectator's remark completely unsettled him.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bemerkung. Masculine ein-word ending -es on irgendeines; noun Zuschauer adds genitive -s.

irgendein/e/r.proTip: Irgendein/e/r declines exactly like ein (irgendeiner, irgendeinen, irgendeinem, irgendeines); irgend- simply adds vagueness, meaning 'some... or other' or 'any old...'.

ironisch.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'ironic', related to the noun die Ironie. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein ironischer Kommentar sorgte für Gelächter im Saal.
nominative.english: An ironic comment caused laughter in the hall.
nominative.hint: Subject of sorgte, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Autor verwendet gern einen ironischen Ton in seinen Texten.
accusative.english: The author likes to use an ironic tone in his texts.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verwendet, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit ironischem Lächeln quittierte sie die Ausrede ihres Kollegen.
dative.english: With an ironic smile she acknowledged her colleague's excuse.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on ironischem.

genitive.german: Der Sinn dieser ironischen Bemerkung erschloss sich nicht jedem.
genitive.english: The point of this ironic remark was not clear to everyone.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Sinn. Feminine genitive determiner dieser; weak adjective ending -en on ironischen.

ironisch.proTip: Ironisch describes statements that mean the opposite of what they literally say; the related noun is die Ironie (irony).

irreal.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'unreal' (ir- + real). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine irreale Vorstellung beherrschte plötzlich sein Denken.
nominative.english: An unreal notion suddenly dominated his thinking.
nominative.hint: Subject of beherrschte, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Roman beschreibt eine völlig irreale Welt voller Fantasiewesen.
accusative.english: The novel describes a completely unreal world full of fantasy creatures.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beschreibt, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit irrealen Erwartungen ging er in das Vorstellungsgespräch.
dative.english: He went into the job interview with unreal expectations.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: plural dative ending -en on irrealen.

genitive.german: Die Wirkung irrealer Ängste auf den Alltag wird oft unterschätzt.
genitive.english: The effect of unreal fears on everyday life is often underestimated.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Wirkung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on irrealer.

irreal.proTip: Irreal means unreal or not corresponding to reality; the grammatical term der Irrealis refers to hypothetical, contrary-to-fact conditional forms.

isoliert.note: Past-participle adjective meaning 'isolated; insulated', from the verb isolieren. It declines like a regular adjective and can describe both physical insulation and social or situational isolation.

nominative.german: Ein isolierter Vorfall reicht nicht aus, um das ganze System zu verurteilen.
nominative.english: A single isolated incident is not enough to condemn the whole system.
nominative.hint: Subject of reicht ... aus, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Elektriker prüfte ein isoliertes Kabel im Sicherungskasten.
accusative.english: The electrician checked an insulated cable in the fuse box.
accusative.hint: Direct object of prüfte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: In einem isolierten Dorf in den Bergen gibt es kaum Internetempfang.
dative.english: In an isolated village in the mountains there is hardly any internet reception.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (location). Neuter mixed declension after einem: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Bewohner des isolierten Tals leben fast völlig autark.
genitive.english: The residents of the isolated valley live almost completely self-sufficiently.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bewohner. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on isolierten; noun Tal adds genitive -s.

isoliert.proTip: Isoliert can describe physical insulation (ein isoliertes Kabel) or social/situational isolation (ein isolierter Vorfall, sozial isoliert); it comes from the verb isolieren.

jahrzehntelang.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'for decades, decades-long', from Jahrzehnt (decade) + -lang (a suffix meaning 'lasting for', as in stundenlang, wochenlang). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine jahrzehntelange Freundschaft verband die beiden Familien.
nominative.english: A decades-long friendship connected the two families.
nominative.hint: Subject of verband, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Verein feierte eine jahrzehntelange Tradition.
accusative.english: The club celebrated a decades-long tradition.
accusative.hint: Direct object of feierte, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Nach jahrzehntelanger Erfahrung kennt der Winzer jeden Weinberg genau.
dative.english: After decades of experience the winemaker knows every vineyard precisely.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on jahrzehntelanger.

genitive.german: Trotz jahrzehntelanger Warnung haben viele Menschen noch immer kein Klimabewusstsein.
genitive.english: Despite decades of warning, many people still have no climate awareness.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Strong declension without an article: feminine genitive ending -er on jahrzehntelanger.

jahrzehntelang.proTip: Jahrzehntelang declines as a normal attributive adjective; related time compounds include stundenlang (for hours) and jahrelang (for years).

jenseits.note: Preposition meaning 'beyond', always governing the genitive case (jenseits der Grenze). It is invariable and never takes endings itself; the non-genitive examples below demonstrate other cases on separate noun phrases within jenseits-sentences.

nominative.german: Jenseits der Grenze liegt ein kleines Dorf.
nominative.english: Beyond the border lies a small village.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es. Jenseits itself stays unchanged and here governs der Grenze in the genitive.

accusative.german: Jenseits des Flusses entdeckten die Wanderer einen alten Turm.
accusative.english: Beyond the river the hikers discovered an old tower.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entdeckten, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Jenseits der Stadtgrenze hilft man den Neuankömmlingen bei der Eingewöhnung.
dative.english: Beyond the city limits, people help the newcomers settle in.
dative.hint: Dative required by helfen. Plural dative article den; plural noun adds -n.

genitive.german: Ich wüsste gern, was mit meinen Daten noch jenseits der Werbung passiert.
genitive.english: I would like to know what else happens to my data beyond advertising.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed directly by jenseits, its own fixed government. Feminine genitive article der; noun Werbung takes no ending.

jenseits.proTip: Jenseits is an invariable preposition that always takes the genitive (jenseits des Flusses); do not confuse it with the noun das Jenseits (the hereafter/afterlife).

jugendgefährdend.note: Present-participle adjective meaning 'harmful to minors, corrupting to youth', from jugendgefährden. It declines like a regular adjective and is a legal/media term for content unsuitable for minors.

nominative.german: Ein jugendgefährdender Film darf im Fernsehen nicht vor 22 Uhr laufen.
nominative.english: A film harmful to minors may not be broadcast on television before 10 p.m.
nominative.hint: Subject of darf ... laufen, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Behörde entfernte einen jugendgefährdenden Beitrag von der Plattform.
accusative.english: The authority removed a post harmful to minors from the platform.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entfernte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit jugendgefährdendem Material handelte der Verkäufer eindeutig illegal.
dative.english: By dealing in material harmful to minors, the seller was clearly acting illegally.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on jugendgefährdendem.

genitive.german: Die Verbreitung jugendgefährdender Inhalte wird strafrechtlich verfolgt.
genitive.english: The distribution of content harmful to minors is prosecuted under criminal law.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Verbreitung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on jugendgefährdender.

jugendgefährdend.proTip: Jugendgefährdend is related to the official media rating term keine Jugendfreigabe; it describes content deemed harmful for young people.

kalkulierbar.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'calculable, predictable', from kalkulieren (to calculate) + -bar. It declines like a regular adjective; opposite: unkalkulierbar.

nominative.german: Ein kalkulierbares Risiko lässt sich versichern.
nominative.english: A calculable risk can be insured.
nominative.hint: Subject of lässt sich versichern, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Die Analysten erwarten einen kalkulierbaren Verlust im nächsten Quartal.
accusative.english: The analysts expect a predictable loss next quarter.
accusative.hint: Direct object of erwarten, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit kalkulierbarem Aufwand lässt sich das Projekt gut planen.
dative.english: With calculable effort the project can be planned well.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative ending -em on kalkulierbarem.

genitive.german: Die Höhe des kalkulierbaren Schadens wurde von Experten geschätzt.
genitive.english: The extent of the calculable damage was estimated by experts.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Höhe. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on kalkulierbaren; noun Schaden adds genitive -s.

kalkulierbar.proTip: Kalkulierbar describes risks or costs that can be reasonably predicted or planned for; its opposite is unkalkulierbar (unpredictable).

karitativ.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'charitable', from Latin caritas (charity, love). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine karitative Organisation sammelte Spenden für die Flutopfer.
nominative.english: A charitable organization collected donations for the flood victims.
nominative.hint: Subject of sammelte, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Konzern unterstützt jährlich ein karitatives Projekt.
accusative.english: The corporation supports a charitable project every year.
accusative.hint: Direct object of unterstützt, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit karitativem Engagement half die Gemeinde den Geflüchteten.
dative.english: With charitable commitment the community helped the refugees.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on karitativem.

genitive.german: Der Erfolg karitativer Projekte hängt oft von Freiwilligen ab.
genitive.english: The success of charitable projects often depends on volunteers.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Erfolg. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on karitativer.

karitativ.proTip: Karitativ derives from Latin caritas; common collocations include karitative Organisation and karitatives Engagement.

karrierebedingt.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'career-related, due to one's career', from Karriere + bedingt ('conditioned by'). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein karrierebedingter Umzug stellte die ganze Familie vor Herausforderungen.
nominative.english: A career-related move presented challenges for the whole family.
nominative.hint: Subject of stellte, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Sie akzeptierte einen karrierebedingten Wohnortwechsel ohne zu zögern.
accusative.english: She accepted a career-related change of residence without hesitation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of akzeptierte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit karrierebedingtem Stress kämpfen viele junge Berufstätige.
dative.english: Many young professionals struggle with career-related stress.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative ending -em on karrierebedingtem.

genitive.german: Die Folgen karrierebedingter Trennungen belasten oft die Partnerschaft.
genitive.english: The consequences of career-related separations often burden the relationship.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Folgen. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on karrierebedingter.

karrierebedingt.proTip: Karrierebedingt describes something caused or necessitated by one's career, such as a move or separation; compare urlaubsbedingt, altersbedingt.

klanglich.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'sonic, acoustic, relating to sound', from Klang (sound, tone). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein klanglicher Unterschied fiel den Musikern sofort auf.
nominative.english: A sonic difference was immediately noticeable to the musicians.
nominative.hint: Subject of fiel ... auf, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Toningenieur suchte einen klanglichen Ausgleich zwischen den Instrumenten.
accusative.english: The sound engineer sought a sonic balance between the instruments.
accusative.hint: Direct object of suchte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit klanglicher Präzision begeisterte das Orchester das Publikum.
dative.english: With acoustic precision the orchestra delighted the audience.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on klanglicher.

genitive.german: Die Philharmonie ist wegen ihrer klanglichen Wirkung weltberühmt.
genitive.english: The philharmonic hall is world-famous for its acoustic effect.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Feminine possessive ihrer takes the weak genitive ending -er... actually ihrer itself is the ending; weak adjective ending -en on klanglichen.

klanglich.proTip: Klanglich describes qualities perceived through sound (klangliche Wirkung, klanglicher Unterschied); compare akustisch, which refers more to sound as a physical phenomenon.

klimafreundlich.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'climate-friendly' (Klima + freundlich). It declines like a regular adjective; near-synonym klimaschonend, opposite klimaschädlich.

nominative.german: Ein klimafreundliches Verkehrsmittel gewinnt in Städten an Bedeutung.
nominative.english: A climate-friendly means of transport is gaining importance in cities.
nominative.hint: Subject of gewinnt ... an Bedeutung, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Die Stadt fördert eine klimafreundliche Mobilität für alle Bürger.
accusative.english: The city promotes climate-friendly mobility for all citizens.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fördert, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit klimafreundlicher Energie lässt sich der Ausstoß deutlich senken.
dative.english: With climate-friendly energy, emissions can be significantly reduced.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on klimafreundlicher.

genitive.german: Der Ausbau klimafreundlicher Energielösungen hat für die Region hohe Priorität.
genitive.english: The expansion of climate-friendly energy solutions is a high priority for the region.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Ausbau. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on klimafreundlicher.

klimafreundlich.proTip: Klimafreundlich is a near-synonym of klimaschonend, both describing the opposite of klimaschädlich (harmful to the climate).

klimaschädlich.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'harmful to the climate' (Klima + schädlich). It declines like a regular adjective; the input example uses the superlative klimaschädlichste.

nominative.german: Ein klimaschädliches Gas entweicht bei der Verbrennung fossiler Brennstoffe.
nominative.english: A gas harmful to the climate escapes when fossil fuels are burned.
nominative.hint: Subject of entweicht, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Die Fabrik stieß jahrelang ein klimaschädliches Nebenprodukt aus.
accusative.english: For years the factory emitted a by-product harmful to the climate.
accusative.hint: Direct object of stieß ... aus, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit klimaschädlichem Verhalten schadet man kommenden Generationen.
dative.english: With behavior harmful to the climate, one harms coming generations.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on klimaschädlichem.

genitive.german: Der Flugverkehr ist wegen seines klimaschädlichen Ausstoßes stark umstritten.
genitive.english: Air travel is highly controversial because of its harmful climate emissions.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine possessive seines; weak adjective ending -en on klimaschädlichen; noun Ausstoß adds genitive -es.

klimaschädlich.proTip: Klimaschädlich describes anything that damages the climate, e.g. klimaschädliche Gase or klimaschädlicher Flugverkehr; opposite: klimafreundlich.

klimaschonend.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'climate-friendly' (Klima + schonend, 'sparing'). It declines like a regular adjective; near-synonym klimafreundlich.

nominative.german: Eine klimaschonende Technik setzt sich zunehmend in der Industrie durch.
nominative.english: A climate-friendly technique is increasingly prevailing in industry.
nominative.hint: Subject of setzt sich ... durch, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Das Unternehmen entwickelte ein klimaschonendes Verfahren zur Stahlproduktion.
accusative.english: The company developed a climate-friendly process for steel production.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwickelte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit klimaschonenden Methoden lässt sich der CO2-Ausstoß senken.
dative.english: With climate-friendly methods, CO2 emissions can be reduced.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: plural dative ending -en on klimaschonenden.

genitive.german: Die Entwicklung klimaschonender Techniken wird von der Regierung gefördert.
genitive.english: The development of climate-friendly techniques is promoted by the government.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Entwicklung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on klimaschonender.

klimaschonend.proTip: Klimaschonend and klimafreundlich are near-synonyms, both contrasting with klimaschädlich (harmful to the climate).

klimaunverträglich.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'harmful to the climate, climate-incompatible' (Klima + unverträglich). It declines like a regular adjective and is a stronger synonym of klimaschädlich.

nominative.german: Ein klimaunverträglicher Lebensstil belastet die Umwelt langfristig.
nominative.english: A climate-incompatible lifestyle burdens the environment in the long term.
nominative.hint: Subject of belastet, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Kritiker nennen den Kurzstreckenflug einen klimaunverträglichen Luxus.
accusative.english: Critics call the short-haul flight a climate-incompatible luxury.
accusative.hint: Accusative predicate complement of nennen (jemanden/etwas als etwas bezeichnen). Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit klimaunverträglichem Konsum schaden wir kommenden Generationen.
dative.english: With climate-incompatible consumption we harm future generations.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative ending -em on klimaunverträglichem.

genitive.german: Die Folgen klimaunverträglichen Verhaltens zeigen sich schon heute.
genitive.english: The consequences of climate-incompatible behavior are already visible today.
genitive.hint: Genitive after Folgen. Strong declension without an article: neuter genitive ending -en on klimaunverträglichen; noun Verhalten adds genitive -s.

klimaunverträglich.proTip: Klimaunverträglich is a stronger, more formal synonym of klimaschädlich, often used in critical or scientific contexts.

knapp.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'tight, scarce, barely enough'; it can also mean 'just under' before numbers (knapp 100 Leute). It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine knappe Mehrheit stimmte für den Vorschlag.
nominative.english: A narrow majority voted for the proposal.
nominative.hint: Subject of stimmte, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Die Familie hatte nur ein knappes Budget für die Reise.
accusative.english: The family only had a tight budget for the trip.
accusative.hint: Direct object of hatte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit knapper Zeit blieb kaum Raum für Fehler.
dative.english: With little time, there was hardly any room for mistakes.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on knapper.

genitive.german: Wegen des knappen Angebots stiegen die Preise sprunghaft.
genitive.english: Because of the scarce supply, prices rose sharply.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on knappen; noun Angebot adds genitive -s.

knapp.proTip: Knapp describes something barely sufficient or narrowly measured (eine knappe Mehrheit, knappe Zeit); with numbers it means 'just under' (knapp 100 Leute).

kognitiv.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'cognitive', relating to mental processes like thinking, memory, and perception. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein kognitiver Prozess steuert die Entscheidungsfindung.
nominative.english: A cognitive process controls decision-making.
nominative.hint: Subject of steuert, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Studie untersuchte einen kognitiven Effekt bei älteren Probanden.
accusative.english: The study examined a cognitive effect in older subjects.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit kognitivem Training verbessern sich die Gedächtnisleistungen.
dative.english: With cognitive training, memory performance improves.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on kognitivem.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung kognitiver Fähigkeiten steht im Zentrum des Projekts.
genitive.english: The study of cognitive abilities is at the center of the project.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Erforschung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on kognitiver.

kognitiv.proTip: Kognitiv relates to mental processes such as thinking, memory, and perception; a common collocation is kognitive Fähigkeiten (cognitive abilities).

komfortabel.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'comfortable, convenient'. Like other adjectives ending in -abel, it drops the e before an ending: komfortabel -> komfortabler, never 'komfortabeler'.

nominative.german: Ein komfortabler Sitz macht die lange Fahrt angenehmer.
nominative.english: A comfortable seat makes the long journey more pleasant.
nominative.hint: Subject of macht, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er (the -abel drops its e before the ending).

accusative.german: Das Hotel bietet ein komfortables Zimmer mit Meerblick.
accusative.english: The hotel offers a comfortable room with an ocean view.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bietet, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit einer komfortablen Lösung sparen die Nutzer viel Zeit.
dative.english: With a convenient solution, users save a lot of time.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine mixed declension after einer: adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Preis des komfortablen Wagens überraschte viele Käufer.
genitive.english: The price of the comfortable car surprised many buyers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Preis. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on komfortablen; noun Wagen adds genitive -s.

komfortabel.proTip: Adjectives ending in -abel drop the e before any ending: komfortabel -> ein komfortabler Sitz (never 'komfortabeler').

kommerziell.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'commercial', from Latin commercium. It declines like a regular adjective; opposite: nichtkommerziell or gemeinnützig.

nominative.german: Ein kommerzieller Erfolg blieb dem Film zunächst verwehrt.
nominative.english: Commercial success was initially denied to the film.
nominative.hint: Subject of blieb ... verwehrt, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Firma verfolgt einen rein kommerziellen Zweck.
accusative.english: The company pursues a purely commercial purpose.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verfolgt, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit kommerziellem Interesse beteiligte sich der Investor am Projekt.
dative.english: With commercial interest, the investor took part in the project.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on kommerziellem.

genitive.german: Die Grenzen des kommerziellen Einsatzes sind gesetzlich geregelt.
genitive.english: The limits of commercial use are regulated by law.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Grenzen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on kommerziellen; noun Einsatz adds genitive -es.

kommerziell.proTip: Kommerziell describes anything oriented toward trade or profit; its opposite is nichtkommerziell or gemeinnützig (non-profit).

kompetent.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'competent', describing someone with the necessary skill or authority. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein kompetenter Berater erkennt die Probleme sofort.
nominative.english: A competent advisor recognizes the problems immediately.
nominative.hint: Subject of erkennt, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Firma sucht eine kompetente Fachkraft für die Buchhaltung.
accusative.english: The company is looking for a competent specialist for accounting.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sucht, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit kompetentem Personal löst die Klinik auch schwierige Fälle.
dative.english: With competent staff, the clinic solves even difficult cases.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: neuter dative ending -em on kompetentem.

genitive.german: Die Meinung eines kompetenten Experten war für die Entscheidung entscheidend.

accusative.hint: Direct object of hielt, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit monologischer Rede überzeugte er die Jury kaum.
dative.english: With a one-sided speech he barely convinced the jury.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on monologischer.

genitive.german: Die Wirkung monologischer Präsentationen lässt oft zu wünschen übrig.
genitive.english: The effect of monologue-style presentations often leaves something to be desired.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Wirkung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on monologischer.

monologisch.proTip: Monologisch (from Monolog) describes one-sided, non-interactive speech; matches the input's man stellt sich ... monologisch vor.

monoton.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'monotonous', describing dull, unvarying repetition. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein monotoner Tagesablauf machte sie zunehmend unzufrieden.
nominative.english: A monotonous daily routine made her increasingly unhappy.
nominative.hint: Subject of machte, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Der Zuhörer bemerkte einen monotonen Tonfall in der Stimme.
accusative.english: The listener noticed a monotonous tone in the voice.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bemerkte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit monotoner Stimme las der Sprecher die Nachrichten vor.
dative.english: With a monotonous voice the announcer read the news.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on monotoner.

genitive.german: Die Vermeidung monotoner Sprechweise verbessert jede Präsentation.
genitive.english: Avoiding a monotonous manner of speaking improves any presentation.
genitive.hint: Genitive after Vermeidung. Strong declension without an article: feminine genitive ending -er on monotoner.

monoton.proTip: Monoton describes dull, unvarying repetition; matches the input's man darf ... nicht monoton werden.

moralisch.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'moral', from Latin mos, moralis, relating to ethics and conduct. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine moralische Frage beschäftigte die Philosophen jahrhundertelang.
nominative.english: A moral question occupied philosophers for centuries.
nominative.hint: Subject of beschäftigte, so nominative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Richter berücksichtigte eine moralische Verpflichtung des Angeklagten.
accusative.english: The judge took into account a moral obligation of the defendant.
accusative.hint: Direct object of berücksichtigte, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit moralischer Unterstützung half die Familie dem Angeklagten.
dative.english: With moral support the family helped the defendant.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on moralischer.

genitive.german: Die Klärung moralischer Fragen erfordert oft viel Zeit.
genitive.english: Clarifying moral questions often requires a lot of time.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Klärung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on moralischer.

moralisch.proTip: Moralisch (from Latin mos, moralis) relates to ethics and conduct; matches the input's es müssen noch viele moralische Fragen diskutiert werden.

motorisiert.note: Past-participle adjective meaning 'motorized', from Motor. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein motorisiertes Fahrzeug erleichtert den Transport der Waren.
nominative.english: A motorized vehicle facilitates the transport of goods.
nominative.hint: Subject of erleichtert, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Der Bauer kaufte einen motorisierten Pflug für den Hof.
accusative.english: The farmer bought a motorized plow for the farm.
accusative.hint: Direct object of kaufte, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit motorisiertem Zugang lässt sich der Campingplatz schneller erreichen.
dative.english: With motorized access, the campsite can be reached faster.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative ending -em on motorisiertem.

genitive.german: Die Nutzung motorisierter Fahrzeuge ist in diesem Naturschutzgebiet verboten.
genitive.english: The use of motorized vehicles is prohibited in this nature reserve.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Nutzung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on motorisierter.

motorisiert.proTip: Motorisiert (from Motor) describes something equipped with an engine; matches the input's ich will keinen motorisierten Zugang zum Campingplatz.

motorsportlich.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'motorsport-related' (Motorsport + -lich), describing anything related to motor racing. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein motorsportliches Ereignis lockte tausende Besucher an.
nominative.english: A motorsport event attracted thousands of visitors.
nominative.hint: Subject of lockte ... an, so nominative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

accusative.german: Der Verein organisierte ein motorsportliches Turnier für Amateure.
accusative.english: The club organized a motorsport tournament for amateurs.
accusative.hint: Direct object of organisierte, so accusative. Neuter mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit motorsportlichem Ehrgeiz trainierte er jeden Tag auf der Strecke.
dative.english: With motorsport ambition he trained every day on the track.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: masculine dative ending -em on motorsportlichem.

genitive.german: Die Organisation motorsportlicher Veranstaltungen erfordert viel Erfahrung.
genitive.english: Organizing motorsport events requires a lot of experience.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Organisation. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on motorsportlicher.

motorsportlich.proTip: Motorsportlich (Motorsport + -lich) describes anything related to motor racing; matches the input's motorsportliche Übungen sind untersagt.

mühsam.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'laborious, arduous' (Mühe + -sam), describing something requiring great effort. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein mühsamer Aufstieg führte die Wanderer schließlich zum Gipfel.
nominative.english: An arduous climb finally led the hikers to the summit.
nominative.hint: Subject of führte, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Handwerker leisteten eine mühsame Arbeit unter der heißen Sonne.
accusative.english: The workers performed laborious work under the hot sun.
accusative.hint: Direct object of leisteten, so accusative. Feminine mixed declension after eine: adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit mühsamer Geduld reparierte er die alte Uhr.
dative.english: With laborious patience he repaired the old clock.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on mühsamer.

genitive.german: Die Ergebnisse mühsamer Recherchen füllten mehrere Ordner.
genitive.english: The results of laborious research filled several folders.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Ergebnisse. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on mühsamer.

mühsam.proTip: Mühsam (Mühe + -sam) describes something requiring great effort; matches the input's comparative seit ich 60 bin, ist das Erinnern schon mühsamer geworden.

mysteriös.note: Attributive adjective meaning 'mysterious', from Mysterium (mystery), describing something puzzling or enigmatic. It declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein mysteriöser Fremder betrat plötzlich das Wirtshaus.
nominative.english: A mysterious stranger suddenly entered the inn.
nominative.hint: Subject of betrat, so nominative. Masculine mixed declension after ein: adjective ending -er (Fremder itself is an adjectival noun with the same ending).

accusative.german: Der Roman beschreibt einen mysteriösen Todesfall im Schloss.
accusative.english: The novel describes a mysterious death in the castle.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beschreibt, so accusative. Masculine mixed declension after einen: adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit mysteriöser Stimme erzählte sie die alte Legende.
dative.english: With a mysterious voice she told the old legend.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Strong declension without an article: feminine dative ending -er on mysteriöser.

genitive.german: Die Lösung mysteriöser Fälle begeistert viele Krimileser.
genitive.english: Solving mysterious cases delights many crime novel readers.
genitive.hint: Genitive plural after Lösung. Strong declension without an article: plural genitive ending -er on mysteriöser.

mysteriös.proTip: Mysteriös (from Mysterium, mystery) describes something puzzling or enigmatic; matches the input's die Geschichte deines neuen Hörbuchs klingt sehr mysteriös.

nachfolgend.note: Adjective meaning 'following, subsequent' (from the verb nachfolgen, 'to follow after'). Used almost exclusively attributively before a noun; there it takes regular adjective endings (strong/weak/mixed) depending on the accompanying article.

nominative.german: Die nachfolgende Regelung gilt für alle Mitarbeiter.
nominative.english: The following regulation applies to all employees.
nominative.hint: Subject of gilt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Bitte lesen Sie den nachfolgenden Abschnitt sorgfältig durch.
accusative.english: Please read the following section carefully.
accusative.hint: Direct object of lesen ... durch, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Nach dem nachfolgenden Verfahren wird der Antrag bearbeitet.
dative.english: According to the following procedure, the application is processed.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Sinn des nachfolgenden Abschnitts erschließt sich erst beim zweiten Lesen.
genitive.english: The meaning of the following section only becomes clear on a second reading.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Sinn. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en; noun Abschnitt adds -s.

nachfolgend.proTip: nachfolgend is used almost only attributively, rarely predicatively; in formal texts it also stands alone as a nominalized neuter, das Nachfolgende (the following, i.e. what comes next).

nachhaltig.note: Adjective meaning 'sustainable' (environmentally or economically durable). Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it takes regular adjective endings depending on the article, or strong endings with none.

nominative.german: Nachhaltige Energie gewinnt in der Industrie zunehmend an Bedeutung.
nominative.english: Sustainable energy is becoming increasingly important in industry.
nominative.hint: Subject of gewinnt, so nominative. No article, so the adjective takes the strong feminine ending -e.

accusative.german: Die Firma fördert ein nachhaltiges Wirtschaften in allen Abteilungen.
accusative.english: The company promotes sustainable management in all departments.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fördert, so accusative. Neuter ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -es on the adjective.

dative.german: Der Verein setzt sich für Projekte mit nachhaltigem Nutzen ein.
dative.english: The association is committed to projects with a sustainable benefit.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine noun Nutzen with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Der Erfolg nachhaltiger Landwirtschaft hängt von vielen Faktoren ab.
genitive.english: The success of sustainable agriculture depends on many factors.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erfolg. Feminine noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong genitive ending -er.

nachhaltig.proTip: nachhaltig originally described sustainable-yield forestry (nachhaltige Forstwirtschaft) before spreading to ecology and economics generally. Related noun: die Nachhaltigkeit (sustainability).

nachteilig.note: Adjective meaning 'disadvantageous, detrimental'. Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Die nachteilige Entwicklung der Wirtschaft beunruhigt viele Bürger.
nominative.english: The detrimental development of the economy worries many citizens.
nominative.hint: Subject of beunruhigt, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Manager wollte diese nachteilige Entscheidung unbedingt vermeiden.
accusative.english: The manager wanted to avoid this disadvantageous decision at all costs.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vermeiden, so accusative. Feminine diese; weak adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Aus nachteiligen Gründen wurde der Vertrag storniert.
dative.english: For disadvantageous reasons, the contract was cancelled.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -en.

genitive.german: Wegen der nachteiligen Folgen entschied sich die Firma dagegen.
genitive.english: Because of the disadvantageous consequences, the company decided against it.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Feminine plural genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en.

nachteilig.proTip: Antonym: vorteilhaft (advantageous). Common pattern: nachteilig für + accusative, e.g. nachteilig für die Gesundheit (detrimental to health).

nachtragend.note: Adjective meaning 'resentful, holding a grudge' (from nachtragen, 'to hold something against someone'). Most common predicatively (nicht nachtragend sein), where it takes no ending; used attributively before a noun it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein nachtragender Kollege vergisst Kritik nie.
nominative.english: A resentful colleague never forgets criticism.
nominative.hint: Subject of vergisst, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -er on the adjective.

accusative.german: Niemand mag einen nachtragenden Chef.
accusative.english: Nobody likes a resentful boss.
accusative.hint: Direct object of mag, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit einem nachtragenden Freund ist die Versöhnung schwierig.
dative.english: With a resentful friend, reconciliation is difficult.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Sticheleien des nachtragenden Nachbarn nervten die ganze Straße.
genitive.english: The jibes of the resentful neighbor annoyed the whole street.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Sticheleien. Masculine genitive des; weak adjective ending -en; Nachbar is a weak noun and adds -n rather than -s.

nachtragend.proTip: The common negated idiom is nicht nachtragend sein (to not hold a grudge), as in the source example. Contrast verzeihen (to forgive), the opposite behavior.

nachweisbar.note: Adjective meaning 'demonstrable, provable, verifiable'. Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it takes regular adjective endings.

nominative.german: Ein nachweisbarer Zusammenhang zwischen beiden Faktoren wurde gefunden.
nominative.english: A demonstrable connection between the two factors was found.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde gefunden, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -er on the adjective.

accusative.german: Die Studie liefert einen nachweisbaren Effekt auf die Gesundheit.
accusative.english: The study provides a demonstrable effect on health.
accusative.hint: Direct object of liefert, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Bei nachweisbarem Betrug wird der Vertrag sofort gekündigt.
dative.english: In the case of provable fraud, the contract is terminated immediately.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine noun Betrug with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Trotz nachweisbaren Erfolgs blieb die Finanzierung ungewiss.
genitive.english: Despite demonstrable success, the funding remained uncertain.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. No article, so the adjective takes the strong masculine genitive ending -en; the noun Erfolg adds -s.

nachweisbar.proTip: Distinguish nachweisbar (adjective: demonstrable, capable of being proven, declines normally) from nachweislich (adverb: demonstrably, invariable — see word-4006).

nachweislich.note: Adverb meaning 'demonstrably, verifiably', modifying a verb or clause to say something can be proven. It is related to the adjective nachweisbar but does not itself decline for case; it is invariable in every position. The examples below show each case on a different noun or pronoun phrase in a sentence containing nachweislich.

nominative.german: Nachweislich hat der Zeuge die Wahrheit gesagt.
nominative.english: The witness demonstrably told the truth.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat ... gesagt, so nominative; masculine nominative article der. Nachweislich itself takes no ending — it modifies the whole statement, not the noun.

accusative.german: Der Arzt konnte nachweislich einen Zusammenhang belegen.
accusative.english: The doctor was demonstrably able to prove a connection.
accusative.hint: Direct object of belegen, so accusative; masculine accusative einen. The case comes from belegen, not from the invariable adverb nachweislich.

dative.german: Nachweislich half die Therapie dem Patienten deutlich.
dative.english: The therapy demonstrably helped the patient significantly.
dative.hint: Dative required by helfen, which always takes a dative object. Nachweislich stays unchanged; the case sits on the noun helfen governs.

genitive.german: Trotz nachweislich hoher Kosten wurde das Projekt genehmigt.
genitive.english: Despite demonstrably high costs, the project was approved.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz; strong plural ending -er on hoher (no article). Nachweislich here modifies the adjective hoher but adds no ending of its own.

nachweislich.proTip: Distinguish nachweislich (adverb: demonstrably, verifiably, invariable) from nachweisbar (adjective: demonstrable, which declines attributively: ein nachweisbarer Erfolg). Nachweislich commonly precedes a verb or an adjective: nachweislich falsch (demonstrably false).

namhaft.note: Adjective meaning 'renowned, well-known'. Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein namhafter Architekt hat das Museum entworfen.
nominative.english: A renowned architect designed the museum.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat ... entworfen, so nominative. Masculine ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -er on the adjective.

accusative.german: Die Stadt engagierte einen namhaften Künstler für das Wandbild.
accusative.english: The city hired a renowned artist for the mural.
accusative.hint: Direct object of engagierte, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Der Preis wurde einem namhaften Wissenschaftler verliehen.
dative.english: The prize was awarded to a renowned scientist.
dative.hint: Dative required by verleihen (indirect object: to whom). Masculine dative einem; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Unterschrift des namhaften Malers erhöht den Wert des Bildes.
genitive.english: The signature of the renowned painter increases the value of the picture.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Unterschrift. Masculine genitive des; weak adjective ending -en; noun Maler adds genitive -s.

namhaft.proTip: From der Name + -haft ('having the quality of'); contrast berühmt (famous) — namhaft implies notable standing rather than pure fame. Also used in eine namhafte Summe (a considerable sum).

nennenswert.note: Adjective meaning 'noteworthy, worth mentioning', almost always appearing with a negation (kein nennenswerter ...) or after trotz/ohne. Attributively it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Kein nennenswerter Fortschritt wurde in diesem Quartal erzielt.
nominative.english: No noteworthy progress was made this quarter.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde erzielt, so nominative. Kein behaves like ein, so the masculine nominative adjective takes the strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Studie fand keinen nennenswerten Unterschied zwischen den Gruppen.
accusative.english: The study found no noteworthy difference between the groups.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fand, so accusative. Masculine accusative keinen; weak adjective ending -en.

dative.german: Mit nennenswertem Aufwand ließe sich das Problem lösen.
dative.english: With significant, noteworthy effort, the problem could be solved.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine noun Aufwand with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Trotz nennenswerter Fortschritte blieb die Lage angespannt.
genitive.english: Despite noteworthy progress, the situation remained tense.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong genitive ending -er.

nennenswert.proTip: From nennen (to name/mention) + -wert (worth); almost always negated or used after trotz/ohne, as in ohne nennenswerten Widerstand (without noteworthy resistance).

neoliberal.note: Adjective meaning 'neoliberal', a loanword formed from neo- + liberal. It declines exactly like other descriptive adjectives.

nominative.german: Die neoliberale Arbeitswelt erscheint vielen Menschen kalt und hart.
nominative.english: The neoliberal working world seems cold and harsh to many people.
nominative.hint: Subject of erscheint, so nominative. Feminine nominative article die; weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Kritiker lehnen die neoliberale Wirtschaftspolitik entschieden ab.
accusative.english: Critics decisively reject neoliberal economic policy.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ablehnen, so accusative. Feminine accusative die; weak adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit neoliberalen Reformen wollte die Regierung den Markt öffnen.
dative.english: With neoliberal reforms, the government wanted to open up the market.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Folgen der neoliberalen Politik spüren viele Arbeitnehmer noch heute.
genitive.english: Many employees still feel the consequences of neoliberal policy today.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Folgen. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en.

neoliberal.proTip: Related noun: der Neoliberalismus. The prefix neo- (from Greek 'new') attaches to many political and cultural terms: neokonservativ, neoklassisch.

neulich.note: Adverb meaning 'recently, the other day', referring to an unspecified point in the recent past. Adverbs do not decline for case; neulich is invariable in every position. The examples below demonstrate each case on other noun or pronoun phrases in sentences containing neulich.

nominative.german: Neulich hat mich ein alter Freund besucht.
nominative.english: The other day an old friend visited me.
nominative.hint: Subject of hat ... besucht, so nominative; masculine ein has no ending, so alter takes the strong ending -er. Neulich itself takes no ending in any position.

accusative.german: Ich habe neulich einen interessanten Artikel gelesen.
accusative.english: I recently read an interesting article.
accusative.hint: Direct object of gelesen, so accusative. Masculine accusative einen; weak adjective ending -en. The case comes from lesen, not from neulich.

dative.german: Neulich bin ich meiner ehemaligen Lehrerin begegnet.
dative.english: The other day I ran into my former teacher.
dative.hint: Dative required by begegnen, which always takes a dative object (and the sein-auxiliary in the perfect tense). Feminine dative meiner; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Neulich wurde mir der Wert unserer Freundschaft erst richtig bewusst.
genitive.english: The other day I only really became aware of the value of our friendship.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert. Feminine genitive possessive unserer; noun Freundschaft takes no ending.

neulich.proTip: neulich refers vaguely to the recent past (unlike a dated event), and contrasts with kürzlich, its more formal near-synonym. Fixed collocation: neulich erst (just recently).

nichtsdestotrotz.note: Adverb meaning 'nevertheless, nonetheless', a fixed, invariable sentence adverb used like trotzdem or dennoch, often placed first with inverted word order. It does not decline for case; the examples below show each case on a different noun or pronoun phrase.

nominative.german: Nichtsdestotrotz gilt diese Regel für alle Mitarbeiter.
nominative.english: Nevertheless, this rule applies to all employees.
nominative.hint: Subject of gilt, so nominative; feminine diese. Nichtsdestotrotz itself contributes no case and takes no ending.

accusative.german: Nichtsdestotrotz sollte man das Risiko nicht unterschätzen.
accusative.english: Nonetheless, one should not underestimate the risk.
accusative.hint: Direct object of unterschätzen, so accusative; neuter das. The case comes from the verb, not from nichtsdestotrotz.

dative.german: Nichtsdestotrotz vertraute sie ihrem alten Freund weiterhin.
dative.english: Nevertheless, she continued to trust her old friend.
dative.hint: Dative required by vertrauen, which always takes a dative object. Masculine dative ihrem; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Nichtsdestotrotz blieb man sich der Verantwortung bewusst.
genitive.english: Nevertheless, one remained aware of the responsibility.
genitive.hint: Genitive required by the fixed phrase sich einer Sache bewusst sein. Feminine genitive article der; noun Verantwortung takes no ending.

nichtsdestotrotz.proTip: A compound of nichts + desto + trotz, literally 'nothing the more for it'. It is invariable and frequently opens a sentence, triggering inverted word order (verb-subject).

nichtsprachlich.note: Adjective meaning 'nonlinguistic, non-verbal' (nicht- + sprachlich). It declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Der nichtsprachliche Ausdruck kann auch falsch interpretiert werden.
nominative.english: Nonlinguistic expression can also be misinterpreted.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann ... interpretiert werden, so nominative. Masculine nominative article der; weak adjective ending -e.

accusative.german: Forscher untersuchen die nichtsprachliche Kommunikation von Kleinkindern.
accusative.english: Researchers study the nonlinguistic communication of toddlers.
accusative.hint: Direct object of untersuchen, so accusative. Feminine accusative die; weak adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit nichtsprachlichen Mitteln lässt sich viel ausdrücken.
dative.english: A lot can be expressed with nonlinguistic means.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Bedeutung nichtsprachlicher Signale wird oft unterschätzt.
genitive.english: The significance of nonlinguistic signals is often underestimated.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bedeutung. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong genitive ending -er.

nichtsprachlich.proTip: Formed with the negating prefix nicht- on sprachlich (linguistic); a close synonym is nonverbal (see word-4014).

nichtssagend.note: Adjective meaning 'meaningless, uninformative', literally 'saying nothing' (nichts + sagend). Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it declines like a regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine nichtssagende Antwort befriedigte die Journalisten nicht.
nominative.english: An uninformative answer did not satisfy the journalists.
nominative.hint: Subject of befriedigte, so nominative. Feminine eine has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -e on the adjective.

accusative.german: Ich fand die nichtssagende Handlung des Films enttäuschend.
accusative.english: I found the meaningless plot of the film disappointing.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fand, so accusative. Feminine accusative die; weak adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Von einer nichtssagenden Rede erwartet niemand Begeisterung.
dative.english: Nobody expects enthusiasm from a meaningless speech.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Feminine dative einer; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Wegen des nichtssagenden Kommentars fühlten sich viele Leser getäuscht.
genitive.english: Because of the meaningless comment, many readers felt deceived.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive des; weak adjective ending -en; noun Kommentar adds -s.

nichtssagend.proTip: Contrasts with aussagekräftig (meaningful, expressive); commonly describes vague political statements or empty plots, as in the source example about a film.

nonverbal.note: Loanword adjective meaning 'nonverbal' (non- + verbal). Without a preceding article it takes strong endings that mirror the definite article; with one it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Nonverbale Kommunikation besteht aus mehreren Teilgebieten.
nominative.english: Nonverbal communication consists of several subfields.
nominative.hint: Subject of besteht, so nominative. No article, so the adjective takes the strong feminine ending -e.

accusative.german: Der Trainer vermittelt nonverbale Körpersprache gezielt.
accusative.english: The trainer specifically teaches nonverbal body language.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vermittelt, so accusative. No article, so the adjective takes the strong feminine ending -e.

dative.german: Mit nonverbalen Signalen drücken wir oft mehr aus als mit Worten.
dative.english: With nonverbal signals we often express more than with words.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Erforschung nonverbaler Kommunikation begann erst im 20. Jahrhundert.
genitive.english: The study of nonverbal communication only began in the 20th century.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erforschung. No article, so the adjective takes the strong feminine genitive ending -er.

nonverbal.proTip: A loanword adjective that declines like any other; when no article precedes, its endings mirror der/die/das exactly. Close synonym: nichtsprachlich (word-4012).

notwendig.note: Adjective meaning 'necessary' (Not + wendig, 'turning need'). Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Eine notwendige Reform des Systems steht längst aus.
nominative.english: A necessary reform of the system is long overdue.
nominative.hint: Subject of steht ... aus, so nominative. Feminine eine has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -e on the adjective.

accusative.german: Der Vorstand beschloss eine notwendige Preiserhöhung.
accusative.english: The board decided on a necessary price increase.
accusative.hint: Direct object of beschloss, so accusative. Feminine eine; mixed adjective ending -e.

dative.german: Mit den notwendigen Unterlagen ging sie zum Amt.
dative.english: With the necessary documents, she went to the office.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural dative article den; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Die Kosten der notwendigen Reparatur überstiegen das Budget.
genitive.english: The cost of the necessary repair exceeded the budget.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Kosten. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en.

notwendig.proTip: Common pattern: notwendig für + accusative (necessary for), e.g. notwendig für den Erfolg; or notwendig, um ... zu + infinitive.

nutzerorientiert.note: Compound adjective (Nutzer + orientiert, from orientieren) meaning 'user-oriented'. It declines like any past-participle-based adjective.

nominative.german: Ein nutzerorientiertes Angebot verbessert die Kundenzufriedenheit.
nominative.english: A user-oriented offering improves customer satisfaction.
nominative.hint: Subject of verbessert, so nominative. Neuter ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -es on the adjective.

accusative.german: Die Firma entwickelt ein nutzerorientiertes Angebot an Transportmitteln.
accusative.english: The company is developing a user-oriented range of transport options.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwickelt, so accusative. Neuter ein; mixed adjective ending -es.

dative.german: Mit einer nutzerorientierten Gestaltung gewinnt die App viele Fans.
dative.english: With a user-oriented design, the app wins many fans.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative einer; weak adjective ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Erfolg des nutzerorientierten Designs überzeugte die Investoren.
genitive.english: The success of the user-oriented design convinced the investors.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erfolg. Neuter genitive des; weak adjective ending -en.

nutzerorientiert.proTip: A compound built on orientieren; similar compounds include zielorientiert (goal-oriented) and praxisorientiert. Emphasizes design geared to user needs, distinct from benutzerfreundlich (ease of use).

nützlich.note: Adjective meaning 'useful'. Used both attributively and predicatively; attributively it declines like any regular adjective.

nominative.german: Ein nützliches Werkzeug erleichtert die tägliche Arbeit.
nominative.english: A useful tool makes daily work easier.
nominative.hint: Subject of erleichtert, so nominative. Neuter ein has no ending, so the mixed declension puts -es on the adjective.

accusative.german: Der Kurs vermittelt nützliche Fähigkeiten für den Berufsalltag.
accusative.english: The course imparts useful skills for everyday work life.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vermittelt, so accusative. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong ending -e.

dative.german: Mit nützlichen Tipps meisterte sie das Vorstellungsgespräch.
dative.english: With useful tips, she mastered the job interview.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong dative ending -en.

genitive.german: Der Wert nützlicher Informationen wird oft unterschätzt.
genitive.english: The value of useful information is often underestimated.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert. Plural noun with no article, so the adjective takes the strong genitive ending -er.

nützlich.proTip: Common pattern: nützlich für + accusative (useful for), e.g. nützlich für die Gesundheit. Antonym: nutzlos (useless).

nutzungsberechtigt.note: Formal/legal compound adjective (Nutzung + berechtigt, from berechtigen) meaning 'authorized to use, entitled to use'. Common predicatively without an ending (as in the source example, Nutzungsberechtigt ist jeder, der ...); attributively before a noun it declines like any regular adjective.
