genitive.hint: Genitive object governed by bedürfen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on notariellen; noun adds -s.

außerdem.proTip: Etymologically composed of außer (outside/besides) + dem (dative demonstrative). Synonyms: zudem, überdies, ferner.

wiedersehen.note: Imported in lowercase; represents both the neuter noun das Wiedersehen ('reunion, meeting again') and the farewell phrase 'Auf Wiedersehen!' ('Goodbye!'). Declension: das Wiedersehen, das Wiedersehen, dem Wiedersehen, des Wiedersehens.

nominative.german: Ein freudiges Wiedersehen nach zwanzig Jahren Trennung rührte die ganze Familie.
nominative.english: A joyful reunion after twenty years of separation moved the whole family.
nominative.hint: Subject of rührte, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on freudiges.

accusative.german: Auf Wiedersehen, lieber Kollege, und eine gute Reise nach Frankfurt!
accusative.english: Goodbye, dear colleague, and have a good journey to Frankfurt!
accusative.hint: Accusative in prepositional farewell formula auf Wiedersehen (auf + Akk.).

dative.german: Bei diesem emotionalen Wiedersehen flossen bei vielen Anwesenden Freudentränen.
dative.english: At this emotional reunion, tears of joy flowed among many present.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on emotionalen.

genitive.german: Der Zauber des ersten Wiedersehens nach dem langen Auslandsaufenthalt war unbeschreiblich.
genitive.english: The magic of the first reunion after the long stay abroad was indescribable.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Zauber. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ersten; noun adds -s.

wiedersehen.proTip: On the phone, German speakers use: 'Auf Wiederhören!' (Goodbye, literally 'until we hear each other again').

stimmt.note: Third-person singular present form of stimmen, used colloquially as an affirmative interjection / discourse formula ('that's true, that's right'). Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Stimmt, der aktuelle Fahrplan gilt erst ab dem kommenden Montag.
nominative.english: That's right, the current timetable is only valid starting next Monday.
nominative.hint: Subject of gilt, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on aktuelle.

accusative.german: Stimmt, diesen wichtigen Aspekt haben wir bei der Budgetkalkulation völlig übersehen.
accusative.english: That's right, this important aspect we completely overlooked in the budget calculation.
accusative.hint: Direct object of übersehen, so accusative. Masculine accusative demonstrative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on wichtigen.

dative.german: Stimmt, mit diesem überraschenden Wahlausgang hatte vorab kein Experte gerechnet.
dative.english: That's right, with this surprising election outcome, no expert had counted beforehand.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Masculine dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on überraschenden.

genitive.german: Stimmt, trotz des massiven Widerstands setzte die Stadtverwaltung das Projekt durch.
genitive.english: That's right, despite the massive resistance, the city council pushed through the project.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on massiven; noun adds -s.

stimmt.proTip: Colloquial short confirmation: 'Stimmt so!' (Keep the change! / That's right!). Opposite: 'Stimmt nicht!' (That's not true!).

verzeihung.note: Imported in lowercase; represents both the polite conversational interjection 'Verzeihung!' ('Pardon! Excuse me!') and the feminine noun die Verzeihung ('forgiveness, pardon'). Declension: die Verzeihung, die Verzeihung, der Verzeihung, der Verzeihung; no plural.

nominative.german: Eine aufrichtige Verzeihung kann langjährige Feindseligkeiten zwischen Menschen beenden.
nominative.english: Sincere forgiveness can end long-standing hostilities between people.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann ... beenden, so nominative. Feminine mixed article Eine; weak adjective ending -e on aufrichtige.

accusative.german: Verzeihung, darf ich Sie kurz nach dem Weg zum Domplatz fragen?
accusative.english: Excuse me, may I ask you briefly for directions to Cathedral Square?
accusative.hint: Polite conversational interjection used to initiate an apology or polite request.

dative.german: Mit aufrichtiger Verzeihung reichten sich die ehemals zerstrittenen Nachbarn die Hand.
dative.english: With sincere forgiveness, the formerly feuding neighbors shook hands.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine without article; strong feminine dative ending -er on aufrichtiger.

genitive.german: Der Wert aufrichtiger Verzeihung zeigt sich oft erst nach vielen Jahren.
genitive.english: The value of sincere forgiveness often only becomes clear after many years.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Wert. With no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine genitive ending -er; the noun Verzeihung adds no genitive -s, as feminine nouns never do.

verzeihung.proTip: Common polite phrases: 'Ich bitte um Verzeihung!' (I beg your pardon / I apologize!), 'Verzeihung bitte!' (Excuse me please!).

absolut.note: Adjective and intensifying adverb meaning 'absolute, completely, utterly, unquestionably'. Declines with regular adjective endings when used attributively: ein absolutes Verbot.

nominative.german: Ein absolutes Halteverbot gilt ab morgen auf der gesamten Länge der Schlossstraße.
nominative.english: An absolute stopping prohibition applies starting tomorrow along the entire length of Castle Street.
nominative.hint: Subject of gilt, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on absolutes.

accusative.german: Der Notfallmediziner verordnete dem Patienten absolute Bettruhe für die kommenden drei Tage.
accusative.english: The emergency physician ordered absolute bed rest for the patient for the next three days.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verordnete, so accusative. Feminine without article; strong accusative ending -e on absolute.

dative.german: Mit absoluter Gewissheit konnte die Zeugin den Tatverdächtigen auf dem Foto identifizieren.
dative.english: With absolute certainty, the witness was able to identify the suspect on the photo.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine without article; strong feminine dative ending -er on absoluter.

genitive.german: Wegen absoluter Geheimhaltung durfte niemand über das Projekt sprechen.
genitive.english: Because of absolute secrecy, nobody was allowed to talk about the project.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen; with no article present, the adjective carries the case itself with the strong feminine genitive ending -er.

absolut.proTip: In modern colloquial German, absolut is frequently used as a standalone affirmative response: 'Kommst du morgen?' - 'Absolut!' (Are you coming tomorrow? - Absolutely!).

vorsicht.note: Imported in lowercase; represents the warning interjection 'Vorsicht!' ('Careful! Watch out!') and the feminine noun die Vorsicht ('caution, prudence, care'). Declension: die Vorsicht, die Vorsicht, der Vorsicht, der Vorsicht; no plural.

nominative.german: Übertriebene Vorsicht kann im Unternehmertum notwendige Innovationen lähmen.
nominative.english: Excessive caution can paralyze necessary innovations in entrepreneurship.
nominative.hint: Subject of kann ... lähmen, so nominative. Feminine without article; strong adjective ending -e on Übertriebene.

accusative.german: Vorsicht beim Überqueren der Gleise, der ICE nähert sich mit hoher Geschwindigkeit!
accusative.english: Watch out when crossing the tracks, the ICE is approaching at high speed!
accusative.hint: Warning interjection / exclamatory accusative formula.

dative.german: Mit größter Vorsicht hob der Archäologe das zerbrechliche Papyrusfragment aus der Kiste.
dative.english: With utmost caution, the archaeologist lifted the fragile papyrus fragment from the box.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine without article; strong feminine dative ending -er on größter.

genitive.german: Aus Gründen der gebotenen Vorsicht wurde die gesamte Schule vorsorglich evakuiert.
genitive.english: For reasons of due caution, the entire school was evacuated as a precaution.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Gründen. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on gebotenen.

vorsicht.proTip: Common saying: 'Vorsicht ist die Mutter der Porzellankiste' (Caution is the mother of the porcelain box = Better safe than sorry).

unbedingt.note: Adjective and emphatic modal adverb meaning 'unconditional, absolute, by all means, without fail'. Declines with standard adjective endings attributively: ein unbedingter Gehorsam.

nominative.german: Ein unbedingter Wille zum Erfolg zeichnet herausragende Spitzensportler aus.
nominative.english: An unconditional will to succeed distinguishes outstanding elite athletes.
nominative.hint: Subject of zeichnet ... aus, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on unbedingter; weak noun Wille.

accusative.german: Ich muss heute unbedingt diese dringende Angelegenheit mit der Bank klären.
accusative.english: I absolutely must clarify this urgent matter with the bank today.
accusative.hint: Direct object of klären, so accusative. Feminine accusative demonstrative diese; weak adjective ending -e on dringende.

dative.german: Mit unbedingtem Vertrauen folgte die Mannschaft den Anweisungen der Trainerin.
dative.english: With unconditional trust, the team followed the coach's instructions.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Neuter without article; strong neuter dative ending -em on unbedingtem.

genitive.german: Trotz des unbedingten Wunsches nach Versöhnung blieben die Fronten verhärtet.
genitive.english: Despite the absolute wish for reconciliation, the positions remained entrenched.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on unbedingten; noun adds -es.

unbedingt.proTip: As an adverb: 'Du musst unbedingt kommen!' (You absolutely must come!). Antonym: bedingt (conditional / qualified).

stopp.note: Imported in lowercase; represents the command interjection 'Stopp!' ('Halt!') and the masculine noun der Stopp ('stop, pause, halt'). Declension: der Stopp, den Stopp, dem Stopp, des Stopps; plural: die Stopps.

nominative.german: Ein kurzer Stopp an der Autobahnraststätte reichte für eine kleine Erfrischung.
nominative.english: A brief stop at the motorway service area was sufficient for a little refreshment.
nominative.hint: Subject of reichte, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on kurzer.

accusative.german: Stopp, bitte betreten Sie den gesicherten Baustellenbereich nicht ohne Schutzhelm!
accusative.english: Stop, please do not enter the secured construction site area without a hard hat!
accusative.hint: Imperative command interjection signaling an immediate halt.

dative.german: Nach einem kurzen Stopp am Aussichtspunkt setzte der Reisebus seine Fahrt fort.
dative.english: After a brief stop at the viewpoint, the coach continued its journey.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on kurzen.

genitive.german: Während des ungeplanten Stopps auf offener Strecke informierte der Lokführer die Fahrgäste.
genitive.english: During the unplanned stop on the open track, the train driver informed the passengers.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by während. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ungeplanten; noun adds -s.

stopp.proTip: Spelled with double 'p' in modern German (der Stopp, das Stoppschild). Common verb: stoppen (to stop, to halt).

raus.note: Invariable directional adverb (colloquial contraction of heraus 'out towards speaker' or hinaus 'out away from speaker') meaning 'out, outside'. Cases are demonstrated on accompanying noun phrases.

nominative.german: Ein kalter Wind wehte von draußen herein, als die Kinder schnell nach draußen raus liefen.
nominative.english: A cold wind blew in from outside as the children quickly ran outside.
nominative.hint: Subject of wehte, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on kalter.

accusative.german: Er warf den alten Müllsack sofort zur Haustür raus in den Abfallcontainer.
accusative.english: He threw the old garbage bag right out the front door into the dumpster.
accusative.hint: Direct object of warf, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on alten.

dative.german: Aus dem brennenden Gebäude kamen die Bewohner glücklicherweise rechtzeitig raus.
dative.english: From the burning building, the residents fortunately got out in time.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on brennenden.

genitive.german: Wegen des anhaltenden Unwetters durfte niemand aus dem Schullandheim raus ins Freie.
genitive.english: Because of the ongoing storm, no one was allowed out into the open from the hostel.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on anhaltenden; noun adds -s.

raus.proTip: Standard German distinguishes direction: heraus (towards the speaker) vs. hinaus (away from the speaker). In spoken German, 'raus' is universally used for both.

drüben.note: Invariable locative adverb indicating a static position on the other side ('over there, across'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Drüben am anderen Ufer des Flusses wartet bereits der nächste Fahrgast auf die Fähre.
nominative.english: Over there on the other bank of the river, the next passenger is already waiting for the ferry.
nominative.hint: Subject of wartet, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on nächste.

accusative.german: Wir sehen drüben auf dem Hügel eine historische Burgruine im Sonnenlicht leuchten.
accusative.english: We see a historic castle ruin gleaming in the sunlight over there on the hill.
accusative.hint: Direct object of sehen, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; weak adjective ending -e on historische.

dative.german: In dem kleinen Straßencafé drüben an der Ecke gibt es den besten Espresso der Stadt.
dative.english: In the little sidewalk cafe over there on the corner, there is the best espresso in town.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on kleinen.

genitive.german: Wegen des großen Parkplatzes drüben am Supermarkt finden Kunden immer eine freie Lücke.
genitive.english: Because of the large parking lot over there by the supermarket, customers always find a free space.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on großen; noun adds -es.

drüben.proTip: Contrast static vs. directional: drüben (static: over there) vs. nach drüben / hinüber (directional: to over there).

rein.note: Directional adverb (contraction of herein 'in towards speaker' or hinein 'in away from speaker') meaning 'in, inside'; also adjective meaning 'pure, clean'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein plötzlicher Platzregen setzte ein, sodass alle schnell ins Haus rein liefen.
nominative.english: A sudden downpour started, so everyone quickly ran in into the house.
nominative.hint: Subject of setzte ... ein, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on plötzlicher.

accusative.german: Der Hausmeister trug den schweren Schreibtisch ins neue Büro rein.
accusative.english: The caretaker carried the heavy desk in into the new office.
accusative.hint: Direct object of trug, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on schweren.

dative.german: In dem trockenen Kellerraum ist es schön kühl, lass uns da rein gehen!
dative.english: In the dry cellar room it is nice and cool, let's go in there!
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on trockenen.

genitive.german: Wegen des strömenden Regens wollten alle Gäste sofort rein ins warme Foyer.
genitive.english: Because of the pouring rain, all guests wanted to get right in into the warm foyer.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on strömenden; noun adds -s.

rein.proTip: Informal spoken German uses rein where written standard uses herein (towards speaker) or hinein (away from speaker).

her.note: Invariable directional adverb denoting movement towards the speaker ('here, hither'). Combines with prepositions (herab, heran, herauf, heraus, herbei). Cases are shown on nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein freundlicher Nachbar rief laut über den Zaun: 'Komm doch mal her!'
nominative.english: A friendly neighbor called out loudly over the fence: 'Do come over here!'
nominative.hint: Subject of rief, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on freundlicher.

accusative.german: Gib mir bitte sofort den ausgeliehenen Schraubenschlüssel her!
accusative.english: Please hand me the borrowed wrench right here!
accusative.hint: Direct object of hergeben, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on ausgeliehenen.

dative.german: Von diesem abgelegenen Bauernhof führt kein befestigter Weg zu uns her.
dative.english: From this remote farmhouse, no paved path leads over here to us.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Masculine dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on abgelegenen.

genitive.german: Trotz des weiten Weges eilte die Großmutter zu ihren Enkelkindern her.
genitive.english: Despite the long distance, the grandmother hurried over here to her grandchildren.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on weiten; noun adds -es.

her.proTip: Crucial distinction in German: her (towards the speaker) vs. hin (away from the speaker). Idiom: 'hin und her' (back and forth).

runter.note: Invariable directional adverb (spoken contraction of herunter 'down towards speaker' or hinunter 'down away from speaker') meaning 'down'. Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal phrases.

nominative.german: Ein erfahrener Bergsteiger stieg den steilen Hang vorsichtig runter.
nominative.english: An experienced mountaineer carefully climbed down the steep slope.
nominative.hint: Subject of stieg ... runter, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on erfahrener.

accusative.german: Der Kurier trug das schwere Paket die Wendeltreppe runter.
accusative.english: The courier carried the heavy package down the spiral staircase.
accusative.hint: Direct object of trug, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on schwere.

dative.german: Von dem hohen Aussichtsturm blickten die Touristen ins weite Tal runter.
dative.english: From the high observation tower, the tourists looked down into the wide valley.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on hohen.

genitive.german: Wegen des eisigen Untergrunds rutschte der Schlitten den Hang unkontrolliert runter.
genitive.english: Because of the icy surface, the sled slid down the slope out of control.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on eisigen; noun adds -s.

runter.proTip: Common compound verbs: runtergehen (to go down), runterfallen (to fall down), runterladen (colloquial for downloaden / herunterladen).

fort.note: Invariable directional adverb / particle meaning 'away, gone, forward, onward'. Combines in separable verbs like fortgehen, fortsetzen. Cases are shown on surrounding nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein starker Windstoß wehte die getrockneten Herbstblätter weit fort.
nominative.english: A strong gust of wind blew the dried autumn leaves far away.
nominative.hint: Subject of wehte ... fort, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on starker.

accusative.german: Die Delegation setzte die schwierigen Friedensgespräche am Nachmittag fort.
accusative.english: The delegation continued the difficult peace talks in the afternoon.
accusative.hint: Direct object of fortsetzen, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on schwierigen.

dative.german: Von seinem vertrauten Heimatort zog der junge Geselle für die Wanderschaft fort.
dative.english: Away from his familiar hometown, the young journeyman moved for his travels.
dative.hint: Dative governed by von. Masculine dative possessive seinem; weak adjective ending -en on vertrauten.

genitive.german: Ungeachtet des schlechten Wetters ritt der Bote ohne Rast fort.
genitive.english: Regardless of the bad weather, the messenger rode away without rest.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by ungeachtet. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on schlechten; noun adds -s.

fort.proTip: Common idioms: 'und so fort' (and so on / etc., abbreviated u.s.f.); fort sein (to be gone / away).

rüber.note: Invariable directional adverb (spoken contraction of herüber 'over towards speaker' or hinüber 'over away from speaker') meaning 'over, across'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein aufmerksamer Nachbar rief freundlich zu uns in den Garten rüber.
nominative.english: An attentive neighbor called over friendly to us into the garden.
nominative.hint: Subject of rief ... rüber, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on aufmerksamer.

accusative.german: Der Junge warf den roten Ball geschickt über den Gartenzaun rüber.
accusative.english: The boy skillfully threw the red ball over across the garden fence.
accusative.hint: Direct object of warf, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on roten.

dative.german: Mit der historischen Seilbahn fuhren die Fahrgäste zur anderen Talseite rüber.
dative.english: With the historic cable car, the passengers rode across to the other side of the valley.
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on historischen.

genitive.german: Trotz des dichten Nebels wagte der Fährmann die Überfahrt ans andere Ufer rüber.
genitive.english: Despite the dense fog, the ferryman dared the crossing over to the other shore.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on dichten; noun adds -s.

rüber.proTip: Colloquial verb: rüberkommen (to come over, or figurately: 'Die Botschaft kommt gut rüber' - the message comes across well).

heraus.note: Invariable directional adverb meaning 'out, out from inside (towards the speaker)'. Separable prefix in herausfinden, herausgeben. Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein dichter Rauch drang aus dem Kellerfenster ins Freie heraus.
nominative.english: Dense smoke penetrated out from the basement window into the open.
nominative.hint: Subject of drang ... heraus, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on dichter.

accusative.german: Die Forscher fanden endlich die wissenschaftliche Ursache des Phänomens heraus.
accusative.english: The researchers finally found out the scientific cause of the phenomenon.
accusative.hint: Direct object of herausfinden, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on wissenschaftliche.

dative.german: Aus dieser schwierigen Notlage half ihr der erfahrene Rechtsanwalt heraus.
dative.english: Out of this difficult predicament, the experienced lawyer helped her.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Feminine dative demonstrative dieser; weak adjective ending -en on schwierigen.

genitive.german: Heraus aus den Tiefen des dunklen Waldes traten die ermüdeten Wanderer.
genitive.english: Out from the depths of the dark forest stepped the fatigued hikers.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after den Tiefen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on dunklen; noun adds -es.

heraus.proTip: Contrast with hinaus (out away from speaker): 'Komm heraus!' (Come out to where I am!) vs. 'Geh hinaus!' (Go out of the room away from me!).

ran.note: Invariable directional adverb (spoken contraction of heran 'up close to speaker' or hinan 'up close away from speaker') meaning 'up to, closer, at it'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein neugieriges Fohlen traute sich ganz nah an den Holzzaun ran.
nominative.english: A curious foal dared to come very close up to the wooden fence.
nominative.hint: Subject of traute sich ... ran, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on neugieriges.

accusative.german: Die Kinder zogen den schweren Bollerwagen ganz dicht an die Picknickbank ran.
accusative.english: The children pulled the heavy handcart very close up to the picnic bench.
accusative.hint: Direct object of zogen, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on schweren.

dative.german: An dieser kniffligen Aufgabe arbeiteten die Schüler mit großer Ausdauer ran.
dative.english: At this tricky task, the students worked with great stamina.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (state/task). Feminine dative demonstrative dieser; weak adjective ending -en on kniffligen.

genitive.german: Trotz des steilen Anstiegs wagten sich die Touristen nah an den Rand der Schlucht ran.
genitive.english: Despite the steep incline, the tourists dared to go close up to the edge of the gorge.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on steilen; noun adds -s.

ran.proTip: Colloquial expressions: 'Ran an die Arbeit!' (Let's get to work!), 'Lass mich mal ran!' (Let me have a go!).

hierher.note: Invariable directional compound adverb (hier + her) meaning '(to) here, hither (movement towards this place)'. Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein berüchtigter Piratenkapitän soll der Legende nach seinen Goldschatz hierher gebracht haben.
nominative.english: A notorious pirate captain is said according to legend to have brought his gold treasure here.
nominative.hint: Subject of soll, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on berüchtigter.

accusative.german: Die Spedition lieferte den neuen Kühlschrank direkt hierher in den zweiten Stock.
accusative.english: The freight forwarder delivered the new refrigerator directly here into the second floor.
accusative.hint: Direct object of lieferte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; mixed adjective ending -en on neuen.

dative.german: Aus einem fernen Land flüchteten die Familien hierher zu ihren Verwandten.
dative.english: From a distant country, the families fled here to their relatives.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Neuter dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on fernen.

genitive.german: Wegen der günstigen Verkehrsanbindung zogen viele Pendler hierher in die Vorstadt.
genitive.english: Because of the favorable transport connections, many commuters moved here to the suburb.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Feminine genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on günstigen.

hierher.proTip: Contrast static vs. directional: hier (static: here, at this place) vs. hierher (directional: to here). 'Komm hierher!' not 'Komm hier!'

rum · herum.note: Invariable adverb pair: herum is standard German, rum is its frequent spoken contraction meaning 'around, in a circle, round about'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein hoher Schutzzaun zieht sich ganz um das gefährdete Werksgelände herum.
nominative.english: A high security fence runs all the way around the vulnerable factory premises.
nominative.hint: Subject of zieht sich, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on hoher.

accusative.german: Der Kapitän steuerte das Frachtschiff sicher um das gefährliche Riff herum.
accusative.english: The captain steered the cargo ship safely around the dangerous reef.
accusative.hint: Accusative object governed by um ... herum. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on gefährliche.

dative.german: Bei diesem verwinkelten Schlossgarten blickte man hinter jeder Hecke neugierig rum.
dative.english: In this winding castle garden, one looked curiously around behind every hedge.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on verwinkelten.

genitive.german: Entlang des gesamten Stadtmauerrings spazierten die Besucher gemütlich um den Altstadtkern herum.
genitive.english: Along the entire city wall ring, visitors strolled leisurely around the old town core.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by entlang. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on gesamten; noun adds -s.

rum · herum.proTip: Prepositional bracket: 'um (+ Akk.) ... herum' (e.g., um das Haus herum). Idioms: um den heißen Brei herumreden (to beat around the bush).

heim.note: Invariable directional adverb meaning 'home, homewards (towards one's home)'. In standard German, nach Hause is also common. Cases are shown on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Der erschöpfte Wanderer kehrte nach Einbruch der Nacht endlich heim.
nominative.english: The exhausted hiker finally returned home after nightfall.
nominative.hint: Subject of kehrte ... heim, so nominative. Masculine definite article Der; weak adjective ending -e on erschöpfte.

accusative.german: Die Mutter begleitete ihr müdes Kind nach dem Laternenumzug heim.
accusative.english: The mother accompanied her tired child home after the lantern procession.
accusative.hint: Direct object of begleitete, so accusative. Neuter accusative possessive determinative ihr; strong adjective ending -es on müdes.

dative.german: Nach einem langen Arbeitstag auf dem Feld eilte der Bauer zufrieden heim.
dative.english: After a long working day in the field, the farmer hurried home contented.
dative.hint: Dative governed by nach. Masculine dative article einem; mixed adjective ending -en on langen.

genitive.german: Trotz des heftigen Schneesturms schafften es alle Bergsteiger wohlbehalten heim.
genitive.english: Despite the fierce blizzard, all mountaineers made it home safe and sound.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on heftigen; noun adds -s.

heim.proTip: Forms compound verbs: heimkehren (to return home), heimfahren (to drive home), heimschicken (to send home), das Heimweh (homesickness).

drin.note: Invariable locative/pronominal adverb (spoken contraction of darin) meaning 'in it, inside, included'. Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein wertvolles Diamantkollier war in dem alten Schmuckkästchen drin.
nominative.english: A valuable diamond necklace was inside the old jewelry box.
nominative.hint: Subject of war ... drin, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on wertvolles.

accusative.german: Der Zollbeamte öffnete den verdächtigen Karton, um zu prüfen, was darin versteckt war.
accusative.english: The customs officer opened the suspicious box to check what was hidden inside.
accusative.hint: Direct object of öffnete, so accusative. Masculine accusative article den; weak adjective ending -en on verdächtigen.

dative.german: In diesem unscheinbaren Umschlag steckte der unterschriebene Kaufvertrag drin.
dative.english: In this inconspicuous envelope, the signed sales contract was tucked inside.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Masculine dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on unscheinbaren.

genitive.german: Wegen des hohen Rabatts ist das Zubehör im Gesamtpreis bereits mit drin.
genitive.english: Because of the high discount, the accessories are already included inside the total price.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on hohen; noun adds -s.

drin.proTip: Informal idiom: 'Das ist zeitlich nicht drin' (That's not feasible / not possible in the timeframe).

zuhause.note: Invariable locative adverb meaning 'at home'; also written zu Hause, or capitalized as the neuter noun das Zuhause ('home, domicile'). Cases are shown on surrounding nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein gemütliches Zuhause bietet Schutz und Geborgenheit im stressigen Alltag.
nominative.english: A cozy home offers protection and security in stressful everyday life.
nominative.hint: Subject of bietet, so nominative (here nominalized das Zuhause). Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on gemütliches.

accusative.german: Die Großeltern schufen für ihre Enkel ein liebevolles Zuhause auf dem Land.
accusative.english: The grandparents created a loving home for their grandchildren in the country.
accusative.hint: Direct object of schufen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article ein; mixed adjective ending -es on liebevolles.

dative.german: In seinem neuen Zuhause fühlt sich der Kater nach anfänglicher Scheu sichtlich wohl.
dative.english: In his new home, the tomcat visibly feels at ease after initial shyness.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Neuter dative possessive seinem; weak adjective ending -en on neuen.

genitive.german: Wegen der behaglichen Atmosphäre ihres Zuhauses verbringen die Bewohner die Abende am liebsten am Kamin.
genitive.english: Because of the cozy atmosphere of their home, the residents prefer spending evenings by the fireplace.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Atmosphäre. Neuter genitive possessive ihres; noun adds -es.

zuhause.proTip: Duden allows both spelling as one word ('zuhause sein') and as two words ('zu Hause sein'). The noun is always capitalized: das Zuhause.

drauf.note: Invariable pronominal adverb (spoken contraction of darauf) meaning 'on it, upon it, onto it, afterwards'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein frischer Zuckerguss kam ganz zum Schluss auf den warmen Kuchen drauf.
nominative.english: Fresh icing was put on top of the warm cake right at the end.
nominative.hint: Subject of kam ... drauf, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on frischer.

accusative.german: Der Handwerker klebte das amtliche Prüfsiegel fest auf die Maschine drauf.
accusative.english: The technician stuck the official inspection seal firmly onto the machine.
accusative.hint: Direct object of klebte, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective ending -e on amtliche.

dative.german: Auf diesem alten Eichentisch stand eine schwere Schreibmaschine drauf.
dative.english: On this old oak table, a heavy typewriter was standing on top.
dative.hint: Dative governed by auf (static location). Masculine dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on alten.

genitive.german: Trotz des glatten Parkettbodens rutschte der schwere Teppich nicht drauf herum.
genitive.english: Despite the smooth parquet floor, the heavy rug did not slip around on it.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on glatten; noun adds -s.

drauf.proTip: Common colloquial idioms: 'gut drauf sein' (to be in a good mood), 'drauf und dran sein, etwas zu tun' (to be on the verge of doing something).

gegenüber.note: Preposition governing the DATIVE case, meaning 'opposite, across from, vis-à-vis, towards'; also locative adverb. Can precede or follow its noun phrase: dem Bahnhof gegenüber / gegenüber dem Bahnhof.

nominative.german: Das neue Rathaus liegt direkt der alten Stadtkirche gegenüber am Marktplatz.
nominative.english: The new town hall is situated directly opposite the old town church on the market square.
nominative.hint: Subject of liegt, so nominative. Neuter definite article Das; weak adjective ending -e on neue.

accusative.german: Die Stadtverwaltung errichtete ein modernes Parkhaus schräg gegenüber der belebten Fußgängerzone.
accusative.english: The municipal administration built a modern parking garage diagonally opposite the bustling pedestrian zone.
accusative.hint: Direct object of errichtete, so accusative. Neuter accusative article ein; mixed adjective ending -es on modernes.

dative.german: Gegenüber dem historischen Hauptbahnhof eröffnet morgen ein elegantes Hotel.
dative.english: Opposite the historic central station, an elegant hotel opens tomorrow.
dative.hint: Dative governed by preposition gegenüber. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on historischen.

genitive.german: Die Fassade des Neubaus gegenüber der Kathedrale wurde aus hellem Sandstein gemauert.
genitive.english: The facade of the new building opposite the cathedral was constructed from light sandstone.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Fassade. Masculine genitive article des; noun adds -s.

gegenüber.proTip: Postposition or preposition: With personal pronouns, gegenüber almost always follows: 'mir gegenüber' (opposite me / towards me), 'ihm gegenüber' (towards him).

dran.note: Invariable pronominal adverb (spoken contraction of daran) meaning 'on it, at it, attached to it, one's turn'. Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein kleiner silberner Schlüssel hing an dem Lederbund fest dran.
nominative.english: A small silver key hung firmly attached to the leather strap.
nominative.hint: Subject of hing ... dran, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective endings -er on kleiner and silberner.

accusative.german: Ich habe den Haken festgeschraubt, damit das Bild sicher dran hängt.
accusative.english: I screwed the hook on tight so that the picture hangs securely on it.
accusative.hint: Direct object of festschrauben, so accusative; masculine der becomes den. Dran is the invariant particle (contraction of daran) and carries no case itself.

dative.german: An dieser schwierigen Aufgabe arbeitet das Forschungsteam schon seit Monaten intensiv dran.
dative.english: On this difficult task, the research team has already been working intensively for months.
dative.hint: Dative governed by an (topic). Feminine dative demonstrative dieser; weak adjective ending -en on schwierigen.

genitive.german: Wegen des enormen Andrangs in der Praxis kam der Patient erst nach Stunden dran.
genitive.english: Because of the enormous crowd in the doctor's office, the patient only got his turn after hours.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on enormen; noun adds -s.

dran.proTip: Everyday idioms: 'Wer ist dran?' (Who's next? / Whose turn is it?), 'gut dran sein' (to be well off), 'schlecht dran sein' (to be badly off).

davor.note: Invariable pronominal adverb (da + vor) meaning 'in front of it, before it (spatial or temporal), before that, of that'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein altersschwacher Zaun stand direkt davor und versperrte den Durchgang.
nominative.english: A decrepit fence stood directly in front of it and blocked the passageway.
nominative.hint: Subject of stand, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on altersschwacher.

accusative.german: Der Chauffeur stellte die gepanzerte Limousine genau davor ab.
accusative.english: The chauffeur parked the armored limousine right in front of it.
accusative.hint: Direct object of abstellte, so accusative. Feminine accusative article die; weak adjective ending -e on gepanzerte.

dative.german: Vor diesem geschichtsträchtigen Denkmal versammelten sich die Bürger zum Gedenken.
dative.english: In front of this historic monument, citizens gathered in commemoration.
dative.hint: Dative governed by vor (static location). Neuter dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on geschichtsträchtigen.

genitive.german: Die Eröffnung des neuen Kongresszentrums war geplant, kurz davor streikten die Bauarbeiter.
genitive.english: The opening of the new convention center was planned; shortly before that, the construction workers went on strike.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Eröffnung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on neuen; noun adds -s.

davor.proTip: Spatial ('Das Auto steht davor' - The car is in front of it) and temporal ('Zwei Tage davor' - Two days before that).

drinnen.note: Invariable locative adverb denoting a static position indoors or inside an enclosed space ('indoors, inside'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein behagliches Kaminfeuer wärmte die Stube, während es draußen stürmte.
nominative.english: A cozy open fire warmed the parlor while it was stormy outside.
nominative.hint: Subject of wärmte, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on behagliches.

accusative.german: Die Bibliothekarin ordnete drinnen im Lesesaal die neu eingetroffenen Fachbücher.
accusative.english: The librarian arranged the newly arrived reference books inside in the reading room.
accusative.hint: Direct object of ordnete, so accusative plural. Plural accusative article die; weak adjective ending -en on eingetroffenen.

dative.german: In dem warmen Gewächshaus drinnen gedeihen tropische Orchideen prächtig.
dative.english: Inside the warm greenhouse, tropical orchids flourish magnificently.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Neuter dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on warmen.

genitive.german: Trotz des ungemütlichen Wetters fühlten sich die Gäste drinnen im Restaurant rundum wohl.
genitive.english: Despite the uncomfortable weather, the guests felt completely at home inside the restaurant.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ungemütlichen; noun adds -s.

drinnen.proTip: Pair of antonyms: drinnen (indoors / inside) vs. draußen (outdoors / outside). Contrast static drinnen with directional rein / hinein.

dagegen.note: Invariable pronominal adverb meaning 'against it, in opposition to it, on the other hand, in contrast'. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein wirksames Gegenmittel wurde im Labor dagegen entwickelt.
nominative.english: An effective antidote was developed in the laboratory against it.
nominative.hint: Subject of wurde ... entwickelt, so nominative. Neuter mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -es on wirksames.

accusative.german: Der Mieterbund legte dagegen fristgerecht einen formellen Widerspruch ein.
accusative.english: The tenants' association lodged a formal objection against it in due time.
accusative.hint: Direct object of einlegte, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on formellen.

dative.german: Bei diesem unfairen Schiedsrichterurteil protestierten die Spieler energisch dagegen.
dative.english: At this unfair referee decision, the players protested vigorously against it.
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Neuter dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on unfairen.

genitive.german: Ungeachtet des heftigen Protests dagegen stimmte der Stadtrat für das Bauprojekt.
genitive.english: Regardless of the fierce protest against it, the city council voted for the construction project.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by ungeachtet. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on heftigen; noun adds -s.

dagegen.proTip: Can function as an adversary pronominal adverb ('Was hast du dagegen?' - What do you have against it?) or as a contrastive connector ('Er liebt Tee, sie dagegen trinkt Kaffee').

draußen.note: Invariable locative adverb denoting a static position outdoors, outside, or in the open air ('outdoors, outside'). Cases are shown on surrounding nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein eisiger Nordwind fegte draußen über die verlassenen Straßen der Stadt.
nominative.english: An icy north wind swept outside across the deserted streets of the city.
nominative.hint: Subject of fegte, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on eisiger.

accusative.german: Die Kinder bauten draußen im Garten einen lustigen Schneemann mit Karottennase.
accusative.english: The children built a funny snowman with a carrot nose outside in the garden.
accusative.hint: Direct object of bauten, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on lustigen.

dative.german: Unter dem schattigen Kastanienbaum draußen im Biergarten lässt es sich wunderbar aushalten.
dative.english: Under the shady chestnut tree outside in the beer garden, one can pass the time wonderfully.
dative.hint: Dative governed by unter (static location). Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on schattigen.

genitive.german: Wegen des dichten Schneetreibens draußen blieben die Schulen heute geschlossen.
genitive.english: Because of the heavy snowfall outside, the schools remained closed today.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on dichten; noun adds -s.

draußen.proTip: Static locative draußen (outside) contrasts with directional raus / hinaus (out, towards outside). Example: 'Lass uns nach draußen gehen!' / 'Wir sitzen draußen.'

ans (= an das).note: Contraction of the two-way preposition an with the neuter definite article in the ACCUSATIVE case (an + das = ans). Denotes direction or target of motion towards a surface or boundary.

nominative.german: Das kleine Fischerdorf schmiegt sich malerisch ans steile Ufer des Meeres an.
nominative.english: The small fishing village nestles picturesquely against the steep shore of the sea.
nominative.hint: Subject of schmiegt sich an, so nominative. Neuter definite article Das; weak adjective ending -e on kleine.

accusative.german: Die Familie fährt in den Sommerferien gerne ans offene Meer zum Entspannen.
accusative.english: The family likes to travel to the open sea in the summer holidays to relax.
accusative.hint: Directional accusative governed by an (ans = an + das). Neuter accusative article das contracted into ans; weak adjective ending -e on offene.

dative.german: Am ruhigen Ufer des Sees verbrachten die Angler einen friedlichen Sonntagmorgen.
dative.english: At the calm shore of the lake, the anglers spent a peaceful Sunday morning.
dative.hint: Contrasting static dative governed by an (am = an + dem). Neuter dative contracted into am; weak adjective ending -en on ruhigen.

genitive.german: Die Fahrt ans andere Ende der Welt erforderte monatelange akribische Vorbereitung.
genitive.english: The journey to the other end of the world required months of meticulous preparation.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Ende; directional phrase contains ans andere Ende. Feminine genitive article der.

ans (= an das).proTip: Crucial distinction: ans (an + das, Accusative for directional motion: 'Ich gehe ans Telefon / ans Meer') vs. am (an + dem, Dative for static location: 'Ich stehe am Telefon / am Meer').

wieso.note: Invariable interrogative causal adverb (wie + so) asking for a reason or explanation ('why, how come'). Often implies mild surprise or skepticism. Cases are demonstrated on clausal nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Wieso hat der zuständige Abteilungsleiter den dringenden Bericht noch nicht unterschrieben?
nominative.english: Why hasn't the responsible department head signed the urgent report yet?
nominative.hint: Subject of hat ... unterschrieben, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on zuständige.

accusative.german: Wieso kritisieren die Journalisten diesen wegweisenden Vorschlag der Kommission?
accusative.english: Why do the journalists criticize this groundbreaking proposal of the commission?
accusative.hint: Direct object of kritisieren, so accusative. Masculine accusative demonstrative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on wegweisenden.

dative.german: Wieso begegnete der Ermittler dem wichtigsten Zeugen mit so viel Misstrauen?
dative.english: Why did the investigator meet the most important witness with so much suspicion?
dative.hint: Dative object governed by begegnen. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on wichtigsten; weak noun Zeuge adds -n.

genitive.german: Wieso bedurfte dieser einfache Vorgang der Genehmigung des gesamten Aufsichtsrats?
genitive.english: Why did this simple procedure require the approval of the entire supervisory board?
genitive.hint: Genitive object governed by bedürfen. Feminine genitive article der.

wieso.proTip: Synonyms: warum, weshalb, weswegen. Wieso is especially frequent in spoken German and when questioning the logic of an action.

soweit.note: Subordinating conjunction of limitation/extent ('as far as') or adverb ('so far, ready'). In subclauses, verbs move to the final position. Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Soweit der offizielle Wetterbericht stimmt, steht uns ein sonniges Frühlingswochenende bevor.
nominative.english: As far as the official weather forecast is correct, a sunny spring weekend lies ahead of us.
nominative.hint: Subject of stimmt, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on offizielle.

accusative.german: Soweit ich diesen komplizierten Gesetzestext verstehe, gibt es eine Ausnahmeregelung für Kleinbetriebe.
accusative.english: As far as I understand this complicated legal text, there is an exception clause for small businesses.
accusative.hint: Direct object of verstehe, so accusative. Masculine accusative demonstrative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on komplizierten.

dative.german: Soweit die Polizei dem anonymen Hinweisgeber vertrauen kann, befindet sich der Täter im Ausland.
dative.english: As far as the police can trust the anonymous informant, the perpetrator is abroad.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by vertrauen. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on anonymen.

genitive.german: Wegen der soweit abgeschlossenen Vorbereitungen kann die Feier wie geplant stattfinden.
genitive.english: Because of the preparations completed so far, the celebration can take place as planned.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Plural genitive article der; weak adjective ending -en on abgeschlossenen.

soweit.proTip: Common formulaic expressions: 'soweit ich weiß' (as far as I know), 'soweit wie möglich' (as far as possible), 'Alles ist soweit' (Everything is ready).

woher.note: Invariable interrogative local adverb (wo + her) asking for origin or source ('from where, whence'). Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Woher stammt der seltene Bernstein, den die Forscher an der Küste fanden?
nominative.english: Where does the rare amber come from that the researchers found on the coast?
nominative.hint: Subject of stammt, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on seltene.

accusative.german: Woher nehmen Sie diesen unerschütterlichen Optimismus angesichts der schwierigen Lage?
accusative.english: Where do you get this unshakeable optimism in the face of the difficult situation?
accusative.hint: Direct object of nehmen, so accusative. Masculine accusative demonstrative diesen; weak adjective ending -en on unerschütterlichen.

dative.german: Aus welchem fernen Land die Antiquität stammt und woher der Händler sie hat, bleibt rätselhaft.
dative.english: From which distant country the antique originates and where the dealer got it from remains mysterious.
dative.hint: Dative governed by aus. Neuter dative interrogative determiner welchem; mixed adjective ending -en on fernen.

genitive.german: Woher das Institut die finanziellen Mittel des millionenschweren Förderprogramms bezieht, ist öffentlich einsehbar.
genitive.english: Where the institute obtains the financial resources of the multi-million-euro funding program from is publicly accessible.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Mittel. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on millionenschweren; noun adds -s.

woher.proTip: Can be split in spoken German: 'Wo hast du das her?' instead of 'Woher hast du das?'. Standard question: 'Woher kommen Sie?' (Where are you from?).

statt.note: Preposition governing the GENITIVE case (in spoken colloquial German often dative), meaning 'instead of'; also conjunction with zu + infinitive. Declension: invariant preposition.

nominative.german: Statt einer teuren Flugreise wählte die umweltbewusste Familie einen erholsamen Campingurlaub am See.
nominative.english: Instead of an expensive flight trip, the environmentally conscious family chose a relaxing camping holiday by the lake.
nominative.hint: Subject of wählte, so nominative. Feminine definite article die; weak adjective ending -e on umweltbewusste.

accusative.german: Die Werkstatt baute statt des defekten Originals einen fabrikneuen Ersatzmotor ein.
accusative.english: The workshop installed a brand-new replacement engine instead of the defective original.
accusative.hint: Direct object of baute ... ein, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on fabrikneuen.

dative.german: Der Chefarzt übertrug die verantwortungsvolle Operation statt dem Assistenten der erfahrenen Oberärztin.
dative.english: The chief physician assigned the responsible surgery to the experienced senior physician instead of the assistant.
dative.hint: Dative recipient object of übertrug. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on erfahrenen.

genitive.german: Statt des erwarteten Gewinns verzeichnete das Unternehmen im letzten Quartal einen spürbaren Verlust.
genitive.english: Instead of the expected profit, the company recorded a noticeable loss in the last quarter.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by preposition statt. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on erwarteten; noun adds -s.

statt.proTip: Longer variant: anstatt (+ Genitiv). In formal and written German, always use the genitive with statt: 'statt des Autos' (not 'statt dem Auto').

wohin.note: Invariable interrogative directional adverb (wo + hin) asking for destination or target of movement ('(to) where, whither'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Wohin führt der schmale Wanderweg durch den dichten Tannenwald?
nominative.english: Where does the narrow hiking trail through the dense fir forest lead?
nominative.hint: Subject of führt, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on schmale.

accusative.german: Wohin hat die Bibliothekarin das wertvolle alte Manuskript gelegt?
accusative.english: Where did the librarian put the valuable old manuscript?
accusative.hint: Direct object of gelegt, so accusative. Neuter accusative article das; weak adjective endings -e on wertvolle and alte.

dative.german: Wohin soll ich dem freundlichen Kellner das Trinkgeld geben?
dative.english: To where should I give the tip to the friendly waiter?
dative.hint: Dative recipient object of geben. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on freundlichen.

genitive.german: Wohin die Reise des frisch vermählten Paares gehen soll, bleibt bis zur Hochzeit eine Überraschung.
genitive.english: Where the journey of the newly wedded couple is to go remains a surprise until the wedding.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Reise. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on vermählten; noun adds -es.

wohin.proTip: Contrast woher (from where) vs. wohin (to where). Can be split in colloquial German: 'Wo gehst du hin?' instead of 'Wohin gehst du?'.

außer.note: Preposition governing the DATIVE case, meaning 'except, apart from, besides, out of'. Declension: invariant preposition.

nominative.german: Außer einem kleinen Schreibfehler enthielt die gesamte Doktorarbeit keine Beanstandungen.
nominative.english: Except for a small typing error, the entire doctoral thesis contained no objections.
nominative.hint: Subject of enthielt, so nominative. Feminine definite article die; weak adjective ending -e on gesamte.

accusative.german: Der Einbrecher entwendete außer dem Familienschmuck auch ein wertvolles Ölgemälde.
accusative.english: The burglar stole a valuable oil painting in addition to the family jewelry.
accusative.hint: Direct object of entwendete, so accusative. Neuter accusative article ein; mixed adjective ending -es on wertvolles.

dative.german: Außer dem diensthabenden Notarzt durfte niemand die Intensivstation betreten.
dative.english: Except for the emergency doctor on duty, no one was allowed to enter the intensive care unit.
dative.hint: Dative governed by preposition außer. Masculine dative article dem; weak adjective ending -en on diensthabenden.

genitive.german: Außer Landes begab sich der Gesandte, um den Friedensvertrag im neutralen Nachbarstaat auszuhandeln.
genitive.english: Out of the country the envoy went to negotiate the peace treaty in the neutral neighboring state.
genitive.hint: Fixed archaic genitive idiom: außer Landes sein / gehen (out of the country).

außer.proTip: Fixed idioms with außer + Dativ: außer Betrieb (out of order), außer Gefahr (out of danger), außer Atem (out of breath), außer Rand und Band (out of control).

wozu.note: Invariable interrogative pronominal adverb (wo + zu) asking for purpose, aim, or reason ('what for, to what end'). Cases are shown on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Wozu dient dieser komplizierte Schalter am Armaturenbrett des Fahrzeugs?
nominative.english: What is this complicated switch on the vehicle's dashboard used for?
nominative.hint: Subject of dient, so nominative. Masculine nominative demonstrative dieser; weak adjective ending -e on komplizierte.

accusative.german: Wozu braucht die Gemeinde einen neuen Sportplatz, wenn der alte noch vollkommen intakt ist?
accusative.english: What does the municipality need a new sports field for when the old one is still completely intact?
accusative.hint: Direct object of braucht, so accusative. Masculine accusative article einen; mixed adjective ending -en on neuen.

dative.german: Wozu verhalf der renommierte Förderpreis der jungen Wissenschaftlerin in ihrer Karriere?
dative.english: What did the prestigious award help the young scientist to in her career?
dative.hint: Dative object governed by verhelfen. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on jungen.

genitive.german: Wozu die Einrichtung des neuen Sonderfonds dienen soll, erläuterte der Finanzminister im Bundestag.
genitive.english: What the establishment of the new special fund is intended to serve, the finance minister explained in the Bundestag.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Einrichtung. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on neuen; noun adds -s.

wozu.proTip: Formulaic usage: 'Wozu das Ganze?' (What's all this for? / What's the point of all this?).

weder … noch.note: Multi-part correlative coordinating conjunction meaning 'neither ... nor'. Coordinates parallel grammatical constituents with identical case. Cases are demonstrated across both conjuncts.

nominative.german: Weder der erfahrene Trainer noch der Vereinsvorstand rechnete mit einer so deutlichen Niederlage.
nominative.english: Neither the experienced coach nor the club board expected such a clear defeat.
nominative.phrase: Weder der erfahrene Trainer noch der Vereinsvorstand
nominative.hint: Coordinated nominative subjects of rechnete. Both parts take masculine nominative article der.

accusative.german: Der Gast bestellte weder den teuren Rotwein noch das angebotene Dessert.
accusative.english: The guest ordered neither the expensive red wine nor the offered dessert.
accusative.phrase: weder den teuren Rotwein noch das angebotene Dessert
accusative.hint: Coordinated accusative direct objects of bestellte. Masculine accusative den teuren Rotwein; neuter accusative das angebotene Dessert.

dative.german: Die Zeugin konnte weder dem ermittelnden Polizisten noch dem Richter eine genaue Beschreibung geben.
dative.english: The witness could give an exact description neither to the investigating police officer nor to the judge.
dative.phrase: weder dem ermittelnden Polizisten noch dem Richter
dative.hint: Coordinated dative recipient objects. Masculine dative dem ermittelnden Polizisten; masculine dative dem Richter.

genitive.german: Der Richter bedurfte weder der Zustimmung der Klägerin noch des Einverständnisses des Beklagten.
genitive.english: The judge required neither the plaintiff's consent nor the defendant's agreement.
genitive.phrase: weder der Zustimmung der Klägerin noch des Einverständnisses
genitive.hint: Coordinated genitive objects governed by bedürfen. Feminine der Zustimmung; neuter des Einverständnisses.

weder … noch.proTip: Correlative pair rule: 'weder' is never used with 'oder'; it always pairs with 'noch'. Verb agreement can be singular or plural in modern usage, singular preferred when subjects are singular.

wofür.note: Invariable interrogative pronominal adverb (wo + für) asking for purpose, cause, or what something is for ('what for, for what, on what'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Wofür ein hochqualifizierter Spezialist gebraucht wird, entscheidet die Projektleitung im Einzelfall.
nominative.english: What a highly qualified specialist is needed for is decided by the project management on a case-by-case basis.
nominative.hint: Subject of gebraucht wird, so nominative. Masculine mixed article ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on hochqualifizierter.

accusative.german: Wofür hat das Unternehmen gestern eine sechsstellige Summe ausgegeben?
accusative.english: What did the company spend a six-figure sum on yesterday?
accusative.hint: Direct object of ausgegeben, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; weak adjective ending -e on sechsstellige.

dative.german: Wofür soll ich bei dieser unklaren Sachlage überhaupt noch danken?
dative.english: What should I thank for at all in this unclear situation?
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative demonstrative dieser; weak adjective ending -en on unklaren.

genitive.german: Wofür die Erträge des städtischen Stiftungsvermögens verwendet werden, legt die Satzung fest.
genitive.english: What the proceeds of the municipal foundation assets are used for is specified in the statutes.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erträge. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on städtischen; noun adds -s.

wofür.proTip: Common question: 'Wofür interessierst du dich?' (What are you interested in?). Prepositional object question for 'sich interessieren für'.

entweder … oder.note: Multi-part correlative disjunctive conjunction presenting mutually exclusive alternatives ('either ... or'). Connects parallel grammatical cases and constituents.

nominative.german: Entweder ein direkter Zeuge oder ein stichhaltiger Sachbeweis ist für eine Verurteilung notwendig.
nominative.english: Either a direct witness or compelling physical evidence is necessary for a conviction.
nominative.phrase: Entweder ein direkter Zeuge oder ein stichhaltiger Sachbeweis
nominative.hint: Coordinated nominative subjects of ist. Both take masculine nominative mixed article ein with strong ending -er.

accusative.german: Die Firma sucht entweder einen erfahrenen Programmierer oder eine qualifizierte Systemanalytikerin.
accusative.english: The company is seeking either an experienced programmer or a qualified systems analyst.
accusative.phrase: entweder einen erfahrenen Programmierer oder eine qualifizierte Systemanalytikerin
accusative.hint: Coordinated direct objects of sucht in accusative. Masculine einen erfahrenen Programmierer; feminine eine qualifizierte Systemanalytikerin.

dative.german: Die Auszeichnung wird entweder dem besten Nachwuchsforscher oder der innovativsten Forschungsgruppe verliehen.
dative.english: The award is conferred either on the best young researcher or on the most innovative research group.
dative.phrase: entweder dem besten Nachwuchsforscher oder der innovativsten Forschungsgruppe
dative.hint: Coordinated dative recipient objects of verliehen. Masculine dem besten Nachwuchsforscher; feminine der innovativsten Forschungsgruppe.

genitive.german: Der Antrag bedarf entweder der schriftlichen Vollmacht des Eigentümers oder eines richterlichen Beschlusses.
genitive.english: The application requires either the owner's written authorization or a judicial order.
genitive.hint: First part of coordinated genitive objects governed by bedürfen; feminine genitive article der.

entweder … oder.proTip: Word order note: 'entweder' can stand in position 1 without causing verb inversion in the first clause: 'Entweder wir fahren heute, oder wir bleiben hier'.

wovon.note: Invariable interrogative pronominal adverb (wo + von) asking about origin, source, topic, or substance ('of what, about what, from what'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Wovon der erfahrene Meister sprach, verstanden die jungen Lehrlinge erst nach Jahren.
nominative.english: What the experienced master spoke of, the young apprentices only understood after years.
nominative.hint: Subject of sprach, so nominative. Masculine definite article der; weak adjective ending -e on erfahrene.

accusative.german: Wovon haben die Ermittler ein so detailreiches Täterprofil anfertigen können?
accusative.english: From what were the investigators able to produce such a detailed perpetrator profile?
accusative.hint: Direct object of anfertigen, so accusative. Neuter accusative article ein; strong adjective ending -es on detailreiches.

dative.german: Wovon träumt ein passionierter Musiker bei seinem ersten großen Auftritt im Konzerthaus?
dative.english: What does a passionate musician dream of during his first big performance in the concert hall?
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Masculine dative possessive seinem; weak adjective endings -en on ersten and großen.

genitive.german: Wovon die Entstehung des Sonnensystems abhing, erforschen Planetologen anhand uralter Meteoriten.
genitive.english: What the formation of the solar system depended on, planetary scientists investigate using ancient meteorites.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Entstehung. Neuter genitive article des; noun adds -s.

wovon.proTip: Everyday question: 'Wovon lebst du?' (What do you live on / earn your living from?). Corresponds to prepositional verb complement: träumen von, abhängen von.

dasselbe.note: Determinative / demonstrative pronoun indicating exact identity ('the very same thing/person'). Inflects like the definite article + selb-: der-/die-/dasselbe, den-/die-/dasselbe, dem-/der-/demselben, des-/der-/desselben.

nominative.german: Dasselbe seltsame Phänomen beobachteten die Wissenschaftler bereits im vorigen Monat.
nominative.english: The very same strange phenomenon the scientists already observed in the previous month.
nominative.hint: Direct object / nominative form dasselbe; in nominative: Dasselbe Phänomen trat erneut auf (Subject of trat auf, so nominative). Neuter definite compound pronoun Dasselbe; weak adjective ending -e on seltsame.

accusative.german: Der Kellner servierte mir versehentlich dasselbe falsche Gericht wie gestern.
accusative.english: The waiter accidentally served me the very same wrong dish as yesterday.
accusative.hint: Direct object of servierte, so accusative. Neuter accusative pronoun dasselbe; weak adjective ending -e on falsche.

dative.german: In demselben alten Hotel verbrachten die Flitterwöchler ihren ersten gemeinsamen Urlaub.
dative.english: In the very same old hotel, the honeymooners spent their first joint holiday.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Neuter dative pronoun demselben; weak adjective ending -en on alten.

genitive.german: Trotz desselben ungünstigen Ausgangspunkts erzielte die zweite Gruppe ein deutlich besseres Ergebnis.
genitive.english: Despite the very same unfavorable starting point, the second group achieved a significantly better result.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by trotz. Masculine genitive pronoun desselben; weak adjective ending -en on ungünstigen; noun adds -s.

dasselbe.proTip: Classic German distinction: dasselbe (identical single object) vs. das gleiche (two identical but separate objects). 'Zwei Frauen tragen das gleiche Kleid, aber niemals dasselbe!'

worauf.note: Invariable interrogative pronominal adverb (wo + [r] + auf) asking for support, target, or topic ('on what, upon what, for what'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Worauf ein moderner Quantencomputer basiert, erklärt die Physikerin in ihrer Vorlesung.
nominative.english: What a modern quantum computer is based on, the physicist explains in her lecture.
nominative.hint: Subject of basiert, so nominative. Masculine mixed article ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on moderner.

accusative.german: Worauf warten die vielen ungeduldigen Fahrgäste am Bahnsteig so lange?
accusative.english: What are the many impatient passengers waiting for on the platform for so long?
accusative.hint: Subject phrase in nominative plural; worauf asks for the prepositional object with auf + accusative (warten auf).

dative.german: Worauf sitzt der alte Uhrmacher bei seiner filigranen Handarbeit?
dative.english: What is the old watchmaker sitting on during his intricate manual work?
dative.hint: Dative governed by bei. Feminine dative possessive seiner; weak adjective ending -en on filigranen.

genitive.german: Worauf die Stabilität des neuen Wolkenkratzers beruht, ist das Fundament aus Spezialbeton.
genitive.english: What the stability of the new skyscraper rests upon is the foundation made of special concrete.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Stabilität. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on neuen; noun adds -s.

worauf.proTip: Forms the question for verbs taking 'auf + Akk.' (warten auf -> worauf wartest du?) or 'auf + Dat.' (sitzen auf -> worauf sitzt du?).

irgendwas.note: Invariable colloquial indefinite pronoun (contraction of irgendetwas) meaning 'something (or other), anything'. Does not inflect. Cases are demonstrated on surrounding nominal arguments.

nominative.german: Irgendwas stimmte an der Geschichte des Tatverdächtigen von Anfang an nicht.
nominative.english: Something was not right with the suspect's story from the very start.
nominative.hint: Subject of stimmte ... nicht, so nominative. Colloquial indefinite pronoun.

accusative.german: Hast du für das gemeinsame Abendessen schon irgendwas Leckeres eingekauft?
accusative.english: Did you already buy something delicious for dinner together?
accusative.hint: Direct object of eingekauft, so accusative. Indefinite pronoun followed by nominalized adjective Leckeres.

dative.german: Mit irgendwas muss der Handwerker die undichte Stelle am Rohr doch abdichten können.
dative.english: With something or other the plumber must surely be able to seal the leaky spot on the pipe.
dative.hint: Dative prepositional phrase governed by mit.

genitive.german: Trotz irgendwelcher Bedenken des Prüfers wurde die Lizenz schließlich erteilt.
genitive.english: Despite any misgivings of the inspector, the license was ultimately granted.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Bedenken. Masculine genitive article des; noun adds -s.

irgendwas.proTip: Colloquial shortened form of irgendetwas; standard in casual spoken German, though in formal writing irgendetwas is preferred.

worüber.note: Invariable interrogative pronominal adverb (wo + [r] + über) asking about topic, subject matter, or cause of emotion ('about what, over what'). Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Worüber die streitenden Parteien debattierten, erfuhr die Öffentlichkeit erst nach der Sitzung.
nominative.english: What the feuding parties were debating about, the public only learned after the meeting.
nominative.hint: Subject of debattierten, so nominative plural. Plural definite article die; weak adjective ending -en on streitenden.

accusative.german: Worüber hat der Minister gestern eine so emotionale Rede gehalten?
accusative.english: What did the minister deliver such an emotional speech about yesterday?
accusative.hint: Direct object of gehalten, so accusative. Feminine accusative article eine; weak adjective ending -e on emotionale.

dative.german: Worüber sprach die Professorin mit ihren interessierten Studierenden nach der Vorlesung?
dative.english: What did the professor speak about with her interested students after the lecture?
dative.hint: Dative governed by mit. Plural dative possessive ihren; weak adjective ending -en on interessierten; noun adds -n.

genitive.german: Worüber die Mitglieder des wissenschaftlichen Beirats uneins waren, betraf die Vergabe der Forschungsgelder.
genitive.english: What the members of the scientific advisory board disagreed on concerned the allocation of research funds.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Mitglieder. Masculine genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on wissenschaftlichen; noun adds -s.

worüber.proTip: Pairs with verbs requiring 'über + Akk.': sprechen über, sich freuen über, nachdenken über. Example: 'Worüber lachst du?' (What are you laughing about?).

irgendetwas.note: Invariable indefinite pronoun meaning 'something, anything, something or other'. Standard German form of colloquial irgendwas. Does not inflect. Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Irgendetwas Unvorhersehbares brachte den gesamten Zeitplan des Projekts durcheinander.
nominative.english: Something unforeseen messed up the entire project schedule.
nominative.hint: Subject of brachte ... durcheinander, so nominative. Indefinite pronoun with capitalized nominalized adjective.

accusative.german: Wir müssen schnell irgendetwas Dringendes unternehmen, um den Wasserschaden zu begrenzen.
accusative.english: We must quickly do something urgent to limit the water damage.
accusative.hint: Direct object of unternehmen, so accusative. Pronoun with nominalized neuter adjective Dringendes.

dative.german: Zu irgendetwas Nützlichem muss diese alte Konstruktion doch zu gebrauchen sein.
dative.english: For something useful, this old construction must surely be usable.
dative.hint: Dative governed by zu. Pronoun with nominalized adjective taking dative ending -em.

genitive.german: Wegen irgendetwas Unwichtigem kam es zu einer heftigen Auseinandersetzung zwischen den Kollegen.
genitive.english: Because of something unimportant, a heated altercation arose between the colleagues.
genitive.hint: Prepositional construction after wegen; invariable irgendetwas with nominalized adjective.

irgendetwas.proTip: Written standard form. When paired with an adjective, the adjective is capitalized and takes strong neuter endings: 'irgendetwas Gutes / Neues / Schönes'.

darum.note: Invariable causal and prepositional pronominal adverb (da + [r] + um) meaning 'therefore, that is why, around it, for that reason'. Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein plötzlicher Wintereinbruch überraschte die Region, darum fiel heute der gesamte Unterricht aus.
nominative.english: A sudden onset of winter surprised the region; that is why all classes were cancelled today.
nominative.hint: Subject of überraschte, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on plötzlicher.

accusative.german: Die Firma expandiert stark, darum stellte sie zehn neue Ingenieure ein.
accusative.english: The company is expanding strongly; that is why it hired ten new engineers.
accusative.hint: Direct object of einstellte, so accusative plural. Plural without article after numeral; strong adjective ending -e on neue.

dative.german: Der Chef vertraut der erfahrenen Buchhalterin vollkommen, darum übertrug er ihr die Kassenprüfung.
dative.english: The boss trusts the experienced bookkeeper completely; that is why he assigned the audit to her.
dative.hint: Dative object governed by vertrauen. Feminine dative article der; weak adjective ending -en on erfahrenen.

genitive.german: Die Erfüllung des ehrgeizigen Klimaziels ist gefährdet, darum bedarf es entschiedener Maßnahmen.
genitive.english: The fulfillment of the ambitious climate goal is at risk; that is why decisive measures are needed.
genitive.hint: Genitive expressing 'of' after Erfüllung. Neuter genitive article des; weak adjective ending -en on ehrgeizigen; noun adds -s.

darum.proTip: Connective adverb causing verb inversion: 'Darum müssen wir handeln' (verb müssen in position 2). Also answers 'Warum?': 'Warum hast du das getan?' - 'Einfach darum!'

irgendwo.note: Invariable indefinite locative adverb meaning 'somewhere, anywhere (in an unspecified place)'. Does not inflect. Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Irgendwo im dichten Dickicht raschelte ein scheues Reh im Unterholz.
nominative.english: Somewhere in the dense thicket, a shy deer rustled in the undergrowth.
nominative.hint: Subject of raschelte, so nominative. Neuter mixed article ein; strong adjective ending -es on scheues.

accusative.german: Der Wanderer hat seinen wasserdichten Rucksack irgendwo am Waldrand vergessen.
accusative.english: The hiker forgot his waterproof backpack somewhere by the edge of the woods.
accusative.hint: Direct object of vergessen, so accusative. Masculine accusative possessive seinen; weak adjective ending -en on wasserdichten.

dative.german: Irgendwo in diesem malerischen Bergdorf muss doch eine gemütliche Gaststätte zu finden sein.
dative.english: Somewhere in this picturesque mountain village, a cozy inn must surely be to find.
dative.hint: Dative governed by in (static location). Neuter dative demonstrative diesem; weak adjective ending -en on malerischen.

genitive.german: Wegen der extremen Abgeschiedenheit des Forschungsstandorts vermuten Astronomen das Observatorium irgendwo in der chilenischen Atacama-Wüste.
genitive.english: Because of the extreme remoteness of the research site, astronomers suspect the observatory is somewhere in the Chilean Atacama Desert.
genitive.hint: Genitive governed by wegen. Masculine genitive article des; noun adds -s.

irgendwo.proTip: Contrast static vs. directional: irgendwo (static: somewhere) vs. irgendwohin (directional: to somewhere) vs. irgendwoher (from somewhere).

deswegen.note: Invariable causal connective adverb meaning 'for that reason, therefore, because of that, that's why'. Causes subject-verb inversion when in position 1. Cases are demonstrated on clausal arguments.

nominative.german: Ein schwerer Maschinenschaden legte das Werk lahm, deswegen musste der Schichtbetrieb vorübergehend ruhen.
nominative.english: Severe machine damage paralyzed the factory; that is why shift operations had to pause temporarily.
nominative.hint: Subject of legte ... lahm, so nominative. Masculine mixed article Ein (no ending); strong adjective ending -er on schwerer.

accusative.german: Die Nachfrage stieg rasant an, deswegen eröffnete das Unternehmen eine weitere Filiale.
accusative.english: Demand rose rapidly; that is why the company opened another branch.
